chunks.title: Orderly SDK v3: Plugin System, Marketplace, and Extensibility
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK v3 introduces a **Frontend Plugin System** and **Module Marketplace** (also referred to as the Builder Marketplace), enabling builders to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of the Orderly trading interface without forking the SDK. ## Overview The Plugin System allows you to extend key areas of the Trading page while keeping your integration upgradable. Instead of maintaining a forked codebase, you write plugins that hook into defined extension points. ### Modules vs. Plugins - **Plugin**: The frontend UI code that plugs into a DEX via the SDK. - **Module**: The complete feature shipped to the marketplace (plugin + optional backend service). Plugins are distributed via the Builder Marketplace at `marketplace.orderly.network`. ### Available Extension Points (v3.1.3+) - **Order Entry** (e.g., `Trading.OrderEntry.SubmitSection`) — Add custom order types or modify the order form - **Chart Overlays** — Inject custom indicators or drawing tools on TradingView charts - **Data List Tabs** — Add new tabs to the data panel (e.g., custom analytics, positions, orders, history) - **Mobile Trading Layout** — Extend the mobile trading experience ## Developer Tools Three primary tools are required for the **skills-first workflow**: 1. **Devkit CLI** (`@orderly.network/devkit`): Scaffolds, builds, and submits plugins. 2. **Plugin Agent Skills** (`OrderlyNetwork/orderly-skills`): Guided AI-agent workflows. 3. **SDK Docs MCP** (`@orderly.network/sdk-docs`): AI-accessible documentation server. ### Installation ```bash # 1. Install Devkit CLI (requires Node.js v20.19.0+) npm install -g @orderly.network/devkit # or pnpm add -g @orderly.network/devkit # 2. Install Agent Skills orderly-devkit skills install # 3. Install SDK Docs MCP orderly-devkit mcp install ``` ## Creating a Plugin Use the `create plugin` command to scaffold a new project from the official template (`OrderlyNetwork/orderly-plugin-template`). ```bash # Interactive mode orderly-devkit create plugin # Non-interactive mode orderly-devkit create plugin --no-interactive \ --name MyPlugin \ --id my-plugin \ --interceptor Trading.OrderEntry.SubmitSection \ --target ./MyPlugin ``` This generates a project with a `.orderly-manifest.json` file. ## Writing Plugin Code Plugins use interceptors that follow the signature `(Original, props, api) => ReactNode`. Key packages include: - `@orderly.network/plugin-core`: Core plugin API (`registerPlugin`, `injectable`). - `@orderly.network/hooks`: React hooks for data and state. - `@orderly.network/ui`: UI components. ### Using `injectable` (Interceptor Pattern) ```tsx import { injectable } from "@orderly.network/plugin-core"; import { useAccount } from "@orderly.network/hooks"; export const MyCustomSection = injectable( "Trading.OrderEntry.SubmitSection", (Original, props) => { const { account } = useAccount(); return (
); } ); ``` ### Using `definePlugin` (Configuration Object Pattern) A typical plugin can also export a configuration object that registers with the SDK: ```typescript import { definePlugin } from '@orderly.network/plugin-sdk'; export default definePlugin({ name: 'my-custom-order-type', version: '1.0.0', // Register extension points extensions: { 'order-entry': { component: () => import('./components/CustomOrderForm'), position: 'after-default' // or 'before-default', 'replace' }, 'chart-overlays': { component: () => import('./components/CustomIndicator') }, 'data-list-tabs': { component: () => import('./components/AnalyticsTab'), tabName: 'Analytics' } } }); ``` ## Integrating a Plugin into a DEX Register the plugin on the `OrderlyAppProvider` using the `plugins` prop. Install plugins from the Module Marketplace or from local packages: ```tsx import { OrderlyAppProvider } from '@orderly.network/react-app'; import myPlugin from './plugins/my-custom-order-type'; import communityAnalytics from '@orderly-marketplace/community-analytics'; import { registerMyPlugin } from "my-plugin-package"; ``` ## Submitting to the Marketplace 1. **Authenticate**: `orderly-devkit login` (uses browser OAuth on port 9876). 2. **Validate**: `orderly-devkit submit --path ./my-plugin --dry-run`. 3. **Submit**: `orderly-devkit submit --path ./my-plugin --tags UI,Trading`. ### Field Validation Rules - `npmName`: Must be a valid npm package name. - `repoUrl`: Must be a GitHub HTTPS URL. - `pluginId`: Must match `/^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$/`. - `tags`: Max 5 from the valid tag set. - `usagePrompt`: Max 8192 characters (used by AI agents). ## AI Agent Integration AI agents can discover modules via the marketplace API (`GET /api/plugins?search=...`) or the `/llm.txt` catalog. The MCP server provides tools like `orderly_docs_search` and `orderly_docs_get_component` for development assistance. ## Responsive Breakpoint Change (v3.0.2+) Starting from v3.0.2, the mobile/desktop responsive breakpoint was raised from **768px to 1024px**. If you have custom CSS media queries, update them accordingly: ```css /* Old breakpoint */ @media (max-width: 768px) { /* mobile styles */ } /* New breakpoint (v3.0.2+) */ @media (max-width: 1024px) { /* mobile styles */ } ``` ## RTL Language Support (v3.1.0+) The SDK supports right-to-left languages (Arabic, Persian, Hebrew) with properly mirrored layouts, typography, and components. No additional configuration is required — the SDK detects the locale and applies mirrored layouts: ```tsx ``` ## Pre-TGE Market Support (v3.1.1+) Enable perpetual trading markets before a token's official Token Generation Event. To list a pre-TGE market: 1. Provide the Orderly team with the token name, initial price, and price tick size for oracle configuration 2. Once the oracle is set up, proceed with listing via the permissionless listing flow in the admin portal 3. Test on testnet first with arbitrary values (e.g., Price $1, Tick $0.001) The insurance fund requirement remains at $25,000. Pre-TGE markets are automatically rendered in the Market Selector when available: ```tsx ``` ## Crypto Market Category (v3.1.3+) A dedicated **Crypto** category is now available across all market discovery experiences (Market Selector, Market Search, Market Sidebar, Markets page), separating crypto assets from RWA (Real-World Assets) and other categories. ## Key SDK v3 Features | Version | Feature | Description | |---------|---------|-------------| | v3.0.0 | Plugin System | Core plugin architecture and Module Marketplace | | v3.0.1 | Developer Toolchain | Enhanced `orderly-devkit` CLI and plugin agent | | v3.0.2 | Responsive Breakpoint | Mobile/desktop breakpoint raised from 768px to 1024px | | v3.0.3 | Permissionless Listing Fix | Fixed empty values in funding rate modal on mobile | | v3.0.4 | Wallet Registration | **High-mandatory** update for wallet registration requests | | v3.1.0 | RTL Language Support | Arabic, Persian, Hebrew with mirrored layouts | | v3.1.1 | Pre-TGE Markets | Perpetual markets before token generation events | | v3.1.3 | Expanded Plugins | New extension points + Crypto market category | ## Migration from v2 to v3 - Upgrades from v2.x to v3.x are **backward compatible** - Update all `@orderly.network/*` packages to v3.x - Review the responsive breakpoint change (768px → 1024px) — adjust custom CSS media queries - If using custom wallet registration, upgrade to v3.0.4+ (mandatory) - Deploy to staging first before production - Orderly One builders can apply upgrades via the Orderly One platform - The `orderly-devkit` CLI should be updated to match your SDK version - Explore the Module Marketplace for community plugins **Recommendation:** All DEXs should upgrade to the latest v3.x version for critical bug fixes and new features.

chunks.title: Advanced Trading Features: Order Types, Margin Modes, and TP/SL
Advanced Deposit and Withdrawal Features: Zap-In, Exclusive Receiver, Multi-Collateral, and Cross-Chain
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK provides advanced deposit and withdrawal features to streamline user onboarding, improve capital efficiency, and simplify the trading experience. This guide covers Deposit Zap-In, Exclusive Receiver Address, multi-collateral support, withdrawals, chain integration, and critical chain-specific notes.

## Deposit Zap-In (v2.10.1+)

Deposit Zap-In allows users to deposit **any token** into their Orderly perpetual account. The deposited token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset (e.g., USDC, USDT, ETH) during the deposit process.

### Enabling Zap-In

Add the `enableSwapDeposit` prop to your `OrderlyAppProvider`:

```tsx
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from '@orderly.network/react-app';

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit  // Enable Deposit Zap-In
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### How It Works

1. User selects any token to deposit (e.g., ARB, OP, MATIC)
2. SDK automatically routes the token through the best swap path
3. Swapped collateral is credited to the user's perp account
4. User sees estimated collateral received before confirming
5. Supports dynamic chain configuration via API (no SDK update needed to add new chains)

### Benefits
- Reduces friction for users who don't hold supported collateral
- Single transaction experience
- No manual swap step required

## Exclusive Receiver Address (v2.12.0+)

Configure a **dedicated deposit address** for your users. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits.

### How It Works
1. Builder configures an exclusive receiver address via the admin dashboard or Orderly One dashboard
2. Users are shown this dedicated address for deposits
3. Funds sent to the address are automatically detected and credited to the user's trading account
4. No wallet signature or gas payment needed from the user

### Key Benefits
- **No gas fees** required from the user for the deposit
- **No wallet connection** needed to receive funds
- Simplifies onboarding for new users unfamiliar with Web3
- Ideal for CEX-to-DEX transfers and institutional deposit workflows

### Configuration

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  exclusiveReceiverConfig={{
    enabled: true,
    // Additional configuration options
  }}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

This feature is configured at the broker level. Contact the Orderly team or use the Orderly One dashboard to set up an exclusive receiver address for your DEX.

## Multi-Collateral Support (v2.5.1+)

Users can deposit multiple assets as collateral without swapping to USDC first. Brokers must upgrade to SDK v2.5.1+ to enable multi-collateral.

### Supported Collateral by Chain

| Chain | Assets |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Ethereum** | USDC, USDT, ETH, WBTC |
| **BNB Chain** | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| **Base** | USDC, ETH |
| **Arbitrum** | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| **Optimism** | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| **Solana** | SOL, USDT, USDC |

### Implementation Notes
- Collateral haircuts apply (e.g., ETH valued at discount vs USDC)
- Use `useCollateral` hook to display multi-asset balances:

```tsx
const { totalCollateral, freeCollateral, totalValue } = useCollateral();
// totalValue reflects USD value of all collateral assets combined
```

### Auto-Matching Collateral (v2.5.2+)

The SDK automatically matches deposit assets to the optimal collateral type.

## Withdrawals

### Withdrawable Balance Formula

Available to withdraw differs from free collateral when there is unsettled PnL:

```
withdrawable = unsettledPnL > 0 
  ? freeCollateral - unsettledPnL 
  : freeCollateral
```

### Withdrawals to External Web3 Wallets (v2.8.9+)

Users can withdraw to external Web3 wallets (not just their connected wallet). Users can search by address or account ID.

**Requirements:** Brokers must **apply to enable** this feature.

### Internal Transfers (v2.4.1+)

Transfer directly to another Orderly account using the recipient's `account_id`:

```tsx
// Withdraw to another Orderly account
await withdraw({
  token: 'USDC',
  amount: '100',
  account_id: 'recipient_account_id', // Internal transfer
  chain_id: 42161
});
```

**Note:** SDK v2.8.0 removed vault balance limitations for internal transfers. SDK v2.8.9 added address/account ID search.

### Vault Withdrawals Fix (v2.12.4+)

Fixed an issue where vaults in a "closed" or "closing" state would block user withdrawals. Users can now always withdraw funds regardless of vault status.

## Solana Deposits

Solana deposits involve pure on-chain interactions by calling the `deposit` function against the Solana Vault contract:

```
Vault Address: ErBmAD61mGFKvrFNaTJuxoPwqrS8GgtwtqJTJVjFWx9Q
```

**Important:** When depositing on Solana, you must fetch the deposit fee and include it in the value of the deposit call, because LayerZero cross-chain fees are calculated on-chain and can vary.

```typescript
// Example: Fetch deposit fee before executing
const depositFee = await fetchDepositFee(chain, token);
const totalValue = depositAmount + depositFee;
```

### Solana Multi-DVN Security Upgrade (v2.12.3+)

**⚠️ MANDATORY for all Solana-integrated DEXs**

The Solana Vault contract was upgraded from a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) to a **3-of-3 consensus model** using three independent DVNs via LayerZero V2.

- DEXs without this upgrade **may experience issues** with Solana deposits and withdrawals
- This is a critical security enhancement

```bash
# Upgrade to v2.12.3 or later immediately
npm install @orderly.network/react-app@^2.12.3
```

## Chain Integration

### Adding New Chains

Use the `chainFilter` prop to add supported chains:

```tsx
import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from '@orderly.network/types';

<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 1514 },       // Story Protocol
      { id: 90009090 },    // Solana
      { id: 80094 },       // Berachain
    ],
  }}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### Supported Chains

Orderly supports 17+ chains including:
- **EVM:** Arbitrum, Optimism, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Base, Polygon, Sonic, Monad, Berachain, Mode, Story Protocol, Morph, Plume, Abstract
- **Non-EVM:** Solana

### BNB Chain USDC Decimals Warning

**Critical for API builders:** USDC on BNB Chain uses **18 decimals** on-chain, but Orderly only supports **6 decimals** for deposits and withdrawals. Always check the `decimals` field in `chain_details` from the Public Token API:

```typescript
// Always verify decimals before processing
const tokenInfo = await fetch('/v1/public/token');
const usdcBnb = tokenInfo.rows.find(
  t => t.token === 'USDC' && t.chain_id === 'bsc'
);
console.log('Orderly decimals:', usdcBnb.decimals); // 6, not 18
```

## Strategy Vaults (VaultSDK - v2.7.3+)

The VaultSDK provides dedicated interaction with Orderly Strategy Vaults:
- Supports both EVM and Solana chains
- Direct SDK integration for deposits, withdrawals, and vault data
- The Omnivault allows USDC deposits used by market makers for liquidity provision

Permissionless Listings, Pre-TGE, RWA Markets, and Market Categories
chunks.content:
Orderly supports permissionless token listings, Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) perpetual markets, and Real-World Asset (RWA) markets, enabling builders to offer trading on new and diverse assets quickly. This guide covers how these features work and how to handle them in your integration.

## Permissionless Listing Framework

The Permissionless Listing framework allows anyone to create perpetual markets on Orderly using any oracle, without requiring centralized approval.

### How It Works

1. **Market Creator** picks their oracle and market maker
2. **Market goes live** on Orderly's infrastructure
3. **Builder earns** 100% of liquidation fees + 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market
4. **Orderly provides** 5 free listing slots per builder

### Broker Requirements

- **Insurance Fund:** A $50K deposit (refundable upon delisting, generates yield from trading activity).
- **Market Maker:** A MM bot (e.g., Tread.fi) to provide liquidity.

### Examples of Permissionlessly Listed Markets

- Individual stocks: $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT, $SAMSUNG, $GOOGL, $TSLA, $NVDA
- Other assets: $LITE, $CBRS, $WDC, $HOOD, $NBIS, $COIN, $META, $KORU, $GLW

### Symbol Naming

Permissionless markets may have an `_arthur` suffix and may be configured as 'isolated only'.

### Builder Responsibilities

When new permissionless markets are listed:

1. **Sync frontend configuration** to include the new symbols
2. **Notify users** about newly available markets
3. **Ensure SDK is up to date** for proper rendering

### SDK Support

| SDK Version | Feature |
|-------------|----------|
| v2.12.0+ | Full UI rendering and trading support for permissionless symbols |
| v3.0.3+ | Fixed empty values for Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee in funding rate modal on mobile |
| v3.1.3+ | Optimized K-line history loading — chart stops requesting unavailable data before market listing time |

### Handling New Listings Programmatically

```tsx
// Monitor for new symbols via the public API
import { useQuery } from '@orderly.network/hooks';

function useNewListings() {
  const { data: symbols } = useQuery('/v1/public/info');
  
  useEffect(() => {
    if (symbols) {
      const newSymbols = detectNewSymbols(symbols);
      if (newSymbols.length > 0) {
        notifyUsers(newSymbols);
        updateMarketCategories(newSymbols);
      }
    }
  }, [symbols]);
}
```

Alternatively, using the `useSymbolsInfo` hook:

```tsx
import { useSymbolsInfo } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

function MarketMonitor() {
  const symbols = useSymbolsInfo();
  
  useEffect(() => {
    // React to new symbols being added
    const newSymbols = Object.keys(symbols).filter(
      s => !previouslyKnownSymbols.has(s)
    );
    if (newSymbols.length > 0) {
      notifyUsersOfNewMarkets(newSymbols);
    }
  }, [symbols]);
  
  return null;
}
```

### K-Line History Optimization (v3.1.3+)

The chart automatically stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, reducing unnecessary API requests and improving page stability for newly listed markets.

### Delisted Markets

Orderly does not natively support re-listing a delisted permissionless market through the API. Contact the Orderly support team to manually revert delisting status or reactivate a market.

## Pre-TGE Perpetual Markets (v3.1.1+)

Pre-TGE market support enables builders to offer perpetual trading markets **before** a token's official Token Generation Event.

### Use Cases

- Allow traders to speculate on upcoming token launches
- Build hype and liquidity before official listing
- Provide price discovery for new projects

### How It Works

1. Builder configures a Pre-TGE market with estimated parameters
2. Market appears in the Market Selector with a Pre-TGE indicator
3. Users can trade perpetual contracts on the upcoming token
4. After TGE, the market transitions to standard perpetual trading

### SDK Integration

Pre-TGE markets are automatically rendered in the UI when available. No additional configuration is needed beyond SDK v3.1.1+:

```tsx
// Pre-TGE markets appear automatically in market discovery
// They are marked with a special indicator in the UI
<TradingPage />
```

### Asset Conversion Fix (v3.1.1)

SDK v3.1.1 also fixes an issue where asset conversion quote estimates could fail for certain market types.

## Real-World Asset (RWA) Markets

Orderly supports RWA perpetual markets with dedicated UI elements:

### Available RWA Markets

| Category | Examples | Max Leverage |
|----------|----------|--------------|
| Commodities | Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG), WTI Crude Oil ($CL), Brent Crude Oil ($BZ) | 20x |
| US Stock Indices | $SPX500, $NAS100 | Varies |
| Individual US Stocks | $NVDA, $TSLA, $GOOGL, $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT | 20x (tradeable 24/7) |
| Forex | $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD | Varies |

### RWA UI Features

- **v2.8.0**: Full RWA Market support with dedicated design elements
- **v2.8.13**: Dedicated RWA tab on the Market page
- **v2.10.2**: Separate RWA and Crypto sections on the Markets page
- **v2.11.0**: Enhanced RWA tab with additional market data
- **v3.1.3**: Added a dedicated Crypto market category to separate RWA and Crypto markets

To make RWA markets more visible, save your DEX configuration in Orderly One to trigger an update that adds a dedicated RWA tab in the asset selection.

### RWA Fee Structure

RWA markets have dedicated base taker fee structures, separate from crypto markets.

## Market Discovery Categories (v3.1.3+)

The SDK organizes markets into discoverable categories:

- **Market Selector** — Dropdown with category tabs
- **Market Search** — Full-text search with category filters
- **Market Sidebar** — Collapsible category navigation
- **Markets Page** — Full market listing with category sections

Each category (Crypto, RWA, Pre-TGE, Permissionless) is clearly delineated for user navigation.

### Custom Asset Categories (SDK v2.12.0+)

Builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  assetCategories={[
    { id: "defi", label: "DeFi", symbols: ["PERP_UNI_USDC", "PERP_AAVE_USDC"] },
    { id: "meme", label: "Meme Coins", symbols: ["PERP_DOGE_USDC", "PERP_PEPE_USDC"] }
  ]}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

chunks.title: Critical SDK Updates and Mandatory Upgrades
chunks.content:
This guide tracks critical SDK updates that require immediate attention. Some updates are mandatory for continued operation, while others fix significant bugs or security issues.

## Mandatory Upgrades

### 🔴 SDK v2.12.3 — Solana Multi-DVN Security (MANDATORY)

**Priority:** Critical / Mandatory for Solana-integrated DEXs

The Solana Vault contract was upgraded from a single DVN to a **3-of-3 consensus model** using three independent DVNs via LayerZero V2.

**Impact:** DEXs without this upgrade may experience **failed deposits and withdrawals** on Solana.

```bash
npm install @orderly.network/react-app@^2.12.3
```

### 🔴 SDK v3.0.4 — Wallet Registration Update (HIGH-MANDATORY)

**Priority:** High-Mandatory for all SDK builders

Critical update for wallet registration requests. The current registration process will continue to work temporarily but **may encounter issues in the future** without this update.

```bash
npm install @orderly.network/react-app@^3.0.4
```

### 🟡 SDK v2.11.2 — Isolated Margin Infrastructure (MANDATORY)

**Priority:** Mandatory for isolated margin support

Includes infrastructure upgrades required for isolated margin mode. Also fixes a critical Privy login bug (duplicate Solana addresses).

```bash
npm install @orderly.network/react-app@^2.11.2
```

## Critical Bug Fixes by Version

### SDK v2.8.12 — Vault Page Fix
- **Issue:** Vault page would fail to open in certain scenarios
- **Impact:** Users unable to access Strategy Vaults
- **Action:** Upgrade immediately

### SDK v2.8.13 — Mobile & Privy Fixes
- Fixed deposit button display on mobile web
- Resolved network switching issues with Privy login
- Improved API efficiency (removed redundant requests)

### SDK v2.8.10 — Solana Wallet Fix
- Fixed Solana wallets disconnecting on page refresh

### SDK v3.1.3 — TradingView & Wallet Fixes
- Fixed Rabby Wallet compatibility
- Fixed Portfolio page scrolling in Chrome (small window heights)
- Fixed TP/SL max quantity display mismatch
- Fixed reduce-only validation errors when closing isolated margin positions from TradingView

## Version-Specific Wallet/Login Fixes

| Version | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| v2.8.10 | Solana wallets disconnecting on page refresh |
| v2.8.13 | Privy login network switching; mobile deposit button |
| v2.11.2 | Duplicate Solana addresses via Privy; API key copy button |
| v3.0.4 | **Critical** wallet registration request update |
| v3.1.3 | Rabby Wallet compatibility |

## Upgrade Checklist

When upgrading your SDK, verify the following:

### Pre-Upgrade
1. Check current SDK version in `package.json`
2. Review changelog for breaking changes between your version and target
3. Back up your codebase

### Post-Upgrade
1. Ensure all `@orderly.network/*` packages are on the **same aligned version**
2. Run `npm install` to update dependencies
3. Clear browser cache and localStorage during testing
4. Test on mainnet (testnet may have environment-specific bugs)
5. Verify responsive breakpoint changes (768px → 1024px in v3.0.2+)

### Common Post-Upgrade Issues

#### Missing Features After Upgrade
If expected features (like 100x leverage for BTC) don't appear:
1. Verify you're testing on **mainnet** (not testnet)
2. Clear cache or test in a private browser
3. Ensure all SDK packages are on the same version
4. Run `npm install` again

#### "Please connect to a supported network" Warning
This can occur when switching between testnet and mainnet:
- The `networkId` cannot be changed dynamically at runtime
- A **hard refresh** is required when switching environments
- MetaMask has a known bug with network detection — try switching network in MetaMask first, then in the UI
- Rabby wallet handles this more reliably

#### Wrong Chain Logo on Mobile
If the wallet connect component shows the wrong chain logo (e.g., Arbitrum instead of Berachain):
- Ensure the chain is included in your `chainFilter` configuration
- Try setting the `defaultChain` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider`

## Python SDK Fix

If using the official Python SDK (`orderly-evm-connector-python`), the `_dispatch_request` function requires modification:

```python
def _dispatch_request(self, http_method, params):
    method_func = {
        "GET": self.session.get,
        "DELETE": self.session.delete,
        "PUT": self.session.put,
        "POST": self.session.post,
    }.get(http_method, "GET")
    if http_method == "POST" or http_method == "PUT":
        self.session.headers.update(
            {'Content-Type': 'application/json;charset=utf-8'}
        )
        return method_func(url=params["url"], json=params["params"])
    else:
        self.session.headers.update(
            {"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8"}
        )
        return method_func(url=params["url"])
```

This ensures POST/PUT requests send JSON bodies with the correct Content-Type header.

## Version History Summary

| Version | Key Feature | Priority |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| v2.8.10 | Solana wallet refresh fix | High |
| v2.8.12 | Vault page critical fix | High |
| v2.8.13 | Mobile + Privy fixes | High |
| v2.11.2 | Isolated margin infrastructure | Mandatory |
| v2.12.3 | Solana Multi-DVN security | **Mandatory** |
| v2.12.4 | Referral code post-binding | Medium |
| v3.0.2 | Responsive breakpoint + bug fixes | High |
| v3.0.4 | Wallet registration update | **High-Mandatory** |
| v3.1.0 | RTL support + ISO max-out fix | Medium-High |
| v3.1.1 | Pre-TGE markets | Medium |
| v3.1.3 | Plugin expansion + fixes | Medium-High |

chunks.title: VaultSDK and Strategy Vaults Integration
SDK Integration Options and Approaches
chunks.content:
Orderly Network offers multiple integration paths to suit different development needs, ranging from no-code launchers to low-level API access. Choosing the right approach depends on your desired level of customization and time-to-market.

### 1. Orderly One (No-Code Launcher)
The fastest way to launch a DEX. Orderly One is a no-code/low-code platform that allows anyone to create and launch a fully functional perpetual DEX in minutes.

- **Best for:** Teams wanting immediate deployment without frontend development.
- **Features:** Multi-chain support, PWA installation, RWA configuration, multisig admin wallets, Amplitude analytics, customizable points system (via Fuul), graduation flow via Base, and manual DEX upgrade detection.
- **Reference:** [Orderly One Platform](https://dex.orderly.network/)
- **Note:** Over 1,500 DEXs have been created using Orderly One. Builders can fork their DEX repository from the dashboard for custom modifications, but automatic SDK updates will no longer apply after forking.

### 2. Components SDK (React Components)
Pre-built, themed React components that handle the full trading experience, including the order book, trading forms, and portfolio views.

- **Best for:** Builders who want to ship quickly with minimal UI development but need more control than Orderly One.
- **Customization:** Primarily via theming (CSS variables), configuration props, and the v3 Plugin System.
- **Reference:** [Components SDK Docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/react/overview) | [Broker Template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-template)

### 3. Hooks SDK (React Hooks)
Offers more flexibility than the Components SDK. You build your own custom UI components while using Orderly's React hooks to handle data fetching, authentication, and order management.

- **Best for:** Teams requiring a fully custom UI/UX who are comfortable with React.
- **Customization:** Full control over the UI layer; logic handled by hooks.
- **Reference:** [Hooks SDK Docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/hooks/overview) | [Example DEX](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex)

### 4. Core SDK
The Core SDK (`@orderly.network/core`) is a minimal wrapper around the REST API and EIP-712 signing logic. It is framework-agnostic and can be used with vanilla JavaScript, Vue, Angular, or mobile frameworks.

- **Best for:** Integrations that do not use React or require very specific architectural control.
- **NPM:** [@orderly.network/core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@orderly.network/core)
- **Note:** Documentation for the Core SDK is currently limited; developers may need to reference the source code or types.

### 5. Direct REST/WebSocket API Integration
For maximum control, integrate directly with Orderly's REST APIs and WebSockets without using any SDK. This requires you to manually implement account registration, EIP-712 signing, and order management.

- **Best for:** Non-standard environments, non-JS backends, or teams who want to implement every layer themselves.
- **Reference:** [Build on Omnichain](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/building-on-omnichain)

### Choosing an Approach
| Approach | Time to Market | Customization | Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Orderly One | ~1 hour | Low (Config-based) | Minimal |
| Components SDK | 1–2 weeks | Medium (Theming + Plugins) | Low–Medium |
| Hooks SDK | 2–3 weeks | High | Medium |
| Core SDK | 3–4 weeks | Very High | High |
| Direct API | 4+ weeks | Total | Very High |

### v2.5.1 (July 2025)

### v2.6.0 - v2.6.3 (Aug-Sep 2025)

- One-click join for Leaderboard Campaigns

### v2.10.1 - v2.10.2 (Mar 2026)

chunks.title: Multi-Collateral, Isolated Margin, and RWA Markets
chunks.content:
This guide covers three major feature areas: multi-collateral deposits, isolated margin trading, and Real-World Asset (RWA) markets.

## Multi-Collateral Support (v2.5.1+)

Multi-collateral allows users to deposit and trade with multiple native assets without swapping to USDC first.

### Supported Assets by Chain

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
| :--- | :--- |
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT |

### Enabling Multi-Collateral

Upgrade to SDK v2.5.1 or later. From v2.5.2+, deposit assets also support auto-matching collateral.

### BNB Chain USDC Precision Note

**Critical:** USDC on BNB Chain uses **18 decimals** on-chain, but Orderly only supports **6 decimals** for deposits and withdrawals. Always refer to the `decimals` field in `chain_details` from the Public Token API:

```tsx
import { useQuery } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { data: tokens } = useQuery("/v1/public/token");
// Always use token.decimals from this response, not hardcoded values
```

## Isolated Margin Mode (v2.11.0+)

Isolated margin mode allows traders to allocate specific collateral to individual positions, limiting risk to the allocated amount. This is in contrast to cross-margin, where collateral is shared across all positions.

### Enabling Isolated Margin

Isolated Margin Mode must be enabled by the Orderly team at the broker level, as it goes through production environment testing. Contact the Orderly team to request enablement for your broker ID. Once enabled, there may be a ~20 minute delay before it becomes active. It must be enabled separately for testnet and mainnet.

### Key SDK Versions

| Version | Update |
| :--- | :--- |
| v2.11.0 | Initial isolated margin SDK support |
| v2.11.2 | Mandatory infrastructure upgrade |
| v2.12.0 | ISO/Cross margin labels on TradingView chart position lines (positions, TP/SL, liquidation) |
| v3.0.0 | Fixed leverage update after switching margin mode |
| v3.1.0 | Fixed ISO max-out order rejection (reserves taker fee buffer) |
| v3.1.3 | Fixed margin mode sent when closing from TradingView position lines |

### Symbol-Level Leverage (v2.7.3+)

Leverage is configured per-symbol per-margin-mode. For example, BTC-PERP can have 10x Cross and 20x Isolated simultaneously. Use the `useLeverage` hook to manage it:

```tsx
import { useLeverage } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [maxLeverage, { update, isMutating }] = useLeverage();

// Set leverage for a specific symbol and margin mode
await update({
  leverage: 20,
  symbol: "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  margin_mode: "ISOLATED"
});
```

```tsx
import { useLeverage } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

function LeverageControl() {
  const [maxLeverage, { update, isMutating }] = useLeverage();

  const handleUpdate = async () => {
    // Set max leverage to 10x for the current symbol and margin mode
    await update({ leverage: 10 });
  };

  return (
    <button onClick={handleUpdate} disabled={isMutating}>
      Set to 10x
    </button>
  );
}
```

### ISO Max-Out Order Fix (v3.1.0)

Prior to v3.1.0, maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% slider was rejected with "margin will be insufficient after." The SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

### Handling Negative USDC Balance

When USDC balance is negative due to cross-margin losses, the withdrawable USDC formula returns 0, blocking USDC withdrawals. To withdraw non-stablecoin collateral (e.g., SOL), deposit a small amount of another collateral (e.g., 1 USDT) or top up USDC until the balance is positive so that at least two withdrawable assets appear in the list.

## RWA (Real-World Asset) Markets

Orderly supports perpetual markets for real-world assets with up to 20x leverage, tradeable 24/7.

### Available RWA Markets

| Category | Symbols |
| :--- | :--- |
| Indexes | $SPX500, $NAS100 |
| Precious Metals | $XAU (Gold), $XAG (Silver) |
| US Stocks | $NVDA, $TSLA, $GOOGL |
| Forex | $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD |
| Commodities | $CL (WTI Crude), $BZ (Brent Crude) |

**RWA Base Fees:** 0% maker / 0.045% taker

### RWA Market Status

Use the `/v1/public/rwa/info` API with the base symbol to determine market trading hours:

```tsx
const { data: rwaInfo } = useQuery("/v1/public/rwa/info?symbol=PERP_NVDA_USDC");
```

**Note:** RWA markets can still be traded on Orderly even when the underlying traditional market is closed.

### RWA UI Features

- **v2.8.0**: Dedicated RWA Market UI elements
- **v2.8.13**: RWA tab on Market page
- **v2.10.2**: Separate RWA and Crypto market sections
- **v3.1.3**: Dedicated Crypto category (separating from RWA)

chunks.title: Deposit, Withdrawal, and Asset Management
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK provides several advanced deposit and withdrawal features to improve user experience and simplify fund management.

## Deposit Zap-in (Auto-Swap Deposits)

**Available from:** SDK v2.10.1

Deposit Zap-in allows users to deposit **any token** into their Orderly perpetual account. The token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral (e.g., USDC) during the deposit process.

### Enabling Zap-in

Set the `enableSwapDeposit` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider`:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit  // Enable auto-swap on deposit
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

Zap-in also supports **dynamic chain configuration via API**, allowing you to adjust supported swap routes without redeploying.

## Exclusive Receiver Address

**Available from:** SDK v2.12.0

Builders can configure a **dedicated deposit address** for each user. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits — **no gas fees or wallet connection required** from the user.

This dramatically simplifies the deposit flow, especially for users depositing directly from centralized exchanges to their DEX account without interacting with a wallet interface.

### Supported Chains

- Arbitrum
- Ethereum
- Base
- Optimism
- BNB Chain

**Note:** Solana support for exclusive deposit addresses is in development.

## Multi-Collateral Support

**Available from:** SDK v2.5.1

Users can deposit multiple assets as collateral for trading:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH, WBTC |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT, USDC |

Auto-matching collateral for deposit assets is available from SDK v2.5.2+.

## External Web3 Wallet Withdrawals

**Available from:** SDK v2.8.9

Users can withdraw to external Web3 wallets (not just their connected wallet). **Brokers must apply to the Orderly team to enable this feature.**

From v2.8.9+, users can also search by address or account ID when withdrawing to other Orderly accounts.

## Internal Transfers

**Available from:** SDK v2.4.1

Enable direct withdrawals to another Orderly account using the recipient's `account_id`:

```tsx
// Internal transfer to another Orderly account
const withdrawalPayload = {
  token: "USDC",
  amount: "100",
  account_id: "recipient_account_id" // Internal transfer
};
```

From SDK v2.8.9, users can search by address or account ID when initiating transfers.

## Retrieving Deposit/Withdrawal History

Use `usePrivateQuery` with the asset history endpoint:

```tsx
import { usePrivateQuery } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { data: assetHistory } = usePrivateQuery("/v1/asset/history");
```

Or use the `useAssetsHistory` hook for filtered queries:

```tsx
import { useAssetsHistory } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [data, { meta, isLoading }] = useAssetsHistory({
  token: "USDC",
  side: "DEPOSIT",
  startTime: Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
  endTime: Date.now(),
  page: 1,
  pageSize: 20
});
```

**Note:** Withdrawal transaction hashes may take time to appear due to block confirmation requirements (e.g., ~500 blocks on Polygon).

## Deposit Status Display

Use `useDepositStatusScript` from `@orderly.network/ui-transfer`:

```tsx
import { useDepositStatusScript } from "@orderly.network/ui-transfer";

const {
  pendingCount,
  completedCount,
  canTrade,
  estimatedTime,
  onClose
} = useDepositStatusScript();
```

## Retrieving Fees

### Deposit Fees

```tsx
const { setQuantity, depositFee } = useDeposit({ /* ... */ });
setQuantity("100"); // Triggers fee calculation
// depositFee is in wei — convert to token decimals manually
```

### Withdrawal Fees

```tsx
import { useChains } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { data: chains } = useChains();
// Access chains[].network_infos.withdrawal_fee
```

## Settling PnL Before Withdrawal

Users cannot withdraw the full amount of profits unless PnL is settled first:

```tsx
import { useWithdraw, useAccountInstance } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { unsettledPnl } = useWithdraw();
const { account } = useAccountInstance();

if (unsettledPnl > 0) {
  await account.settle();
}
// Now proceed with withdrawal
```

## Solana Deposit Implementation

The Solana deposit function is more complex than Ethereum. The reference implementation is located at:
```
packages/default-solana-adapter/src/helper.ts (line ~493)
```
in the [js-sdk repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/js-sdk).

### Common Solana Deposit Issues

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| "Invalid public key input" | RPC CORS error | Use a dedicated RPC provider (Alchemy, QuickNode) |
| Balance shows 0 | Default public RPC blocked | Configure custom RPC in `ConnectionProvider` |
| Deposit fails silently | Outdated SDK | Upgrade to SDK v2.0.1-alpha.4+ |

```tsx
// Proper Solana RPC configuration
import { ConnectionProvider } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react";

<ConnectionProvider endpoint="https://your-rpc-provider.com/solana-mainnet">
  {/* ... */}
</ConnectionProvider>
```

## Solana Multi-DVN Security Upgrade (v2.12.3)

**Mandatory for all Solana-integrated DEXs.** SDK v2.12.3 upgrades the Solana Vault contract from a single DVN to a 3-of-3 consensus model using three independent Decentralized Verifier Networks under LayerZero V2. DEXs without this upgrade may experience issues with Solana deposits and withdrawals.

chunks.title: Wallet Integration and Authentication Guide
chunks.content:
This guide covers wallet integration patterns, authentication flows, custom providers, and common wallet-related issues when building with the Orderly SDK.

## Default Wallet Connection

The SDK uses `@orderly.network/wallet-connector` for wallet management:

```tsx
import { WalletConnectorProvider } from "@orderly.network/wallet-connector";

<WalletConnectorProvider>
  <OrderlyAppProvider brokerId="..." networkId="mainnet">
    <YourApp />
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorProvider>
```

## Custom Wallet Connector Integration (SDK v2)

For SDK v2, implement a custom wallet connector by providing a `WalletConnectorContext.Provider` that wraps the Orderly provider. The main change in v2 is the `walletAdapters` prop on the config provider.

```tsx
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react-app";
import { WalletConnectorContext } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

// Your custom wallet adapter
const walletAdapter = new DefaultEVMWalletAdapter(new EthersProvider());

function App() {
  return (
    <WalletConnectorContext.Provider value={yourWalletContext}>
      <OrderlyAppProvider
        brokerId="your_broker"
        networkId="mainnet"
        walletAdapters={[walletAdapter]}
      >
        <YourApp />
      </OrderlyAppProvider>
    </WalletConnectorContext.Provider>
  );
}
```

For external wallet providers (e.g., Magic Link, custodial wallets):

```tsx
import { WalletConnectorContext } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

<WalletConnectorContext.Provider
  value={{
    connect: async () => { /* your logic */ },
    disconnect: async () => { /* your logic */ },
    chains: supportedChains,
    connectedChain: currentChain,
    wallet: walletInstance,
    // ... implement all required fields
  }}
>
  <OrderlyAppProvider>
    <TradingPage />
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorContext.Provider>
```

Reference: [Custom wallet connection provider docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/react/wallet#custom-wallet-connection-provider)

## Privy Wallet Integration

Privy is supported as a wallet provider starting from SDK v2.2 (custom UI from v2.4.1). Implement a custom `PrivyProvider` by replacing the default `EthersProvider`:

```tsx
// See: OrderlyNetwork/example-dex/app/providers/OrderlyProvider.tsx
<PrivyProvider appId={YOUR_PRIVY_APP_ID}>
  <OrderlyAppProvider
    brokerId="your_broker"
    networkId="mainnet"
  >
    {children}
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</PrivyProvider>
```

For custom UI (without prebuilt React components):

```tsx
import { WalletConnectorPrivyProvider } from "@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy";

<WalletConnectorPrivyProvider
  network={networkId === 'mainnet' ? Network.mainnet : Network.testnet}
  privyConfig={{
    appid: privyAppId,
    config: { loginMethods: ['email'] }
  }}
  wagmiConfig={{ connectors: getEvmConnectors() }}
  solanaConfig={getSolanaConfig(networkId)}
>
  <OrderlyAppProvider brokerId="..." brokerName="..." networkId={networkId}>
    <YourCustomUI />
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorPrivyProvider>
```

**Critical:** You must connect through `useWalletConnector().connect()` with `WalletConnectType.PRIVY`:

```tsx
import { useWalletConnector } from '@orderly.network/hooks';
import { WalletConnectType } from '@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy';

const { connect } = useWalletConnector();

async function connectPrivy() {
  await connect({ walletType: WalletConnectType.PRIVY });
}
```

> **Do NOT** just call Privy's login hooks and expect Orderly to infer the wallet. The account is only recognized when connected through `useWalletConnector`.

### Privy Fixes by Version
- **v2.8.13**: Fixed network switching issues with Privy login
- **v2.11.2**: Fixed duplicate Solana addresses via Privy

## EIP-712 Signing

The Orderly TradingPage uses **ethers.js** (default) or **web3.js** for EIP-712 signing, depending on the wallet adapter configuration.

Reference implementation: [etherAdapter.ts](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/js-sdk/blob/main/packages/core/src/wallet/etherAdapter.ts#L200-L202)

## Account Abstraction (AA) Support

Orderly uses wallet adapters, so if the adapter supports Coinbase Smart Wallet or Base Accounts, Orderly can support it. For AA, builders have customized Privy login (which supports smart wallets).

**Known Issue:** There is a tracked SDK issue with Base Account/Coinbase Smart Wallet signature failures during account creation.

## Delegate Signer (Contract Accounts)

Trading with Contract Accounts (CAs) is supported via the **Delegate Signer** feature, but it is **not implemented in any SDK** (Components, Hooks, or Core).

CAs cannot directly interact with Orderly because the platform relies on EIP-712 signing, which requires an EOA. The delegate signer flow allows an EOA to delegate signing authority to a CA.

```typescript
// Example implementation (without trading):
// https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-registration
```

## API Key Management

Orderly API keys and secrets are automatically saved to localStorage by the SDK when created via `createOrderlyKey`. Keys are created locally (in the browser) and the public key is registered with Orderly's backend via EIP-712 signature.

### Generating Keys

1. **SDK UI:** Portfolio > API Key page
2. **Universal UI:** [broker-registration](https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/)

### Retrieving Keys Programmatically

```tsx
const { account } = useAccount();
const orderlyKey = account.keyStore.getOrderlyKey();
```

Keys are stored under `orderly_${networkId}_${walletAddress}` in localStorage.

### Removing a Key

POST to `https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/remove_orderly_key` with `orderly_key` in the body.

### IP Restrictions

Set IP restrictions via the private API endpoint for enhanced security.

### Testing Without a Broker ID

During development, use any existing `broker_id`. Retrieve available brokers:

```
GET /v1/public/broker
```

## Listening for Wallet Disconnect

```tsx
import { useAccount, AccountStatusEnum } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { state } = useAccount();

useEffect(() => {
  if (state.status === AccountStatusEnum.NotConnected) {
    // Handle disconnect
  }
}, [state]);
```

## Chain Switching

Switch the active chain for data hooks:

```tsx
const { account } = useAccount();
account.switchChainId(targetChainId);
```

Once switched, all underlying hooks (e.g., `useCollateral`, `useMarketsStream`) return data for the selected chain. **Note:** Trading data like orders and positions are aggregated across all chains.

## Chain Filtering

Add or exclude chains using `chainFilter`:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum, Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story
    ],
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

## Mobile-Specific Features

| Feature | SDK Version |
|---------|-------------|
| Left-Hand Mode | v2.8.14 |
| Mobile tab navigation | Recent versions (configure in app config) |
| Responsive breakpoint 1024px | v3.0.2 |

## Common Wallet Issues

### iOS Safari WalletConnect Redirect Loop

**Cause:** WalletConnect WebSocket connections are terminated when the app enters the background on iOS Safari.

**Mitigation:**
1. Use the wallet's built-in in-app browser (MetaMask browser)
2. Ensure latest MetaMask Mobile version
3. Close the DApp and generate a new WalletConnect session
4. Open in Chrome or Safari instead of in-app browsers

### Mobile Deposit Infinite MetaMask Redirect

**Cause:** Wallet-read polling (balance/allowance checks every 3000ms) triggers deep links before WalletConnect session is settled.

**Fix:**
1. Disable wallet reads on page mount
2. Start wallet reads only after explicit user intent
3. Implement a 'readiness gate' to block reads until wallet state stabilizes

### Binance Wallet Chain-Switching Errors

**Cause:** Binance Wallet connected via WalletConnect has compatibility issues.

**Solution:**
- SDK v2+: Binance Blocknative connector is included natively
- SDK v1: Install `@binance/w3w-blocknative-connector`

### Solana Wallet Disconnects on Refresh

**Fixed in:** SDK v2.8.10

Upgrade to prevent Solana wallet state from being lost on page refresh.

### Google OAuth in Telegram Mini Apps (v2.12.3+)

Google blocks OAuth from embedded WebViews. SDK v2.12.3+ detects `window.Telegram?.WebApp` and routes OAuth through the external browser via `Telegram.WebApp.openLink()`. Users can authenticate via Google OAuth when using Orderly-powered DEXs inside Telegram Mini Apps.
