**Solution**: Upgrade to **SDK v3.1.3+**, which fixed the calculation of max quantity for TP/SL orders.

### Issue: Referral codes not applied
**Symptom**: Referral codes are not being recognized or applied to trades.
**Cause**: Earlier SDK versions had a bug where referral codes were not sent in uppercase to the API.
**Solution**: Upgrade to **SDK v3.0.2+**.

### Issue: Permissionless symbols not displaying on mobile
**Symptom**: Newly permissionless-listed symbols do not show funding rate fields on mobile.
**Solution**: Upgrade to **SDK v3.0.3+**, which fixed display issues for permissionless symbols on mobile devices.

## Wallet and Connection Issues

### Issue: Solana wallet disconnects on refresh
**Symptom**: Solana wallet connection is lost when the page is refreshed.
**Solution**: Upgrade to **SDK v2.8.10+** or **v2.11.2+**, which fixed connection persistence for Solana wallets.

### Issue: Duplicate Solana addresses with Privy
**Symptom**: Using Privy with Solana generates duplicate addresses.
**Solution**: Upgrade to **SDK v2.11.2+**, which resolved the Privy-Solana integration bug.

## General Debugging Tips

1. **Check SDK Version**: Many issues are resolved in newer versions. Always check the changelog.
2. **Clear Cache**: Browser localStorage can cache old settings. Clear it when testing upgrades.
3. **Verify Network**: Ensure your `networkId` (mainnet/testnet) matches your Broker ID registration.
4. **Monitor Console**: Look for specific error codes in the browser console to identify the root cause.

chunks.title: Core Integration Flows for Orderly Builders
chunks.content:
When building on Orderly Network, implementing these core integration flows first will ensure a solid foundation for your trading application.

## 1. API Authentication
Orderly uses Ed25519 signatures for API authentication. You must generate an Orderly Key pair and register it on-chain.

### Required Headers
- `orderly-timestamp`: Current timestamp in milliseconds.
- `orderly-account-id`: Your Orderly Account ID.
- `orderly-key`: Your Public Orderly Key.
- `orderly-signature`: Ed25519 signature of `{timestamp}{http_method}{url_path}{payload}`.

**Note**: The SDK handles this automatically. If using the Core SDK or Direct API, you must implement the signing logic.

## 2. Account Registration
Before trading, users must register an Orderly account and map their wallet to your Broker ID.

### Lifecycle Steps
1. **Connect Wallet**: User connects their Web3 wallet.
2. **Register Account**: Call the registration endpoint (or `createAccount` in SDK) to create an Orderly account.
3. **Register Key**: Sign an EIP-712 message to register the Orderly Key for trading.

```tsx
import { useAccount } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { createAccount, createOrderlyKey } = useAccount();

const onboard = async () => {
  await createAccount();
  await createOrderlyKey(30); // Valid for 30 days
};
```

## 3. Deposits and Withdrawals
Implement the asset flow between the user's wallet and the Orderly Vault.

### Deposits
1. **Approve Token**: Call `approve` on the ERC-20 token contract.
2. **Calculate Fee**: Use `getDepositFee` to estimate gas/bridge fees.
3. **Deposit**: Call `deposit` on the Vault contract.

### Withdrawals
1. **Fetch Nonce**: Get the current withdrawal nonce from the API.
2. **Sign Message**: Sign an EIP-712 Withdraw message.
3. **Request**: Call the Create Withdraw Request API.

## 4. WebSocket API
Stream real-time data for a responsive UI.

### Public Data
- **Endpoint**: `wss://ws-evm.orderly.org/ws/stream/{account_id}`
- **Topics**: `orderbook`, `trade`, `ticker`, `kline_1m`

### Private Data
- **Endpoint**: `wss://ws-private-evm.orderly.org/v2/ws/private/stream/{account_id}`
- **Topics**: `account`, `balance`, `position`, `executionreport`

## 5. SDK Selection
Choose the right SDK based on your needs:
- **React Components**: Fastest time-to-market.
- **React Hooks**: Custom UI with managed state.
- **Core SDK**: Framework-agnostic logic.
- **Direct API**: Full control over every layer.

chunks.title: Broker Setup, Fee Configuration, and Revenue Management
chunks.content:
Setting up a broker on Orderly Network involves registering a unique Broker ID, configuring an admin wallet, and managing custom fee structures. This guide covers the complete broker lifecycle.

## Step 1: Registering a Broker ID

To register a broker ID, provide the Orderly team with:

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| **Broker ID** | Unique short string identifier with no spaces | `my_dex`, `panda_terminal`, `sharpe_ai` |
| **Broker Name** | Human-readable display name | `My DEX`, `Panda Terminal` |
| **Default Taker Fee** | In basis points | `0.06%` (6 bps) |
| **Default Maker Fee** | In basis points | `0.02%` (2 bps) |
| **Tier** | Public, Silver, Gold, Platinum, or Diamond | `public` |

After the broker ID is provisioned (requires multisig approval, ~1–2 days), register your admin wallet at:
- **Mainnet**: https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/
- **Testnet**: https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/ (select a testnet chain)

> **Note:** You can use Orderly One (https://dex.orderly.network/ or https://dex.orderly.network/graduation) for automated broker setup ($10 (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate)), or request manual setup from the Orderly team at no cost.

**Cross-chain note:** The same Broker ID works across both EVM and Solana chains, but EVM and Solana use different wallet addresses and cannot share the same account. You only need to register the admin wallet on **one chain** — no need to register separately on Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, etc.

## Step 2: Fee Structure and Revenue

Orderly charges a **base fee** that it retains:
- **Base Taker Fee**: 3 bps (0.03%) — reducible via Builder Staking Programme
- **Base Maker Fee**: 0 bps

Brokers set fees **on top** of the base. The difference is 100% broker revenue:

```
Broker Revenue = Broker Fee - Base Fee
```

| Broker Taker Fee | Orderly Base | Broker Revenue |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 6 bps | 3 bps | 3 bps |
| 5 bps | 3 bps | 2 bps |
| 10 bps | 3 bps | 7 bps |

**Example:** If a broker sets a 0.06% taker fee and Orderly's base is 0.03%, the broker earns 0.03% per taker trade and 0.03% per maker trade (full amount, since base maker fee is 0%).

Fees are calculated on **notional trading volume** (e.g., $1,000 at 10x leverage = $10,000 volume). Fees are collected on both opening and closing/liquidation of positions.

As of May 2026, **maker fee rebates** are available: maker fees can be set to negative values (-0.20bps to 0), meaning Orderly subsidizes makers.

### Builder Staking Programme Tiers

Reduce your base taker fee by staking ORDER tokens or achieving volume thresholds:

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Requirement |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Public | 3 bps | Default |
| Silver | 2.75 bps | 100K ORDER staked |
| Gold | 2.5 bps | 300K ORDER staked |
| Platinum | 2 bps | ≥$750M 30-day volume OR 3M ORDER staked |
| Diamond | 1 bps | ≥$2B 30-day volume OR 7M ORDER staked |

Stake at: https://app.orderly.network/staking

Staking benefits include co-marketing support, reduced fees, and staking yield (60% of Orderly fees go to stakers). Unstaking takes 7 days.

## Step 3: Admin Wallet Configuration

- **EOA wallets** are preferred for admin wallets
- **Multisig (Safe)** wallets are supported — use the delegate signer feature
- The admin wallet has exclusive access to: fee management APIs, referral code creation, fee rebate APIs, and broker-specific endpoints
- Accessing the admin dashboard at https://admin.orderly.network/
- To use a multisig: connect the EOA delegate address, sign the login message via the EOA

### Multisig Setup

When using a multisig wallet:
1. Register the multisig as the admin wallet
2. Delegate a single EOA signer to perform administrative actions
3. The multisig serves as the deposit address for fee withdrawals
4. Only one delegate signer can be associated per broker ID

### Logging into the Admin Panel

Log in at https://admin.orderly.network/ using the delegate signer address credentials (Orderly Key and Secret). The account ID corresponds to the delegate signer address. API keys can be generated from the broker registration page or via Portfolio > API Keys in the DEX.

### Changing the Admin Wallet

To change the master/admin wallet:
1. Register the new wallet address as an Orderly account at the broker registration tool
2. Request the change from the Orderly team, providing the new wallet address and broker ID

The change causes no downtime and does not affect historical fee data. Ownership transfer must be done **manually by the Orderly team**.

### Changing Broker Display Name

The display name can be updated by the Orderly team upon request. Provide the DEX ID and Broker ID to the Orderly DevRel team.

## Step 4: Updating Fees Programmatically

### Default Broker Fees

Set default fees via the admin portal at `https://admin.orderly.network/` or via API:

```
POST /v1/broker/fee_rate/default
PUT /v1/builder/fee
```

Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/evm-api/restful-api/private/update-default-builder-fee

**Required Headers:** `orderly-key`, `orderly-signature`, `orderly-timestamp`, `orderly-account-id` (all from admin wallet)

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "maker_fee_rate": "0.00028",
    "taker_fee_rate": "0.00058"
  }
}
```

To verify changes:
```
GET https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/broker/user_info
```

> **Important:** Testnet and mainnet fee configurations are independent. You must update fees separately for each environment. Use `https://testnet-api-evm.orderly.org` for testnet and `https://api-evm.orderly.org` for mainnet.

### Per-User Custom Fees

Brokers can set custom fee rates per user based on any criteria (volume, staking, holdings):

```
PUT /v1/client/fee_rate
GET /v1/user_fee_rates  (retrieve all accounts with custom fees)
```

**Important:** Brokers cannot offer fees lower than their own base fee (determined by their broker tier).

### Volume-Based Fee Tiers

Orderly does not provide automatic tiered fees. Brokers must implement their own tiering logic:

1. Run a daily script to check each user's trading volume using: `GET /v1/builder/users/volumes`
2. Call the fee update API to adjust per-user rates
3. Reference implementation: https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin

### Per-Order Custom Fees (Order Enums)

As of April 2026, Orderly supports custom fees applied on a per-order basis via **order enums**. This is recommended for copy trading, KOL revenue sharing, or automated strategies.

- **Referral codes (order_tag)**: Apply standard fees, override existing referral relationships
- **Order enums**: Add additional fees on top of standard fees, respect existing referrals
- Only one can be used per order (cannot be combined)

Integration guide: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/order-enum-integration-guide

## Step 5: Fee Collection and Withdrawal

- Fees are distributed **daily** to the broker's Orderly account (not directly to an external wallet)
- Check fee balance via: `GET /v1/client/holding` with admin credentials
- Retrieve detailed broker transactions: `GET /v1/builders/users/volumes`

Broker fees can be withdrawn using:
1. **Orderly broker fee withdrawal app** (UI-based) — log in with the broker admin wallet address and withdraw from the Orderly account balance
2. **Delegate signer withdraw API** (programmatic):
   ```
   POST /v1/broker/admin/delegate_signer_withdraw_request
   ```
3. **Broker registration tool** (useful for multisig): https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/
4. **Standard withdrawal flow** with EIP-712 signing

## Common Issues

| Issue | Solution |
|:---|:---|
| `Permission Denied` (-1108) on fee endpoints | Ensure you're signing with the registered admin wallet |
| UI still shows old fees after API update | Clear browser cache; fees may take minutes to propagate |
| Fees not accruing | Verify admin wallet is registered and linked to broker ID on backend |
| Testnet vs Mainnet confusion | Use correct base URL: `testnet-api-evm.orderly.org` vs `api-evm.orderly.org` |

chunks.title: Campaigns, Leaderboards, and Points API Integration
chunks.content:
Orderly provides a comprehensive Campaigns API for running trading competitions, points programs, and leaderboards. This guide covers setup, endpoints, data freshness, and integration patterns.

## Setting Up a Campaign

Campaigns must be configured by the Orderly team **before** they start. Provide:
- **Campaign Name**
- **Start Time** (UTC) — cannot be changed retroactively
- **End Time** (UTC) — can be extended after start
- **Calculation Scope**: trading volume, deposit, PnL, staking, referral count
- **Broker ID(s)**

> **Lead time:** At least 1 day advance notice. Historical data before the campaign start time is NOT captured.

## Campaign API Endpoints

### 1. Campaign User Info (Individual Progress)
```
GET /v1/public/campaign/user?campaign_id={id}&address={address}
```

Optional parameters: `broker_id`, `symbol` (format: `PERP_{BASE}_{QUOTE}`, e.g., `PERP_FARTCOIN_USDC`)

**Response fields:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "volume": 15000,
    "total_deposit_amount": 5000,
    "total_withdrawal_amount": 1000,
    "pnl": 250.50,
    "start_account_value": 5000,
    "end_account_value": 5250.50,
    "filled_order_count": 42,
    "total_staked_order": 1000,
    "total_staked_esorder": 500,
    "new_invited_referee": 3,
    "new_traded_referee": 2
  }
}
```

### 2. Campaign Ranking (Leaderboard)
```
GET /v1/public/campaign/ranking?campaign_id={id}&sort_by=volume&size=50&page=1
```
- Includes **unrealized PnL (UPnL)**
- Use for public-facing leaderboards

### 3. Campaign Statistics
```
GET /v1/public/campaign/stats/details?campaign_id={id}&symbols={symbol}
```

### 4. General Broker Leaderboard (Non-Campaign)
```
GET /v1/broker/leaderboard/daily
```
- Reflects **realized PnL only**
- Updates around 1-2 AM UTC daily

## PnL Calculation

Campaign PnL is calculated at the **account level**:
```
PnL = end_account_value - start_account_value - total_deposits + total_withdrawals
```

- Cannot be attributed to individual symbols
- A user may show positive PnL with zero trading volume if they had unrealized PnL from positions opened before the campaign that was realized during the campaign period

## Data Update Frequency

| Metric | Update Frequency |
|:---|:---|
| Trading Volume | Near real-time (1-2 minutes) |
| Staking Data | ~10 minutes |
| PnL / Deposits | Hourly |
| Deposit Verification | Up to 1 hour (cross-chain confirmations) |

> **Important:** If a user stakes and immediately unstakes before the next update cycle, the staking action may not be recorded. Advise users to wait at least 10 minutes.

## Symbol Filtering

The `symbol` parameter filters volume by specific trading pairs:
```
GET /v1/public/campaign/user?symbol=PERP_FARTCOIN_USDC&campaign_id=110&address=$address&broker_id=woofi_pro
```

> **Limitation:** A single campaign cannot natively aggregate multiple symbols. To track volume across multiple pairs, query each symbol separately and sum results, or request a data export post-campaign.

## Staking Task Tracking

To track ORDER/esORDER staking in campaigns:
1. Include 'staking' in the Calculation Scope when creating the campaign
2. Campaign ID must be added to Apollo config: `campaign.staking.record.campaignIds`
3. Check fields: `total_staked_order`, `total_staked_esorder`

For standalone staking verification:
```
GET /v1/staking/balance?address=$address
```
Check `resp.data.total_staked_balance`

## Quest Platform Integrations (Galxe, Layer3, Gate Wallet)

### Galxe Integration
Use the campaign user API with a JavaScript expression:
```javascript
function(resp) {
  if (resp.data.volume != null && resp.data.volume >= 5000) {
    return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}
```

### Custom Response Formats
Platforms like Gate Wallet or Layer3 may require custom response formats. Orderly can develop custom endpoints with advance notice. Standard format wraps data in a `data` object:
```json
{"success": true, "data": {"volume": 1000}}
```

## Campaign Data Archiving

- Campaigns before ID 75: Archived 1 month after end date
- Campaigns from ID 75+: Archived 6 months after end date
- Once archived, data is no longer accessible via API
- **Export needed data before the archiving deadline**

## Points System (Orderly One)

Orderly One brokers can activate a customizable points system powered by Fuul integration:

- **Trading Points** = Daily Perps Volume × Trading Coefficient
- **PNL Points** = |Daily Settled PNL| × PNL Coefficient
- **Referral Points** = L1 Invitee Points × L1 Coefficient + L2 Invitee Points × L2 Coefficient

Parameter updates take effect from the next 00:00 UTC. Historical points are final.

Staging API docs: https://staging-docs.orderly.network/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-user-points-statistics

## Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Empty PnL data with `success: true` | Wrong date format | Use `YYYY-MM-DD` format |
| Deposit not showing | Cross-chain delay | Wait up to 1 hour |
| Staking not recorded | Update cycle missed | Wait 10+ minutes |
| Campaign start date change needed | Not supported | Start dates are fixed once set |

chunks.title: Withdrawals, Deposits, Internal Transfers, and PnL Settlement API Guide
chunks.content:
This guide covers the complete lifecycle of fund movements on Orderly Network, including deposits, withdrawals, internal transfers, and PnL settlement.

## Deposits

Deposits are made on-chain to Orderly's asset vaults on each supported chain. Track deposit status via WebSocket:

```
Subscribe: /v1/ws/private/wallet-transactions
```

Deposits take time to reflect depending on the origin chain, as the cross-chain transaction must be finalized. Once credited, verify via `GET /v1/asset_history`.

### Multi-Collateral Support

Orderly supports multiple collateral assets beyond USDC:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|:---|:---|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH, WBTC |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT |

### USDC Decimal Handling (BNB Chain)

> **Critical:** USDC on BNB Chain uses **18 decimals** on-chain, but Orderly only supports **6 decimals** for deposits and withdrawals. Always check the `decimals` field in `chain_details` from the Public Token API before processing transactions.

## PnL Settlement

Unsettled PnL from closed positions inflates `total_collateral_value` but is NOT available in `holding` (withdrawable balance). Any realized profit from open or recently closed positions must be settled before it is added to your `withdrawable_balance`.

### Balance Discrepancy

| Field | Includes |
|:---|:---|
| `total_collateral_value` | Deposits + Settled PnL + **Unsettled PnL** |
| `holding` | Deposits + Settled PnL only |

### Three-Step Settlement Process

1. **Get a settlement nonce** from the Get Settle PnL Nonce endpoint
2. **Sign an EIP-712 message** containing:
   - `brokerId` (string — your Builder/Broker ID)
   - `chainId` (int — connected chain ID)
   - `settleNonce` (int — from step 1)
   - `timestamp` (int — current UNIX milliseconds)
3. **Submit via the Request PnL Settlement API**

### Example EIP-712 Message

```json
{
  "brokerId": "woofi_dex",
  "chainId": 80001,
  "settleNonce": 1,
  "timestamp": 1685973017064
}
```

```
POST /v1/settle_pnl
```

> **Note:** PnL settlement is not automatic because it triggers an upload to Orderly Chain with associated gas fees. It is safe to auto-settle when a user requests to close a position or withdraw. PnL settlement can be triggered at any time by the account owner or by other users.

## Withdrawals

### Five-Step Withdrawal Flow

1. **Choose a supported target chain** from the Smart Contract Addresses page
2. **Check target chain liquidity** — if insufficient, an additional cross-chain fee is deducted
3. **Obtain a withdrawal nonce** from `GET /v1/withdraw_nonce`
4. **Sign an EIP-712 typed data message** of type `Withdraw` using the **on-chain domain** targeting the Orderly Ledger contract (not the off-chain domain used for key registration)
5. **Submit via `POST /v1/withdraw_request`**

### Withdraw EIP-712 Message Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `brokerId` | string | Builder/Broker ID |
| `chainId` | uint256 | Chain ID |
| `receiver` | address | Must equal account address (change to withdraw to a different address) |
| `token` | string | Token symbol (e.g., "USDC") |
| `amount` | uint256 | Raw amount with decimals |
| `withdrawNonce` | uint64 | From GET /v1/withdraw_nonce |
| `timestamp` | uint64 | UNIX milliseconds |

### Critical Type Difference

| Context | `amount` Type |
|---------|---------------|
| EIP-712 signature message | Numeric (uint256/BigInt) |
| REST API JSON payload | **String** |

Using the wrong type in either context will cause signature verification or request validation to fail.

### Withdrawal Fees

Fees are **deducted from the withdrawal amount** (not charged separately):

| Chain | Approximate Fee |
|:---|:---|
| Solana | ~1 USDC |
| Most EVM chains | ~1 USDC |
| Ethereum | Higher (gas-dependent) |

Check dynamic fees via: `GET /v1/public/token`

### Common Withdrawal Errors

#### Error Code 5: "Amount error"
**Cause:** Withdrawal amount is less than the withdrawal fee.
**Solution:** Ensure `withdrawal_amount > withdrawal_fee`. For example, on Solana with a ~1 USDC fee, request at least 1.1 USDC.

#### Error Code 9: "Address and signature do not match"
**Cause:** Mismatch between signing address and `userAddress` in request.
**Solution:**
1. Ensure EIP-712 message is signed by the exact wallet in `userAddress`
2. Verify `verifyingContract` matches the correct contract for the chain
3. Check message structure matches API requirements

#### Error Code 20: "Withdrawal Pre Margin Check Failed"
**Cause:** `holding` balance is less than withdrawal amount, even if `total_collateral_value` appears sufficient.
**Explanation:** `total_collateral_value` includes unsettled PnL, while `holding` reflects only settled balances.
**Solution:** Call the PnL settlement endpoint before withdrawing.

#### Stuck Withdrawals
Check the [Orderly Support Dune Dashboard](https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-support-dashboard), then the [LayerZero Explorer](https://layerzeroscan.com/) (Source: Orderly) for cross-chain message delays.

## Internal Transfers

Internal transfers move funds between accounts under the **same broker ID** (e.g., main account to sub-account).

### Three-Step Process

1. **Obtain a transfer nonce** from `GET /v1/transfer_nonce` (with standard Orderly authentication headers)
2. **Sign an EIP-712 message** of type `InternalTransfer` using the **on-chain domain** with the Ledger contract address as `verifyingContract`
3. **Call `POST /v2/internal_transfer`** with the signature, message, and metadata

### EIP-712 InternalTransfer Message

The signature message contains **only four fields**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `receiver` | bytes32 | Orderly Account ID of receiver (converted to bytes32) |
| `token` | string | Token symbol (e.g., "USDC") |
| `amount` | uint256 | Raw value with decimals (e.g., 1000000 for 1 USDC) |
| `transferNonce` | uint64 | From GET /v1/transfer_nonce |

### REST API Payload vs. EIP-712 Message

The REST API request body includes **two additional helper fields** that must **NOT** be included in the EIP-712 signature:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "receiver": "0x...",
    "token": "USDC",
    "amount": "1000000",
    "transferNonce": "12345",
    "chainId": "42161",
    "chainType": "EVM"
  },
  "signature": "<EIP-712 signature>",
  "userAddress": "<sender wallet address>",
  "verifyingContract": "0x6F7a338F2aA472838dEFD3283eB360d4Dff5D203"
}
```

**Critical:** Including `chainId` and `chainType` in the EIP-712 message during signing will cause gateway validation to fail. Also note that `receiver` is `bytes32` in the EIP-712 message but a hex string (with `0x` prefix) in the API payload.

### Required Headers
- `orderly-account-id`
- `orderly-key` (full string including `ed25519:` prefix)
- `orderly-signature`
- `orderly-timestamp`
- `Content-Type: application/json`

### Full REST API Parameters for POST /v2/internal_transfer

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `message.receiver` | string | Orderly Account ID of receiver |
| `message.token` | string | Token symbol |
| `message.amount` | string | Transfer amount |
| `message.transferNonce` | string | Must match nonce used in signature |
| `message.chainId` | string | Chain ID |
| `message.chainType` | string | `"EVM"` or `"SOL"` |
| `signature` | string | EIP-712 signature |
| `userAddress` | string | Sender wallet (must match signer) |
| `verifyingContract` | string | Ledger contract address used in EIP-712 domain |

### Ledger Contract Addresses

| Environment | Chain | Address |
|-------------|-------|---------|
| Mainnet | Arbitrum One (42161) | `0x6F7a338F2aA472838dEFD3283eB360d4Dff5D203` |
| Testnet | Arbitrum Testnet (421614) | `0x1826B75e2ef249173FC735149AE4B8e9ea10abff` |

Find the correct ledger address for other chains at: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/addresses

### Common Internal Transfer Errors

| Error | Cause | Solution |
|:---|:---|:---|
| "invalid request signature" | Wrong verifying contract | Use the Orderly **ledger address** for your chain, not the standard `0xCcCC...` address |
| "Please use the latest version" | Cross-broker transfer | Internal transfers only work between accounts under the **same broker ID** |
| "pre-margin check" failure | Chained operations | Wait for deposit to complete before initiating internal transfer |

## Tracking Fund Movements

Subscribe to the wallet transactions WebSocket for real-time status updates:

```javascript
// WebSocket subscription
{
  "id": "track_transfers",
  "event": "subscribe",
  "topic": "wallet-transactions"
}
```

- **Deposits/Withdrawals:** Not instant; poll WebSocket for status changes
- **Internal Transfers:** Nearly instant but may require a few seconds

## Asset History API

```
GET /v1/asset_history
```

Records are sorted by `created_time` (database creation time). For accurate chronological ordering matching on-chain events:
- Sort by `block_time` descending
- Filter by `status=COMPLETED` (only completed transactions have `block_time`)

Available timestamps:
- `created_time`: When record was created in Orderly's database
- `updated_time`: When transaction was completed
- `block_time`: On-chain block timestamp (completed transactions only)

chunks.title: Order Placement, Algo Orders, Margin Modes, and Position Management API
chunks.content:
This guide covers the complete lifecycle of orders, algorithmic orders, margin modes, and position management via the Orderly REST API.

## Order Management Endpoints

All order endpoints require authentication with a valid Trading Key (Orderly Key with `trading` scope).

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| POST | `/v1/order` | Create a single order |
| POST | `/v1/batch-order` | Create multiple orders at once |
| PUT | `/v1/order` | Edit an existing order |
| DELETE | `/v1/order` | Cancel a specific order |
| DELETE | `/v1/orders` | Cancel all pending orders |
| GET | `/v1/order/{oid}` | Get order by order ID |
| GET | `/v1/orders` | Get multiple orders |

WebSocket is used for data feeds, not order submission.

## Order Flow Architecture

When a user places an order, it flows through four layers:
1. **Broker Front-end Layer** — forwards the request with the user's Trading Key
2. **Messaging Layer** — verifies the Trading Key
3. **Engine Layer** — matches the order against the order book
4. **Settlement Layer** — trade data is uploaded on execution

The user receives order and execution updates directly from the Engine Layer. Trade execution is sub-50ms on mainnet for taker orders. Trades settle on-chain in batches (~15 seconds).

## Creating Orders

### Market Orders (Futures/Perpetual)

In Futures mode, market orders require `order_quantity` (base asset units), **not** `order_amount` (quote asset value).

```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_quantity": 0.001
}
```

### Limit Orders

```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "LIMIT",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_price": 3000.00,
  "order_quantity": 0.5,
  "margin_mode": "ISOLATED"
}
```

If `margin_mode` is omitted, the symbol's default margin mode is used.

> **Critical:** Use `order_quantity` (base asset units), NOT `order_amount` (quote asset units). The `order_amount` parameter is not supported for perpetual futures.

### Precision and Tick Sizes

Before placing an order, fetch symbol rules via `GET /v1/public/info` or `GET /v1/public/info/:symbol`:
- **`quote_tick`**: Minimum price increment.
- **`base_tick`** (or `base_tick_size`): Minimum quantity increment (lot size).
- **`min_notional`**: Minimum order value (default $1 USD).

**Important:** Trim (do not round) values to the correct precision. For example, if `base_tick` is 0.0001, quantities must be rounded to 4 decimal places.

```json
// ❌ Wrong precision for BTC (5 decimal places required)
{"order_quantity": 0.0009800000000000002}

// ✅ Correct
{"order_quantity": 0.00098}
```

### Price Range Filter

To prevent overly aggressive limit orders, Orderly enforces a price range filter:
- **BUY**: `price <= asks[0].price * (1 + price_range)`
- **SELL**: `price >= bids[0].price * (1 - price_range)`

If your order exceeds this range, you will receive error `-1103`.

### Common Error: Code -1005
**"Placing orders by this order amount is not supported in Futures mode"**

**Cause:** Using `order_amount` instead of `order_quantity`.
**Fix:**
```json
// ❌ Wrong
{"symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC", "order_type": "MARKET", "side": "BUY", "order_amount": 1000}

// ✅ Correct
{"symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC", "order_type": "MARKET", "side": "BUY", "order_quantity": 0.1}
```

### Precision Requirements (Price Filter Error: Code -1104)
**"order does not meet the price filter requirement"** or **"The order must fit in the filter requirement"**

**Cause:** Price or quantity doesn't conform to the symbol's tick size/lot size filters.
**Fix:**
1. Ensure `order_price` is in `quote_tick` increments
2. Ensure `order_quantity` respects `base_tick_size` decimal precision
3. Check symbol trading rules from the available symbols endpoint

## Editing Orders

When editing via `PUT /v1/order`, only send `order_id` and the fields you want to change:

```json
{
  "order_id": "123456",
  "order_price": 3100,
  "order_quantity": 0.6
}
```

> **Error -1005:** "You can not change other order info" — do not include `symbol`, `side`, `order_type`, or `client_order_id` in edit requests.

## Dead Man's Switch

Use `POST /v1/order/cancel_all_after` as a safety mechanism to automatically cancel all open orders if connectivity is lost.

```json
{
  "trigger_in": 60000
}
```

The `trigger_in` parameter specifies the time in milliseconds. If the client doesn't reset the timer before it expires, all open orders are cancelled.

## Hidden (Iceberg) Orders and Fee Classification

Any portion of an order filled as "hidden" (not visible in the order book) is treated as a **taker** order for fee purposes. Only the visible portion that rests on the book qualifies as **maker**.

To achieve iceberg behavior while retaining maker status on the visible portion:

```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "order_type": "LIMIT",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_price": 60000,
  "order_quantity": 1.0,
  "visible_quantity": 0.1
}
```

> If using `POST_ONLY`, do **not** pass `visible_quantity`.

## Maker vs. Taker Fee Determination

Fees are determined by whether an order **adds or removes liquidity**, not by whether it opens or closes a position:
- **Maker**: A buy limit order placed **below** the current market price (rests on the book, adds liquidity)
- **Taker**: Matches an existing order or **crosses the spread** and fills immediately (removes liquidity)

Stop-limit orders **cannot** guarantee maker status. If a limit order fills immediately, it incurs the taker fee.

### Reading Fee Rates

Use the `/v1/client/info` endpoint for fee calculations:
- **Use:** `futures_taker_fee_rate` and `futures_maker_fee_rate`
- **Ignore:** `taker_fee_rate` and `maker_fee_rate` (not used for futures)

Values represent basis points (e.g., 10 = 0.010%).

## Order Tags for Partner Tracking

Track orders from specific partners using the `order_tag` parameter. It functions similarly to a referral code and overrides the user's default referral code, allowing third-party integrations to attribute trades and receive a share of broker fees.

```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "LIMIT",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_price": 3000,
  "order_quantity": 1.0,
  "order_tag": "partner_xyz_referral_code"
}
```

The tag is set per-order by the integrator and does not need to be pre-created by Orderly. Retrieve volume filtered by tag: `GET /v1/private/get-brokers-users-volumes?order_tag=partner_xyz_referral_code`

## Fetching Order Details

When using `GET /v1/order/{order_id}`:
- `amount` is always `null` — the API returns `quantity` (base token) for open/filled orders.
- `price` is `null` for MARKET orders — use `average_executed_price` for the fill price.

## Order Data Retention

Orderly archives order data based on these rules:
- If total orders ≤ 2,000: Data from the last **90 days** is retained
- If total orders > 2,000: Only the most recent **2,000 orders** are kept
- If orders on a single day exceed 2,000: Only that day's orders are retained

Archived data will not appear even when paginating through the API.

## Reconciling Orders and Trades

If your order quantity delta doesn't sum to zero when reconciling `/v1/orders` and `/v1/trades`, this is typically caused by **liquidation records**, which are not included in the `/v1/orders` endpoint. Fetch liquidation records separately.

## Algorithmic Orders (TP/SL)

### Endpoint
```
POST /v1/algo_order
```

For algo orders (STOP, TP/SL, BRACKET), refer to the [Algo Order Samples documentation](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/algo-order-samples).

### Bracket Order with TP/SL
Use `algo_type: "BRACKET"` with child orders:

```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "algo_type": "BRACKET",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_quantity": 1.0,
  "child_orders": [
    {
      "algo_type": "TP_SL",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "TAKE_PROFIT",
          "trigger_price": 3500
        },
        {
          "type": "STOP_LOSS",
          "trigger_price": 2800
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Alternative bracket order format with `POSITIONAL_TP_SL`:
```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "algo_type": "BRACKET",
  "quantity": "0.1",
  "side": "BUY",
  "type": "MARKET",
  "child_orders": [
    {
      "algo_type": "POSITIONAL_TP_SL",
      "child_orders": [
        { "algo_type": "TAKE_PROFIT", "side": "SELL", "type": "CLOSE_POSITION", "trigger_price": "2600", "reduce_only": true },
        { "algo_type": "STOP_LOSS", "side": "SELL", "type": "CLOSE_POSITION", "trigger_price": "2200", "reduce_only": true }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
**Note:** Child TP/SL orders may show `quantity: 0` in API responses because they are close-position orders.

### TP/SL Rules
- A `TP_SL` child order must contain **exactly two** children: one `TAKE_PROFIT` and one `STOP_LOSS`
- Quantities must match between TP and SL
- You **cannot** define multiple take-profits at different levels within a single TP_SL bracket
- For partial TP scenarios: send a regular market order first, then create separate algo orders for each TP/SL level

### Algo Order Rate Limits
Algo order endpoints have a strict limit of **1 request per second** per account.

## Cross Margin vs. Isolated Margin

| Feature | Cross Margin | Isolated Margin |
|---------|-------------|----------------|
| Balance sharing | Shared across all positions | Dedicated per position |
| Loss exposure | Account-wide liquidation possible | Capped at assigned margin |
| Profit offset | Profitable positions offset losing ones | No offset between positions |
| Capital efficiency | Higher | Lower |
| Risk control | Broader | Tighter per-trade |

### Setting Leverage

Use the **singular** `/v1/client/leverage` endpoint (not the plural `/v1/client/leverages`) for isolated margin:

```json
POST /v1/client/leverage
{
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "leverage": 3,
  "margin_mode": "ISOLATED"
}
```

**Important:** The `/v1/client/leverages` (plural) endpoint updates all symbols atomically with Cross margin behavior.

Each symbol maintains independent leverage settings per margin mode. Query current leverage with:
```
GET /v1/client/leverage?symbol=PERP_ETH_USDC&margin_mode=ISOLATED
```

**Note:** You can only switch margin mode when you have **no open positions or pending orders** on that symbol. Verify margin mode first:
```
GET /v1/client/margin_modes
```

### Changing Default Margin Mode

Use `POST /v1/client/margin_mode` to change the default display mode. This is primarily for frontend display and does not restrict which mode you can trade in.

### Adding Margin to Isolated Positions

```json
POST /api/v1/adjust_isolated_margin
{
  "subaccountId": "12345",
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "amount": 100,
  "type": "ADD"
}
```

Set `type` to `"ADD"` for increasing margin or `"REDUCE"` for decreasing.

### IMR Factor

The `imr_factor` (Initial Margin Requirement factor) is found on the **account information** endpoint (not the symbol info endpoint), because it is account-dependent:
```
GET /v1/client/info
```

For base initial margin requirements per symbol, use `base_imr` from:
```
GET /v1/public/available_symbols
```

## Position Management

### Key Positions and Holdings Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `GET /v1/positions` | Active positions and unrealized PnL |
| `GET /v1/client/holding` | Collateral balances |
| `GET /v1/client/aggregate/holding` | Aggregate holdings including isolated margin fields |
| `GET /api/v1/isolated_positions` | Isolated positions with `estimatedLiquidationPrice` |
| `GET /v1/position/{symbol}?margin_mode=ISOLATED` | Isolated position for a symbol |

### Querying Isolated Margin Positions

**Key response fields:**
- `margin` — allocated margin amount
- `margin_mode` — ISOLATED
- `leverage` — current leverage
- `est_liq_price` — estimated liquidation price
- `position_qty` — position size
- `unsettled_pnl` — current unsettled PnL
- `imr` — initial margin ratio
- `mmr` — maintenance margin ratio

For real-time updates, subscribe to the private `position` WebSocket topic.

### Isolated-Margin Fields in Balance Endpoint

`GET /v1/client/aggregate/holding` includes:
- `isolated_margin` — total margin allocated to all isolated positions
- `isolated_order_frozen` — margin frozen in pending isolated orders

### Frozen Funds

In the current holdings API response (`GET /v1/client/holding`), the `frozen` field indicates funds that are temporarily locked due to:
- Pending withdrawal requests
- Pending orders

### Closing Positions

To close a long position, send a SELL order with `reduce_only: true`:

```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "side": "SELL",
  "reduce_only": true,
  "order_quantity": "0.008"
}
```

For a limit close, set `order_type: "LIMIT"` and include `order_price`.

> **Note:** Position quantity is positive for long and negative for short positions.

> **Testnet Issue:** If a `reduce_only` market order returns success but the position remains open, it's likely due to insufficient liquidity on testnet. Try a more liquid pair.

### Filtering Closed Positions

A position with `position_qty: 0` may still appear if it has:
- Unsettled PnL
- Pending open orders

These are automatically removed after PnL settlement. **To get only open positions**, filter where `position_qty !== 0`.

**To fully close a zero-quantity position:**
1. Settle the PnL: `POST /v1/settle_pnl`
2. Cancel remaining open orders: Check via `GET /v1/orders`

### Trading Fee in Position History

The `trading_fee` field in position history represents accumulated trading fees while the position was open. To determine exact fees, fetch all trades that created or modified the position. Note that `liquidatorFee` is a separate field for liquidation costs.

### Liquidation Price
The liquidation price is **dynamically recalculated** based on:
1. **Mark Price updates** (via WebSocket, every 1 second)
2. **Position changes** (quantity or average entry price)
3. **Collateral changes** (account balance or collateral value)

> The liquidation price will fluctuate in real-time even when the position hasn't changed, because the Mark Price updates continuously.

### Stop-Loss and Liquidation Race Condition
When mark price moves rapidly and both the stop-loss trigger and liquidation threshold are breached within the same tick, the liquidation engine acquires the lock first. The stop-loss is rejected with `APPLICATION_LIQUIDATING`.

**Mitigation:**
1. Leave a wider buffer between SL price and liquidation threshold.
2. Reduce effective leverage.
3. Avoid high-leverage positions near the liquidation threshold.

### Hedge Mode
Orderly does **not** support holding both long and short positions on the same asset simultaneously. Traders needing strategies like strangles must use separate accounts.

## Settling PnL

Realized and unrealized PnL must be "settled" into the account's collateral balance. PnL must be settled before withdrawing funds.

### Settlement Flow
1. **Detect** unsettled PnL ≠ 0 via `GET /v1/client/info`
2. **Get nonce**: `GET /v1/settle_pnl_nonce` (or `GET /v1/settle_nonce`)
3. **Sign and submit**: `POST /v1/settle_pnl` (or `POST /v1/pnl_settlement`)
4. **Confirm**: Poll `GET /v1/client/info` until `unsettledPnl == 0`
5. **Then** initiate withdrawal

The API returns settled holdings. The UI shows a dynamically calculated balance including floating unrealized PnL.

### Sub-Account Settlement

**Critical:** Sub-accounts must use a different endpoint:
- Main accounts: `POST /v1/settle_pnl`
- Sub-accounts: `POST /v1/sub_account_settle_pnl`

Using the wrong endpoint causes error `-1109 (Signature user mismatch)` because the settle nonce is tracked separately per account type.

## Real-Time Account Health via WebSocket

Subscribe to these topics for real-time monitoring:

### Account Topic
```
/v1/ws/private/account
```
Returns: `marginMode`, `futuresLeverage`, `maintenanceCancelFlag`

### Balance Topic
```
/v1/ws/private/balance
```
Returns: real-time `holding`, `frozen`, and `pending` quantities

### Position Push Topic
```
/v1/ws/private/position-push
```
Returns: `imr` (initial margin ratio), `mmr` (maintenance margin ratio), `estLiqPrice` (estimated liquidation price)

## Common Order Errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| -1005 | 400 | Parameter format error (e.g., `order_price` must be positive, or using `order_amount` in futures) |
| -1101 | 400 | Margin/risk issue — exposure too high or insufficient margin |
| -1103 | 400 | Price range filter violation |
| -1104 | 400 | Quantity/price does not conform to `base_tick`/`quote_tick` |
| -1012 | 400 | Off-chain engine balance insufficient or internal module rejection (account in liquidation). Wait for deposit processing or retry after a few seconds |
| -1007 | 409 | Duplicate request |
| -1003 | 429 | Rate limit exceeded |

**200 OK but Position Remains Open**: The order passed pre-trade risk checks but was cancelled at the matching stage (e.g., due to wide spread on low-volume pairs).

## Maintenance Windows

During monthly maintenance windows (~2 hours):
- All trading activity is paused
- Pending orders are **NOT** automatically cancelled unless users enable auto-cancellation

### Auto-Cancellation Configuration
```
POST /v1/private/maintenance-config
```
or
```
POST /v1/client/maintenance-config
```
Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/evm-api/restful-api/private/set-maintenance-config

> Advise users to cancel pending orders before maintenance, as prices may resume at different levels.

Join the Orderly System Updates Telegram channel for notifications: https://t.me/+VnpoOvYpJXA2ZTc1

## Sub-Account Trading

To trade on a sub-account, include the sub-account ID in the header:
```
orderly-account-id: {sub_account_id}
```

Sub-accounts share the same Orderly key and rate limits as the main account. Use the same endpoints for order placement, position queries, and statistics.

## Third-Party Position Tracking

To track open positions for users without requiring their private API keys, use the Orderly indexer API:

```
GET https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/ranking/positions?account_id={account_id}&offset=0&limit=30&order_by=DESC
```

For read-only access with user consent, prompt users to create a **read-only Orderly API key**, then call:
```
GET /v1/positions  (with user's API key authentication)
```

## Copy Trading and Automated Strategies

Orderly does not provide a built-in copy trading feature. Builders must implement the logic:

1. Capture trading signals from lead traders
2. Programmatically execute corresponding trades on follower accounts via the API
3. Handle signal distribution, follower management, and trade replication

For smart contract vaults, use the **delegate signer** feature to register a smart contract as a user: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/delegate-signer

chunks.title: Orderly Network API: Rate Limits, WebSocket Streams, Market Data, and Best Practices
chunks.content:
This comprehensive guide covers Orderly Network's REST and WebSocket APIs, including rate limits, authentication, market data endpoints, error handling, infrastructure details, and best practices for building reliable trading applications.

## Environment URLs

| Environment | REST API | WebSocket Public | WebSocket Private |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Mainnet (EVM) | `https://api-evm.orderly.org` | `wss://ws-evm.orderly.org/ws/stream` | `wss://ws-private-evm.orderly.org/v2/ws/private/stream/{account_id}` |
| Testnet (EVM) | `https://testnet-api-evm.orderly.org` | `wss://testnet-ws-evm.orderly.org/ws/stream` | `wss://testnet-ws-private-evm.orderly.org/v2/ws/private/stream/{account_id}` |
| NEAR | `https://api.orderly.org` | — | — |
| VIP Gateway | `https://api-vip-evm.orderly.org` (requires IP whitelist) | — | — |

**Broker Admin WebSocket:** `wss://ws-broker.orderly.org/ws/stream/{account_id}` — brokers can subscribe to push notifications for all users under their broker.

**Orderly L2 RPC:** `rpc.orderly.network` (built on Optimism stack, listed at [chainlist.org](https://chainlist.org/?search=Orderly)). For indexing trade data, use the open-source [Orderly Dashboard Indexer](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-dashboard) rather than direct RPC queries.

**Plume Network (Updated):** Mainnet RPC: `https://rpc.plume.org`, Explorer: `https://explorer.plume.org` (old `.xyz` domains shut down).

## Rate Limits

Orderly uses a **call-weight-based approach** (not simple requests-per-second), where different endpoints have different weights.

### Two Layers of Rate Limiting

| Layer | Limit | Scope |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Gateway (GCP Cloud Armor) | 600 requests per 5 minutes | Per IP |
| Endpoint-specific | Varies per endpoint | Per account or IP |

### Public API
- **Scope:** Per IP address
- **Default:** ~10 requests per second per IP
- **Applies to:** Market data, symbol info, public endpoints

### Private API
- **Scope:** Per account (main account and sub-accounts share the same limit)
- **Tier-based:** Limits depend on builder volume tier
- **Reference:** https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-builder-volume

### Specific Endpoint Limits

| Endpoint Category | Rate Limit |
|:---|:---|
| `POST /v1/order` | 10 requests per second |
| Order placement (specific) | 50 per 1 second |
| Order cancellation (specific) | 50 per 1 second |
| Algo Orders | 1 request per second per account |
| `GET /v1/positions` | 30 requests per 10 seconds (fixed, non-adjustable) |
| Portfolio/History | 10 requests per minute |
| General Trading | Configurable per builder tier |
| GCP Infrastructure (IP-level) | 600 requests per 5 minutes |
| Archival Database (`include_historical_data`) | 1 request per 60 seconds |
| WebSocket connections | 150 per account ID |

### Batch Endpoints
For high-frequency operations, use batch endpoints to avoid hitting per-request limits:
- **Batch Create**: `POST /v1/batch-order` (up to 10 orders per request)
- **Batch Cancel**: `DELETE /v1/batch-order` (up to 10 orders per request)

### Market Maker (MM) Accounts
50 create/cancel requests per second (requires 75% maker volume ratio).

### Rate Limit Error
When rate limited, you'll receive HTTP 429 with error code **-1003** ("You have exceeded the rate limit").

### Requesting Higher Limits / IP Whitelisting
Contact the Orderly team with:
- Your IP addresses (CIDR blocks are **not** supported — only specific IPs)
- Specific endpoints hitting limits
- Use case description
- Broker ID and target request rate

If your backend serves many users and hits IP-level throttling, request IP whitelisting on GCP Cloud Armor. Once whitelisted, only account-level limits apply. Proxies may not work if they forward real-IP headers. Notify the Orderly team proactively as you onboard more traders so limits can be adjusted accordingly.

### How IP Detection Works
Orderly reads the IP address directly from the connection, **not** from HTTP headers like `X-Forwarded-For` (which can be spoofed).

## WebSocket API

### Authentication (Private Streams)

Private WebSocket connections use Ed25519 authentication. The signature message is the **timestamp only** (method, path, and body are blank). Public streams do not require authentication.

```python
import websocket
import base64
import time
import json
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

def connect_private_ws(account_id, private_key_b58, api_key):
    ws_url = f"wss://ws-private-evm.orderly.org/v2/ws/private/stream/{account_id}"
    
    def on_open(ws):
        timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)
        message = str(timestamp).encode('utf-8')
        key_bytes = base64.b58decode(private_key_b58)
        private_key = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(key_bytes)
        signature = private_key.sign(message)
        sig_b64 = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(signature).decode('utf-8')
        
        auth_msg = {
            "id": "auth_1",
            "event": "auth",
            "params": {
                "orderly_key": f"ed25519:{api_key}",
                "sign": sig_b64,
                "timestamp": timestamp
            }
        }
        ws.send(json.dumps(auth_msg))
    
    def on_message(ws, data):
        msg = json.loads(data)
        print(f"Received: {msg}")
    
    ws = websocket.WebSocketApp(
        ws_url,
        on_open=on_open,
        on_message=on_message,
        ping_interval=10,
        ping_timeout=5
    )
    ws.run_forever()
```

### Maintaining the Connection
Send `{"event": "ping"}` regularly (every 20–30 seconds) and expect a `pong` response as a heartbeat. If authentication fails, the connection will be disconnected. Implement auto-reconnect logic with exponential backoff for network issues or idle timeouts.

### Subscription Pattern

All subscriptions follow the same JSON structure:
```json
{
  "id": "client-generated-id",
  "topic": "TOPIC_STRING",
  "event": "subscribe"
}
```

Unsubscribe by sending the same structure with `event` set to `"unsubscribe"`.

### Available Public Topics (Market Data)

| Topic | Format | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `orderbook` | `{symbol}@orderbook` | Full depth-100 orderbook snapshots every 1 second |
| `order-book-update` | — | Incremental orderbook updates |
| `trade` | `{symbol}@trade` | Real-time trade execution events (all market trades across all brokers) |
| `ticker` | `{symbol}@ticker` | Ticker updates |
| `kline` / `kline_1m` | `{symbol}@kline_1m` | Candlestick data (various resolutions available) |
| `liquidation-push` | — | Market-wide liquidation events |

**Subscribe to Orderbook Example:**
```json
{
  "id": "clientID2",
  "topic": "PERP_WOO_USDC@orderbook",
  "event": "subscribe"
}
```

**Data push (every 1 second):**
```json
{
  "topic": "PERP_WOO_USDC@orderbook",
  "ts": 1614152140945,
  "data": {
    "symbol": "PERP_WOO_USDC",
    "asks": [[0.31075, 2379.63], [0.31076, 4818.76]],
    "bids": [[0.30891, 2469.98], [0.3089, 482.5]]
  }
}
```
Each entry in `asks` and `bids` is a `[price, quantity]` array.

**Subscribe to Trade Events Example:**
```json
{
  "id": "clientID3",
  "topic": "PERP_WOO_USDC@trade",
  "event": "subscribe"
}
```

**Data push (real-time):**
```json
{
  "topic": "PERP_WOO_USDC@trade",
  "ts": 1618820361552,
  "data": {
    "symbol": "PERP_WOO_USDC",
    "price": 0.37988,
    "size": 300,
    "side": "BUY"
  }
}
```

### Available Private Topics (User Data)

| Topic | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `executionreport` | Order fills, partial fills, cancellations, rejections |
| `algoexecutionreport` | Algo order execution updates |
| `algoexecutionreportv2` | Enhanced algo order updates |
| `balance` | Account balance changes |
| `position` | Real-time position changes |
| `account` | Account-level updates |
| `wallet` / `wallet-transactions` | Deposit/withdrawal/internal transfer events |
| `liquidationsaccount` | Account liquidation events |

**Subscribe to Execution Reports (Private):**
```json
{
  "id": "clientID3",
  "topic": "executionreport",
  "event": "subscribe",
  "params": {
    "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC,PERP_ETH_USDC"
  }
}
```
- `params.symbol` is optional — omit to receive reports for all symbols
- Comma-separated string for multiple symbols

**Execution report fields:** `symbol`, `clientOrderId`, `orderId`, `type`, `side`, `quantity`, `price`, `tradeId`, `executedPrice`, `executedQuantity`, `fee`, `feeAsset`, `totalExecutedQuantity`, `avgExecutedPrice`, `status`, `reason`, `totalFee`, `visibleQuantity`, `timestamp`, `marginMode`, `maker` (boolean), `match_id`, `seq`.

### Important WebSocket Behaviors
- **No Request ID in Error Responses:** WebSocket errors do **not** include the `id` field from the original request. Maintain your own mapping of pending requests to correlate responses.
- **Duplicate Subscribe Events:** The `wallet` topic may push duplicate subscribe events when multiple transactions occur in a short interval. This is expected behavior.
- **No Initial Snapshot:** Topics like `balance` and `account` only push data when values change. Use REST APIs to fetch the initial state, then use WebSocket for incremental updates.
- **Orderbook Snapshots:** The orderbook pushes full depth-100 snapshots every second, not incremental updates.

## Market Data Endpoints

### Available Symbols and Token Info

```
GET /v1/public/info              (available symbols from token metadata)
GET /v1/public/available_symbols (includes base_imr per symbol)
GET /v1/public/token             (token details including chain-specific decimals)
GET /v1/public/futures           (includes broker_id for permissionless listings)
```

**Filtering Permissionless Listings:** Check the `broker_id` field in `/v1/public/futures`. If `broker_id` has a value, the symbol is community-listed (permissionless).

### Price Data Sources

| Display | Endpoint | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| TradingView chart | `/public/24-hour-ticker` | 24-hour ticker data |
| Orderbook mid price | `/public/orderbook` | Reflects real trades, most up-to-date |
| Mark price | `/public/mark-price` | Used for PnL and liquidation calculations |

### Historical Kline (Candlestick) Data

For TradingView-compatible historical bars:
```
GET /tv/history?symbol=PERP_BTC_USDC&resolution=15&from=<unix_timestamp>&to=<unix_timestamp>
```
Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-tradingview-history-bars
Supports up to 1,000 rows per request.

**Note:** The `/v1/kline` endpoint requires the `orderly-account-id` header (not fully public). For public historical market data without authentication, use the TradingView history endpoint or external data providers.

### Historical Funding Rates
```
GET /v1/public/funding-rate  (paginated)
```
Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-funding-rate-for-all-markets

### Other REST Market Data Endpoints
- **Market Trades**: `GET /v1/public/market-trades` (returns max 500 recent trades; no paging)
- **Open Interest**: `GET /v1/public/market-info-for-all-symbols` (returns OI in base token units; multiply by index price for USD value)

### Market Data Consistency
The market API (public data: trades, order books, klines) is **the same across all Orderly-based DEXs** since it's served by Orderly's shared infrastructure. User-specific data (history, positions, rewards) must be provided by individual brokers.

### Bulk Historical Data
For bulk data needs beyond the API (e.g., full database exports for offline analysis or agent training), contact the Orderly team to arrange a database export. Very old historical data (e.g., before April 2025 for some symbols) may not be available via the public API.

### Orderbook Liquidity
Orderly does not provide a single REST endpoint for exact public liquidity. Use the WebSocket `orderbook` stream to maintain a local orderbook snapshot. The private REST endpoint `/v1/orderbook/{symbol}` requires authentication and returns a snapshot for a specific user/broker context.

## Common Error Codes

| Code | Error | Cause | Solution |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| -1000 | 500 Internal Server Error | Incorrect `Content-Type` header | For `POST`/`PUT`: use `application/json`; for `GET`/`DELETE`: use `application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8` |
| -1003 | Rate limit exceeded | Too many requests | Implement throttling/caching; use WebSocket; use batch APIs |
| -1005 | Order amount not supported / "You can not change other order info" | Used `order_amount` instead of `order_quantity`, or editing order incorrectly | Use `order_quantity` for futures; when editing via `PUT /v1/order`, only `order_price` and `order_quantity` can be modified, and the request must include **all original order fields** exactly as placed (`client_order_id`, `order_tag`, `symbol`, `order_type`, `side`). Special characters like `-` or `_` in `client_order_id` may cause issues. |
| -1104 | Price filter requirement | Wrong tick/lot size | Check symbol trading rules |
| -1108 | Permission Denied | Wrong wallet for admin endpoints | Use registered admin wallet |
| -1601 | Address invalid (Solana) | Missing chainType | Include `chainType: "SOL"` |
| -1607 | Account does not exist | Wrong environment URL or unregistered wallet | Use correct mainnet/testnet base URL; ensure wallet has registered an account on Orderly before creating an Orderly key |
| -3001 | "RelayerV2: out of counters" | Rate limiting on cross-chain messages (USDC faucet) | Keep retrying — resolves when rate limit window resets |
| 5 | Amount error (withdrawal) | Amount < withdrawal fee | Ensure amount exceeds fee |
| 9 | Address/signature mismatch | Wrong signing address | Verify EIP-712 message signer matches `userAddress` |
| 20 | Pre-margin check failed | Unsettled PnL | Call PnL settlement endpoint first |
| 71 | Internal transfer failed | Transfers between unrelated main accounts blocked by default | Contact Orderly team to whitelist your broker; use `v2/internal_transfer` endpoint with wallet signature. Transfers between a main account and its subaccounts work without special permission. |

Full library of API error codes: [Error Codes Documentation](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/error-codes#error-codes)

### 401 Unauthorized
**Cause:** Orderly key not properly registered. Ensure the key was added via the `add orderly key` endpoint before making authenticated calls.

### 403 Forbidden (HTML Response)
**Cause:** GCP Cloud Armor classifying your IP as originating from an embargoed region, flagged as bot traffic, or identified by Google Threat Intelligence as a 'known malicious IP.' This commonly affects certain VPN or hosting provider IPs and cloud infrastructure IPs (e.g., DigitalOcean). This occurs at the infrastructure level and also applies to WebSocket connections (e.g., `wss://ws-private-evm.orderly.org`).

**Resolution:**
- Submit affected IPs to Orderly support for GCP allowlisting (may take several days)
- Switch networks or reset connection (toggle airplane mode)
- Reassign floating IP or recreate instance for a fresh IP
- Test candidate IPs: `GET https://api.orderly.org/v1/public/system_info` (200 = clean, 403 = flagged)
- Check IP info: `curl https://api.orderly.org/v1/ip_info`

## Best Practices

### 1. Use WebSocket for Real-Time Data
Instead of polling REST endpoints, subscribe to WebSocket topics for `executionreport`, `balance`, `position-push`, and `wallet-transactions`.

### 2. Cache Static Data
Cache data that rarely changes: available symbols and trading rules, token information and chain details, broker configuration.

### 3. Separate Read-Only Keys for Monitoring
Create independent API keys with read-only scope for monitoring services:
```
POST /v1/orderly_key
{ "scope": "read" }
```
Monitoring rate limits don't affect trading API keys since they have separate configurations.

### 4. Handle Timestamp Drift
Ensure system clock synchronization. Requests with timestamps differing from server time by >300 seconds are rejected.

### 5. Chain Operations Carefully
When chaining operations (e.g., deposit → internal transfer → trade), wait for each operation to complete via WebSocket before initiating the next.

### 6. WebSocket Best Practices
- **Always use a unique `id`** per subscription to correlate confirmations.
- **Implement heartbeat** — send `{"event": "ping"}` every 20–30 seconds.
- **Handle reconnection** — WebSocket connections can drop; implement exponential backoff.
- **Filter private topics** — use `params.symbol` on `executionreport` to reduce noise.

## IP Restrictions on API Keys

Restrict API key usage to specific IPs:
```http
POST /v1/client/set_orderly_key_ip_restriction
{
  "orderly_key": "ed25519:...",
  "ip_restriction_list": "192.168.0.1,10.0.0.1"
}
```

## Infrastructure Details

### Server Location
Orderly's API infrastructure is hosted in **GCP Tokyo**.

**Typical latency:**
- GCP LB: 7-10ms
- Orderly gateway: 15-18ms
- Total: ~25ms
- Orderbook/matching engine: 20-50ms

Optimize backend-to-Orderly connections accordingly.

## Security Considerations

### Exposed API Keys
If `orderly-account-id` and `orderly-key` (public/secret) are exposed:
- ❌ Attacker **cannot** withdraw funds (requires wallet EIP-712 signature)
- ⚠️ Attacker **can** place orders, modify settings (if key has trade permissions)
- ✅ Actions requiring EIP-712 signatures remain protected

### Key Expiration
- Default expiration: **30 days** if not explicitly set
- Custom expiration can be set during key creation (e.g., 1 year)
- Expired keys must be replaced by generating new ones

### Delegate Signer for Smart Contracts
Smart contracts cannot sign EIP-712 messages directly. Use the delegate signer feature:
- Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/delegate-signer
- Reference implementation: https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/delegate-signer
- When constructing EIP-712 typed data for delegate withdrawals, ensure `delegateContract` field type is `address` (not `string`)

## Withdrawal Issues

### Accepted but Not Arriving
A withdrawal may be accepted by the API but rejected asynchronously by the risk engine if margin would be insufficient. This happens when pending orders (e.g., unfilled limit orders) lock up margin.

**Solution:** Cancel all pending orders before withdrawing the full balance.

### Custom Receiver Addresses
Withdrawals to addresses other than the connected wallet are disabled by default. Brokers can request the Orderly team to enable this at the broker level or for specific whitelisted accounts.

## Notification Inbox API

### Mark as Read
```http
POST /v1/notification/inbox/mark_read
{
  "ids": [14257831],
  "flag": 1
}
```

### Mark All as Read
Ensure you pass the `flag` field (e.g., `?flag=1`), otherwise the endpoint may acknowledge success but not update the read state.

> **Note:** Order fills do **not** trigger inbox notifications. TRADE notifications are only for: deposits, interest, KYC events, margin calls, withdrawals, new listings, and maintenance. Use WebSocket `executionreport` for fill tracking.

## System Maintenance

During scheduled maintenance:
- **Trading**: Suspended. The frontend blocks all operations.
- **Withdrawals**: API cannot be called.
- **Deposits**: Remain available.
- **Algo Orders**: Stop/TPSL orders will not trigger.

### Monitoring Maintenance
Use the public endpoint `GET /v1/public/system_info` to check system status. During maintenance, API endpoints return system maintenance errors. There is also an announcement API:
```
GET /v1/public/announcement
```
Builders can consume this to display maintenance warnings. There is also a user-level option to automatically close all positions during maintenance.

### Rolling Risk Service Updates
During rolling updates, individual accounts may experience ~3-second interruptions. Orders may temporarily return: `"The risk service is updating. Please try again in a moment."`

## Geo-Restrictions

Orderly is available worldwide except: **United States, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Ukraine.** Orderly does not enforce geo-blocking on its APIs. VPN access issues are typically on the VPN provider side.

## CCXT Integration (Python)

Use the `ccxt.woofipro` exchange class (not `ccxt.woo`, which targets the WooX CEX):

```python
import ccxt

exchange = ccxt.woofipro({
    'apiKey': 'ed25519:XXXXXXXXX',
    'secret': 'ed25519:XXXXXXXXX',
    'accountId': '0xxxxxxxx'
})
exchange.options['brokerId'] = 'your_broker_id'
exchange.urls['api'] = {
    'public': 'https://api.orderly.org',
    'private': 'https://api.orderly.org',
}
```

**Common Error:** Using `ccxt.woo` instead of `ccxt.woofipro` results in 400 Bad Request or 'path not found' errors because `woo` targets the WooX CEX v3 API.

## OpenAPI Specification

The OpenAPI/Swagger specification for Orderly's EVM API:
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/openAPI-EVM
- **Indexer Swagger UI**: https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/swagger-ui/#/

## Supported Third-Party Platforms

- **Tealstreet**: Integrated and supported
- **Hummingbot, 3Commas, WunderTrading**: Not currently integrated
- Custom integrations via REST/WebSocket API (Python, Node, etc.) are always possible

## Testing Best Practices

1. **Use testnet first:** `testnet-api-evm.orderly.org`
2. **Test fee changes on staging:** https://testnet-admin.orderly.network/login
3. **Make base URL configurable** in your application
4. **Verify registration** using: `GET /v1/public/check_if_wallet_is_registered`
5. **Use demo broker IDs** (`brokerId='demo'`) from the public broker list for initial testing. All WebSocket and REST endpoints work identically to production. However, the admin wallet is a dummy address, so broker fee earnings are lost.
6. **You cannot run your own Orderly instance or fork the environment.** Stub the Orderly backend API for integration/e2e tests instead.

### Testnet Faucet

**EVM:**
```
POST https://testnet-operator-evm.orderly.org/v1/faucet/usdc
```
Body: `{ "user_address": "...", "chain_id": ..., "broker_id": "..." }`

**Solana:**
```
https://testnet-operator-sol.orderly.org/v1/faucet/usdc
```

You can also log in to your DEX on testnet and request faucet tokens from the Orderly interface, then withdraw them for further testing. There is no standalone external faucet.

**Note:** USDC is credited to your Orderly account, not sent directly to the chain. If you receive a 429 error, try a different wallet address or broker_id.

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings, Custom Oracles, and Market Lifecycle
chunks.content:
Orderly supports permissionless market creation, custom oracle price feeds, and a community-driven token delisting process. This guide covers the mechanics, APIs, and builder responsibilities for managing market listings.

## Permissionless Listing Framework

The Permissionless Listing framework allows brokers to list new perpetual markets (crypto, RWA, pre-TGE) without centralized approval. Listed markets are visible across **all Orderly DEXs** (though by default they appear only on the listing broker's platform; other brokers can manually enable them).

### Eligibility & Revenue

- **Diamond tier brokers** (or any tier during promotional periods; all tiers can list up to **5 assets** as a promotional allowance).
- Initiator earns **50% of Orderly's trading fee share** for the listed pair.
- Initiator earns **100% of liquidation fees**.
- Initiator earns **APY on the liquidation fund** and receives **Diamond tier broker status**.

### Listing Process

1. **Review documentation:** [Permissionless Listing Docs](https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/permissionless-listing)
2. **Use the admin portal:** [https://admin.orderly.network/permissionless-listing](https://admin.orderly.network/permissionless-listing)
3. Initiator lists the market, sets parameters, and provides liquidity by depositing an insurance/liquidation fund (minimum amount required).
4. Select the asset, choose the oracle, and connect a market maker. Market-making can be managed through the admin portal or third-party MM infrastructure such as [Tread.fi](https://docs.tread.fi/bots/market-maker-bot).
5. For pre-TGE or custom assets, provide the token name, initial price, and price tick to the Orderly team for oracle configuration.

### Standard Listing Criteria (Non-Permissionless)

For tokens that don't use permissionless listing, contact the Orderly listing team. Requirements include:
1. Price index availability with 3+ price feed sources
2. A market maker integrated with Orderly
3. 20M+ market cap

### Builder Responsibilities on Listing

When new markets are listed, builders must:
1. **Sync frontend** configurations to support new symbols.
2. **Notify users** of newly available markets.

Markets listed through this framework have included stocks ($AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT, $COIN, $META), crypto tokens ($EIGEN, $GRAM), and other instruments.

## Custom Oracles

Custom Oracles allow builders to push asset prices directly to Orderly for permissionless perpetual markets on any asset type without waiting for Orderly to add data sources:
- FX pairs
- US stocks
- Commodities
- Interest rates
- Crypto tokens
- Pre-TGE tokens
- Real World Assets (RWAs)

Builders combine their own price sources with existing CEX/oracle feeds and push price data directly to Orderly's oracle system, giving full control over market expansion.

Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/custom-oracle#custom-oracle

### RWA Markets

Orderly sources RWA index price data from multiple providers: Pragma, Tradermade, and Finage.

**NASDAQ CFD Trading Hours:** For NASDAQ CFD trading, Orderly follows **CME Globex trading hours** rather than standard U.S. stock market hours. Liquidity is typically higher during regular U.S. market hours when market makers can more easily hedge.

## Funding Parameters for Permissionless Markets

When configuring permissionless markets, funding parameters have specific constraints:

| Parameter | Allowed Values |
|:---|:---|
| **Funding Period** | 1h, 4h, 8h |
| **Funding Cap** | Min: 0.75%, Max: 4% |
| **Funding Floor** | Min: -4%, Max: -0.75% |
| **Interest Rate** | `0.0001 * funding_period / 28800` |

> **Note:** Setting funding to zero (e.g., `funding_cap = funding_floor = 0`) is NOT supported.

## Order Book Depth Thresholds

Permissionless markets are monitored for liquidity and may be automatically delisted:

| Event | Condition |
|:---|:---|
| **Move to Reduce-only** | ±2% depth stays below $6,250 for 10 minutes |
| **Exit Reduce-only** | ±2% depth reaches/exceeds $10,000 for 10 minutes |
| **Full Auto-delist** | Depth stays below limit continuously for 24 hours |

When a market enters reduce-only mode, only position-closing orders are accepted. Builders should handle reduce-only mode gracefully in the UI.

## Token Delisting and Vote to Retain

Orderly periodically reviews listed tokens and opens a community **Vote to Retain** process.

### Voting Mechanics
- To retain a token: **>3% of staked $ORDER** (or 5% in some cases) must vote AGAINST delisting.
- Voting period: **5 days**.
- Tokens without sufficient votes are delisted.

### Delisting Price Fixing
When a token is delisted:
- The index/mark price is **fixed** at the average price of the last hour before delisting time (used for open interest settlement).
- Builders should sync frontend configurations and notify users.

### Common Delisting Reasons
- Sustained low metrics (volume, liquidity)
- Project rebranding (e.g., $TON)
- Token swaps (e.g., $IP)
- Market disruptions (e.g., $H)

## Insurance Fund and ADL

Orderly maintains an insurance fund and Auto-Deleveraging (ADL) system for perpetual futures.

### Query Insurance Fund Info
```
GET /v1/public/insurance_fund_info
```
Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-insurance-fund-info

Details on mechanics: https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/insurance-fund-and-adl

## Market Data APIs

### Open Interest
System-wide open interest (not per-broker):
```
GET /v1/public/open_interests
```
Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-open-interests-for-all-symbols

### Kline (Candlestick) Data
```
GET /v1/kline
```
> **Limitation:** Returns a maximum of 1000 rows. Does not support filtering by specific date ranges. Only the most recent 1000 rows are available.

### Futures Market Info
```
GET /v1/public/futures_market?broker_id={your_broker_id}
```

### CoinMarketCap Integration Endpoints
```
# Contracts
GET /md/cmc/contracts?broker_id={your_broker_id}

# Orderbook Futures
GET /md/cmc/orderbook_futures/

# Futures Market (includes status)
GET /v1/public/futures_market?broker_id={your_broker_id}
```

> **Note:** The `orderbook_futures` endpoint may return 404 if the trailing slash is omitted or if `broker_id` is missing.

### Available Symbols & Token Icons

Get available symbols from:
```
GET /v1/public/available_symbols
```

Token logos are hosted at:
```
https://oss.orderly.network/static/symbol_logo/${name}.png
```
Derive the logo name by removing prefix (`PERP_`) and suffix (`_USDC`) from the symbol.

### Announcements

Monitor announcements via:
```
GET /v1/public/announcement
```

## Permissionless Vaults

### Creating a Vault

Vault creation is done via an **on-chain transaction**, not a REST API:
```
https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/permissionless-vault#creating-a-vault
```
Once the transaction is picked up by the indexer, the vault becomes available automatically.

**Testnet:** `https://staging-app.orderly.network/vaults/create`

### OmniVault Mechanics

- Withdrawal requests are processed in **batches every 3 hours**.
- **48-hour cooldown** period before withdrawals are available after depositing.
- No IOU or receipt token is currently issued upon deposit.

## Chain Integration Requirements

### LayerZero v2

Orderly requires **LayerZero (LZ) v2** support for new chain integrations. All Vault and settlement infrastructure runs on LayerZero v2. Using a different messaging layer (e.g., CCIP) would require rewriting contracts and conducting new security audits.

### Requirements for New Chains

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|----------|
| RPC URLs | For both testnet and mainnet |
| Native tokens | ~100 for mainnet, 500+ for testnet (for gas) |
| USDC support | Native or wrapped USDC contract addresses |
| LayerZero config | Endpoint, sendLib, receiveLib, DVNs |

**LayerZero metadata:** `https://metadata.layerzero-api.com/v1/metadata/deployments`

### Chain-Wide Integration

Orderly integration is **chain-wide by design**. Once a chain is integrated, any broker can use it. A `broker_id` is created per broker, but underlying chain support is available to all brokers.

## Multi-Collateral Support

Supported collateral assets by chain:

| Chain | Assets |
|-------|--------|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT, USDC |

Additional chains and tokens are being added over time.

## DefiLlama Integration

### Listing on DefiLlama Yields

1. Open a PR to the DefiLlama yield-server repository.
2. Each pool must specify a single chain (no multi-chain pools).
3. If on-chain TVL resides on Orderly L2, use a supported deposit network (Arbitrum, Base, etc.).
4. APY data can be fetched from an off-chain API.

### TVL Discrepancies

DefiLlama may show lower TVL if not tracking all vault sources (e.g., Ceffu-held funds). Resolving this may require providing Ceffu API access.

chunks.title: Broker Administration and Fee Management
chunks.content:
Every Orderly-based DEX (broker) requires an admin wallet to manage fees, referral codes, and access broker-specific APIs. This guide covers the full broker administration lifecycle.

## Registering a Broker Admin Wallet

After receiving your `broker_id` from the Orderly team, register an admin wallet:

1. **Provide Broker Details:** Share your desired Broker ID (lowercase, no spaces), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, and Default Maker Fee with the Orderly team.
2. **Use the Broker Registration Tool:** [https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/](https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/)
3. Register on **both testnet and mainnet** (you can use different wallets for each).
4. Many brokers use a **multisig** (e.g., Safe) on mainnet via the Delegate Signer feature.
5. Share the registered address with the Orderly team to complete setup.

> **Important:** The admin wallet collects broker fees and has exclusive access to referral code management and fee rebate APIs. Only one admin wallet per broker is currently supported.

## Generating Admin API Credentials

Log in to the admin portal at [https://admin.orderly.network/login](https://admin.orderly.network/login) using your admin wallet. Click **"Create Orderly Key"** to generate API credentials (public key and secret). These keys are tied to your admin account.

Alternatively, generate keys from your DEX UI: **Portfolio → API Key**.

## Fee Structure

Orderly uses a revenue-sharing model:

| Component | Rate |
|-----------|------|
| Orderly Base Taker Fee | 3 bps (0.03%) |
| Orderly Base Maker Fee | 0 bps (0%) |
| Broker Custom Fee | Set by broker (on top of base) |

**Example:** If your broker sets a 6 bps taker fee, you earn 6 - 3 = **3 bps per trade**.

### Setting Default Broker Fees

Use the admin portal or the API:

```http
POST /v1/broker/fee_rate/default
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

{
  "taker_fee_rate": 6,
  "maker_fee_rate": 2
}
```

> Fee rates are in **basis points** (e.g., 3 = 0.03%).

### Custom Per-User Fee Tiers
