- **On-chain failure**: Transaction submitted to blockchain but reverted, ran out of gas, or stuck pending. Inspect in the relevant block explorer using the transaction hash.
- **API failure**: Occurs before or instead of an on-chain transaction. Indicated by an API error code or error message.

### Step 2: Collect Context

Before troubleshooting or escalating, collect:
- User's wallet address
- Builder ID (`broker_id`)
- Chain
- Market symbol
- Timestamp of the failure
- Transaction hash or order ID
- API error message received
- Failing request payload
- Block explorer or API response evidence

### Step 3: Check Prerequisites

- **Wallet/account setup issues**: Verify the user followed the account registration and Orderly Key binding flows correctly
- **Trading request failures**: Confirm the correct payload was submitted and cross-reference the error code
- **Chain-specific issues**: Confirm the user is interacting with a supported deployment, then inspect the transaction in the block explorer for revert reasons, gas issues, or confirmation delays

### Step 4: Diagnose Stuck Withdrawals

1. **Check the [Orderly Support Dune Dashboard](https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-support-dashboard)** — verify whether the withdrawal went through to any chain (users sometimes request withdrawals to the wrong chain)
2. **Check the [LayerZero Explorer](https://layerzeroscan.com/)** — select "Source: Orderly" and look for cross-chain messages. If a message is in-flight and was created more than 10 minutes ago, the delay is caused by LayerZero cross-chain messaging
3. **Escalate to Orderly support** with the user's address, withdrawal amount, and approximate time

## System Maintenance

Use the system maintenance status endpoint to detect maintenance periods. During maintenance:
- Market data and user positions will be unavailable
- Open positions remain open and can still be liquidated if market conditions change after trading resumes
- Your UI should clearly communicate maintenance status and which actions remain available

Request builder Telegram channel access from the Orderly team for maintenance notifications.

## Pre-Launch Testing Checklist

Before going live, validate the full integration on testnet:

1. ✅ Registration flow
2. ✅ Authentication (Orderly Key binding)
3. ✅ Deposits
4. ✅ Withdrawals
5. ✅ Trading (create, edit, cancel orders)
6. ✅ PnL Settlement
7. ✅ System maintenance status endpoint handling
8. ✅ UI maintenance window display
9. ✅ Support ownership and incident communication plan
10. ✅ Launch coordination with Orderly

## Timestamp Validation

The `orderly-timestamp` header must not differ from the API server time by more than **300 seconds (5 minutes)**. Ensure your system clock is synchronized via NTP.

## Base URLs

| Environment | REST API | WebSocket (Public) | WebSocket (Private) |
|-------------|----------|-------------------|---------------------|
| Mainnet | `https://api.orderly.org` | `wss://ws-evm.orderly.org/ws/stream/{account_id}` | `wss://ws-private-evm.orderly.org/v2/ws/private/stream/{account_id}` |
| Testnet | `https://testnet-api.orderly.org` | `wss://testnet-ws-evm.orderly.org/ws/stream/{account_id}` | `wss://testnet-ws-private-evm.orderly.org/v2/ws/private/stream/{account_id}` |

chunks.title: Broker Registration, Fee Configuration, and Revenue Management
chunks.content:
This guide covers how to register a broker ID, configure trading fees, manage fee tiers, and withdraw broker revenue on Orderly Network.

## Registering a Broker ID

To register a broker ID, provide the following information to the Orderly team:

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| **Broker ID** | Unique lowercase string identifier | `mydex` |
| **Broker Name** | Display name | `My DEX` |
| **Default Taker Fee** | Base taker fee in bps | `6` (0.06%) |
| **Default Maker Fee** | Base maker fee in bps | `3` (0.03%) |
| **Broker Tier** | Initial tier level | `public` |
| **Admin Wallet** | EVM wallet for fee management | `0x1234...` |

After registration, the Orderly team configures your broker in the system. You then set up your admin wallet to self-manage fee adjustments via the admin portal at `https://admin.orderly.network/login`.

## Fee Structure and Revenue

### Base Fees
- **Crypto Markets**: 0 bps maker / 3 bps taker (Public tier default)
- **RWA Markets**: 0 bps maker / 1–3 bps taker (aligned with crypto fees as of July 2026)

### Broker Revenue Model
Brokers set fees on top of Orderly's base fee. **100% of the markup goes to the broker.**

```
Broker Revenue = (Broker Fee - Orderly Base Fee) × Trade Volume
```

**Example:** If you set a 6 bps taker fee and Orderly's base is 2.5 bps:
- You earn 3.5 bps on every taker trade
- Maker fee rebates range from -0.20 bps to 0 (you can earn rebates or pass them to users)

### Custom Trading Fee Per Order (April 2026+)
As of the April 28, 2026 upgrade, Orderly supports **custom trading fees per order**, allowing granular fee configuration beyond broker-level defaults. Contact the Orderly team for implementation details.

## Builder Tier System

Tiers are determined by **30-day average trading volume** OR **ORDER tokens staked**:

| Tier | Volume Requirement | ORDER Staked | Base Taker Fee |
|------|-------------------|--------------|----------------|
| **Public** | Default | — | 3 bps |
| **Silver** | ≥$50M | 100K ORDER | 2.75 bps |
| **Gold** | ≥$200M | 300K ORDER | 2.5 bps |
| **Platinum** | ≥$750M 30d | 3M ORDER | 2 bps |
| **Diamond** | ≥$2B 30d | 7M ORDER | 1 bps |

> **Note:** Current volume thresholds: Platinum ≥$750M, Diamond ≥$2B.

### Upgrading Tiers
Staking the required ORDER tokens does **not** automatically upgrade your tier. Contact the Orderly team with your admin wallet address and staking transaction to have your tier enacted manually.

### Negative Maker Fee Rebates
Maker fees can range from **-0.20 bps to 0**, meaning DEXs can effectively pay users to trade as makers. Builders can:
- Keep the rebate as broker revenue
- Pass it to users as trading incentives to boost volume

## Volume-Based Fee Tiers for Users

By default, all users have the same fees. To implement volume-based tiers:

1. Use the broker fee admin script: [orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin](https://github.com/wuzhong-orderly/orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin)
2. Update tier values in your configuration script based on your desired fee structure
3. For a flat fee, simply set the default rate

## Withdrawing Broker Revenue

Trading fees are credited to your broker account **daily**.

### Steps to Withdraw:
1. Log in to your DEX trading interface using the **admin wallet**
2. Accumulated fees appear as trading balance
3. Initiate a withdrawal to your preferred chain

> **Note:** Withdrawals incur gas fees (~$1 on most chains, ~$10 on Ethereum). LayerZero bridging fees may apply for cross-chain withdrawals.

### Changing the Admin Wallet
- **Trading fees**: Can be changed directly in the admin console
- **Admin wallet address**: Requires contacting the Orderly team for assistance
- Only **one admin wallet** is supported per broker per environment

## Affiliate and Referral Configuration

### Setting Up Referrals in Orderly One
Configure the referral section in your dashboard:
- **Referral Type**: Single-level or Multi-level
- **Max Rebate (%)**: Maximum rebate percentage
- **Required Trading Volume**: Set to `0` for immediate referral code generation

Users can customize their referral code name and split rebate percentages between themselves and referees.

### Custom Affiliate Fees
Brokers can assign lower fee rates to specific affiliate wallets. Referees signing up through those codes inherit the lower rates. Affiliates can adjust the rebate proportion shared with referees (0% up to their max rebate %).

## Monitoring and Analytics

- **Dune Dashboard**: Filter by broker ID at `https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-dashboard`
- **Orderly Dashboard**: `https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/`
- **Leaderboard**: Built-in at your DEX URL path `/leaderboard`
- **Affiliate Statistics**: Collected daily; rebates derived from trading fees minus Orderly's base fee

chunks.title: Supported Markets, Listings, and Delistings
chunks.content:
This guide covers the markets supported on Orderly Network, how new tokens are listed (including permissionless listings), and the delisting process.

## Supported Markets

Orderly Network is a **perpetual futures DEX** (spot trading is not supported). It supports a wide variety of trading symbols across multiple categories.

### Crypto Perpetuals
Major assets like BTC, ETH, SOL with up to **100x leverage**. The full list is available at:
- Demo site: `demo.orderly.network`
- Documentation: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/supported-markets`

### RWA (Real-World Asset) Markets
Orderly supports 24/7 trading on traditional assets with up to **20x leverage**:

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Stock Indices** | $SPX500, $NAS100 |
| **Individual Stocks** | $NVDA, $TSLA, $GOOGL, $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT, $META, $SAMSUNG |
| **Precious Metals** | Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG) |
| **Commodities** | WTI Crude Oil ($CL), Brent Crude Oil ($BZ) |
| **Forex Pairs** | $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD |

> **RWA Funding Fee Schedule:** Settlements for RWA markets like XAU occur every **4 hours** (vs. 8 hours for crypto pairs).

### Multi-Collateral Support
Orderly supports multi-collateral margin across chains:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| **Ethereum** | USDC, USDT, ETH, WBTC |
| **BNB Chain** | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| **Base** | USDC, ETH |
| **Arbitrum** | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| **Solana** | SOL, USDC, USDT |

> **Important:** USDC remains the base currency on all pairs. Using USDT or ETH as collateral does **not** change the trading pair symbol (e.g., it stays `PERP_BTC_USDC`, not `PERP_BTC_USDT`).

### Supported Chains
Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, BNB Chain, Solana, Avalanche, SEI, Sonic, Monad, Berachain, Plume Network, Abstract, Story Protocol, and Mode. New chains are added regularly.

## Standard Token Listing Requirements

To list a new perpetual trading pair on Orderly:

1. **Price Index**: At least 3 oracle sources (Tier 1 & 2 CEXs and on-chain oracles)
2. **Market Cap/FDV**: Minimum $20 million
3. **Market Maker**: Integrated with Orderly (project can bring their own or use Orderly's MMs)
4. **Liquidity Requirements**:
   - Minimum $20K USD in -2% depth
   - Minimum $20K USD in +2% depth
   - Minimum 15 levels in both -2% and +2% depth
   - Spread ≤ 50 bps
   - Uptime ≥ 90%

Listings are typically processed within hours. Submit proposals via the listing form or contact the Orderly team.

### Auto-Propagation to Brokers
When a new pair is listed by Orderly, it **automatically appears on all DEXs** built on Orderly infrastructure. No action is required on the broker's side.

## Permissionless Listings

Builders can list any asset (crypto or RWA) without Orderly team approval.

### How to Create a Permissionless Listing
1. Access the admin panel: `https://admin.orderly.network/permissionless-listing`
2. Select your oracle and market maker
3. Deposit **$50K** into the Insurance Fund (generates yield while listed, returned upon delisting)

### Revenue for Market Owners
- **100%** of liquidation fees
- **50%** of Orderly's base fee on that market

### Permissionless Market Parameters
- **Leverage**: Only 5x, 10x, and 20x supported (1x is not available)
- **Oracle Update Frequency**: At least 1 update/second, hard cap of 10/second
- **Timeout Policy**: Warning after 10 minutes of no price push; auto-deactivated after 1 hour

### Common Error: `Access denied: feature not enabled` (code -1002)
This indicates the market hasn't been fully activated on the backend. Contact Orderly support to enable trading.

## Delisting Process

### Reasons for Delisting
- Sustained low trading volume
- Token rebranding/migration
- Community vote outcomes
- Market disruption

### Community Vote to Retain
When tokens are under review for delisting:
1. A **5-day voting period** is opened
2. To retain a token, **>3%** (or >5% for some proposals) of staked $ORDER must vote **AGAINST** delisting
3. Tokens without sufficient votes are delisted

### Settlement on Delisting
- The **mark/index price is fixed** at the average price of the **last hour** before delisting time
- Open positions are settled at this fixed price
- If an oracle update causes margin ratio to fall below maintenance margin during delisting, liquidation triggers immediately
- Brokers should inform users in advance to close or manage positions

## Minimum Trade Size
The minimum trade size is **$10 total position size** (not collateral). A trader can open a leveraged position with less than $10 in collateral as long as the total leveraged position meets or exceeds $10.

chunks.title: Leverage, Margin, Liquidation, and Risk Management
chunks.content:
This guide explains how leverage, margin modes, liquidation, and risk management work on Orderly Network perpetual futures.

## Margin Modes Overview

Orderly supports both Cross Margin and Isolated Margin modes. Both modes can operate simultaneously on the same account — traders specify the margin mode per order and can even hold a Cross long and an Isolated short on the same symbol at the same time.

| Feature | Cross Margin | Isolated Margin |
|---------|-------------|----------------|
| Collateral | Entire account balance | Fixed allocation per position |
| Max Loss | Entire account balance | Capped at allocated margin |
| Collateral Assets | USDC, USDT, ETH, BNB, SOL (chain-dependent) | **USDC only** |
| Simultaneous Positions | Shared margin pool | Independent per position |
| Permissionless Markets | Not supported | Supported |

> **Note**: As of late 2024, Orderly primarily supports cross-margin. Isolated margin features are being rolled out.

### Cross-Margin
- All positions share the same account collateral
- Unrealized PnL from one position offsets margin requirements of others
- Leverage is calculated at the **account level**, not per position:

```
Leverage = Total Position Size / Total Collateral
Account Margin Ratio = 1 / Leverage
```

**Example:** $1,000 balance → open $5,000 position (5x) → open additional $3,000 position → total $8,000 position (8x leverage).

With cross-margin, as a position becomes profitable, the **displayed leverage decreases** because unrealized PnL is added to margin:

```
Example:
- Start: $100 margin, $400 position → 4x leverage
- Price doubles: margin = $500 ($100 + $400 PnL), position = $800
- Displayed leverage: 800/500 = 1.6x
```

### Isolated Margin Behavior
- Settlement (type=7) continuously marks unrealized PnL to margin
- `margin_qty` erodes over time through settlement deductions
- Equity formula: `equity = margin_qty + (holding × current_mark_price − cost_position)`
- When an Isolated position is liquidated, **only the margin assigned to that position is lost**. All other positions and remaining balance are untouched.

**Why Full Margin Can Be Consumed:** With 50x leverage, initial margin = 2% of notional, MMR = 0.6%, so only 1.4% adverse movement can be absorbed. Remaining ~0.6% is consumed by liquidation fees. Users must manually add margin to isolated positions before reaching the liquidation threshold.

### Adding/Reducing Margin on Isolated Positions

Use the `POST /v1/position_margin` endpoint:

**Add Margin (lowers liquidation price):**
```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "amount": "100",
  "type": "ADD"
}
```

**Reduce Margin (frees up balance):**
```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "amount": "50",
  "type": "REDUCE"
}
```

- **ADD**: Transfers from available balance → isolated position
- **REDUCE**: Transfers from isolated position → available balance

## Leverage

Leverage is set **per symbol, per margin mode** independently:

```
Example:
- BTC-PERP Cross Margin: 10x
- BTC-PERP Isolated Margin: 20x
- ETH-PERP Isolated Margin: 5x
```

Higher leverage in Isolated mode means less margin allocated and a tighter liquidation price.

### Maximum Leverage by Asset
| Asset Category | Max Leverage |
|---------------|-------------|
| **Major Crypto** (BTC, ETH, SOL) | Up to 100x |
| **RWA Markets** (Stocks, Gold, Silver) | Up to 20x |
| **Permissionless Markets** | 5x, 10x, or 20x only |

> **Note:** Brokers **cannot** customize maximum leverage for trading pairs. Leverage rates are set by Orderly's backend risk control parameters. Orderly does NOT support leverage above 100x. High leverage (500x-1000x) is deliberately excluded for risk management.

### Setting Leverage
- **Update**: Use the private `Update Leverage Setting` endpoint
- **Query**: Use the public `Get Leverage Configuration` endpoint

### Effective Maximum Leverage
The actual maximum leverage available depends on existing open positions and available margin. If other positions consume margin, you may not be able to open a full maximum leverage position.

### Position-Size-Dependent Margin (IMR Factor)

For large positions, margin requirements scale with notional size:

```
Effective_MMR = Base_MMR × IMR_Factor × |Position_Notional|^(4/5)
```

#### Small Notional Limit
```
Small_Notional_Limit = (Base_IMR / IMR_Factor)^(5/4)
```

- Below this threshold: Maximum leverage applies (no penalty)
- Above this threshold: Margin requirements increase, reducing effective leverage

**UI Guidance**: Frontends should display position-size-dependent leverage limits rather than a single maximum leverage figure.

## Liquidation Mechanics

### When Liquidation Triggers
Liquidation occurs when the **Margin Ratio (MR)** falls below the **Minimum Maintenance Margin Ratio (MMR)**:

```
Margin Ratio = (total_balance + unrealized_PnL) / holding_notional
Liquidation triggers when: MR < MMR
```

> **Important:** Liquidation always occurs **before** the bankruptcy price because the maintenance margin is greater than zero.

### MMR Examples
| Asset | Base MMR |
|-------|----------|
| BTC-PERP | 0.6% (0.006) |
| ETH-PERP | Varies by tier |

### Liquidation Price Formula

```
Position Liq. Price = max(
  mark_price_i + (
    total_collateral_value - sum(abs(position_qty_i) * mark_price_i * MMRi)
  ) / (abs(position_qty_i) * MMRi - position_qty_i),
  0
)
```

Where:
- `mark_price_i` = mark price of the position
- `total_collateral_value` = total collateral in the account
- `position_qty_i` = position quantity (signed)
- `MMRi` = Maintenance Margin Rate for the symbol (e.g., 0.05 for 5%)
- `Total MM = positionQty * MMR`

#### Short Position Formula
```
P_liq = P_entry × (1 + 1/L) / (1 + MMR)
```

Where:
- `P_entry` = average entry price
- `L` = leverage
- `MMR` = maintenance margin ratio

#### Estimated Liquidation Price (with existing position)
```
Est. Liq. Price = max(
  mark_price + (total_collateral - new_total_MM - order_fee) / 
  (abs(position_qty + new_order_qty) * new_MMR - (position_qty + new_order_qty)),
  0
)
```

Where:
- `order_fee = new_order_qty × order_price × taker_fee_rate`
- `new_MMR = Max(Base_MMR, (Base_MMR / Base_IMR) × IMF × Abs(notional)^(4/5))`

### Why Displayed Liquidation Price May Differ
1. **Large positions**: The UI assumes static MMR, but IMR factor scales with notional
2. **Multiple positions**: Other positions' PnL affects overall account margin
3. **Collateral fluctuation**: Non-stablecoin collateral value changes with market price
4. **Liquidation fees**: The displayed price may not account for the liquidation fee, which can be significant
5. **Funding fees**: Accumulated funding fees can erode collateral and shift the liquidation price
6. **Cross-margin interactions**: Other losing positions in cross-margin mode consume shared collateral

### Liquidation Fees
Liquidation fees vary by asset. For BTC, the fee is approximately **0.6%** of the position notional value. If a position is only partially liquidated, the full liquidation fee is not charged.

Fees are split: 50% to liquidator, 50% to insurance fund.

Full details: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/liquidations`

### Liquidation Record Fields
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `abs_liquidator_fee` | Actual fee amount paid |
| `liquidator_fee` | Fee ratio (varies by symbol) |
| `position_qty` | Quantity of the liquidated position |
| `cost_position` | Position cost basis |
| `price_transfer` | `cost_position / position_qty` |

### Liquidation at Unexpected Prices
Liquidation is triggered by mark price (based on index price — weighted average of spot prices from multiple exchanges). If a spot price on one index source surges:
- Index and mark price inflate even if perp prices on other exchanges remain lower
- During low liquidity, MMs may stop quoting, causing mark price to converge toward raw index

## Mark Price and Index Price

- **Index Price**: Aggregated from external CEX sources (Binance, OKX, KuCoin, Gate, Bybit), weighted by volume
- **Mark Price**: Based on index price plus Orderly market conditions
- **Oracle System**: Orderly uses its own aggregator pulling from 3+ sources (CEX spot + on-chain oracles like Pyth/Stork)

**Note on Price Differences:** Orderly displays prices in **USDC** (settlement asset), while most exchanges display in USDT. Converting USDT prices to USDC (dividing by ~1.0006) typically aligns them with Orderly's prices.

## Stop-Loss vs. Liquidation Priority

Both Stop-Loss and liquidation are triggered by **Mark Price** changes (updated every ~1 second). NOT based on last traded price. When SL and liquidation prices are very close:

1. A single Mark Price drop can trigger both simultaneously
2. Whichever order is confirmed **first** by the risk engine executes
3. The other is canceled

**Best Practice:** Ensure sufficient distance between your SL price and the liquidation price, especially during volatile conditions.

### Stop-Loss is NOT Guaranteed
Stop-loss orders are **trigger orders**, not guaranteed executions. If the liquidation trigger price is reached before the stop-loss trigger price, the position will be liquidated and the SL order will not execute.

### Common SL Issues

#### SL Not Triggering Before Liquidation
If the SL trigger price is very close to the liquidation price:
1. Mark price may jump past the SL trigger between 1-second updates
2. Position gets liquidated before SL can execute
3. **Result**: SL order is cancelled, never triggered

#### SL Order Cancelled Instead of Filled
When triggered, SL generates a market order. It may be cancelled if:
- Insufficient liquidity at trigger time
- Slippage exceeds acceptable limits

**Reference price calculation**:
```
reference_price = max(
  mark_price × (1 - symbol_price_range),
  mark_price - (total_collateral / position_i),
  (bid1 + ask1) / 2 × (1 - slippage)
)
```

## TP/SL Order Limits

| Order Type | Limit Per Trading Pair |
|-----------|----------------------|
| `POSITIONAL_TP_SL` | 1 untriggered order per (user, symbol, close-side) combination |
| `TP_SL` (e.g., BRACKET_ORDER) | 10 untriggered orders per asset |

**Example:** If you hold positions in ETH and BTC, you can have up to 10 TP_SL orders on ETH + 10 on BTC (20 total), plus 1 POSITIONAL_TP_SL per pair. Users can have separate TP/SL on each open position.

### TP/SL and Margin Calculations
TP/SL and STOP_LIMIT orders are **excluded** from `maxQty` and `totalCollateral` calculations because they are reduce-only orders that don't require initial margin.

### Why TP/SL PnL May Differ from Input
When you input a PnL target, the frontend calculates the corresponding price, but prices have limited decimal precision and must be rounded. The displayed PnL is recalculated from the rounded price, which may differ slightly. Broker fees are also factored in.

## Multi-Collateral Support

Orderly supports native multi-collateral trading — no need to swap to USDC first. Different assets have different collateral weights (haircuts):

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH, wBTC |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDC, USDT |

**Note:** Isolated Margin positions require **USDC only**. Convert other assets to USDC before trading in Isolated mode.

**Collateral Weight Example**: SOL has an 80% collateral ratio — depositing $550 of SOL yields ~$440 in available margin.

### Discount Factors
Orderly applies a **discount factor** that reduces the collateral ratio as collateral quantity increases. Larger deposits of non-USDC collateral (USDT, ETH, etc.) receive progressively lower weightings.

### Maximum Withdrawal Calculation
The max withdrawal may differ from total portfolio value due to separate per-asset formulas:

**USDC:**
```
max_withdraw = max(0, min(USDC_balance, free_collateral - max(uPnL, 0)))
```

**Other Collateral (e.g., USDT):**
```
max_withdraw = min(collateral_qty, free_collateral / (index_price × (1 + buffer) × weight))
```
Where `buffer` is typically 0.002 for price volatility.

### Key Balance Fields
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Account Value** | USDC + non-USDC holdings + isolated margin + unsettled PnL |
| **Total Collateral Value** | Account value adjusted by collateral weight/discount |
| **Free Collateral** | `totalCollateral - totalInitialMarginWithOrders` |
| **Available Balance** | USDC holdings + unsettled PnL (withdrawable, not trading collateral) |

### Custom Margin Assets (e.g., USSD)

For brokers offering custom margin assets:
1. Broker manages a special Orderly account (not enabled for perps trading)
2. On liquidation, custom asset is converted to USDC at market price
3. Broker must ensure sufficient USDC and perform periodic rebalancing
4. Provide Orderly account ID to the Orderly team for configuration

## Funding Fees and PnL

The funding rate uses a fixed formula and is capped. It is charged based on market conditions — heavily skewed trading activity results in larger funding rates. Full formula: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/funding-rate#funding-rate`

### How Fees Affect Position
```
unsettled_pnl = position_qty × mark_price - cost_position - accrued_funding
```

- **Funding fees**: Adjust `cost_position`, margin unchanged, included in `unsettled_pnl` immediately
- **Trading fees**: Also part of `cost_position`
- Both affect total account balance before settlement

### Unrealized vs Realized PnL Discrepancy
- **Unrealized PnL**: Uses mark price (stable, index-based)
- **Realized PnL**: Uses actual market execution price (subject to slippage)
- Large market orders on thin-liquidity pairs can sweep through the order book, filling at progressively worse prices

### Negative PnL on Winning Trades
Positions closed above entry price can show negative PnL when total fees exceed the gross profit:

```
Realized PnL = (close_price - open_price) × quantity - total_fees
```

If price movement is less than the round-trip fee cost, net PnL will be negative. Ensure trading bots account for this when setting minimum profit targets.

## Market Order Risks

### Price Impact and Slippage
Large balance reductions when opening/closing with market orders are typically caused by **bid-ask spread and price impact**, not just fees.

**Example:** Opening and closing with market orders costs ~8 bps each way (16 bps total) plus spread/slippage.

**Mitigation:**
- Use **limit orders** (~4 bps each way, no spread)
- Traverse the order book to show users price impact vs. index price before execution

### Sudden Liquidity Gaps
Market orders may fill far from the mark price during brief liquidity gaps (e.g., when market makers are replacing orders). Use limit orders in smaller or less liquid markets.

## Speed Bump (Taker Delay)

- **150ms** taker delay to protect market makers
- Reduces adverse selection, encourages aggressive quoting
- **Cannot** be adjusted by brokers

chunks.title: Orderly Architecture: Matching, Settlement, and Gas Fees
chunks.content:
This guide explains Orderly Network's trading architecture, including order matching, on-chain settlement, gas fee structure, and trade verification.

## Order Matching Engine

Orders are matched in Orderly's **off-chain backend trading engine**, delivering performance comparable to centralized exchanges. All DEXs built on Orderly share the **same backend and liquidity pool**.

### Key Architecture Points
- **Order Book Model**: Orderly uses a traditional order book (not a liquidity pool like GMX)
- **Shared Liquidity**: All brokers share the same orderbook — no liquidity fragmentation
- **Market Makers**: 50+ professional MMs including Sellini, Wintermute, Kronos, and RiverSide Hedge
- **Liquidity Ranking**: Top 3 overall among perp DEXs, comparable to Hyperliquid on major pairs

### Trade Execution Flow
```
1. User places order (off-chain, no gas)
2. Order matched in Orderly's off-chain engine (instant)
3. Settlement recorded on Orderly Chain (OP Stack L2)
4. On-chain record appears ~10-20 seconds after execution
```

## On-Chain Settlement

Settlement results are recorded on **Orderly's own chain** (an OP Stack L2). The only delay is the time for settled trades to appear on-chain.

### Batch Transactions
Orderly uses **batch transactions**, packaging multiple trades into a single on-chain transaction. This is why the same transaction ID may appear associated with multiple symbols and sides (BUY/SELL).

### Viewing Trade Details
- **Human-readable dashboard**: `https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/`
- **Block explorer**: `https://explorer.orderly.network/`
- **Per-address view**: `https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{address}?broker_id={broker_id}`

## Gas Fee Structure

| Action | Gas Fee? |
|--------|----------|
| **Placing/editing orders** | ❌ No gas |
| **Order matching** | ❌ No gas |
| **Settlement** | ❌ No gas (Orderly L2) |
| **Deposits** | ✅ Yes (source chain gas) |
| **Withdrawals** | ✅ Yes (destination chain gas) |

Gas costs for deposits/withdrawals depend on the user's chosen chain (e.g., Solana, Ethereum, Arbitrum).

## Price Feeds and Oracle System

### Index Price
Derived from a **volume-weighted aggregation** of prices from major exchanges. Details: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/mark-price-index-price-and-last-price#index-price`

### Mark Price
Used for liquidation and TP/SL triggers. Updates every **1 second**.

### Last Trade Price
Reflects actual executed trades on the Orderly orderbook. This is what TradingView charts display.

### K-Line (Candlestick) Data
K-line data is composed of two sources:
1. **Actual transaction records**
2. **BBO mid-price** (Best Bid and Offer) during periods with no trades

> **Note:** During low-volume periods, candlestick prices may show levels derived from BBO mid-price that don't correspond to executable liquidity.

## Hidden Orders
Hidden orders do not appear in the public orderbook. They are only recorded on-chain after execution. There is **no performance difference** compared to normal orders.

## Order Routing and Aggregation

### Can a trade be split across orderbooks?
**No.** A trade cannot be partially filled on both Orderly and another DEX. An order is sent to one orderbook and executed entirely there.

**Recommended approach:** Build an aggregator that routes orders to whichever orderbook offers the best price.

## Account and Broker Architecture

### Account per Broker
Each broker creates a **separate account** even when using the same wallet address. Trades are executed on Orderly's off-chain engine, and volume is credited to both the chain of deposit and the connected broker.

### Sub-Accounts
- Funds transfer between main and sub-accounts via **internal transfer**
- Flow: Deposit → Main Account → Internal Transfer → Sub-Account → Trade
- To withdraw: Settle PnL → Transfer back to Main → Withdraw
- **Cannot withdraw directly from sub-accounts**
- There is a **limit** on sub-accounts per main account (cannot be increased for security)
- For scalable architectures (hundreds/thousands of users), create a **separate wallet per user**

### Orderly Keys
- No limit on the number of Orderly keys per account ID
- Keys can be created without trading privileges (useful for team members who only need admin access)

## Vault and Custody

### Non-Custodial Vaults
Orderly vaults are **non-custodial**. Funds are held in smart contracts, not by Orderly. Users retain control over their assets.

### Vault Usage Restrictions
Funds deposited into Orderly vaults can **only** be used within the Orderly ecosystem (perpetuals trading, vaults). They cannot be used for external features like prediction markets or unrelated swap integrations.

## AI Agent Trading (MCP Server)

Builders can launch their own **MCP (Model Context Protocol) server** so AI agents can trade directly on their DEX by adding their brokerID to the Orderly MCP.

## System Maintenance

During scheduled maintenance (~30 minutes):
- Users cannot place or cancel orders
- Algorithmic orders do not trigger
- Withdrawals are suspended

Maintenance is used to deploy updates like order enum changes, tick size adjustments, and new features. Builders should inform users in advance.

chunks.title: Permissionless Vaults, OmniVault, and Trading Competitions
chunks.content:
This guide covers Orderly's vault products and competition systems: Permissionless Vaults for custom strategy deployment, OmniVault for yield optimization, and configurable trading competitions.

## Permissionless Vaults

Permissionless Vaults allow **anyone** to deploy yield strategies on Orderly-powered DEXs in under 30 minutes — without coding — creating a closed-loop growth and monetization system. Launched April 2026 alongside Permissionless Listings.

### What You Can Do
- **List any asset** (crypto or RWA) via Permissionless Listing
- **Provide liquidity** as a market maker
- **Launch your own vault** and raise funds from the community
- **Earn performance fees** on managed strategies
- **Monetize trading strategies** without Orderly team approval

### Getting Started
1. Access the vault deployment interface: `http://app.orderly.network/vaults`
2. Configure vault parameters (e.g., performance fee percentage)
3. Deploy your strategy (~30 minutes from creation to live vault)
4. Raise funds from the community

### Documentation
`https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/permissionless-vault`

### How It Works with Permissionless Listing
1. List a new asset permissionlessly
2. Provide market-making liquidity for that asset
3. Launch a vault trading that asset
4. Attract community deposits
5. Earn performance fees

### Vault Architecture

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Strategy Provider (SP)** | Creates and manages the vault's trading strategy |
| **SP Sub-account** | Isolated trading account for vault operations |
| **Community Depositors** | Users who allocate funds to the vault |
| **Performance Fee** | Fee charged on profits above high-water mark |

### Reserved Margin
- Fixed at **50,000 USDC** for permissionless vaults
- Ensures sufficient collateral for strategy execution

### Performance Fee Settlement
- Auto-settles when SP exceeds the **high-water mark**
- Paid as **additional SP shares** (not cash)
- Aligns incentives between SP and depositors

### Builder Benefits

#### Volume Attribution
- Vault trading volume and fees can be attributed to a specific **broker ID**
- Counts toward your builder tier volume requirements
- Increases overall DEX trading activity

#### Revenue Streams
1. **Trading fees** from vault activity
2. **Increased volume** helping achieve higher builder tiers
3. **Community engagement** through vault participation

### Configuration for Builders
- Ensure the vault's trading activity is linked to your broker ID for proper volume tracking
- Vaults operate on top of Orderly's infrastructure with no additional smart contract deployment required
- Vault UI accessible through your DEX or the main Orderly app

## Tread.fi Market-Making Vault Partnership

Orderly partners with Tread.fi to offer specialized market-making vaults:

### How It Works
1. Users deposit **USDC** into Tread.fi vaults
2. Vaults run market-making strategies through the builder's DEX
3. Participants earn rewards from a prize pool based on vault trading volume and uptime consistency

### Builder Benefits
- Additional trading activity and fees on your DEX
- Access to Tread.fi's market-making infrastructure
- Support for future token listings and trading strategies

## OmniVault

OmniVault is Orderly's **yield-optimizing vault product** with professional strategy management.

### Key Features
| Feature | Details |
|---------|----------|
| **Strategy Providers** | Vovega (current), Kronos (previous) |
| **Strategy Type** | Fully-hedged framework minimizing net exposure and drawdowns |
| **Custodian** | Ceffu integration for Binance trading access and diversified smart contract risk |
| **TVL** | Over $22.5M |
| **Integrations** | Binance Web3 Wallet, Gate, DeBank |
| **Chain Support** | Multiple chains including SEI |

### Strategy Framework
- Focuses on **stable returns** with minimal drawdowns
- Uses sub-accounts for strategy management
- Ceffu custodian integration unlocks Binance trading opportunities
- Diversifies smart contract risk

### For Brokers
Brokers on **Orderly One** can toggle adding vaults to their DEX interface. Community vaults from strategy providers (Kronos, Vovega) are also available.

### Deposits and Withdrawals
- Users deposit/withdraw to Strategy Vaults via their Orderly DEX account
- Strategy-based vault withdrawals and sub-account aggregation are supported

## Liquidity and Funding Rate Management

### How Liquidity Works
Liquidity on Orderly is supported by:
1. **External market makers** (50+ professional MMs)
2. **OmniVault** protocol vault (supplements baseline liquidity within active MM strategies and risk controls)

> **Note:** OmniVault is not an unlimited shock absorber — it operates within defined strategy bounds.

### Funding Rate Imbalances
Funding rates are determined by the deviation of the Orderly market price from the Mark Price (sourced from other exchanges).

If funding rates become uncompetitive:
- The Orderly team can mobilize market makers to balance the market
- Brokers experiencing persistent funding rate discrepancies should escalate to the Orderly team

## Perps Competition System

Orderly supports season-based trading competitions with configurable parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `season_id` | Unique competition identifier |
| `start_at` / `trading_end_at` | Unix timestamps for trading period |
| `claim_start_at` / `claim_end_at` | Reward claim window |
| `base_prize_pool` | e.g., 24000 USDC |
| `alpha` / `beta` | Prize distribution coefficients |
| `variable_bps` | Variable basis points |
| `loser_buff_percentage` | Bonus for lower-ranked traders |
| `referral_bonus_percentage` | Referral incentive |
| `social_sharing_bonus_points` | Social engagement rewards |

These parameters are configured via the backend and can be updated before the competition starts.

### Partner Competitions
- Partner with **Fuul** for permissionless trading competitions
- Points programs available for all Orderly One DEXs (no coding required)

### Network-Wide Competitions
- Orderly One DEXs can participate in network competitions (e.g., 'I Love Perps')
- Enable campaigns in the Orderly One dashboard
- Users register at: `https://app.orderly.network/campaigns/perps-competition`
- Works regardless of public/private leaderboard setting

chunks.title: TradingView Integration and DEX Branding
chunks.content:
This guide covers how to integrate and customize TradingView charts in your Orderly-powered DEX, including licensing, branding, and CSS customization.

## TradingView License Requirements

### When You Need a License
If you host your DEX on a **custom domain**, you must apply for a **free TradingView license** by filling out their form to inform them you'll use their charts on your URL.

- You can deploy first and fill out the form later — charts will still work
- License approval may take time, so plan accordingly
- Apply through the normal TradingView application process (no special Orderly expedited process)

### TradingView Advanced Charts Requirements
TradingView requires agreements to be signed with **incorporated companies** for the Advanced Charts library. Operating as an individual is not accepted.

**Recommended solution:** Register a company. Orderly has acknowledged this as a known issue and is exploring potential solutions.

### Orderly One Integration
TradingView Advanced Charts are **already integrated** into Orderly DEXs. However, DEXs on custom domains still need their own per-domain license.

## Hiding Orderly Branding

### Why 'Orderly' Appears on Charts
The 'Orderly' text appears because the **price feed** displayed on the chart is provided by Orderly Network. This is separate from the TradingView license.

### Method 1: CSS Override (Self-Hosted)
Apply custom CSS to hide the exchange name and footer branding.

**Hide exchange name in chart legend:**
```css
/* In /public/tradingview/chart.css */
[data-name="legend-source-exchange"] {
  display: none !important;
}

/* Alternative selector */
[class*="titleWrapper-"][class*="exchangeTitle-"] {
  display: none !important;
}
```

**Hide 'Powered by Orderly' footer:**
```css
/* In app/styles/theme.css */
.oui-scaffold-footer-powered-by {
  display: none !important;
}
```

> **Important:** This CSS customization is **not supported** in the Orderly One no-code solution. You must fork the DEX template, apply CSS modifications, and self-host.

### Method 2: Config Override (Open-Source Template)
In the `config.tsx` file, use the `tradingViewConfig` object to hide the exchange name:

```tsx
const tradingViewConfig = {
  // Hide the exchange name displayed on the chart
  hideExchangeName: true,
  // ... other config
};
```

## Chart Data Sources

### What the Chart Displays
- **TradingView charts display the Last Trade Price** (actual executed trades on Orderly's orderbook)
- This is different from the Index Price or Mark Price used for liquidations

### K-Line Data Composition
Candlestick data combines:
1. Actual transaction records
2. BBO (Best Bid/Offer) mid-price during periods with no trades

During low-volume periods, chart prices may not correspond to executable liquidity.

## DEX Branding with Orderly One

### Image Requirements
| Asset | Dimensions | Usage |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **Primary Logo** | 600 × 120 px | Top of trading page |
| **Secondary Logo** | 120 × 120 px | Top of mobile app |
| **Favicon** | 96 × 96 px | Browser tab icon |

### Custom Domain Configuration
Configure custom domains in your DEX profile. For non-standard extensions (e.g., `.trading`), try using a subdomain format like `dex.yourdomain.trading`.

## PnL Card QR Codes

QR codes on PnL cards are **automatically generated** when a user shares a card. No configuration needed.

When scanned, the QR code directs to the trading URL with the **referral code** of the trader who shared the card automatically appended.

## Additional Orderly One Features

### Points Programs
Integrate with **Fuul** to design and manage custom points/rewards systems. Toggle directly within Orderly One.

### Swap Functionality
Add a Swap tab to let users trade spot assets cross-chain, creating an additional revenue stream. Enable via the Orderly One platform.

### Leaderboards
Built-in leaderboard accessible at your DEX URL path `/leaderboard`. Use the point campaigns feature to configure custom leaderboards based on trading volume or PnL.

chunks.title: Order Execution, Positions, and Trade Data Reference
chunks.content:
This guide covers order execution mechanics, position management, liquidation, trade data formats, and common trading scenarios on Orderly Network.

## Order Placement

### Key Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `order_quantity` | Amount in base asset (e.g., ETH for PERP_ETH_USDC) |
| `order_type` | LIMIT, MARKET, etc. |
| `side` | BUY or SELL |
| `reduce_only` | If true, order can only reduce/close an existing position |
| `slippage` | Expressed as a percentage where 1 = 1% maximum |

> **Common Error**: Using `order_amount` instead of `order_quantity` in Futures mode triggers error `-1005: Placing orders by this order amount is not supported in Futures mode`.

### Order Quantity Calculation

#### From USD Input
To allow users to enter a USD amount, convert to base token quantity:

```javascript
// General formula
const quantity = amountUSD / currentPrice;

// Example: User wants to buy $1000 worth of ETH at $3000
const amountUSD = 1000;
const price = 3000;
const quantity = amountUSD / price; // 0.3333 ETH
```

#### Executed Quantity Representation
In Orderly trade data:
- The **symbol** always remains in base/quote format (e.g., `PERP_ETH_USDC`) regardless of BUY or SELL
- `executed_quantity` always represents the **base asset** amount (e.g., ETH)
- Quote asset amount = `executed_price × executed_quantity`

### Reduce-Only Orders

When `reduce_only: true`:
- The order can only reduce an existing position, never open or increase one
- If placed in the opposite direction of a position, it closes (or partially closes) the position
- Users may inadvertently trigger closures if reduce-only is enabled without awareness

**Why reduce-only orders get cancelled:**
- If the position's tokens are locked by active Algo Orders (TP/SL), the system only fills tokens that are free/available
- Remaining tokens are cancelled because reserved tokens cannot be touched
- **Solution**: Ensure reduce-only order quantity does not exceed the unlocked portion of the position

### Stop Orders vs TPSL Orders

| Feature | Stop Order | TPSL Order |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Auto-cancel on position close | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Manual cancellation needed | Yes | No |
| Use case | Standalone triggers | Attached to positions |

> **Note**: You cannot cancel an individual child order (TP or SL) from a `Position_TP_SL` trigger. You must cancel the entire parent order and recreate it.

## Entry Price and Fill Data

### Getting the Average Execution Price
For filled orders, use the `average_executed_price` field:

```json
{
  "order_id": "123456",
  "status": "FILLED",
  "price": "3000.00",           // Limit price set by user (limit orders only)
  "average_executed_price": "2998.50",  // Actual average fill price
  "executed_quantity": "1.5",
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC"
}
```

- `price`: Only populated for limit orders (the user's limit price)
- `average_executed_price`: The actual average price at which the order was filled
- For positions, the **average open price** is used rather than a separate entry price

## Market Orders with Slippage Protection

### On-Chain Orders (IOC/FOK)
To execute a market order with slippage protection on-chain:

```javascript
// Buy with max 2% slippage
const currentPrice = 3000;
const maxSlippage = 0.02;
const limitPrice = currentPrice * (1 + maxSlippage); // 3060

// FOK: Fully execute at limit price or better, or cancel entirely
const order = {
  symbol: "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  side: "BUY",
  order_type: "FOK",
  order_quantity: "1.0",
  price: limitPrice.toString()
};

// IOC: Execute as much as possible immediately, cancel remainder
const orderIOC = {
  ...order,
  order_type: "IOC"
};
```

> **Note:** On-chain orders without a limit price will be rejected.

## Leverage

Leverage on Orderly is **account-level** (cross margin), not per-order:

- The configured max leverage is a cap preventing excessive position sizes
- Actual leverage is estimated based on total collateral, open positions, and pending orders
- Example: $100 USDC collateral with 20x max leverage → can place orders worth up to $2,000

### Hedge Mode

Hedge mode (simultaneous long and short on the same ticker) is **not currently supported** under the same margin mode. Workarounds:
1. Use sub-accounts to hold opposing positions
2. Use a combination of isolated margin + cross margin modes on the same symbol

## Margin and Collateral Calculations

### Why 'Margin Insufficient' After Opening Max Position
When opening a position at 100% max quantity and immediately trying to open a full opposite position:
- Available margin may decrease due to **negative unrealized PnL** from market movements between orders
- Even small price movements can reduce available collateral enough to fail the second order
- The backend may take a few seconds to update available quantities

This is expected behavior in **cross-margin mode**.

### Algo Orders and Margin
TP/SL and STOP_LIMIT orders are **excluded** from `maxQty` and `totalCollateral` calculations:
- They are reduce-only orders that don't require initial margin
- Total collateral only reflects current holdings
- Algo orders are explicitly filtered out before calculating `maxQty`

### Isolated Margin
Isolated margin support was introduced at the system level in the March 2026 upgrade. Margin adjustment history for isolated positions is not currently tracked.

## Liquidation Mechanics

### Partial vs Full Liquidation

**Partial Liquidation**: Occurs when margin ratio falls below threshold but is not critically low. Only a portion of the position is liquidated to restore required margin.

**Full Liquidation**: Occurs when:
- Margin ratio falls to a critically low level
- Account's total notional value falls below minimum threshold
- Margin ratio equals the target ratio

The outcome also depends on the liquidator, position notional value, and symbol.

### Impact Margin Notional

As of October 3, 2025, the impact margin notional is **1000** for all perpetual contracts.

### Liquidation Execution

- Liquidation orders are handled **off-chain** on Orderly
- There is **no on-chain transaction hash** associated with liquidations
- There is no way to immediately trigger a liquidation for testing
- There is no way to subscribe to liquidation events filtered by broker ID

For liquidation bot development, refer to: [liquidation-searcher](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/liquidation-searcher)

### Liquidation API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Get Positions Under Liquidation | Positions that can still be claimed by a liquidator |
| Get Liquidated Positions Info | Positions already claimed by a liquidator |

## Orders and Positions Relationship

Orders and positions are **separate entries** in the Orderly system:
- A single position can be constructed from many orders in both directions
- There is no built-in mechanism to tag positions with custom metadata (e.g., external order IDs)

## Execution Latency

Orderly's median latency is approximately **0.2 seconds**, matching or beating competitors. Makers may experience faster execution due to a 0.15s delay applied to taker orders.

## Deposit and Trading Flow

### Deposit Flow
Users must deposit funds into **Orderly vaults** to access the orderbook:
```
1. User initiates deposit (pays source chain gas)
2. Funds arrive in Orderly vault smart contract
3. Balance reflected in Orderly trading account
4. User can now trade (no gas for any trading operations)
```

### On-Chain Swap Balance Requirements
On-chain swaps require sufficient balance **deposited into the Orderly asset manager** (not just in the wallet):

```
Required deposited balance = quantity × limit_price
```

**Example:** To buy 2 USDT at limit price 1.0204, you need at least 2.0408 USDC deposited in your Orderly account. Ensure tokens are deposited before initiating the swap.

## Sub-Accounts

- Only the **main account** can make deposits and withdrawals
- Sub-accounts only support internal fund transfers between main and sub-account
- Funds deposited always go to the main account first
- Sub-accounts and main accounts share the same credentials
- Internal transfers appear in the **Withdrawal History** tab, not Transfer History

## Trade Monitoring

### Backend Monitoring Limitations
Orderly does **not** currently provide a way to confirm trades or detect closures/TP/SL triggers from a backend without the user's Orderly key.

**Workaround:** Have the frontend record trade data to your backend after execution.

### Viewing On-Chain Trade Records
- **Dashboard**: `https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/`
- **Explorer**: `https://explorer.orderly.network/`
- Trades are submitted on-chain approximately every **10–20 seconds** for bookkeeping

### Dune Analytics
Query deposit/withdrawal counts per broker:
- **Deposits**: Query ID `3368805` filtered by `broker_id`
- **Withdrawals**: Query ID `3404504` filtered by `broker_id`

## Orderly Merits (Points)

Points for the current epoch are **dynamic** and calculated based on relative trading activity:
- A user's points depend on how much other users are trading
- Points update live
- Users in lower tiers may see slower accrual
- No fixed volume threshold required to earn specific points

## Withdrawal Issues

### Common Causes of Delays
1. **Cross-chain messaging issues** (LayerZero DVN verification delays)
2. **Ledger bookkeeping service issues** (incorrect calculations stalling the pipeline)
3. **Gas fee configuration** problems on specific chains

### What to Do
- Funds remain **safe** in the vault during delays
- Try withdrawing via an **alternative chain** (e.g., Arbitrum instead of Ethereum)
- Monitor the Orderly announcement channel for status updates
- The Orderly team cannot manually force withdrawals (non-custodial design)

### Testnet Deposit Rate Limits
On **Arbitrum Sepolia testnet**, deposits may revert due to LayerZero rate limits. Use alternative testnets: OP Sepolia, Polygon Mumbai, or Base Sepolia.

chunks.title: Token Listing Requirements and Permissionless Markets
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports both standard (Orderly-managed) and permissionless token listings for perpetual futures markets.

## Standard Listing Requirements

To list a new perpetual market on Orderly, the following criteria must be met:

### Market Criteria
1. **Market Cap**: Minimum $20M FDV (ideally $30-35M)
2. **Price Index Availability**: At least 3 price feed sources from:
   - Tier 1 & 2 CEX spot listings (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Coinbase, etc.)
   - On-chain oracles (Pyth, Chainlink, Stork)
3. **Market Maker**: A market maker integrated with Orderly must provide liquidity

### Liquidity Requirements (Market Maker)
| Metric | Requirement |
|--------|-------------|
| Depth at -2% | ≥ $20,000 USD |
| Depth at +2% | ≥ $20,000 USD |
| Levels (legs) at ±2% | ≥ 15 levels each side |
| Spread | ≤ 50 bps |
| Uptime | ≥ 90% |

### Additional Requirements
- Project team must co-run a listing campaign (minimum $10K budget)
- Tokens already listed on Binance Futures generally qualify automatically

## Permissionless Listings

Builders can independently list any asset not currently on Orderly through the Permissionless Listing framework.

### Requirements
1. **Insurance Fund Deposit**: Minimum $25,000–$50,000 USDC (generates yield, returned upon delisting)
2. **Valid Price Oracle**: Connect a supported oracle feed
3. **Market Making**: Provide your own market maker for the asset

### Revenue for Market Owners
- **100%** of liquidation fees on the market
- **50%** of Orderly's base fee (vs. 100% to Orderly in permissioned markets)

### Fee Structure (Permissionless Markets)
```
Total Fee = Base Fee + Custom Fee

Example (4bps base + 2bps custom):
- 2bps → Orderly
- 2bps → Permissionless Market Creator
- 2bps → Builder (custom fee)
```

### Access
- Admin panel: `https://admin.orderly.network/permissionless-listing`
- Diamond-tier brokers can list pairs that appear on their platform by default
- Other brokers can manually enable permissionlessly listed pairs

## Token Delisting: Vote to Retain

When tokens are flagged for delisting (low volume, market disruption, rebranding):

1. A **Community Vote to Retain** is initiated (typically 5-day voting period)
2. To save a token: **>3% of staked $ORDER** must vote AGAINST delisting
3. Tokens without sufficient votes are delisted
4. **Settlement**: Index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting
5. Open positions are automatically closed at the settlement price

### Builder Action Items for Delistings
- Notify users in advance
- Adjust frontend configurations to remove the pair
- Monitor Snapshot governance: `https://snapshot.box/#/s:orderlygov.eth/`

## RWA (Real-World Assets) Markets

Orderly supports perpetual contracts for real-world assets:

| Category | Assets | Max Leverage |
|----------|--------|--------------|
| Stock Indices | $SPX500, $NAS100 | 20x |
| Precious Metals | Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG) | 20x |
| Individual Stocks | $NVDA, $GOOGL, $TSLA, $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT | 20x |
| Forex | $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD | 20x |
| Commodities | $CL (WTI), $BZ (Brent) | 20x |

### RWA Trading Notes
- Tradeable **24/7** including weekends
- During off-hours/weekends: ±1% price bands applied to mark price for manipulation protection
- Liquidity sourced from CME via market makers
- As of July 2026: RWA taker fees aligned with crypto (1–3 bps based on tier)

chunks.title: Trading Fees, Builder Tiers, and Revenue Management
chunks.content:
Understanding Orderly's fee structure is essential for builders to optimize revenue and offer competitive rates to traders.

## Fee Architecture

```
Total Trading Fee = Base Fee (Orderly) + Custom Fee (Builder Revenue)
```

- **Base Fee**: Goes to Orderly Network (varies by builder tier)
- **Custom Fee**: 100% retained by the builder
- **Maker Fees**: Can be negative (rebates) for Silver tier and above
- **Funding Fees**: Paid between long/short positions (not collected by Orderly or builder)
- **Liquidation Fees**: Split between liquidator and insurance fund

**Important:** Fees are collected in the **received (converted) token**, not the source token. For example, if a user swaps USDC → ETH, fees are charged in ETH. Fees are deducted post-trade and do not affect the order price.

## Builder Tier System

Tiers are determined by **30-day average trading volume** OR **$ORDER tokens staked**.

| Tier | 30-Day Volume | ORDER Staked | Base Taker Fee | Maker Fee |
|------|---------------|--------------|----------------|-----------|
| **Public** (default) | < $50M | — | 3 bps | 0 bps |
| **Silver** | ≥ $50M | ≥ 100K ORDER | 2.75 bps | -0.05 bps |
| **Gold** | ≥ $200M | ≥ 300K ORDER | 2.5 bps | -0.10 bps |
| **Platinum** | ≥ $750M | ≥3M ORDER | 2 bps | -0.15 bps |
| **Diamond** | ≥ $2B | ≥ 7M ORDER | 1 bps | -0.20 bps |

> **Note**: Current tier thresholds: Silver ≥$50M, Gold ≥$200M, Platinum ≥$750M, Diamond ≥$2B. Maker rebates: Silver -0.05, Gold -0.10, Platinum -0.15, Diamond -0.20 bps. RWA base fees aligned with crypto.

Higher tiers unlock benefits including marketing support, listing campaigns, and reduced base fees.

### Current Fee Rates (Crypto & RWA Permissionless)
- **Maker**: -0.20 bps (rebate)
- **Taker**: 1 bps

### Example Minimum Fee Configuration (Diamond Tier)

```
Crypto: Maker -0.002%, Taker 0.01%
RWA:    Maker -0.002%, Taker 0.03%
```

## Negative Maker Fees (Rebates)

- Applied to Silver tier and above (ranging from -0.20 bps to 0 bps)
- Settle **immediately** on each execution for traders
- Builder maker/taker revenue is batched and settled **once per day** at 00:00 UTC
- Builders can keep the rebate as revenue or pass it to users as volume incentives

## Custom Fees Per Order

As of the April 28, 2026 upgrade, Orderly supports **custom trading fees per order**, allowing granular fee configuration at the individual order level.

## Configuring Custom Fees

### Via Admin Portal
```bash
# Update default broker fees
# Navigate to: https://admin.orderly.network/fee_rate
# Note: UI may only support limited decimal places (e.g., 0.042% not 0.0425%)
```

### Via CLI (Backend)
```bash
python3 app/main.py update-broker-default-fee <maker_fee> <taker_fee>
# Example: python3 app/main.py update-broker-default-fee 0.0000 0.0003
```

**Important**: Fee updates propagate with a ~20–30 minute async delay for inactive users. Run `update-user-rate-base-volume` periodically to sync.

### Configuring Volume-Based Fee Tiers

Use the Python fee admin script to configure per-user fee tiers based on trading volume:

```bash
# Clone the fee admin tool
git clone https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin
```

Configure tiers in a YAML file:

```yaml
rate:
  fee_tier:
  - maker_fee: 0.03%
    taker_fee: 0.07%
    tier: '1'
    volume_max: 500000
    volume_min: 0
  - maker_fee: 0.02%
    taker_fee: 0.05%
    tier: '2'
    volume_max: 2000000
    volume_min: 500001
```

**Important:** This script updates **per-user** fee tiers — it does not change the default/static fee displayed on the UI. Run it periodically (e.g., via cron job). Default fees are changed separately in the admin console at `https://admin.orderly.network/`.

### Per-User Fee Overrides
Trading fees can also be adjusted for specific users from the DEX admin dashboard.

## Builder Staking Program

Brokers can stake $ORDER to reduce base fees without meeting volume thresholds.

### Setup
1. Designate a staking wallet (can be different from admin/builder wallet)
2. Provide the staking wallet address to the Orderly team
3. Tier is automatically upgraded based on staked amount

**Example**: Staking ~6.9M ORDER qualifies for Platinum tier.

> **Note**: ORDER staking does NOT support delegation. Router contracts staking on behalf of users will have rewards assigned to the router, not the end user.

## Revenue Collection and Withdrawal

### How Fees Are Distributed
- **Maker volume**: 100% of fees go to the broker
- **Taker volume**: Base fee goes to Orderly, remainder to broker
- Staking $ORDER reduces Orderly's share, increasing broker revenue

### Where Fees Are Deposited
- Trading fees accrue **daily** in the broker's Orderly trading account
- Fees are NOT automatically sent to an external wallet
- Access via the **admin wallet** used to create the DEX

### Viewing and Withdrawing Fees

**Method 1: DEX Frontend**
1. Log into your DEX with the admin wallet
2. Navigate to **Portfolio → Distribution**
3. View daily fee credits and withdraw

**Method 2: Broker Registration Portal**
```
https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/
```
Supports withdrawal to any supported chain.

**Method 3: Orderly Dashboard**
```
https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/
```
View broker-specific metrics by filtering with your broker ID.

### Multisig Wallets
- Multisig wallets **cannot** be used for direct trading
- Multisig **can** be configured as the broker admin/fee wallet
- Ensure you log in with the exact multisig address to access fees

## Referral System Revenue

Referral commissions are calculated on the **broker's portion** (net fee = gross fee minus Orderly's base fee):

```
Example:
- Total fee paid by user: 4 bps taker / 1 bps maker
- Orderly base fee: 1 bps / 0 bps
- Broker net fee: 3 bps / 1 bps
- With 50/50 referral split:
  - Broker: 1.5 / 0.5 bps
  - Referrer: 1.5 / 0.5 bps
  - Trader: no discount
```

The `order_tag` parameter overrides any existing referral code. Rebates are credited daily.

### Multi-Level Referral
- Orderly supports up to **15-layer** multi-level referral structures
- Configure at: `https://dex.orderly.network/en/referral`
- Set default commission rates and manually assign codes to specific traders

## Market Maker Fee Configuration

### Setting Up an MM Account
1. MM connects EVM address at: `https://dmm.orderly.network/perp/PERP_ETH_USDC`
2. Enable trading to generate Orderly UID
3. Provide EVM address to Orderly team for custom fee rates

### MM Reward Program (Epoch 49+)
- **700,000 ORDER** per epoch total allocation
- **200,000 ORDER** dedicated to Permissionless Listing Markets
- Eligibility: Maker market share > 5%, daily maker volume ratio > 75%

## Excalibur Club

Brokers earn a **0.5 bps rebate** on all trading volume from users exceeding **250M USDC** in trailing 30-day volume. Rewards are calculated and paid monthly.

## Vanguard Distributor Program

Brokers referring other DEX projects earn credit:
- Referred DEX's volume counts toward referring broker's tier
- Bindings are permanent, settled daily
- Entry: `https://dex.orderly.network/distributor/`

## Tracking Volume and Revenue

Use the Dune Analytics dashboard filtered by broker ID:
- Daily volume: `https://dune.com/queries/3369147/5652166`
- Daily active users: `https://dune.com/queries/3369187/5652252`
- Full dashboard: `https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-dashboard`

chunks.title: Real-World Assets (RWA) Trading on Orderly
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports perpetual futures contracts for Real-World Assets (RWAs), enabling 24/7 trading of traditional financial instruments through DeFi infrastructure.

## Supported RWA Markets

### Stock Indices
| Symbol | Asset | Max Leverage |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| PERP_SPX500_USDC | S&P 500 Index | 20x |
| PERP_NAS100_USDC | NASDAQ 100 Index | 20x |

### Precious Metals
| Symbol | Asset | Max Leverage |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| PERP_XAU_USDC | Gold | 20x |
| PERP_XAG_USDC | Silver | 20x |

> **Note (Jan 2026)**: Symbols updated for clarity — XAU (Gold), XAG (Silver). No impact on trading logic or settlement.

### Individual Stocks
| Symbol | Asset |
|--------|-------|
| PERP_NVDA_USDC | NVIDIA |
| PERP_GOOGL_USDC | Alphabet |
| PERP_TSLA_USDC | Tesla |
| PERP_AAPL_USDC | Apple |
| PERP_AMZN_USDC | Amazon |
| PERP_MSFT_USDC | Microsoft |
| PERP_SAMSUNG_USDC | Samsung |

Additional stocks available via the permissionless listing framework.

### Forex
| Symbol | Pair |
|--------|------|
| PERP_JPY_USD | JPY/USD |
| PERP_EUR_USD | EUR/USD |

### Commodities
| Symbol | Asset |
|--------|-------|
| PERP_CL_USDC | WTI Crude Oil |
| PERP_BZ_USDC | Brent Crude Oil |

## How RWA Trading Works

### Architecture
- RWA perpetuals use the **same mechanism** as crypto markets
- Collateral: **USDC** (no actual token or on-chain settlement for the underlying asset)
- Purely a perpetual contract tracking the reference price

### Price Feeds
Orderly uses multiple oracle sources with median calculation:
- **Finage**, **Tradermade**, **Pragma**, **Pyth**, **Stork**, **Chainlink**
- For some permissionless listings: Binance futures index + Pyth

### Liquidity
- Commodities (Gold, Silver): Liquidity sourced from **CME** via market makers
- Stocks: Market maker-provided quotes

## Weekend and Off-Hours Trading

RWA markets remain tradeable **24/7**, including when traditional markets are closed.

### Price Band Protection
During weekends and off-hours:
- **±1% price bands** applied to mark price
- Protects against manipulation during thin liquidity periods
- When traditional markets reopen: bands removed, liquidity normalizes

### What to Expect
- **Wider spreads** during weekends/off-hours due to thinner liquidity
- Static index prices when source markets are closed
- MM-provided quotes maintain basic market function

## RWA Fee Structure

### Updated July 2026
RWA fees are now **aligned with crypto fees**:

| Tier | Taker Fee | Maker Fee |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| Public | 3 bps | 0 bps |
| Platinum | 1–3 bps | Negative (rebate) |
| Diamond | 1 bps | -0.20 bps |

Previously, RWA taker fees were 1–3 bps due to higher market-making costs.

### Permissionless RWA Markets
- Fee structure: **Maker -0.20 bps / Taker 1 bps**
- Same revenue split as permissionless crypto markets

## Leverage Considerations for Stocks

- Stock perps generally support **10x–20x** leverage
- **Ultra-high leverage (50x+) is NOT available** for stock perps
- **Reason**: Price gaps of 2–3% during off-hours could cause significant liquidations
- Orderly prioritizes automatic leverage reduction features before expanding limits

## Builder Integration Notes

### Adding RWA Markets to Your DEX
1. RWA markets are available by default on Orderly-powered DEXs
2. Enable specific pairs in your Orderly One dashboard
3. Ensure your frontend displays RWA-specific disclaimers if required by your jurisdiction

### Geo-Fencing Limitations
- You **cannot** hide specific pairs based on user IP/location
- You **can** geo-fence the entire platform by region
- You **can** hide pairs globally for all users

### Oracle Configuration
For permissionless RWA listings:
- Offchain feed delivery is supported and preferred
- Typically requires 2–3 reliable price feeds
- Median Price logic filters outliers

## AI Trading Agent Integration (MCP)

Builders can launch their own **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** to allow AI agents to trade directly on their DEX:
1. Add your `brokerID` to the Orderly MCP
2. AI-powered trading strategies execute through your Orderly-powered DEX
3. Details available via Orderly announcements

chunks.title: TradingView Integration and DEX Customization
chunks.content:
This guide covers TradingView chart licensing, DEX domain configuration, and UI customization for Orderly-powered platforms.

## TradingView Advanced Charts License

### Requirements
TradingView charts are included by default in Orderly DEXs, but builders **must apply for a license** once their site is live.

### Application Process
1. **Prerequisites**:
   - Site must be publicly accessible
   - Working SSL certificate
   - Custom domain configured and propagated
   - Personal GitHub profile (enterprise accounts NOT accepted)
   - Corporate email address (Gmail/ProtonMail NOT accepted)

2. **Apply at**: `https://www.tradingview.com/advanced-charts/`
   - Registered company: Not required
   - Data feed: Indicate you have your own data feed
   - Create a GitHub profile if you don't have one

3. **Timeline**:
   - DNS propagation: Up to 24 hours
   - License approval: Typically a few days to a week
   - Secure your domain BEFORE applying to avoid back-and-forth

### Important Notes
- **One license per domain**: Each DEX on a separate domain needs its own license
- The TradingView attribution link is included in the DEX by default
- Without a valid license, TradingView may contact the builder
- License is **free** to use

## Custom Domain DNS Configuration

### Setup Steps
1. Add a **CNAME** DNS record for your subdomain
2. Point to the deployment target

**Example** (V2 DEX Creator):
```
Type: CNAME
Name: trade (or your subdomain)
Value: orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io
```

### Propagation Times
| Provider | Typical Time |
|----------|-------------|
| Cloudflare | ~5 minutes |
| cPanel | May take longer |
| Others | Up to 24 hours |

## PnL Poster Customization

### Configuration
In the DEX creator, navigate to PnL poster settings and upload custom backgrounds.

### Specifications
| Property | Requirement |
|----------|-------------|
| Aspect Ratio | 16:9 |
| Recommended Size | 960 × 540 px |
| Left Side | Dark colors (for text contrast) |

### Design Notes
- Trading data overlays the **left side** of the image
- Both profit and loss trades use the same poster unless separate configurations are added
- Ensure sufficient contrast for overlaid white/light text

## Markets Page Configuration

### Enabling via Orderly One
- Navigate to navigation menus configuration
- Enable the Markets page toggle

### Custom Market Pages
For features beyond the default Orderly One offering:
1. Fork the existing repository
2. Self-host your DEX
3. Add custom code for market page features

## Spot Swap Module

Orderly One DEXs include integrated spot swap functionality (powered by WOOFi).

### Enable Swap
1. Open Orderly One dashboard
2. Enable the swap page in configuration

### Example URL
```
https://dex.orderly.network/{your-dex}/swap
```

### Source Code
```tsx
// Available at:
// https://github.com/OrderlyNetworkDexCreator/{your-dex}/blob/main/app/pages/swap/Index.tsx
```

### Notes
- Swap is an on-chain transaction
- Trading fees viewable from the Orderly One graduation page

## Referral System Setup

### Multi-Level Referral
1. Navigate to: `https://dex.orderly.network/en/referral`
2. Login credentials available via button on the referral page
3. Set default commission rate (e.g., 10%)
4. Manually assign referral codes to specific traders

### Configuration Options
| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Commission Rate | Percentage of broker fee shared with referrer |
| Minimum Volume | Threshold before referral link generates (cannot be absolute 0) |
| Multi-Level | Up to 15 layers supported |

### Current Limitations (v1 Multi-Level)
- Affiliates cannot create multiple tracking links themselves
- Cannot rename/label links
- Cannot filter reporting by individual tracking link and date
- Only root (L1) affiliate codes can be created by builders

### Referral Fee vs Rebate
- **Referral Fee**: Portion given to the referrer
- **Rebate**: Portion given back to the referee as a discount

### Admin Dashboard
```
https://admin.orderly.network/referral
```
View volume, commissions, and earnings per client.

## DEX Board Listing

### Getting Listed
1. Fill out DEX information: `https://dex.orderly.network/dex/card`
2. Complete at least one test trade (non-zero volume)
3. Your DEX appears at: `https://dex.orderly.network/board`

### Volume Tracking
- DEX board: `https://dex.orderly.network/board`
- Updates approximately every hour
- Set up your board on Orderly One

## Geo-Fencing and Pair Visibility

### What You CAN Do
- Hide trading pairs **globally** for all users
- Geo-fence the **entire platform** by region (block/allow access)

### What You CANNOT Do
- Hide specific pairs based on user IP address
- Selectively remove individual pairs by geography

## Trading Competitions

### Network-Wide Competitions
1. Enable campaign in Orderly One dashboard
2. Campaign displays at top of your DEX
3. Users register at: `https://app.orderly.network/campaigns/perps-competition`
4. Works with public or private leaderboard settings

### Custom Competitions
- Partner with **Fuul** for permissionless competitions and points programs
- No coding required
- Multi-level referral system (CEX-style, up to 15 levels)

## Competition Winnings Distribution
- Sent to user's **Orderly trading account** (AccountID)
- NOT sent to external Web3 wallet
- Appears as internal deposit/transfer
- Users check trading account balance for credited amount

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings and Custom Markets
chunks.content:
Orderly's Permissionless Listing framework allows builders to list any perpetual market — crypto, RWA, Pre-TGE tokens, forex, commodities — without waiting for Orderly to add data sources.

## Overview

Permissionless Listings operate under an **isolated-risk model**:
- Listed markets are available in **Isolated Margin only** (no Cross Margin)
- Each builder gets **5 free listing slots**
- Market owners earn **100% of liquidation fees** plus **50% of Orderly's base fee** on that market
- No listing fee required

## Standard Listing Requirements

For standard (non-permissionless) listings, the following criteria must be met:

1. **Price Index**: At least 3+ price feed sources
2. **Market Maker**: An integrated MM must be engaged with Orderly
3. **Minimum FDV**: 20M+
4. **Liquidity Requirements**:
   - Minimum 20K USD in -2% depth
   - Minimum 20K USD in +2% depth
   - Minimum 15 levels in -2% and +2% depth
   - Spread ≤ 50 bps
   - Uptime ≥ 90%

## Custom Oracles

With Permissionless Listing, builders can push their own asset price data directly to Orderly:

- Custom oracle feeds can be **combined** with existing CEX and oracle price feeds
- Orderly covers the cost of price feeds (including Pyth and Stork) for permissionless listings
- Builders do not need to source or pay for their own price feeds

Documentation: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/custom-oracle#custom-oracle`

## Supported Asset Categories

Orderly supports a wide variety of markets beyond crypto:

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Crypto Perpetuals | BTC, ETH, SOL, and 100+ altcoins |
| RWA - Stock Indices | SPX500, NAS100 |
| RWA - Precious Metals | Gold (XAU), Silver (XAG) — up to 20x leverage |
| RWA - Individual Stocks | NVDA, TSLA, GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN, MSFT — up to 20x, 24/7 |
| RWA - Commodities | WTI Crude Oil, Brent Crude Oil |
| RWA - Forex | JPY/USD, EUR/USD |
| Pre-TGE Markets | Synthetic Pre-TGE Oracle with tightened risk caps |

## Listing Workflow

1. **Choose your asset** and ensure price data availability
2. **Configure your oracle** (custom or existing feeds)
3. **Engage a market maker** or deploy an MM bot
4. **List the market** via the Permissionless Listing interface
5. **Sync your frontend** configuration to display the new market

**Important:** New permissionless markets require frontend configuration sync to display correctly on your DEX.

## RWA Market Details

Orderly operates its own orderbook and liquidity infrastructure for RWA markets — it does not rely on third-party RWA providers. Prices are sourced through oracles, and market makers provide liquidity to keep markets aligned with reference prices.

### RWA Fee Structure (Updated July 2026)

RWA pair fees are now **equal to crypto pair fees**:
- RWA Taker Fee: reduced from 1–3 bps to **1–3 bps**
- RWA Maker Fee: 0 bps (rebates available)

## Community Vote to Retain

Tokens with sustained low metrics may face delisting via a community vote:

- A 5-day voting period is opened
- To retain a token, **>3% (or 5%) of staked $ORDER** must vote "AGAINST Delisting"
- Tokens without sufficient votes are delisted
- The index/mark price is **fixed at the average price of the last hour** before delisting

Brokers are encouraged to participate and inform their communities about tokens at risk.

## Viewing Supported Markets

- Full market list: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/supported-markets`
- Demo site with all symbols: `demo.orderly.network`

## Symbol Format

Orderly uses the format `PERP_<SYMBOL>_USDC` for all trading pairs:
```
PERP_ETH_USDC
PERP_BTC_USDC
PERP_NVDA_USDC
PERP_XAU_USDC
```

chunks.title: Broker Setup, Admin, and DEX Operations
chunks.content:
This guide covers the operational aspects of running an Orderly-powered DEX, from initial setup to ongoing management.

## Broker Registration

### Setting Up a Broker ID

Register at: `https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/` (supports EVM and Solana)

**Required Information:**
- Broker ID (e.g., 'mybroker')
- Broker Name
- Default Taker Fee
- Default Maker Fee
- Domain (needed for TradingView license)

**Base Fees:** Orderly charges 0.03% taker / 0% maker. Anything above the base taker fee is retained by the broker.

### Admin Wallet Setup

1. Register your wallet at the broker registration portal
2. Orderly team upgrades it to admin status
3. Connect to your DEX UI with the admin wallet
4. Accumulated fees appear and can be withdrawn

**Important:** Fees are only collected from registration time forward (not retroactively). Multisig wallets are supported on EVM.

### Using a Solana Wallet as Admin

The registration UI doesn't yet support Solana wallet selection directly. Workaround:
1. Clone the DEX creator template
2. Change broker ID in `.env`
3. Switch to Solana chain
4. Complete registration

Alternatively, use an EVM wallet as admin even for Solana-only trading.

### Depositing from a Multisig Wallet

1. Connect via WalletConnect
2. Select the proper chain
3. Select 'EOA wallet' as registration type (even for multisig)
4. Sign the approval transaction in the multisig interface
5. Initiate the deposit transaction (also routed to multisig)
