chunks.title: DNS Configuration and Custom Domain Hosting
chunks.content:
Hosting your Orderly-powered DEX on a custom domain requires proper DNS configuration. This guide covers common setups and troubleshooting.

## Subdomain Setup (Recommended)

If your main domain (e.g., `www.yourdomain.com`) is already assigned to another service via a CNAME record, you **cannot** assign a second CNAME with the same name. Use a subdomain instead.

### Step 1: Configure DNS

In your DNS provider (e.g., GoDaddy, Cloudflare), add a new CNAME record:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Type** | CNAME |
| **Name** | `app` (or your chosen subdomain) |
| **Value** | `orderlynetworkcreator.github.io` |
| **TTL** | 3600 (or automatic) |

This will make your DEX accessible at `app.yourdomain.com`.

### Step 2: Configure Orderly One

1. In the Orderly One dashboard, set the domain to your subdomain (e.g., `app.yourdomain.com`)
2. Redeploy the DEX

> **Note:** You do not need to purchase a new domain. A subdomain of your existing domain is sufficient.

## Main Domain Setup

If your main domain is **not** already in use:

1. Set a CNAME record for `www` pointing to `orderlynetworkcreator.github.io`
2. Configure the root domain (`@`) with an A record or ALIAS record as supported by your DNS provider
3. Set the domain in Orderly One to your main domain

## Security Considerations

### HTTPS Enforcement

Ensure that HTTPS connections are enforced on your DNS server. If users encounter errors on mobile when accessing your DEX subdomain, verify:
- SSL/TLS certificates are properly configured
- HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS
- Your DNS provider supports automatic SSL (e.g., Cloudflare Universal SSL)

### Developer Access

**Developers do NOT need access to your admin wallet private key** to configure DNS or domain settings. DNS configuration is handled independently of the DEX admin wallet.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| DEX not loading on custom domain | CNAME not propagated | Wait up to 48 hours for DNS propagation |
| SSL certificate error | HTTPS not configured | Enable SSL in your DNS provider or hosting |
| `www` domain conflicts | Existing CNAME on `www` | Use a subdomain (e.g., `app.` or `trade.`) |
| Mobile browser errors | Mixed content or missing HTTPS | Enforce HTTPS redirect at DNS/server level |

## Updating DEX Card Information

Builders who launched via Orderly One can update their DEX card information at:

```
https://dex.orderly.network/en/dex/card
```

The process takes approximately 3 minutes and can significantly improve the DEX's visibility on the Orderly ecosystem.

chunks.title: Broker Fee Collection and Revenue Management
chunks.content:
Understanding how broker fees accrue, where they are stored, and how to withdraw them is essential for DEX operators on Orderly Network.

## Fee Accrual Mechanism

Broker fees are **not** sent directly to your on-chain wallet balance. Instead:

1. Fees accrue to the **admin wallet's Orderly account balance** (on Orderly L2).
2. Fees are distributed **daily**, typically around **midnight UTC**.
3. Fees are paid in **USDC** on Orderly's network.
4. The balance is added to the **portfolio balance** of the admin wallet.

## Accessing and Withdrawing Fees

### Method 1: DEX Frontend
1. Log into your DEX frontend using the **admin wallet address**.
2. Navigate to your portfolio/balance section.
3. Fees will be visible within the Orderly account balance.
4. Withdraw to any supported chain.

### Method 2: Broker Registration Portal
Useful for multisig wallets or when the DEX frontend is unavailable:
```
https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/
```
Or the legacy portal:
```
https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/
```

### Method 3: API
Check accumulated fees using the private `Get Current Holding` endpoint:
```bash
curl -X GET https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/client/holding \
  -H "orderly-key: <ADMIN_PUBLIC_KEY>" \
  -H "orderly-signature: <SIGNATURE>" \
  -H "orderly-timestamp: <TIMESTAMP>" \
  -H "orderly-account-id: <ADMIN_ACCOUNT_ID>"
```

## Fee Revenue Breakdown

| Component | Rate | Recipient |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Base Taker Fee | 3 bps (0.03%) | Orderly Network |
| Broker Taker Markup | Configurable (e.g., 3 bps) | Broker |
| Maker Fee | 0% base (configurable) | Broker (if set > 0%) |

**Example:** If the broker sets a 6 bps taker fee:
- Orderly retains 3 bps.
- Broker earns 3 bps per taker transaction.

## Updating Fee Configuration

Fee rates can be adjusted after initial setup via the admin wallet:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/client/update_fee \
  -H "orderly-key: <ADMIN_PUBLIC_KEY>" \
  -H "orderly-signature: <SIGNATURE>" \
  -H "orderly-timestamp: <TIMESTAMP>" \
  -H "orderly-account-id: <ADMIN_ACCOUNT_ID>" \
  -d '{"maker_fee_rate": 0.0002, "taker_fee_rate": 0.0005}'
```

> **Note:** Fee changes may not be immediate and are often applied during periodic backend checks (next-day).

## Monitoring Revenue

- **Dune Dashboard:** Use the Dune dashboard builder section to monitor net fees.
- **Admin Dashboard:** The revamped beta dashboard at `https://dex-beta.orderly.network` provides detailed finances & fee management tools.

## Troubleshooting Fee Discrepancies

If there is a discrepancy between dashboard revenue figures and the actual USDC balance:
1. Verify you are connected with the correct admin wallet.
2. Check that fees have been distributed (daily at ~midnight UTC).
3. Contact Orderly support with your wallet address for investigation.

## Changing the Fee Collection Wallet

The fee collection wallet and admin wallet **must be the same address**. To change it:
1. Register a new wallet as described in the Admin Wallet Configuration guide.
2. Contact the Orderly team to update the configuration.
3. Note: Changing the fee wallet detaches the Orderly One account from the original admin wallet.

chunks.title: Wallet Connection Troubleshooting
chunks.content:
This guide addresses common wallet connection issues encountered by users and developers on Orderly-powered DEXes.

## Spinning/Loading Circle on Wallet Connect

**Symptom:** The DEX frontend shows a spinning/loading circle indefinitely when trying to connect a wallet.

**Cause:** The app is trying to fetch the on-chain balance through the wallet's RPC and the call is not completing.

**Solutions:**
1. **Switch wallets:** Try a different wallet (e.g., MetaMask) to determine if the issue is wallet-specific.
2. **Check VPN status:** Certain regions (e.g., Indonesia) may have connectivity issues that prevent RPC calls from completing. Disable the VPN or switch regions.
3. **Verify SSL certificate:** Ensure the SSL certificate for your custom domain has been properly created and propagated.

## Mainnet Switch Button Not Clickable

**Symptom:** The mainnet switch button in the broker template is unresponsive.

**Causes and Solutions:**
1. **Network mismatch:** The connected wallet network does not match the web application's expected network. Ensure the wallet is connected to the correct chain.
2. **Broker ID casing:** Ensure the Broker ID in the `.env` file uses **lowercase letters only** (e.g., `bgsc` not `Bgsc`).

## Phantom Wallet Red Warning / Blocked Transactions

**Symptom:** Phantom wallet shows a red warning or blocks deposit transactions.

**Cause:** The DEX frontend uses a non-standard wallet connector (e.g., Reown/WalletConnect + Proxy provider) instead of the standard WalletConnector or Privy's Solana adapter. This alters the provider configuration, preventing Phantom from parsing and simulating the transaction.

**Solutions:**
1. Switch to the **default Orderly connector** or **Privy connector**.
2. Ensure the domain is reviewed and trusted by Phantom/Blowfish.

## WalletConnect for Mobile EVM Wallets

**Symptom:** Mobile users on iOS Safari cannot connect EVM wallets.

**Cause:** Safari on iOS does not support built-in EVM wallet injection.

**Solution:**
1. Obtain a **Project ID** from [Reown](https://dashboard.reown.com/) (formerly WalletConnect).
2. Configure the Reown Project ID in the Orderly One dashboard or your `.env` file.
3. Clear the site cache to ensure WalletConnect appears as a connection option.

## Privy Embedded Wallet Issues

### "Embedded wallet is only available over HTTPS"
**Cause:** Privy requires an HTTPS connection. If the site is served over HTTP (e.g., waiting for SSL certificate provisioning on GitHub Pages), the app will throw this error.

**Solution:** Ensure your hosting enforces HTTPS and that the SSL certificate is properly configured and active.

### HTTP to HTTPS Redirect Issues
**Cause:** Custom domain not properly configured with HTTPS.

**Solution:** Ensure the domain has valid HTTPS certificates and proper redirect rules.

### "Fund Wallet" Error on Email-Based Wallet Creation
**Cause:** A disabled setting in the Privy configuration.

**Solution:** Toggle the relevant funding option **on** in the Privy settings panel for the DEX.

## Coin98 Wallet Integration

To integrate Coin98 wallet:
1. Turn off other wallet providers in Web3 Onboard.
2. Turn on **'Override Metamask'** on Coin98.
3. Test the Connect Wallet flow.

## Tangem Wallet Compatibility

Tangem wallet is compatible with Orderly Network because it is supported through **WalletConnect**.

## Web3-Onboard (Blocknative) to ThirdWeb Migration

**No migration required.** After ThirdWeb acquired Web3-Onboard from Blocknative, ThirdWeb confirmed that current Web3-Onboard users will experience no interruptions. Web3-Onboard remains operational, actively supported, and will be enhanced over time.

## General Debugging Checklist

| Check | Action |
|:---|:---|
| Wallet connected to correct chain? | Verify chain ID matches expected network |
| Broker ID lowercase in config? | Check `.env` and config files |
| SSL certificate active? | Verify HTTPS is working |
| Reown Project ID configured? | Required for WalletConnect/mobile |
| VPN disabled? | Some regions block RPC calls |
| Wallet provider compatible? | Check supported wallet list |

chunks.title: Deposit and Withdrawal Troubleshooting
chunks.content:
This guide covers common issues with deposits and withdrawals on Orderly Network, including cross-chain relay fees, gas errors, and balance discrepancies.

## Deposit Issues

### CALL_REVERTED Error on Mainnet Deposits

**Symptom:** A `CALL_REVERTED` error occurs during a deposit on mainnet.

**Cause:** The user does not have enough ETH (or the native gas token) in their wallet to cover the **cross-chain message relay fees** charged by LayerZero.

**Solution:** Ensure the user's wallet holds sufficient native token balance before initiating the deposit.

### Additional ETH Transfer on Arbitrum Deposits

**Symptom:** A deposit transaction on Arbitrum includes an additional ETH transfer.

**Explanation:** When depositing tokens (e.g., USDC) into Orderly Network on Arbitrum, an additional ETH amount is attached to cover the cost of the cross-chain message relayed from Arbitrum to Orderly chain via LayerZero. If the attached ETH exceeds the actual relay cost, the **excess amount is refunded** back to the sender's wallet.

### Calculating Deposit Fees Programmatically

Call the Vault smart contract's `getDepositFee` function:

```solidity
// DepositData struct
struct DepositData {
    bytes32 accountId;
    bytes32 brokerHash;    // keccak256(brokerId)
    bytes32 tokenHash;     // keccak256(tokenSymbol)
    uint256 tokenAmount;
}

// Call getDepositFee to get required msg.value in WEI
uint256 fee = vault.getDepositFee(userAddress, depositData);
```

The returned fee must be sent as `msg.value` when calling the deposit function.

### Deposits from CEX or Custodial Wallets

If users are depositing from a **Centralized Exchange (CEX)** or a custodial wallet that does not support DApp interactions:
- Use the **Deposit by Transfer** method instead of the Standard Vault Deposit.
- The Standard Vault Deposit requires the user to connect their wallet and invoke the Vault contract's `deposit` function, which is not possible from CEX or custodial wallet contexts.

### Solana Deposit Gas Errors

**Symptom:** Fee or gas error when trying to deposit on Solana via an Orderly DEX.

**Cause:** Depositing on Solana is an on-chain action that requires native **SOL tokens** in the user's wallet to pay for gas fees.

**Solution:** Ensure the wallet has sufficient SOL for the transaction to proceed.

### MetaMask call_reverted on Arbitrum

**Solutions:**
1. Ensure sufficient ETH in the wallet for gas fees on Arbitrum.
2. Verify funds are being sent to the correct **Orderly Vault address** (not an incorrect contract address).
3. If the issue persists, contact Orderly support with the transaction ID.

## Withdrawal Issues

### User Cannot Withdraw Full PnL or Balance

**Common causes:**

1. **Open positions with unrealized PnL:**
   - Users must close all positions and settle unrealized PnL before withdrawing.
   - Check for any remaining open positions (even small ones).

2. **Fees accrued in Orderly account, not external wallet:**
   - Broker fees accumulate in the Orderly account and must be withdrawn via the broker registration portal.

3. **Withdrawal delays:**
   - Cross-chain withdrawals (especially Solana) may experience delays during security upgrades or LayerZero DVN migrations.

**Debugging:** Provide the user's wallet address to Orderly tech support to check backend data including `totalCollateral`, `totalUpnl`, and open positions.

### Tracking Cross-Chain Withdrawals

1. Search for the user's transactions on the Orderly dashboard:
   ```
   https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{WALLET_ADDRESS}?broker_id={BROKER_ID}
   ```
2. Find the withdrawal transaction and use the transaction ID (txid) to track it on [LayerZero Scan](https://layerzeroscan.com).

## Margin and Order Errors

### Error -1101: "The margin will be insufficient after"

**Cause:** Not enough margin (collateral) in the Orderly account.

**Solution:** Deposit USDC (or the relevant collateral token) into the Orderly account before placing orders. Orderly **cannot** automatically deduct tokens from the user's wallet — the user must explicitly send the deposit transaction.

### Isolated Margin Order Failure with Sufficient Balance

**Possible causes:**
1. **Unsettled PnL** from previous positions reducing available balance.
2. **Order quantity exceeding maximum position size** for the configured leverage tier.
3. **Incorrect tick size/step size formatting** — each symbol has its own minimum tick size.
4. In isolated margin mode, only the **allocated margin** is considered, not the total account free balance.

## Recovering Funds Deposited Under Wrong Broker ID

If a user deposited under `demo` or `orderly` instead of the custom Broker ID:

1. Access the recovery dashboard with correct parameters:
   ```
   https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{WALLET}?broker_id=demo&user_id={USER_ID}
   ```
2. Or connect to any DEX using the Orderly or Demo Broker ID:
   - Orderly: `https://dex.orderly.network/{broker-slug}/`
   - Demo: `https://dex.orderly.network/demo/perp/PERP_ETH_USDC`

## Cross-Chain Architecture Notes

Orderly uses a single **CrossChainManager (CCManager)** contract:
- **EVM chains:** Uses the `LedgerCrossChainRelay` channel.
- **Solana:** Uses a separate `SolConnector` contract based on LayerZero V2.
- Direct interaction from unsupported chains via LayerZero is **not possible**. Use a supported chain as an intermediate step.

chunks.title: EIP-712 Domain Configuration for Account Registration
Position Management and Trading Edge Cases
chunks.content:
This guide covers important trading behaviors, position constraints, and edge cases that developers and users should understand when building on Orderly Network.

## Position Constraints

### One Position Per Symbol Per Wallet
A wallet can only hold **one position per symbol** at a time. You cannot hold both a long and short position for the same symbol simultaneously.

- You **can** have multiple open (unfilled) orders for the same symbol.
- To gradually build a position (similar to TWAP), submit multiple smaller orders over time that aggregate into a single position as they fill.

### Hedge Mode
Hedge mode (holding both long and short positions for the same symbol) is **on Orderly's roadmap** but not yet available. In the meantime, implementing split accounts for the same wallet would need to be developed independently by the broker.

### Sub-Accounts
Sub-account support is planned but was not available as of early 2025. The feature is on the roadmap for future release.

> **Note:** A maximum of **10 sub-accounts** can be created under a main account (when available). This is a security constraint.

## Liquidation Behavior

### Partial Liquidations
If a user's position shows a **smaller quantity** than their filled order, a partial liquidation likely occurred.

**How it works:**
- Liquidations are triggered when the **maintenance margin ratio (MMR)** is breached:
  ```
  start_collateral / start_holding_notional < MMR
  ```
- The position quantity is **reduced** during liquidation.
- The remaining quantity stays open.

**Debugging:**
- Check the user's position history for liquidation events.
- Use the Orderly dashboard:
  ```
  https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{ADDRESS}?broker_id={BROKER_ID}
  ```
- Provide the wallet address to Orderly tech support for detailed backend analysis.

## Referral Code Management

### Changing Referral Codes
Once a referral code has been **bound to at least one referee**, it **cannot be changed**. A new code can only be created if no referees are bound yet.

**Workaround:** To use a different code, the user must register with a new wallet.

### Migrating Referral Relationships
Referral relationships **cannot be migrated** between wallets. As an alternative, the Orderly team can manually reduce the rebate rate on the existing referral chain.

## Governance and Token Mechanics

### $ORDER Governance
Orderly has a governance system where $ORDER stakers can vote on proposals:
- A passed governance proposal redirects up to **60% of Orderly fees** into $ORDER buybacks.
- **50%** goes to stakers (as esORDER with 3-month vesting).
- **50%** goes to a community-controlled wallet (usage decided via vote).
- The community can also vote on token delistings via the **'Vote to Retain'** process.

### Staking and Unstaking
- **Unstaking ORDER** requires a **7-day waiting period**.
- **esORDER** requires a **90-day conversion period** to ORDER with no yield during conversion.
- Brokers can stake ORDER from the Orderly One dashboard's graduation page or any wallet (provide staking address to Orderly support for manual configuration).

## NEAR-Specific Notes

### Checking Bridged nETH Balance
Bridged nETH may not appear in the NEAR Wallet UI due to indexing issues. Verify via CLI:

```bash
NEAR_ENV=mainnet near view aurora ft_balance_of '{"account_id": "<your_account>.near"}'
```

### Bridging from Gnosis Safe to NEAR
There is no Gnosis Safe equivalent on NEAR. The recommended approach:
1. Bridge assets from Gnosis Safe to a regular ETH wallet.
2. Use Rainbow Bridge to transfer to NEAR.
3. On NEAR, use **Sputnik DAO** as a multisig alternative.

## Permissionless Vault (PMV)

Permissionless Vault lets any EOA wallet deploy a fully functional Strategy Vault in a single transaction:
- No applications, approvals, or manual onboarding required.
- Backend automation handles cross-chain registration, account provisioning, and configuration.
- Time to live is under **30 minutes** with zero manual intervention.
- Leverages deterministic contract deployment (CREATE3), cross-chain messaging (LayerZero V2), and automated backend provisioning.

> **Disclaimer:** A permissionlessly created vault is deployed and operated by its creator, not by Orderly. Orderly does not vet, operate, or backstop these vaults.

chunks.title: Broker Configuration and Fee Structures
chunks.content:
Setting up and managing your broker identity, fee structures, and revenue sharing is fundamental to operating an Orderly-powered DEX. This guide covers broker registration, fee tiers, and revenue mechanics.

## Broker Registration

To configure a new broker on Orderly Network, provide the following information to the Orderly team:

1. **Environment**: Testnet or Mainnet
2. **Broker ID**: A unique string identifier (e.g., `my_dex`)
3. **Broker Name**: Display name for your DEX
4. **Default Taker Fee Rate**: Must be ≥ 0.03% (3 bps)
5. **Default Maker Fee Rate**: Must be ≥ 0%
6. **Broker Admin Account**: EVM address (registered after broker ID is configured)

### Testing vs Production

- **Testing**: Use the `demo` broker ID for initial development and testing.
- **Production**: Create your own broker ID via Orderly One for $10 (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate).

> **Warning**: Never use the default `Orderly` Broker ID in production. It is reserved for Orderly's internal use and may result in higher fees, account visibility issues, and lost asset access.

### Changing Your Broker ID

The broker ID and name are configured on the Orderly backend and cannot be renamed directly. To change your DEX name:
1. Set up a new broker ID
2. Update the broker ID in your DEX's `.env` file
3. Note: Existing users will lose access to their transaction history under the old broker ID (funds are not lost but become inaccessible under the new ID)

You can display any name on your UI regardless of the underlying broker ID.

## Fee Structure

### Base Fees (What Orderly Charges)

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Base Maker Fee | Requirements |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------------|
| Public | 3 bps (0.03%) | 0 bps | Default |
| Silver | 2.75 bps | -0.05 bps | 100,000 $ORDER staked |
| Gold | 2.5 bps | -0.10 bps | 300,000 $ORDER staked |
| Platinum | 2 bps | -0.15 bps | ≥$750M 30-day volume OR 3M $ORDER staked |
| Diamond | 1 bps | -0.20 bps | ≥$2B 30-day volume OR 7M $ORDER staked |

### Broker Revenue

Brokers set their own user-facing fees. The revenue is the difference between what you charge users and Orderly's base fee:

```
Broker Revenue = User Fee - Orderly Base Fee
```

**Example (Gold Tier, 2.5 bps base):**
- You charge 6 bps taker, 3 bps maker
- Orderly keeps 2.5 bps taker, 0 bps maker
- **You earn**: 3.5 bps taker, 3 bps maker

On $10M volume (100% taker): $3,500 broker revenue
On $10M volume (100% maker): $3,000 broker revenue

### Fee Tier Updates

Fee tier changes (from staking ORDER tokens) are processed by a backend script that runs daily around 00:10 UTC. Changes typically take effect by 2-3 AM UTC the following day.

### Referral and Affiliate Fees

- Orderly's base fee is **excluded** from referral fee splits
- Only the broker's fee portion is shared with referral participants
- Brokers configure maximum rebate and initial referral ratio
- Referrers can adjust the ratio afterwards

**Example**: If taker fee is 4 bps with 3 bps going to Orderly, the remaining 1 bps (broker fee) is split between builder, referrer, and referred user.

### Withdrawal Fees

Withdrawal fees are retained entirely by Orderly and are not shared with broker partners.

### Swap Fees

Swap fees can be configured in the Orderly One dashboard:
- Maximum fee: 100 basis points (1%)
- 70% of the markup goes to the DEX broker
- A fee under 0.2% is recommended to remain competitive

## Campaigns and Competitions

A single campaign can track activity across multiple broker IDs simultaneously. Provide broker IDs as a comma-separated list:

```
woofi_pro, vooi, bitoro_network, what_exchange
```

> **Note**: Broker IDs can be added before the campaign starts, but adding brokers after the campaign has begun may not retroactively capture earlier data.

To add a campaign page to your Orderly One DEX, enable the 'Campaign' option in your dashboard.

chunks.title: Omnichain Architecture, Cross-Chain Operations, and Solana Configuration
chunks.content:
Orderly Network operates as an omnichain perpetual trading infrastructure built on an OP Stack L2 settlement layer. Understanding the cross-chain architecture is essential for proper integration.

## High-Level Architecture

Orderly splits the stack into three layers:

1. **Asset Layer (Vaults)**: Smart contracts deployed on each supported chain where users deposit and withdraw funds
2. **Settlement Layer (Orderly L2)**: An OP Stack L2 that acts as the transaction ledger
3. **Engine Layer (Orderbook)**: Provides order matching and execution services

### How Cross-Chain Works

Tokens are **not** actually moved across chains. The flow is:

1. User deposits into the Orderly Vault smart contract on Chain A
2. LayerZero sends a cross-chain message to Orderly's L2 to track the deposit
3. User can withdraw from Chain B — Orderly rebalances the Vault smart contracts internally
4. All transaction records are securely logged on Orderly Chain

## Supported Chains

Orderly supports 17+ chains including:
- **EVM**: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, BNB Chain, Mantle
- **Non-EVM**: Solana, Movement (Fungible Asset standard only)

> **Note**: Polygon is not available due to an exclusivity agreement with another broker. Some chains may not be available to all brokers.

### Chain Requirements for New Integrations

For Orderly to deploy on a new chain, it must have:
1. EVM compatibility
2. USDC support (native or wrapped)
3. LayerZero integration for cross-chain messaging

> **Important**: LayerZero integration is a hard requirement. Native bridges alone (e.g., Hyperlane) are not sufficient.

## Multi-Collateral Support

Multi-collateral varies by chain:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH, YUSD, wBTC |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDC, USDT |

ETH has an 80% collateral margin ratio. Additional chains and tokens are added over time.

## Deposit Operations

### Deposit Fees

Orderly does not charge deposit fees. Costs include:
- Network gas fee on the source chain
- LayerZero cross-chain messaging fee (varies by chain and network conditions)

Fees must be fetched on-chain via the vault contract's `depositFee` function at transaction time — they cannot be reliably hardcoded.

### Depositing on Behalf of Another User

Use the `depositTo` function on the Vault smart contract instead of the standard `deposit`:

```solidity
// Vault contract (e.g., Arbitrum: 0x816f722424B49Cf1275cc86DA9840Fbd5a6167e9)
vault.depositTo(accountId, brokerHash, tokenHash, amount);
```

### Decoding Deposit Transaction Data

The deposit function uses selector `0x322dda6d`. Parameters (32 bytes each):
1. Account ID
2. Broker Hash (identifies the broker/frontend)
3. Token Hash (Keccak-256 hash of the token symbol string)
4. Token Amount (uint256)

To identify a token from its hash, compute `keccak256("USDT")` and match against the data field.

### AI Agent / Bot Deposits

Orderly settlement occurs on Arbitrum. When depositing from other chains:
- Bridge tokens to Arbitrum first, then call the deposit function, OR
- Use the proper cross-chain deposit flow

> **Critical**: Sending tokens directly to a vault address on a non-Arbitrum chain (e.g., sending Base USDC to an Arbitrum vault address on Base) will result in **unrecoverable loss**.

Reference: [Orderly Skills Repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/skills)

## Withdrawal Operations

### Withdrawable Balance Calculation

```
Withdrawable ≈ Total Balance + Unrealized PnL - Maintenance Margin
```

Capped by total account balance. When a position is closed, realized PnL is added to collateral.

### Vault Liquidity

Most vaults support 1M+ withdrawals. If a vault has insufficient liquidity:
- Orderly's auto-rebalancer moves funds between chains (typically < 1-2 minutes)
- Users can withdraw from another chain with available liquidity instantly

### Handling Unsupported Token Deposits

If a user deposits an unsupported token (e.g., USDT to a USDC-only address):
- Funds are held in the smart contract but not credited
- Once native support launches, the backend indexer automatically scans historical blocks and credits funds (may take up to a day)
- For manual recovery before native support, contact Orderly support

## Cross-Chain Messaging (LayerZero DVN)

Following security upgrades, Orderly pathways require at least a 3/3 DVN configuration:

- **Required**: Canary
- **Optional**: Horizen, LZ Labs, Nethermind
- **Optional Threshold**: 2

When selecting DVN addresses from metadata, use the address where `lzReadCompatible` is `false` if multiple addresses exist for the same provider.

### Solana Address Mapping

For deposits/withdrawals, Orderly saves the original Solana address as bytes32. For staking/rewards, the Solana address is converted to EVM via keccak256 hashing truncated to 20 bytes.

## Solana Cross-Chain Configuration

### Solana Transaction Size: Devnet vs Mainnet

When working with Solana transactions on Orderly, devnet and mainnet transactions with the **same payload** may have different sizes. This is expected behavior caused by differences in transaction structure, not payload length.

**Devnet transactions** typically include full executor instructions:
```
[executor: pre_execute, oapp: lz_receive, executor: post_execute]
```

**Mainnet transactions** may only contain the core OApp instruction if executed directly:
```
[oapp: lz_receive]
```

### Address Lookup Tables (ALTs)

Address Lookup Tables compress accounts differently depending on which accounts are covered. This is a major factor in transaction size differences between environments.

**Best Practices:**
- Ensure ALTs are properly configured for **both** devnet and mainnet environments
- Verify that all required accounts are included in the ALT for each environment
- Test transaction sizes on devnet with production-equivalent ALT configuration
- Monitor transaction size to ensure it stays within Solana's 1,232-byte limit

```typescript
// Example: Checking transaction size before submission
const transaction = new Transaction();
// ... add instructions ...
const serializedTx = transaction.serialize({ requireAllSignatures: false });
console.log(`Transaction size: ${serializedTx.length} bytes`);

if (serializedTx.length > 1232) {
  throw new Error('Transaction exceeds Solana size limit. Check ALT configuration.');
}
```

### OApp Configuration: ADI Testnet Executor

When configuring OApp (Omnichain Application) settings for pathways involving the **ADI testnet**, use the following executor address:

```
Executor Address: 0x701f3927871efcea1235db722f9e608ae120d243
```

```typescript
// OApp configuration for ADI testnet pathway
const oappConfig = {
  executor: "0x701f3927871efcea1235db722f9e608ae120d243",
  // ... other OApp settings
};
```

### Solana RPC Configuration

> **⚠️ Critical:** The default Solana public RPC (`api.mainnet-beta.solana.com`) often returns **403 Forbidden** due to CORS restrictions when called from browsers. You **must** use a dedicated RPC provider (Alchemy, QuickNode, Helius, etc.).

```tsx
import { ConnectionProvider } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-react";

<ConnectionProvider endpoint="https://solana-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY">
  {/* ... */}
</ConnectionProvider>
```

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Devnet tx succeeds but mainnet tx fails (size) | Different instruction sets and ALT coverage | Configure ALTs for mainnet to match devnet coverage |
| Transaction exceeds 1,232 bytes | Too many accounts not covered by ALT | Add missing accounts to ALT or reduce instruction count |
| OApp message not delivered on ADI testnet | Wrong executor address | Use `0x701f3927871efcea1235db722f9e608ae120d243` |
| CORS errors on Solana RPC | Using public RPC from browser | Switch to dedicated RPC provider |

chunks.title: Orderly One: DEX Deployment, Customization, Migration, and Graduation
chunks.content:
Orderly One is the low-code/no-code DEX creation platform for Orderly Network, enabling the creation, customization, deployment, and migration of perpetual DEX frontends. This guide covers the full lifecycle from creation to deployment.

## Getting Started

Access Orderly One at [https://dex.orderly.network/](https://dex.orderly.network/). A tutorial video is available at [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TKtT4yagr0A).

### Testnet

Testnet is enabled by default when creating a new DEX unless you explicitly check 'disable testnet' during setup.

## Deploying a New DEX

### Step-by-Step Process

1. **Visit Orderly One:** Go to [https://dex.orderly.network](https://dex.orderly.network)
2. **Connect your wallet:** This wallet becomes the admin wallet for fee collection and management.
3. **Configure your DEX:**
   - Set your Broker ID
   - Select supported chains
   - Configure wallet support (e.g., Abstract via Privy, EVM, Solana)
   - Apply CSS theming in the theme editor
   - Set up custom menu entries, Reown Project ID, and images
4. **Graduate your DEX** (see Graduation section below).
5. **Configure custom domain** via CNAME DNS entry.

### Wallet Configuration
- The DEX creator supports **disabling specific wallet types** (EVM, Solana).
- Filter to specific chains as needed.
- Configure **Reown App ID** (formerly WalletConnect Project ID) for mobile wallet support.

## Theme and UI Customization

### Logo Setup

- Use a transparent background (alpha channel) image
- Dimensions: 600x120 pixels
- Icon on the left, text on the right
- For seamless top navigation bar integration: remove the logo background or match it to your DEX background color

### Secondary Logo

Configure the Secondary Logo in broker settings to prevent the UI from falling back to the default Orderly Network logo during certain interactions.

### Color Configuration

- Click 'Edit Desktop' and click directly on page sections to change colors
- The color picker is available directly from the section editing screen (no need to go into 'Themes')
- **Primary color** affects: leverage indicator, close buttons, and UI elements
- Links at the top use a gradient between 'Primary' and 'Primary Light'

### CSS Customization

Apply custom CSS via the Orderly One dashboard using CSS variables prefixed with `--oui-`:

```css
:root {
  --oui-color-primary: #your-color;
  --oui-font-family: "Your Font", sans-serif;
  --oui-rounded-lg: 8px;
  --oui-spacing-md: 16px;
}
```

#### Hiding 'Powered by Orderly'

```css
.oui-scaffold-footer-powered-by {
  display: none;
}
```

Or for the bottom-right label:

```css
body>div.oui-scaffold-root>div.oui-box.oui-scaffold-footer>div>div.oui-box.oui-flex {
  display: none;
}
```

> **Known Issue**: Platform upgrades may override custom CSS styling. Re-apply your custom CSS after upgrades.

> **Known Bug**: Brand gradient and button colors may not sync with the primary color setting. Set these via CSS directly as a workaround.

### PnL Card Customization

Configure PnL card settings in `app/utils/config.tsx`. Reference: [Sample Config](https://gist.github.com/wuzhong-orderly/419c8bd0fbc38f91444cbb84aa39d528)

Replace the PnL share background image in the `public/pnl` folder. Reference dimensions: [broker-template/pnl](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-template/tree/main/public/pnl)

## Custom Domain Setup

### DNS Configuration

For a subdomain (e.g., `app.yourdomain.xyz`):

| Type | Name | Value |
|------|------|-------|
| CNAME | app | cname.vercel-dns.com |
| CNAME | testnet | cname.vercel-dns.com |

For Orderly One hosted DEXes, point CNAME to `orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io` (use a dot, not a hyphen). Replace any previous CNAME (e.g., `cname.vercel-dns.com`).

### Configuration Steps

1. Enter the full subdomain (e.g., `dex.holylabs.xyz`) in the custom URL field
2. Select 'DNS Only' option (disable proxy/CDN features like Cloudflare's orange cloud)
3. Ensure no conflicting DNS entries exist
4. Enforce HTTPS for automatic redirects
5. SSL certificate propagation can take 1-2 days

> **Tip**: Use a subdomain like `app.yourdomain.xyz` to avoid collisions with a landing page on the root domain.

### Domain Card Configuration

Configure domain and card info at `https://dex.orderly.network/dex/card` to prevent broken links when self-hosting.

## Graduation Process

Graduation activates revenue generation for your DEX. Before graduation, the DEX is functional but does **not** generate revenue.

### Benefits
- Gain access to customize fees
- Monetize your platform
- Get your DEX card displayed on the Orderly One board

### Cost
- **Flat fee:** $10 (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate)

> **Note**: Staked ORDER tokens cannot be used for graduation. The fee must be paid with liquid (unstaked) funds.

### Process
1. Navigate to the graduation page: `https://dex.orderly.network/dex/graduation`
2. Click **'Register with Orderly and Start Earning'**.
3. Complete the payment.
4. Register your admin wallet if not already done.

### Payment Methods
- **EOA wallet:** Pay directly through the Orderly One platform.
- **Multisig wallet:** Make the payment manually and provide the transaction hash to the Orderly team.

> **Known Bug**: The graduation UI may not accept decimal fee values. Use whole numbers during graduation and adjust fees afterward. Alternatively, use the beta panel at `https://dex-beta.orderly.network/`.

### Troubleshooting Graduation

#### "Quorum not met" Error
**Cause:** Occurs during graduation fee verification even when the correct token and chain are selected.

**Solution:** If the manual verification field (for entering the transaction hash) is not clickable, provide your wallet address and desired Broker ID to Orderly support for manual processing.

#### Verification Fails Despite Successful Transfer
**Causes:**
1. Using the wrong payment token (e.g., ORDER instead of USDC when USDC was selected).
2. Wrong chain selected for verification.
3. Indexer has not picked up the transaction.

**Solutions:**
- Ensure you select the **correct payment token and chain** matching the transaction.
- If the indexer fails, provide the transaction hash and wallet address to Orderly support.
- A legacy incompatibility may require the DEX to be created first via `https://dex.orderly.network/en/dex` before graduation can proceed.

#### Automated Process Fails
If the automated Broker ID graduation fails, the Orderly DevRel team can manually process it. Provide:
- Transaction hash
- Wallet address used on Orderly One
- Desired Broker ID
- Verify the selected chain matches the token's chain

## Migrating an Existing DEX to Orderly One

### Migration Steps

1. Visit [https://dex.orderly.network/](https://dex.orderly.network/) and connect your wallet.
2. Configure the DEX settings (skip optional steps if needed — they can be refined later).
3. Apply your theme CSS in the theme editor.
4. Set up custom menu entries, Reown Project ID, and images.
5. Copy over existing CSS themes, logos, and Reown App IDs from your previous deployment.
6. Once configured and tested, update your DNS CNAME record.
7. Contact the Orderly team to switch your Broker ID.

> **Important:** Open orders, positions, and deposits on the old deployment may need to be closed before migration.

### Linking Broker ID to Orderly One
If a DEX was created using Orderly One and you have an existing Broker ID:
1. Provide the Broker ID and DEX URL to Orderly support.
2. If an admin wallet was already configured separately, the team will verify compatibility and complete the linkage.

## Reown App ID

The Reown App ID (formerly WalletConnect Project ID) is used for WalletConnect integration:
- Found in your project's `.env` file.
- When migrating, you can reuse your existing Reown App ID or create a new one.
- This step is optional during Orderly One setup but required for mobile wallet support.

## Feature Configuration

### OmniVault Deposits

1. Enable the Vaults menu from the Orderly One dashboard
2. Click 'Update DEX' to apply
3. Deposits available via the Vault page or `https://app.orderly.network/`

### Affiliate/Referral Program

- Supported on the no-code white-label product
- Multi-level affiliate system available from the DEX admin dashboard
- Activate directly from the admin panel

### Analytics

- **Orderly One**: Amplitude analytics available as a built-in feature
- **Custom deployments**: Integrate Google Analytics or other providers by modifying frontend code

## Known Issues

### Chain Disappearing After Config Changes

Orderly One disables certain chains by default. When a broker ID is manually configured to support additional chains (like SEI), any UI configuration change resets supported blockchains to the default set. Contact the Orderly team to re-enable unsupported chains after config changes.

### Affiliate Link Reverting

Referral links may revert to the default `orderly.network` domain instead of your branded domain. Contact the Orderly team to apply a fix. The issue may reappear after DEX configuration changes.

### 'Visit DEX' Link

The 'Visit DEX' link set during graduation cannot be modified from the UI. Contact the Orderly DevRel team to manually update it on the backend.

chunks.title: Governance, Staking, and Token Delisting
chunks.content:
Orderly Network includes governance mechanisms, a staking program, and community-driven token retention processes that brokers should understand and communicate to their users.

## $ORDER Staking

### Staking Overview

- **APR**: Approximately 20%, paid in USDC
- **Supported Chains**: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon
- **Staking Page**: [https://app.orderly.network/staking](https://app.orderly.network/staking)

> **Note**: Airdrop claims are only available on Ethereum, but staking can be done on any supported chain.

### Smart Contract Integration

Staking is done through the proxy contract at `0xC8A8Ce0Ab010E499ca57477AC031358febCbbF17`.

```javascript
// 1. Approve ORDER token for the proxy contract
const ORDER_TOKEN = "0x4E200fE2f3eFb977d5fd9c430A41531FB04d97B8";
await orderToken.approve(PROXY_CONTRACT, amount);

// 2. Fetch LayerZero fee
const lzFee = await proxyContract.quoteStakeOrder(amount, userAddress);

// 3. Call stakeOrder with LZ fee as value (app multiplies by 1.1 for safety)
await proxyContract.stakeOrder(amount, userAddress, { value: lzFee * 1.1n / 10n });
```

### Third-Party Staking Integration

Protocols can integrate Orderly staking via two strategies:

1. **USDC-Based Strategy**: Users deposit USDC; a portion buys and stakes ORDER in the background
2. **ORDER-Based Strategy**: Users deposit ORDER directly, earning both Orderly staking APR (USDC) and additional protocol rewards

### Unstaking

Press the down arrow in the staking interface to reveal the unstake button.

## Builder Staking Program Tiers

Staking ORDER tokens reduces the base taker fee for brokers:

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Requirement |
|------|---------------|-------------|
| Public | 3 bps | Default |
| Silver | 2.75 bps | 100,000 $ORDER staked |
| Gold | 2.5 bps | 300,000 $ORDER staked |
| Platinum | 2 bps | ≥$750M 30-day volume OR 3M $ORDER staked |
| Diamond | 1 bps | ≥$2B 30-day volume OR 7M $ORDER staked |

Fee changes take effect the day after staking (processed around 00:10 UTC, effective by 2-3 AM UTC).

## Community Vote to Retain

### How It Works

When tokens are identified for potential delisting due to sustained low metrics, a **Vote to Retain** governance process is initiated.

### Voting Mechanics

- **Threshold**: More than 3% (or 5% depending on the proposal) of total staked $ORDER must vote **'AGAINST Delisting'**
- **Voting Period**: Typically 5 days
- **Voting Token**: Staked $ORDER tokens only

### Broker Responsibilities

Brokers are encouraged to:
1. Inform their communities about upcoming votes
2. Encourage participation using staked $ORDER
3. Monitor the Orderly governance blog for vote announcements

Tokens that do not receive sufficient 'AGAINST Delisting' votes are delisted from the platform.

## Snapshot Voting Configuration

To configure Snapshot voting for Orderly governance:

```json
{
  "name": "orderly-staked-order",
  "params": {
    "symbol": "ORDER"
  }
}
```

The `address` and `decimals` parameters are not needed. Only `symbol` is required to display voting power in the UI.

Reference: [snapshot-strategies PR #1775](https://github.com/snapshot-labs/snapshot-strategies/pull/1775)

### Embedding Snapshot on Link3

Use the Snapshot block under the "Other" category. Legacy URL format required:
```
https://snapshot.org/#/orderlygov.eth
```

## Permissionless Listings

Builders can list any asset themselves without relying on Orderly:
- Earn 50% of Orderly's base fees from listed assets
- Earn 100% of liquidation fees from listed assets

## Negative Maker Fees

Orderly pays builders for placing maker orders with rebates of up to **0.20 bps** depending on DEX tier and asset. This helps bootstrap liquidity and tighten spreads.

## Permissionless Vaults

Users can create community vaults and monetize their strategies on any Orderly-powered DEX. OmniVault deployment requires coordination with the Orderly team as a strategy provider.

Reference: [OmniVault Onboarding Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1scvOWLkgK556mMl4xZrPeXgYixAxdgsQlfArMW0gf1U)

chunks.title: DefiLlama, Analytics, and External Integrations
chunks.content:
This guide covers how to list your Orderly-powered DEX on analytics platforms, integrate with external services, and leverage Orderly's ecosystem tools.

## DefiLlama Integration

### Listing Your DEX

To report fees and volumes to DefiLlama:

1. Fork the DefiLlama dimension-adapters repository
2. Use the Orderly adapter template: [defillama-adapter-template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/defillama-adapter-template/tree/main)
3. Set the chain to `'Orderly Chain'` in your adapter configuration
4. Submit a PR with your broker ID

**Example PR**: [DefiLlama dimension-adapters #4361](https://github.com/DefiLlama/dimension-adapters/pull/4361)

### Holders Revenue Dashboard

Listing requirements for the Holders Revenue, Fees, Revenue, and Earnings dashboards are documented at: [DefiLlama Docs](https://docs.llama.fi/list-your-project/other-dashboards)

## Dune Analytics

DEX data is available on the Orderly Dune dashboard and can be filtered by `brokerID`:

[Orderly Dune Dashboard](https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-dashboard)

> **Note**: The Dune Index has been sunsetted, but its methodology is still documented and can be replicated using existing Dune queries. Reference: [Dune Index Methodology](https://docs.dune.com/data-catalog/dune-index/introduction)

## Google Analytics

- **Orderly One DEXes**: Amplitude analytics is available as a built-in feature
- **Custom deployments**: Integrate Google Analytics by modifying the frontend code

## Fiat On-Ramp / Off-Ramp

Orderly does not provide native on-ramp/off-ramp services. Builders can integrate third-party providers:

- **Onramper** and similar services can be integrated independently
- Orderly can facilitate introductions to on-ramp providers

> **Note**: A MoonPay integration was explored but not finalized.

## WOOFi Swap Integration

Orderly uses WooFi for spot swaps, aggregating liquidity from sources like 1inch and Near Intents.

- **Integration Docs**: [Integrate WOOFi as Liquidity Source](https://learn.woo.org/dev-docs/guides/integrate-woofi-as-liquidity-source)

To register a plugin, submit a PR to the `elizaos-plugins/registry` repository pointing to your plugin's GitHub repository.

## ORDER Token Addresses

## Testnet Support

| Network | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Sepolia (EVM chains) | ✅ Supported — Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Mantle, Ethereum, Avalanche, Sonic, BNB Smart Chain |
| Solana Arctic Devnet | ✅ Supported |
| Goerli (ARB/OP) | ❌ Deprecated — migrated to Sepolia |
| SEI, Bera, Mode testnets | ❌ Mainnet only |

Testnet addresses **vary by chain**. Refer to the testnet deployment documentation or API responses for the correct testnet contract addresses.

## Usage in Code

```typescript
// Example: Interacting with VaultCrossChainManager on Arbitrum
import { ethers } from 'ethers';

const VAULT_CROSS_CHAIN_MANAGER = '0xa0a07a78c7d31E6f8698F48Fc9219f9a3030f38C';
const CROSS_CHAIN_RELAY = '0x173B47eDBeCa665125edc24C509bfE545CDA60a9';

// BNB Chain requires different addresses
const BNB_VAULT_CROSS_CHAIN_MANAGER = '0x6Fb848801aCa77E724A8AB22D0006cb317e69492';
const BNB_CROSS_CHAIN_RELAY = '0x461C12FBa639303Da045255dd32eEa7E38AC69b0';

function getContractAddresses(chainId: number) {
  if (chainId === 56) { // BNB Smart Chain
    return {
      vaultCrossChainManager: BNB_VAULT_CROSS_CHAIN_MANAGER,
      crossChainRelay: BNB_CROSS_CHAIN_RELAY
    };
  }
  return {
    vaultCrossChainManager: VAULT_CROSS_CHAIN_MANAGER,
    crossChainRelay: CROSS_CHAIN_RELAY
  };
}
```

## Contract ABIs

All Orderly contracts are verified on their respective chain explorers. You can also find the latest ABI files on GitHub:

```
https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/contract-evm-abi
```

## Plume Network

Deployed contract addresses for Plume mainnet are documented at:
```
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/addresses#plume
```

## Important Notes

- Always verify contract addresses against the official deployment records before interacting
- Testnet addresses differ from mainnet and vary by chain
- The OmniVault is currently deployed on 4 chains (Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Sei)
- BNB Smart Chain is the only mainnet EVM chain with different VaultCrossChainManager/CrossChainRelay addresses

## Chain Deprecation Policy

Orderly may propose governance votes to sunset support for chains with low volume and builder activity over a 90-day period. If a chain is deprecated:
- User funds remain **100% safe**
- Users can withdraw funds to any of Orderly's other active supported chains

chunks.title: Fee Structure, Referral System, and Builder Staking Program
chunks.content:
This guide covers Orderly's fee architecture, broker revenue, referral/rebate mechanics, and the Builder Staking Program.

## Base Protocol Fees

Orderly's base fee structure:

| Fee Type | Rate |
|----------|------|
| **Taker** | 3 bps (0.03%) |
| **Maker** | 0 bps (0.00%) |

There are **no infrastructure fees**. Partners/brokers keep **100%** of any additional fees charged on top of the base fee.

## Default Broker Fee Setup

The typical default fee configuration for a new broker:

| Fee | Rate | Breakdown |
|-----|------|-----------|
| Taker | 6 bps (0.06%) | 3 bps Orderly base + 3 bps broker revenue |
| Maker | 3 bps (0.03%) | 0 bps Orderly base + 3 bps broker revenue |

These rates can be customized per broker integration.

## Builder Staking Program

Brokers can reduce their base taker fee through staking ORDER tokens or achieving volume milestones:

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Requirements |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| **Public** (default) | 3 bps | — |
| **Silver** | 2.75 bps | 100,000 ORDER staked |
| **Gold** | 2.5 bps | 300,000 ORDER staked OR ≥$200M 30-day volume |
| **Platinum** | 2 bps | ≥$750M 30-day volume OR 3M ORDER staked |
| **Diamond** | 1 bps | ≥$2B 30-day volume OR 7M ORDER staked |

Higher staking tiers increase the broker's revenue share, which directly increases the maximum rebate available through referral codes.

## Perpetuals vs Swaps Fees

| Product | Fee Structure |
|---------|---------------|
| **Perpetuals** | Base fee applies; brokers set their own fee on top |
| **Swaps** | Routing fees apply depending on the routing provider; Orderly is working on allowing brokers to charge on top of base routing fees |

## Referral System

### How Referral Fee Splits Work

The referral fee percentage applies **only to the broker's portion** of fees (the fee added on top of Orderly's base fee).

**Example:**
- Orderly base fee: 0.03%
- Broker adds: 0.05%
- Total taker fee: 0.08%
- Referral split: 50%
- Referrer earns: 50% of broker's 0.05% = **0.025%**

### Maximum Referral Rebate

The maximum rebate you can return via referral codes is **100% of the revenue you would earn** as a broker. The actual amount depends on your Builder Staking Programme tier.

**Example (Public tier, 3 bps base):**
- If you set a 5 bps taker fee
- Your revenue share = 5 - 3 = 2 bps
- Maximum rebate to users = 2 bps (100% of your share)

### Referral Code Uniqueness

Referral codes are **unique system-wide** across all Orderly brokers. The same code string (e.g., `'TEALSTREET'`) cannot be created on multiple brokers. If integrating with multiple brokers, use different referral code strings for each:

```
Broker A: 'TEALSALSA'
Broker B: 'TEALKODIAK'
```

### Referral Cashback Limitations

- Referral cashback **cannot** be split between maker and taker fees
- You can only rebate your own revenue share
- If the taker fee is 0.05% and Orderly's share is 0.025%, the maximum rebate is your 0.025% share

### Reducing Commission Rates on Existing Referral Codes

Reducing the commission rate for an existing multi-level referral code requires **manual intervention** from the Orderly team (downward adjustment automation is planned). When reduced:
- The deduction is absorbed **top-to-bottom**: the target affiliate's earnings are reduced first
- If insufficient, the remaining deduction cascades to downstream affiliates
- Alternatively, all downstream rates can be reset to 0%

### Referral Description Field

The referral description field in the broker admin console is for **internal reference only** — it does not appear in the DEX UI.

## Graduation and Monetization

After building your DEX on Orderly One:

1. Click **'Graduate Now'** on the [builder board](https://dex.orderly.network/board)
2. Pay the **$10 graduation fee (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate)
3. Once graduated, you can:
   - Set commission rates
   - Access the admin panel
   - Configure the affiliate/referral system

## Admin Portal

After onboarding, manage your broker settings at:
```
https://admin.orderly.network
```

chunks.title: Collateral Support and Multi-Collateral Configuration
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports multiple collateral types across different chains. This guide covers supported assets, chain-specific configurations, and important implementation notes.

## Primary Collateral

**USDC** is the primary collateral supported across all chains.

## Multi-Collateral Support

Orderly supports additional collateral types beyond USDC:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| **Ethereum** | USDC, USDT, ETH, WBTC |
| **BNB Chain** | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| **Arbitrum** | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| **Base** | USDC, ETH |
| **Solana** | USDC, SOL, USDT |

Multi-collateral support on Solana was introduced in a September 2025 upgrade. The platform continues to expand collateral options to align with user demand.

## BNB Chain USDC Precision

**Critical implementation note:** USDC on BNB Chain uses **18 decimals** on-chain, but Orderly only supports **6 decimals** for deposits and withdrawals.

Always use the `decimals` field from the Public Token API rather than hardcoding values:

```typescript
import { useQuery } from '@orderly.network/hooks';

const { data: tokens } = useQuery('/v1/public/token');

// Always use token.decimals from this response
const usdcDecimals = tokens.find(t => t.token === 'USDC')?.decimals;
```

## Enabling Multi-Collateral in SDK

Upgrade to **SDK v2.5.1+** for multi-collateral support. From v2.5.2+, deposit assets also support auto-matching collateral.

## Deposit Zap-In (SDK v2.10.1+)

Allows users to deposit any token — it's automatically swapped to supported collateral:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit={true}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

## TVL Calculation Methodology

Orderly calculates on-chain TVL by tracking token balances deployed into its Vault smart contracts across all supported chains combined. This methodology is implemented in the [DefiLlama adapter](https://github.com/DefiLlama/DefiLlama-Adapters/blob/main/projects/orderly-network/index.js).

**Note:** Orderly's official TVL also includes **Ceffu** (off-exchange settlement), which cannot be tracked on-chain. This is why DefiLlama and Dune TVL figures may differ from Orderly's official reported TVL.

chunks.title: Error Codes, Troubleshooting, and Support Resources
chunks.content:
This guide covers common error codes, diagnostic steps, and support resources for Orderly Network integrations.

## Common Error Codes

### Error -1006 (HTTP 400) — Data Not Found

The requested data does not exist on the server.

**Common cause:** Attempting to cancel an order that is already in the `CANCELLED` state.

```typescript
// Always check order status before canceling
const order = await getOrder(orderId);
if (order.status !== 'CANCELLED' && order.status !== 'FILLED') {
  await cancelOrder(orderId);
}
```

### Error -1104 (HTTP 400) — Order Quantity Validation Failure

The order quantity fails validation for one of these reasons:
- Quantity is below the minimum allowed amount (`base_min`)
- Quantity exceeds the maximum allowed amount (`base_max`)
- Quantity does not match the required step size
- Visible quantity does not match the step size

**Solution:** Fetch symbol info and validate before submitting:

```typescript
const symbolInfo = await getSymbolInfo('PERP_BTC_USDC');
const { base_min, base_max, base_tick } = symbolInfo;

// Ensure quantity is within bounds and matches step size
const validQuantity = Math.max(base_min, Math.min(base_max, 
  Math.round(quantity / base_tick) * base_tick
));
```

### Error -1202 (HTTP 400) — No Liquidation Needed

The user's margin is sufficient (no liquidation required), or the given `liquidationId` cannot be found.

### Error 71 — Internal Transfer Failed

Internal transfers are only supported between a **main account and its sub-accounts**. Transfers between two unrelated accounts (different main accounts) will fail.

**Solution:** Ensure both sender and receiver are in a main/sub-account relationship.

## TP/SL Visibility Issue

### Custom-Quantity TP/SL Orders Not Visible in `usePositionStream`

When a TP/SL is placed with a custom quantity (not the full position), the algo order type is `TP_SL` rather than `POSITIONAL_TP_SL`. The internal `findPositionTPSLFromOrders` function filters only for `type === 'POSITIONAL_TP_SL'`, so custom-quantity TP/SL orders are excluded.

**Fix:** Update the filter to also include `TP_SL` type orders:

```typescript
// Include both types when filtering for TP/SL orders
const tpslOrders = orders.filter(
  o => o.type === 'POSITIONAL_TP_SL' || o.type === 'TP_SL'
);
```

## On-Chain Transaction Failures

### Step 1: Verify Contract Address

Confirm the user is interacting with a supported contract deployment:
```
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/addresses
```

### Step 2: Inspect the Transaction

Check the transaction in the relevant block explorer for:
- Revert reasons
- Gas issues
- Confirmation delays

### Polygon Deposit Failures

Deposits on Polygon may fail with `Call Reverted` or `execution reverted` if your broker is not approved for Polygon access. Contact the Orderly team to verify access.

## Batch Leverage Update Behavior

When calling `POST /v1/client/leverages` **without** a `symbol` parameter:

| Margin Mode | Behavior |
|-------------|----------|
| **Cross** | All cross-margin symbols update atomically (all succeed or none do) |
| **Isolated** | Only applies to symbols with no active isolated positions or pending orders; eligible symbols always update |

## Candle (Kline) Data Intervals

Supported intervals for candle data:

```
1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d, 1w
```

## Support Resources

### Troubleshooting Workflow

1. **Integration FAQs:** [orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/integration-faqs](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/integration-faqs)
2. **Troubleshooting Section:** Check docs for common issues and diagnostic steps
3. **Orderly Dashboard:** [orderly-dashboard.orderly.network](https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/) — retrieve user account state and transaction history for diagnostics
4. **Discord Support:** Submit a support ticket at [discord.gg/orderlynetwork](https://discord.gg/orderlynetwork)

### Integration Checklist

A step-by-step guide covering the full integration path:
```
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/integration-checklist
```

### Example Code

Reference implementation with concrete integration patterns:
```
https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex
```

### Node.js Requirements

The Orderly devkit CLI requires **Node.js v20.19.0** or newer.

## Strategy Vault Audits

Orderly has completed **two independent audits** on its Strategy Vault smart contracts. Audit reports are available at:
```
https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/Audits
```

Users should assess their risk tolerance before depositing into any strategy vault.

chunks.title: Community Governance: Token Retention Votes and Delisting
chunks.content:
Orderly Network uses a community governance mechanism to handle token delisting decisions. This guide explains the Vote to Retain process and how builders can participate.

## Community Vote to Retain

When tokens are identified for potential delisting due to **sustained low metrics** (volume, liquidity, activity), they are put through a community governance vote.

### How It Works

1. **Identification:** Tokens with sustained low metrics are flagged for potential delisting
2. **Vote Initiation:** A 'Vote to Retain' governance process is initiated
3. **Voting Period:** Typically lasts **5 days**
4. **Threshold:** To save a token from delisting, more than **3%** (or **5%** in some cases) of total staked $ORDER must vote **'AGAINST Delisting'**
5. **Outcome:** If the threshold is not met, the token is delisted

### Builder Responsibilities

Brokers and builders are encouraged to:
- **Inform their communities** about active votes affecting tokens they trade
- **Encourage participation** using staked $ORDER tokens
- **Monitor governance proposals** for tokens relevant to their platform

### Staking Requirement

Only **staked $ORDER** tokens can be used for voting. Users must have their ORDER tokens staked before the voting period begins to participate.

## Permissionless Listing and Delisting

With the April 1, 2026 upgrade, Orderly introduced:
- **Permissionless listing** feature — anyone can create perpetual markets
- **Tick size adjustments** for better market configuration

### Delisted Markets

Orderly does not natively support re-listing a delisted permissionless market through the API. To manually revert a delisting status or reactivate a market, contact the Orderly support team.

## Chain Sunset Policy

Orderly may propose governance votes to sunset support for chains with low volume and builder activity over a **90-day period**. If a chain is deprecated:
- User funds remain **100% safe**
- Users can withdraw their funds to any of Orderly's other active supported chains
- No action is required from builders beyond informing their users

chunks.title: Permissionless Vaults: Creation, Fees, and Cross-Chain Recovery
chunks.content:
Orderly's Permissionless Vault system allows builders to create custom strategy vaults. This guide covers the creation process, associated fees, and cross-chain recovery mechanisms.

## Creating a Permissionless Vault

Permissionless Vaults are created through a factory contract that deploys the vault and syncs its configuration to the Orderly Chain ledger via LayerZero V2.

## Required Fees

Three fees are paid in a **single transaction** during vault creation:

### 1. Gas Fee
- Standard blockchain gas for deploying the vault contract and executing on-chain operations
- Varies with network congestion

### 2. Cross-Chain Fee
- LayerZero V2 messaging fee for syncing vault configuration to the Orderly Chain ledger
- Quoted via `quoteFee()` on the factory contract
- Any excess fee is **refunded**

### 3. Vault Operation Reserve
- A **non-refundable** native token (ETH) deposit of **0.1 ETH per chain**
- Deposited into the vault contract via `assetsTransferCrossChainFee()` on the factory contract
- Covers future cross-chain transfer operations (moving user funds from Vault to DEX)

**Important:** None of these fees are collected by Orderly Network. They are paid to the blockchain network and cross-chain infrastructure providers.

## Cross-Chain Recovery

If the LayerZero cross-chain message fails to deliver during vault creation (due to network issues or gas spikes), the vault will be deployed on the EVM chain but **not yet registered** on the Orderly Chain ledger.

### Recovery Options

#### 1. Automatic Retry
LayerZero V2 has built-in retry for queued messages. In many cases, the message will be delivered automatically.

#### 2. Manual Re-send
The creator can call `resendConfiguration()` on the factory to re-trigger the cross-chain message:

```solidity
// Safe to call multiple times — ledger configuration is idempotent
factory.resendConfiguration(vaultAddress);
```

This is safe because the ledger configuration is **idempotent** — calling it multiple times has no adverse effects.

#### 3. Timeout Alert
If registration hasn't completed within **30 minutes**, the system alerts the operations team for manual intervention.

### Vault Usability During Recovery

While waiting for cross-chain registration:
- ✅ The vault remains **usable on its deployment chain** (deposits and withdrawals work)
- ❌ Cross-chain settlement is **blocked** until ledger registration completes

## Strategy Vault vs OmniVault

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Strategy Vault** | The underlying smart contract and clearing infrastructure |
| **OmniVault** | The official protocol-level vault implementation built on top of Strategy Vault |

Documentation: [orderly.network/docs/introduction/orderly-omniVault/overview](https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/orderly-omniVault/overview)

## Security Audits

Orderly has completed **two independent audits** on its Strategy Vault smart contracts. Reports are available at:
```
https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/Audits
```

Users should carefully assess their risk tolerance and the vault's risk profile before depositing, as every strategy vault carries its own risks.

chunks.title: Position Margin, Collateral, and Liquidation Calculations
chunks.content:
This guide covers how Orderly calculates free collateral, position margin, and liquidation thresholds across cross-margin and isolated-margin modes.

## Free Collateral by Margin Mode

### Cross Margin

For cross-margin positions, free collateral is calculated as:

```
free_collateral = total_collateral - maintenance_margin
```

**Unsettled PnL is included** in the total collateral calculation, meaning unrealized profits increase your available margin and unrealized losses decrease it.

### Isolated Margin

For isolated-margin positions, **unsettled PnL is NOT included** in the free collateral calculation. Free collateral for isolated margin only changes when:
- Opening a new position
- Closing an existing position
- Adding or removing margin from the position

Fluctuations in unrealized PnL do not affect free collateral in isolated mode.

The total collateral value for an isolated margin position is:

```
total_collateral_value = isolated_position_margin + unsettled_PNL
```

### Retrieving Collateral Data

```tsx
import { useCollateral, usePositionStream } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const {
  totalCollateral,
  freeCollateral,
  availableBalance
} = useCollateral({ dp: 2 });

const { positions } = usePositionStream();
// positions[].position_margin
// positions[].position_value
// positions[].unsettled_pnl
```

| Metric | Hook | Property |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Available balance (incl. settled PnL) | `useCollateral` | `availableBalance` |
| Free collateral (excl. unsettled PnL for ISO) | `useCollateral` | `freeCollateral` |
| Account equity / total collateral | `useCollateral` | `totalCollateral` |
| Unrealized PnL | `usePositionStream` | Via position data |
| Maintenance margin | `usePositionStream` | Position info |

## Liquidation Fees and Thresholds

Liquidation fees are **part of the liquidation threshold calculation**. The system accounts for the liquidation fee when determining whether a position should be liquidated. This means the fee is effectively deducted from the position's value as part of the liquidation process.

When estimating liquidation price, the formula already factors in:
- Maintenance margin requirement
- Pending liquidation fees
- Current mark price

### Estimated Liquidation Price

#### Before Entering a Position

```tsx
const { formattedOrder } = useOrderEntry(symbol, {
  watchOrderbook: true
});
// formattedOrder contains est_liq_price
```

#### For Existing Positions

```tsx
const { positions } = usePositionStream();
// positions[].est_liq_price
```

## Current Leverage

Current leverage is calculated as:

```
currentLeverage = 1 / accountMarginRatio
```

```tsx
import { useMarginRatio } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { crossMarginRatio, crossAccountLeverage } = useMarginRatio();
```

| Property | Source | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `maxLeverage` | `useLeverage` | Maximum leverage the user can set |
| `currentLeverage` | `useMarginRatio` | Computed dynamically from open positions |

## Common Issue: Deposit Not Showing in Balance

If a user deposits funds but their available balance does not appear to increase, this typically occurs when:

1. The user previously opened a position with **maximum leverage**
2. The position is currently in a **loss**
3. The deposited funds are **automatically used to top up the initial margin** required to maintain the position

In this scenario, the deposit is credited to the account but immediately consumed by the margin requirement, so the free/available balance remains unchanged.

**Solution:** Check the user's open positions and margin ratio. If they are near liquidation, the deposit is being used to prevent liquidation rather than increasing available balance.

chunks.title: PnL Settlement and Withdrawal UX Best Practices
PnL Card Sharing: Troubleshooting and Configuration
chunks.content:
This guide covers common issues with PnL card sharing and how to configure PnL sharing in the Orderly SDK.

## Common Issue: Invisible Text or QR Code on PnL Cards

### Problem

Users cannot share PnL cards, or the shared card shows a blank/empty image where text and QR codes should appear.

### Root Cause

The PnL card text color is **white by default**. If your DEX uses a **light background** for the PnL card, the white text and QR code become invisible against the light background.

### Solution

Change the PnL card background to a **dark color** so the white text and QR code become visible. This applies to both desktop and mobile sharing.

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  shareOptions={{
    pnl: {
      profitColor: '#22c55e',
      lossColor: '#ef4444',
      backgroundImages: [
        '/images/dark_poster_bg_1.png',  // Use dark backgrounds
        '/images/dark_poster_bg_2.png',
      ],
      layout: {
        message: {
          width: 100,
          height: 25,
          fontSize: 16,
          position: { left: 300, top: 150 }
        }
      }
    }
  }}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### Checklist for PnL Card Visibility

- [ ] Background images are dark enough for white text contrast
- [ ] QR code area has a dark or contrasting background
- [ ] Test on both desktop and mobile sharing flows
- [ ] Verify the generated image in a share preview before deploying

## PnL Sharing Configuration

### Basic Configuration via TradingPage

```tsx
import { TradingPage } from "@orderly.network/trading";

const SHARE_PNL_CONFIG = {
  backgroundImage: '/path/to/dark_background.png',
  // Additional configuration options
} as TradingPageProps['sharePnLConfig'];

<TradingPage
  symbol="PERP_BTC_USDC"
  sharePnLConfig={SHARE_PNL_CONFIG}
  tradingViewConfig={TRADING_VIEW_CONFIG}
/>
```

### Referral Code on PnL Cards

Referral codes are displayed on PnL cards **by default** if the user's account has a bound referral code. The referral code input auto-capitalizes (since SDK v2.1.2).

### PnL Card Leverage Display

The PnL social sharing card always displays the user's **maximum account leverage setting**, not the effective leverage of an individual position. This is by design to reflect the user's configured risk parameters.

## Testing PnL Sharing

1. Open a position and close it with a profit or loss
2. Navigate to the PnL sharing option in the UI
3. Preview the generated card image
4. Verify all text, numbers, and QR codes are clearly visible
5. Test sharing to social media platforms and messaging apps
6. Confirm the shared image renders correctly on the target platform

chunks.title: Permissionless Vaults: System Parameters and Configuration
chunks.content:
This guide documents the system-level parameters for Permissionless Vaults on Orderly Network. These parameters are set by the system and apply uniformly to all Permissionless Vaults.

## Fixed System Parameters

The following operational parameters are **not configurable** by Strategy Providers or builders in the current version:

| Parameter | Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Deposit Amount (LP)** | 300 USDC | Minimum amount a liquidity provider can deposit into a vault |
| **Minimum Withdrawal Amount** | 10 USDC | Minimum amount that can be withdrawn from a vault |
| **Period Duration** | 3 days (4,320 minutes) | Duration of each vault operational period |
| **Deposit Lock-up Duration** | 7 days (10,080 minutes) | Lock-up period starting from the beginning of the vault period in which the deposit is processed |
| **Reserve Margin (SP)** | 50,000 USDC | Minimum margin the Strategy Provider must maintain in the vault |

## Understanding the Parameters

### Deposit Lock-up Duration

The 7-day lock-up does **not** start from the exact time of deposit. Instead, it starts from the **beginning of the vault period** in which the deposit is processed. This means:

- If you deposit on day 2 of a 3-day period, your lock-up starts from day 1 of that period
- Effective lock-up may be slightly less than 7 days depending on when within the period the deposit occurs

### Reserve Margin (Strategy Provider)

The Strategy Provider (SP) must maintain a minimum of **50,000 USDC** as reserve margin. This ensures:
- The SP has sufficient skin in the game
- There is a buffer to absorb trading losses
- Alignment of interests between the SP and liquidity providers

### Period Duration

Vaults operate in 3-day periods. At the end of each period:
- PnL is calculated and distributed
- LPs may be able to withdraw (subject to lock-up)
- The vault rolls into the next period

## Future Configurability

These parameters are currently fixed at the system level but **may become configurable** in future versions of the Permissionless Vaults system. Builders and Strategy Providers should monitor Orderly Network announcements for updates.

## Interacting with Vaults via SDK

```tsx
// VaultSDK is available from SDK v2.7.3+ for EVM and Solana
// Use it to interact with Strategy Vaults directly

import { useQuery } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

// Query vault information
const { data: vaultInfo } = useQuery("/v1/vault/info");
```

## Key Considerations for Builders

- Ensure your UI clearly communicates the 300 USDC minimum deposit to users
- Display the lock-up period prominently before users confirm deposits
- Show the current vault period and time remaining
- Clearly indicate when users will be eligible to withdraw based on their deposit timing
