Broker Setup and DEX Configuration
chunks.content:
This guide covers the initial setup process for new brokers/DEXs on Orderly Network, including required information, design configuration, and the Orderly One no-code solution.

## New Broker Setup Requirements

To set up a new broker/DEX on Orderly Network, the following information is required:

### 1. Website Domain
- Your DEX's primary domain (e.g., `trade.mydex.com`)

### 2. Broker Details
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Broker ID | Unique identifier for your DEX (e.g., `mydex`) |
| Broker Name | Display name shown to users |
| Admin Wallet Address | Wallet for broker administration |
| Default Taker Fee | Base taker fee rate (e.g., `0.0005` = 0.05%) |
| Default Maker Fee | Base maker fee rate (e.g., `0.0002` = 0.02%) |

### 3. Design Preferences
- Logo (main and mobile variants)
- Brand colors (primary, secondary, accent)
- Font family preferences
- Overall style (dark/light theme, rounded/sharp corners)

## Theme Builder

Use the [Theme Builder](https://storybook.orderly.network/?path=/story/package-trading-tradingpage--page&globals=theme:custom) to preview and configure design preferences:

1. Open the Theme Builder link
2. Select your desired colors, fonts, and style options
3. Preview the trading interface with your branding
4. Copy the generated CSS code
5. Share with the Orderly team or apply to your project

## Orderly One: No-Code DEX Launcher

[Orderly One](https://dex.orderly.network/) is a no-code solution that allows anyone to launch a perpetual DEX in minutes.

### Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Multi-chain Support | Access to 17+ chains powered by Orderly |
| 130+ Assets | Full access to Orderly's market catalog |
| Up to 100x Leverage | Configurable per-symbol leverage |
| PWA Support | Users can install DEX as a mobile app |
| RWA Configuration | Enable Real-World Asset markets |
| Multisig Admin Wallets | Secure admin key management |
| Amplitude Analytics | Built-in analytics integration |
| Customizable Points | Points system via Fuul integration |
| Graduation Flow | Base chain graduation ($10 fee) |
| Swap Toggle | Add cross-chain swaps for additional revenue |

### Getting Started with Orderly One

1. Visit [dex.orderly.network](https://dex.orderly.network/)
2. Configure branding, appearance, and fees
3. Deploy your DEX (hosted on Orderly's GitHub)
4. Manage via the Orderly One Dashboard

### Updating Your Orderly One DEX

Updates are pushed automatically. Click **"Update DEX"** in the Orderly One Dashboard to apply new SDK updates and features.

### Migrating from Custom SDK to Orderly One

1. Create your DEX using Orderly One at [dex.orderly.network/dex](https://dex.orderly.network/dex)
2. Notify the Orderly team to link your current `brokerID` to the new DEX
3. The DEX will be hosted on Orderly's GitHub with automatic updates

## Broker Admin Setup

To perform broker-level operations (setting fees, managing users):

1. Register a wallet as a normal user under your Broker ID
2. Retrieve the API Key/Secret from the UI's "Manage Account" modal
3. Use these credentials in backend scripts or admin tools

**Note:** The wallet address is **not** the `account_id`. Use the specific `account_id` associated with the registered wallet.

## Fee Configuration

### Default Fees

Set default fees for new users via the Admin Tool or API:

```bash
# Update default broker fee
curl -X POST https://api.orderly.org/v1/broker/fee \
  -H "orderly-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"taker_fee": 0.0005, "maker_fee": 0.0002}'
```

### Custom Fee Tiers

Orderly stores a specific fee rate per user. Brokers implement their own tiering logic:

1. Track user volume via the Builder's Leaderboard API
2. Calculate tier based on your tiering rules
3. Update user fee rates via the admin API

### Per-Order Custom Fees

Available after the April 28, 2026 upgrade, builders can configure custom trading fees on a per-order basis.

## Wallet Support

Orderly Network supports most mainstream wallet plugins:

| Wallet | Chains | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| MetaMask | EVM | Standard EVM wallet |
| Rabby Wallet | EVM | Better network switching |
| Phantom | Solana | Primary Solana wallet |
| OKX Wallet | EVM + Solana | Multi-chain |
| Privy Wallet | EVM + Solana | Social login, Google OAuth in Telegram Mini Apps |
| WalletConnect | EVM | Broad wallet support |
| Abstract Global Wallet | EVM | Abstract chain |

### Web3Auth Custom Wallet Connection

Web3Auth custom wallet connection is not natively supported by Orderly One and requires implementing a custom wallet connection provider. See the [Custom Wallet Connection Provider docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/react/wallet#custom-wallet-connection-provider).

## Integration Documentation

Official documentation for building on Orderly Network:
- **Main Docs:** [orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/building-on-omnichain](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/building-on-omnichain)
- **SDK Overview:** [orderly.network/docs/sdks/overview](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/overview)
- **Migration Guide:** [orderly.network/docs/sdks/migrate](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/migrate)

chunks.title: SDK Integration Options and Approaches
chunks.content:
Orderly Network offers multiple integration paths to suit different development needs, ranging from no-code launchers to low-level API access. Choosing the right approach depends on your desired level of customization and time-to-market.

### 1. Orderly One (No-Code Launcher)
The fastest way to launch a DEX. Orderly One is a no-code/low-code platform that allows anyone to create and launch a fully functional perpetual DEX in minutes.

- **Best for:** Teams wanting immediate deployment without frontend development.
- **Features:** Multi-chain support, PWA installation, RWA configuration, multisig admin wallets, Amplitude analytics, customizable points system (via Fuul), graduation flow via Base, and manual DEX upgrade detection.
- **Reference:** [Orderly One Platform](https://dex.orderly.network/)
- **Note:** Over 1,500 DEXs have been created using Orderly One. Builders can fork their DEX repository from the dashboard for custom modifications, but automatic SDK updates will no longer apply after forking.

### 2. Components SDK (React Components)
Pre-built, themed React components that handle the full trading experience, including the order book, trading forms, and portfolio views.

- **Best for:** Builders who want to ship quickly with minimal UI development but need more control than Orderly One.
- **Customization:** Primarily via theming (CSS variables), configuration props, and the v3 Plugin System.
- **Reference:** [Components SDK Docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/react/overview) | [Broker Template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-template)

### 3. Hooks SDK (React Hooks)
Offers more flexibility than the Components SDK. You build your own custom UI components while using Orderly's React hooks to handle data fetching, authentication, and order management.

- **Best for:** Teams requiring a fully custom UI/UX who are comfortable with React.
- **Customization:** Full control over the UI layer; logic handled by hooks.
- **Reference:** [Hooks SDK Docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/hooks/overview) | [Example DEX](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex)

### 4. Core SDK
The Core SDK (`@orderly.network/core`) is a minimal wrapper around the REST API and EIP-712 signing logic. It is framework-agnostic and can be used with vanilla JavaScript, Vue, Angular, or mobile frameworks.

- **Best for:** Integrations that do not use React or require very specific architectural control.
- **NPM:** [@orderly.network/core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@orderly.network/core)
- **Note:** Documentation for the Core SDK is currently limited; developers may need to reference the source code or types.

### 5. Direct REST/WebSocket API Integration
For maximum control, integrate directly with Orderly's REST APIs and WebSockets without using any SDK. This requires you to manually implement account registration, EIP-712 signing, and order management.

- **Best for:** Non-standard environments, non-JS backends, or teams who want to implement every layer themselves.
- **Reference:** [Build on Omnichain](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/building-on-omnichain)

### Choosing an Approach
| Approach | Time to Market | Customization | Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Orderly One | ~1 hour | Low (Config-based) | Minimal |
| Components SDK | 1–2 weeks | Medium (Theming + Plugins) | Low–Medium |
| Hooks SDK | 2–3 weeks | High | Medium |
| Core SDK | 3–4 weeks | Very High | High |
| Direct API | 4+ weeks | Total | Very High |

chunks.title: SDK v3 Plugin System and Extensibility
chunks.content:
SDK v3 (released May 2026) introduces a **Frontend Plugin System** and **Module Marketplace**, enabling builders to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of the Orderly trading interface without forking the SDK.

## Overview

The Plugin System allows DEX builders to extend key areas of the trading interface with custom functionality. Instead of maintaining a forked codebase, builders can install plugins from the marketplace or develop their own.

## Extension Points

As of SDK v3.1.3, the following extension points are available:

| Extension Point | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Order Entry** | Add custom order types or modify the order form |
| **Chart Overlays** | Add custom indicators or overlays to TradingView charts |
| **Data List Tabs** | Add custom tabs to the data panel (positions, orders, etc.) |
| **Mobile Trading Layout** | Extend the mobile trading interface |

## Developer Toolchain

The plugin development workflow is supported by:

- **`orderly-devkit` CLI**: Command-line tool for scaffolding, building, and testing plugins
- **Plugin Agent Capabilities**: AI-assisted plugin development features
- **SDK Docs MCP Server**: Model Context Protocol server for AI agent integration

### Getting Started with Plugin Development

```bash
# Install the devkit
npm install -g @orderly.network/devkit

# Scaffold a new plugin
orderly-devkit create-plugin my-custom-order-type

# Build and test locally
orderly-devkit build
orderly-devkit serve
```

## Installing Plugins

Plugins can be installed and configured in your `OrderlyAppProvider`:

```tsx
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react-app";
import { customOrderTypePlugin } from "@my-org/orderly-plugin";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  plugins={[customOrderTypePlugin]}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

## Responsive Breakpoint Changes

SDK v3.0.2 raised the mobile/desktop responsive breakpoint from **768px to 1024px**. Builders with custom CSS media queries should update their breakpoints accordingly.

## Version History

| Version | Key Changes |
| :--- | :--- |
| v3.0.0 | Initial Plugin System and Module Marketplace |
| v3.0.1 | Devkit CLI and plugin agent improvements |
| v3.0.2 | Responsive breakpoint change (768px → 1024px), critical bug fixes |
| v3.0.3 | Permissionless listing symbol display fix on mobile |
| v3.0.4 | **High-mandatory**: Wallet registration request update |
| v3.1.0 | RTL language support (Arabic, Persian, Hebrew) |
| v3.1.1 | Pre-TGE perpetual market support |
| v3.1.3 | Expanded extension points, Crypto market category, K-line optimization |

chunks.title: Mandatory and Critical SDK Upgrades
chunks.content:
Certain SDK releases contain critical security patches or infrastructure changes that are mandatory for continued operation. This guide tracks these upgrades and their impact.

## Critical Upgrade Tracker

### SDK v2.12.3 — Solana Multi-DVN Security Upgrade
**Priority: Very High (Mandatory for Solana-integrated DEXs)**

The LayerZero V2 security model for the Solana Vault was upgraded from a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) to a **3-of-3 consensus model** using three independent DVNs.

- **Impact:** DEXs without this upgrade may experience failures with Solana deposits and withdrawals.
- **Action:** Upgrade to v2.12.3 or later immediately.
- **Note:** Temporary withdrawal delays occurred after migration while new DVNs ramped up processing speed.

### SDK v3.0.4 — Wallet Registration Update
**Priority: High-Mandatory**

Contains a critical feature update for wallet registration requests.

- **Impact:** The current registration process continues to work temporarily but may encounter issues in the future without this upgrade.
- **Action:** Upgrade to v3.0.4 or later. Orderly One builders can apply via the platform dashboard.

### SDK v2.11.2 — Isolated Margin Infrastructure
**Priority: Mandatory for Isolated Margin**

Contains a critical fix for Privy login (duplicate Solana addresses bug) and infrastructure upgrades required for isolated margin mode.

- **Action:** Required if enabling isolated margin trading.

### SDK v2.5.1 — Multi-Collateral Support
**Priority: Essential for Multi-Collateral**

Enables multi-collateral deposit functionality (USDT, ETH, BNB, SOL as collateral).

- **Action:** Required to offer non-USDC collateral options.

### SDK v2.3.0 — BNB Chain Support
**Priority: Mandatory for BNB Chain**

Required for BNB Chain integration. USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly supports 6 decimals for deposits/withdrawals.

- **Action:** Upgrade if supporting BNB Chain, or use `chainFilter` to exclude it.

## Applying Upgrades

### For SDK Builders
```bash
# Update all Orderly packages to the same version
npm install @orderly.network/react-app@latest @orderly.network/hooks@latest
# Ensure all @orderly.network/* packages are aligned
```

### For Orderly One Builders
1. Navigate to **My Dex** in the Orderly One dashboard
2. Click **Upgrade Dex** to apply the latest SDK version
3. **Note:** If you've forked your repository, you must handle updates manually

## Monitoring for Updates

- Join the Orderly builder Telegram/Discord groups for release notifications
- Monitor the SDK changelog in documentation
- Subscribe to GitHub release notifications on Orderly repositories

chunks.title: Advanced Trading Features: Margin Modes, TP/SL, and Order Types
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK supports a comprehensive set of trading features including multiple margin modes, advanced order types, and sophisticated TP/SL management.

## Margin Modes

### Cross Margin (Default)
- Leverage is account-wide; all positions share the same collateral pool
- The leverage slider sets the **maximum allowed leverage**, not the actual leverage used per trade
- Maximum account leverage: 100x (since SDK v2.2.0)

### Isolated Margin (SDK v2.11.0+)
- Margin is allocated per-position, limiting risk to the assigned amount
- Rolled out gradually across Orderly DEXs; requires backend activation
- SDK v2.12.0+ displays ISO/Cross labels on TradingView position lines
- SDK v3.1.0 fixed max-out order rejection (reserves taker fee buffer)
- SDK v3.1.3 fixed reduce-only validation when closing from TradingView lines

```tsx
// Check current margin mode
const { marginMode } = useAccount();

// Switch margin mode (per-symbol)
await account.setMarginMode("PERP_BTC_USDC", "ISOLATED");
```

### Symbol-Level Leverage (SDK v2.7.3+)
Configure leverage per symbol instead of account-wide:

```tsx
const [maxLeverage, { update }] = useLeverage();
await update({ 
  leverage: 50, 
  symbol: "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  margin_mode: "ISOLATED" 
});
```

## Advanced Order Types

### Trailing Stop Orders (SDK v2.6.3+)
Activate at a trigger price, track price extremes, and execute on retrace.

### Scaled Orders (SDK v2.4.1+)
Place multiple limit orders across a defined price range with customizable distribution.
- Terminology updated in v2.6.0: "Upper/Lower Price" → "Start/End Price"

### One-Click Reverse Position (SDK v2.8.6+)
Instantly close a current position and open the opposite position in one action.
- v2.8.9: Improved edge case handling
- v2.12.3: Added Estimated PnL display in modal

### TP/SL with Limit Orders (SDK v2.6.0+)
- **Partial TP/SL:** Supports both market and limit execution
- **Full Position TP/SL:** Supports market orders only
- **Chart Integration (v2.6.1+):** Set TP/SL directly from TradingView charts
- **Edit Pending (v2.6.2+):** Modify TP/SL on pending orders
- **Mark Price Logic (v2.12.2+):** Chart-dragging uses mark price instead of entry price, enabling lock-profit stop-loss scenarios
- **Offset Values (v2.12.3+):** Offset and Offset% calculated from Mark Price

```tsx
import { useTPSLOrder } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [order, { setValue, submit }] = useTPSLOrder({
  symbol: "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  average_open_price: 60000,
  position_qty: 0.1
});

// Set TP by PnL amount
setValue("tp_pnl", 100);

// Set SL by offset percentage from mark price
setValue("sl_offset_percent", 5);

await submit();
```

## Multi-Collateral Support (SDK v2.5.1+)

Users can deposit assets other than USDC as trading collateral:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
| :--- | :--- |
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT, USDC |

## Deposit Zap-In (SDK v2.10.1+)

Allows users to deposit any token; it's automatically swapped to supported collateral:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit={true}  // Enable Zap-In
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings and Market Categories
chunks.content:
Orderly supports a **Permissionless Listing Framework** that allows new markets to be listed without the standard centralized approval process. Builders must ensure their frontend properly handles dynamically listed symbols.

## How Permissionless Listings Work

New markets (crypto tokens, stocks like $AAPL/$AMZN/$MSFT, and other assets) can be listed permissionlessly. When new markets are added:

1. Orderly announces the new listing
2. Builders must sync their frontend configuration to support the new symbols
3. Users can immediately trade the new markets

## SDK Support

### Full UI Rendering (SDK v2.12.0+)
SDK v2.12.0 and later include complete UI rendering and trading support for permissionlessly listed symbols. No additional configuration is needed beyond keeping the SDK updated.

### Mobile Display Fix (SDK v3.0.3+)
Fixed an issue where permissionless symbols showed empty values for:
- Interval
- Funding Cap/Floor
- Estimated Funding Fee

...in the funding rate modal on mobile devices.

### K-Line History Optimization (SDK v3.1.3+)
The chart now stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, reducing unnecessary API calls and improving stability for newly listed markets.

## Market Categories

### RWA Markets (SDK v2.8.0+)
Real-World Asset markets are supported with dedicated UI elements:
- **Stock Indices:** $SPX500, $NAS100
- **Precious Metals:** Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG) — up to 20x leverage
- **Individual Stocks:** $NVDA, $GOOGL, $TSLA, $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT — up to 20x leverage
- **Forex Pairs:** $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD
- **Crude Oil:** CL/WTI, BZ/Brent

SDK v2.8.13 added a dedicated RWA tab on the Market page.

### Crypto Market Category (SDK v3.1.3+)
A dedicated Crypto market category was added across:
- Market Selector
- Market Search
- Market Sidebar
- Markets Page

This separates RWA and Crypto markets for better discoverability.

### Custom Asset Categories (SDK v2.12.0+)
Builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  assetCategories={[
    { id: "defi", label: "DeFi", symbols: ["PERP_UNI_USDC", "PERP_AAVE_USDC"] },
    { id: "meme", label: "Meme Coins", symbols: ["PERP_DOGE_USDC", "PERP_PEPE_USDC"] }
  ]}
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

## Pre-TGE Markets (SDK v3.1.1+)

Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) perpetual markets enable builders to offer perpetual trading before a token's official launch. This allows users to trade perpetual contracts on tokens not yet available on spot markets.

## Handling New Listings Programmatically

```tsx
import { useSymbolsInfo } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

function MarketMonitor() {
  const symbols = useSymbolsInfo();
  
  useEffect(() => {
    // React to new symbols being added
    const newSymbols = Object.keys(symbols).filter(
      s => !previouslyKnownSymbols.has(s)
    );
    if (newSymbols.length > 0) {
      notifyUsersOfNewMarkets(newSymbols);
    }
  }, [symbols]);
  
  return null;
}
```

## Delisted Markets

Orderly does not natively support re-listing a delisted permissionless market through the API. Contact the Orderly support team to manually revert delisting status or reactivate a market.

chunks.title: Deposit Features: Exclusive Receiver, Zap-In, and Multi-Collateral
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK provides several advanced deposit features to improve user onboarding and capital efficiency.

## Exclusive Receiver Address (SDK v2.12.0+)

Builders can configure a **dedicated deposit address** for their users. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits — **no gas fees or wallet connection required** from the user.

### How It Works
1. Builder configures an exclusive receiver address via the admin dashboard
2. Users are shown this dedicated address for deposits
3. Funds sent to the address are automatically detected and credited to the user's trading account
4. No wallet signature or gas payment needed from the user

### Use Cases
- Simplified onboarding for users unfamiliar with Web3
- CEX-like deposit experience
- Institutional deposit workflows

## Deposit Zap-In (SDK v2.10.1+)

Allows users to deposit **any token** into their Orderly perpetual account. The token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral during the deposit process.

### Enabling Zap-In

```tsx
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react-app";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit={true}  // Enable Zap-In Deposit
>
  <TradingPage />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### Features
- Supports dynamic chain configuration via API
- Automatic routing to best swap path
- User sees estimated collateral received before confirming

## Multi-Collateral Support (SDK v2.5.1+)

Users can deposit assets other than USDC as trading collateral.

### Supported Collateral by Chain

| Chain | Assets |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Ethereum** | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| **BNB Chain** | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| **Base** | USDC, ETH |
| **Arbitrum** | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| **Solana** | SOL, USDT, USDC |

### Implementation Notes
- Brokers must upgrade to SDK v2.5.1+ to enable multi-collateral
- Collateral haircuts apply (ETH valued at discount vs USDC)
- Use `useCollateral` hook to display multi-asset balances

```tsx
const { totalCollateral, freeCollateral, totalValue } = useCollateral();
// totalValue reflects USD value of all collateral assets combined
```

## Solana Deposits

Solana deposits involve pure on-chain interactions by calling the `deposit` function against the Solana Vault contract:

```
Vault Address: ErBmAD61mGFKvrFNaTJuxoPwqrS8GgtwtqJTJVjFWx9Q
```

**Important:** When depositing on Solana, you must fetch the deposit fee and include it in the value of the deposit call, because LayerZero cross-chain fees are calculated on-chain and can vary.

```typescript
// Example: Fetch deposit fee before executing
const depositFee = await fetchDepositFee(chain, token);
const totalValue = depositAmount + depositFee;
```

## Strategy Vaults (VaultSDK - SDK v2.7.3+)

The VaultSDK provides dedicated interaction with Orderly Strategy Vaults:
- Supports both EVM and Solana chains
- Direct SDK integration for deposits, withdrawals, and vault data
- The Omnivault allows USDC deposits used by market makers for liquidity provision

## Withdrawal Notes

### Withdrawable Balance Formula
Available to withdraw differs from free collateral when there is unsettled PnL:

```
withdrawable = unsettledPnL > 0 
  ? freeCollateral - unsettledPnL 
  : freeCollateral
```

### External Wallet Withdrawals (SDK v2.8.9+)
Users can withdraw to external Web3 wallets. Brokers must apply to the Orderly team to enable this feature.

### Vault Withdrawal Fix (SDK v2.12.4)
Fixed an issue where vault withdrawals were blocked when vaults were in 'closed' or 'closing' state.

SDK v3 Plugin System and Extensibility
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK v3 introduces a powerful Frontend Plugin System and Module Marketplace, enabling builders to extend the trading interface without forking the SDK. This architecture allows DEXs to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of Orderly's trading UI.

## Plugin System Overview

The plugin system provides extension points across key areas of the Trading page:

- **Order Entry**: Add custom order types or modify the order form
- **Chart Overlays**: Inject custom indicators or visual elements on TradingView charts
- **Data List Tabs**: Add custom tabs to the data panel (positions, orders, history)
- **Mobile Trading Layout**: Extend the mobile trading experience

## Key Version Milestones

| Version | Feature |
| :--- | :--- |
| v3.0.0 | Initial Plugin System and Module Marketplace launch |
| v3.0.1 | Enhanced `orderly-devkit` CLI and plugin agent capabilities |
| v3.0.2 | Mobile/desktop responsive breakpoint raised from 768px to 1024px |
| v3.1.3 | Expanded Trading page extension points (Order Entry, Chart Overlays, Data List Tabs, Mobile layout) |

## Developer Toolchain

The SDK v3 plugin ecosystem includes:

- **`orderly-devkit` CLI**: Command-line tool for scaffolding, building, and testing plugins
- **Plugin Agent**: Capabilities for automated plugin management
- **SDK Docs MCP Server**: Machine-readable documentation for AI-assisted development

## Responsive Breakpoint Change

Starting from v3.0.2, the mobile/desktop responsive breakpoint was raised from **768px to 1024px**. If you have custom CSS media queries, update them accordingly:

```css
/* Old breakpoint */
@media (max-width: 768px) { /* mobile styles */ }

/* New breakpoint (v3.0.2+) */
@media (max-width: 1024px) { /* mobile styles */ }
```

## RTL Language Support (v3.1.0+)

SDK v3.1.0 added full right-to-left (RTL) language support for Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew. Layouts, typography, and components automatically mirror for RTL locales. No additional configuration is required — the SDK detects the locale and applies mirrored layouts.

## Pre-TGE Market Support (v3.1.1+)

SDK v3.1.1 enables builders to offer perpetual trading markets before a token's official Token Generation Event (TGE). To list a pre-TGE market:

1. Provide the Orderly team with the token name, initial price, and price tick size for oracle configuration
2. Once the oracle is set up, proceed with listing via the permissionless listing flow in the admin portal
3. Test on testnet first with arbitrary values (e.g., Price $1, Tick $0.001)

The insurance fund requirement remains at $25,000.

## Crypto Market Category (v3.1.3+)

SDK v3.1.3 adds a dedicated **Crypto** market category across all market discovery experiences:
- Market Selector
- Market Search
- Market Sidebar
- Markets page

This separates crypto assets from RWA (Real-World Assets) and other categories for better user navigation.

## Upgrade Notes

- Upgrades from v2.x to v3.x are **backward compatible**
- Deploy to staging first before production
- Orderly One builders can apply upgrades via the Orderly One platform
- The `orderly-devkit` CLI should be updated to match your SDK version

chunks.title: Advanced Order Types: TP/SL, Trailing Stop, and Scaled Orders
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK supports several advanced order types beyond basic limit and market orders. This guide covers Take Profit/Stop Loss (TP/SL), Trailing Stop, and Scaled Orders.

## Take Profit / Stop Loss (TP/SL)

TP/SL orders are stop orders with `reduce_only` enabled. To create both TP and SL for a position, submit two separate orders.

### Creating TP/SL Orders

Use the `useTPSLOrder` hook for TP/SL-specific operations:

```tsx
import { useTPSLOrder } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [order, { setValue, submit, validate }] = useTPSLOrder({
  symbol: "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  average_open_price: 60000,
  position_qty: 0.1
});

// Set TP by PnL amount
setValue("tp_pnl", 100);

// Set SL by percentage offset
setValue("sl_offset_percent", 0.05); // 5%

// Submit
await submit();
```

### Fetching TP/SL Orders

Use `useOrderStream` with the `includes` parameter to fetch algorithmic orders:

```tsx
import { useOrderStream, AlgoOrderRootType } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [orders] = useOrderStream({
  includes: [
    AlgoOrderRootType.TP_SL,
    AlgoOrderRootType.POSITIONAL_TP_SL
  ]
});
```

### Canceling TP/SL Orders

**Important:** Use `cancelAlgoOrder` (not `cancelOrder`) to cancel TP/SL and other algorithmic orders.

### TP/SL Feature Evolution

| SDK Version | Feature |
| :--- | :--- |
| v2.6.0 | Partial TP/SL (market + limit), Full Position TP/SL (market only) |
| v2.6.1 | Set TP/SL directly from TradingView charts |
| v2.6.2 | Edit TP/SL on pending orders |
| v2.12.2 | TP/SL uses mark price for chart-dragging (enables lock-profit stop-loss) |
| v2.12.3 | Offset and Offset% values calculated from Mark Price |

### TP/SL Notes

- When creating TP/SL for an entire position, quantity may show as `0` — this represents the full position
- Offset percentage inputs use decimal format (`0.1` = 10%)
- Starting from v2.12.2, chart-dragging interactions use **mark price** instead of entry price for TP/SL detection

## Trailing Stop Orders (v2.6.3+)

Trailing Stop orders activate at a trigger price, track price extremes, and execute on retrace:

1. **Activation**: Order becomes active when the market reaches the trigger price
2. **Tracking**: The stop price follows the market price at a specified distance
3. **Execution**: When the market retraces by the trailing amount, the order executes

## Scaled Orders (v2.4.1+)

Scaled Orders allow placing multiple limit orders across a price range with customizable distribution:

- Define a start price and end price (labeled "Start Price" and "End Price" from v2.6.0+)
- Set the number of orders and total quantity
- Choose distribution type (flat, ascending, descending)

## Order Tags (v2.6.3+)

The Order API passes `order_tag` to distinguish orders originating from different routes or UI components. This is useful for analytics and tracking order sources.

## TradingView Chart Integration for TP/SL

When using TradingView charts with the Orderly SDK:

- **v2.6.1+**: Users can drag TP/SL lines directly on the chart
- **v2.8.6+**: Enhanced stop-loss protection prevents placing SL too close to liquidation price
- **v2.10.2+**: TP/SL lines display position quantity and PnL details
- **v2.12.0+**: Liquidation price line toggle available
- **v2.12.2+**: Chart-dragging uses mark price for lock-profit scenarios

```tsx
<TradingPage
  symbol={symbol}
  tradingViewConfig={TRADING_VIEW_CONFIG}
  sharePnLConfig={SHARE_PNL_CONFIG}
/>
```

chunks.title: Multi-Collateral, Isolated Margin, and RWA Markets
chunks.content:
This guide covers three major feature areas: multi-collateral deposits, isolated margin trading, and Real-World Asset (RWA) markets.

## Multi-Collateral Support (v2.5.1+)

Multi-collateral allows users to deposit and trade with multiple native assets without swapping to USDC first.

### Supported Assets by Chain

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
| :--- | :--- |
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT |

### Enabling Multi-Collateral

Upgrade to SDK v2.5.1 or later. From v2.5.2+, deposit assets also support auto-matching collateral.

### BNB Chain USDC Precision Note

**Critical:** USDC on BNB Chain uses **18 decimals** on-chain, but Orderly only supports **6 decimals** for deposits and withdrawals. Always refer to the `decimals` field in `chain_details` from the Public Token API:

```tsx
import { useQuery } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { data: tokens } = useQuery("/v1/public/token");
// Always use token.decimals from this response, not hardcoded values
```

## Isolated Margin Mode (v2.11.0+)

Isolated margin mode allows traders to allocate specific collateral to individual positions, limiting risk to the allocated amount.

### Key SDK Versions

| Version | Update |
| :--- | :--- |
| v2.11.0 | Initial isolated margin SDK support |
| v2.11.2 | Mandatory infrastructure upgrade |
| v2.12.0 | ISO/Cross margin labels on TradingView chart position lines |
| v3.0.0 | Fixed leverage update after switching margin mode |
| v3.1.0 | Fixed ISO max-out order rejection (reserves taker fee buffer) |
| v3.1.3 | Fixed margin mode sent when closing from TradingView position lines |

### Symbol-Level Leverage (v2.7.3+)

Leverage is configured per-symbol per-margin-mode. For example, BTC-PERP can have 10x Cross and 20x Isolated simultaneously:

```tsx
import { useLeverage } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [maxLeverage, { update }] = useLeverage();

// Set leverage for a specific symbol and margin mode
await update({
  leverage: 20,
  symbol: "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  margin_mode: "ISOLATED"
});
```

### ISO Max-Out Order Fix (v3.1.0)

Prior to v3.1.0, maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% slider was rejected with "margin will be insufficient after." The SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

## RWA (Real-World Asset) Markets

Orderly supports perpetual markets for real-world assets with up to 20x leverage, tradeable 24/7.

### Available RWA Markets

| Category | Symbols |
| :--- | :--- |
| Indexes | $SPX500, $NAS100 |
| Precious Metals | $XAU (Gold), $XAG (Silver) |
| US Stocks | $NVDA, $TSLA, $GOOGL |
| Forex | $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD |
| Commodities | $CL (WTI Crude), $BZ (Brent Crude) |

**RWA Base Fees:** 0% maker / 0.045% taker

### RWA Market Status

Use the `/v1/public/rwa/info` API with the base symbol to determine market trading hours:

```tsx
const { data: rwaInfo } = useQuery("/v1/public/rwa/info?symbol=PERP_NVDA_USDC");
```

**Note:** RWA markets can still be traded on Orderly even when the underlying traditional market is closed.

### RWA UI Features

- **v2.8.0**: Dedicated RWA Market UI elements
- **v2.8.13**: RWA tab on Market page
- **v2.10.2**: Separate RWA and Crypto market sections
- **v3.1.3**: Dedicated Crypto category (separating from RWA)

chunks.title: Deposit, Withdrawal, and Asset Management
chunks.content:
This guide covers deposit and withdrawal flows, including advanced features like Deposit Zap-in, Exclusive Receiver Addresses, and external wallet withdrawals.

## Deposit Zap-in (v2.10.1+)

Deposit Zap-in allows users to deposit any token into their Orderly perp account. The token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral during the deposit process.

### Enabling Zap-in

Set the `enableSwapDeposit` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider`:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

Zap-in also supports dynamic chain configuration via API.

## Exclusive Receiver Address (v2.12.0+)

Builders can configure a dedicated deposit address for each user. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits — **no gas fees or wallet connection required** from the user.

### Supported Chains

- Arbitrum
- Ethereum
- Base
- Optimism
- BNB Chain

**Note:** Solana support for exclusive deposit addresses is in development.

### Use Case

This feature is ideal for users who want to deposit directly from centralized exchanges to their DEX account without interacting with a wallet interface.

## External Web3 Wallet Withdrawals (v2.8.9+)

Users can withdraw to external Web3 wallets (not just their connected wallet). **Brokers must apply to enable this feature.**

From v2.8.9+, users can also search by address or account ID when withdrawing to other Orderly accounts.

## Internal Transfers (v2.4.1+)

Enable direct withdrawals to another Orderly account using the recipient's `account_id`:

```tsx
// Internal transfer to another Orderly account
const withdrawalPayload = {
  token: "USDC",
  amount: "100",
  account_id: "recipient_account_id" // Internal transfer
};
```

## Retrieving Deposit/Withdrawal History

Use `usePrivateQuery` with the asset history endpoint:

```tsx
import { usePrivateQuery } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { data: assetHistory } = usePrivateQuery("/v1/asset/history");
```

Or use the `useAssetsHistory` hook for filtered queries:

```tsx
import { useAssetsHistory } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const [data, { meta, isLoading }] = useAssetsHistory({
  token: "USDC",
  side: "DEPOSIT",
  startTime: Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
  endTime: Date.now(),
  page: 1,
  pageSize: 20
});
```

**Note:** Withdrawal transaction hashes may take time to appear due to block confirmation requirements (e.g., ~500 blocks on Polygon).

## Deposit Status Display

Use `useDepositStatusScript` from `@orderly.network/ui-transfer`:

```tsx
import { useDepositStatusScript } from "@orderly.network/ui-transfer";

const {
  pendingCount,
  completedCount,
  canTrade,
  estimatedTime,
  onClose
} = useDepositStatusScript();
```

## Retrieving Fees

### Deposit Fees

```tsx
const { setQuantity, depositFee } = useDeposit({ /* ... */ });
setQuantity("100"); // Triggers fee calculation
// depositFee is in wei — convert to token decimals manually
```

### Withdrawal Fees

```tsx
import { useChains } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { data: chains } = useChains();
// Access chains[].network_infos.withdrawal_fee
```

## Settling PnL Before Withdrawal

Users cannot withdraw the full amount of profits unless PnL is settled first:

```tsx
import { useWithdraw, useAccountInstance } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { unsettledPnl } = useWithdraw();
const { account } = useAccountInstance();

if (unsettledPnl > 0) {
  await account.settle();
}
// Now proceed with withdrawal
```

## Solana Multi-DVN Security Upgrade (v2.12.3)

**Mandatory for all Solana-integrated DEXs.** SDK v2.12.3 upgrades the Solana Vault contract from a single DVN to a 3-of-3 consensus model using three independent Decentralized Verifier Networks under LayerZero V2. DEXs without this upgrade may experience issues with Solana deposits and withdrawals.

chunks.title: TradingView Integration and Chart Configuration
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK integrates with TradingView's Advanced Charts library for professional-grade charting. This guide covers licensing, configuration, and customization.

## Licensing Requirements

Orderly uses the **TradingView Advanced Charts** library, which requires a free license from TradingView:

1. Apply at https://www.tradingview.com/advanced-charts/
2. Click "Get the Library" to request access
3. Add the library during build time (e.g., as a git submodule)

**Important:** The SDK requires the library to be passed via path configuration, so it does not need to be included in public repositories (complying with TV license clause 2.5(b)).

### TradingView Version Compatibility

Starting from **TV v29**, `createOrderLine`, `createPositionLine`, and `createExecutionShape` are **Trading Platform (paid) only** APIs. The Orderly SDK uses these to display order/position lines on charts.

**Recommendation:** Use the TV version bundled/recommended by Orderly (v27.x) or obtain a Trading Platform license for position display features.

## Basic Configuration

Pass the TradingView configuration to the `TradingPage` component:

```tsx
import { TradingPage } from "@orderly.network/trading";

const TRADING_VIEW_CONFIG = {
  scriptSRC: "/assets/chart/charting_library/charting_library.js",
  library_path: "/assets/chart/charting_library/"
};

<TradingPage
  symbol="PERP_ETH_USDC"
  tradingViewConfig={TRADING_VIEW_CONFIG}
  sharePnLConfig={SHARE_PNL_CONFIG}
/>
```

## Custom CSS and Overrides

Pass custom CSS via the `tradingViewCustomCssUrl` prop and overrides via the overrides object:

```tsx
const TRADING_VIEW_CONFIG = {
  scriptSRC: "/charting_library/charting_library.js",
  library_path: "/charting_library/",
  customCssUrl: "/tradingview/chart.css", // Must be prefixed with root path
  overrides: {
    "paneProperties.background": "#1a1a2e",
    "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.upColor": "#00c853"
  }
};
```

**Note:** You may need to clear the browser's localStorage for overrides to take effect.

## PnL Sharing Configuration

Configure the `sharePnLConfig` prop for PnL sharing features:

```tsx
const SHARE_PNL_CONFIG = {
  backgroundImage: '/path/to/background.png',
  // other config options
} as TradingPageProps['sharePnLConfig'];

<TradingPage
  symbol={symbol}
  sharePnLConfig={SHARE_PNL_CONFIG}
  tradingViewConfig={TRADING_VIEW_CONFIG}
/>
```

## Chart Features by SDK Version

| Version | Feature |
| :--- | :--- |
| v2.6.1 | Set TP/SL directly from chart |
| v2.8.6 | Enhanced SL protection on chart |
| v2.10.2 | TP/SL line details (position qty and PnL) |
| v2.12.0 | ISO/Cross Margin labels on position lines, Liquidation price line toggle |
| v2.12.2 | TP/SL chart-dragging uses mark price |
| v3.1.3 | Chart Overlays plugin extension point |

## Data Feed API

The TradingView history bars endpoint is available at:
```
GET /v1/public/tradingview/history-bars
```

However, it is **highly recommended** to use the Orderly SDK for TradingView integration, as significant data manipulation is needed to update charts in real time using WebSockets.

## Alternative: Simple Charts

If you don't have a TradingView Advanced Charts license yet, you can use the TradingView Simple Charts library as a temporary alternative. See the example at `OrderlyNetwork/example-dex` repository.

## Optimized K-line History (v3.1.3+)

Starting from v3.1.3, the chart stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time. This prevents unnecessary API calls for newly listed markets.

chunks.title: Wallet Integration and Authentication Patterns
chunks.content:
This guide covers wallet integration patterns, authentication flows, and common wallet-related issues when building with the Orderly SDK.

## Custom Wallet Connector Integration (SDK v2)

For SDK v2, implement a custom wallet connector by providing a `WalletConnectorContext.Provider` that wraps the Orderly provider.

```tsx
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react-app";
import { WalletConnectorContext } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

// Your custom wallet adapter
const walletAdapter = new DefaultEVMWalletAdapter(new EthersProvider());

function App() {
  return (
    <WalletConnectorContext.Provider value={yourWalletContext}>
      <OrderlyAppProvider
        brokerId="your_broker"
        networkId="mainnet"
        walletAdapters={[walletAdapter]}
      >
        <YourApp />
      </OrderlyAppProvider>
    </WalletConnectorContext.Provider>
  );
}
```

The main change in v2 is the `walletAdapters` prop on the config provider.

## Privy Wallet Integration

Privy is supported as a wallet provider starting from SDK v2.2. Implement a custom `PrivyProvider` by replacing the default `EthersProvider`:

```tsx
// See: OrderlyNetwork/example-dex/app/providers/OrderlyProvider.tsx
<PrivyProvider appId={YOUR_PRIVY_APP_ID}>
  <OrderlyAppProvider
    brokerId="your_broker"
    networkId="mainnet"
  >
    {children}
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</PrivyProvider>
```

### Privy Fixes by Version
- **v2.8.13**: Fixed network switching issues with Privy login
- **v2.11.2**: Fixed duplicate Solana addresses via Privy

## Account Abstraction (AA) Support

Orderly uses wallet adapters, so if the adapter supports Coinbase Smart Wallet or Base Accounts, Orderly can support it. For AA, builders have customized Privy login (which supports smart wallets).

**Known Issue:** There is a tracked SDK issue with Base Account/Coinbase Smart Wallet signature failures during account creation.

## Delegate Signer (Contract Accounts)

Trading with Contract Accounts (CAs) is supported via the **Delegate Signer** feature, but it is **not implemented in any SDK** (Components, Hooks, or Core).

CAs cannot directly interact with Orderly because the platform relies on EIP-712 signing, which requires an EOA. The delegate signer flow allows an EOA to delegate signing authority to a CA.

```typescript
// Example implementation (without trading):
// https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-registration
```

## API Key Management

Orderly API keys and secrets are automatically saved to localStorage by the SDK when created via `createOrderlyKey`.

### Retrieving Keys Programmatically

```tsx
const { account } = useAccount();
const orderlyKey = account.keyStore.getOrderlyKey();
```

Keys are stored under `orderly_${networkId}_${walletAddress}` in localStorage.

### Removing a Key

POST to `https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/remove_orderly_key` with `orderly_key` in the body.

### IP Restrictions

Set IP restrictions via the private API endpoint for enhanced security.

## Listening for Wallet Disconnect

```tsx
import { useAccount, AccountStatusEnum } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { state } = useAccount();

useEffect(() => {
  if (state.status === AccountStatusEnum.NotConnected) {
    // Handle disconnect
  }
}, [state]);
```

## Chain Switching

Switch the active chain for data hooks:

```tsx
const { account } = useAccount();
account.switchChainId(targetChainId);
```

Once switched, all underlying hooks (e.g., `useCollateral`, `useMarketsStream`) return data for the selected chain. **Note:** Trading data like orders and positions are aggregated across all chains.

## Chain Filtering

Add or exclude chains using `chainFilter`:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum, Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story
    ],
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

## Common Wallet Issues

### iOS Safari WalletConnect Redirect Loop

**Cause:** WalletConnect WebSocket connections are terminated when the app enters the background on iOS Safari.

**Mitigation:**
1. Use the wallet's built-in in-app browser (MetaMask browser)
2. Ensure latest MetaMask Mobile version
3. Close the DApp and generate a new WalletConnect session
4. Open in Chrome or Safari instead of in-app browsers

### Mobile Deposit Infinite MetaMask Redirect

**Cause:** Wallet-read polling (balance/allowance checks every 3000ms) triggers deep links before WalletConnect session is settled.

**Fix:**
1. Disable wallet reads on page mount
2. Start wallet reads only after explicit user intent
3. Implement a 'readiness gate' to block reads until wallet state stabilizes

### Google OAuth in Telegram Mini Apps (v2.12.3+)

Google blocks OAuth from embedded WebViews. SDK v2.12.3+ detects `window.Telegram?.WebApp` and routes OAuth through the external browser via `Telegram.WebApp.openLink()`.

chunks.title: Trading Calculations: Margin, Leverage, and Liquidation
SDK Integration Options and Approaches
chunks.content:
Orderly Network offers multiple integration paths to suit different development needs, ranging from pre-built UI components to low-level API access. Choosing the right approach depends on your desired level of customization and time-to-market.

### 1. Components SDK (React Components)
This is the fastest way to launch a DEX. It provides pre-built, themed React components that handle the full trading experience, including the order book, trading forms, and portfolio views.

- **Best for:** Builders who want to ship quickly with minimal UI development.
- **Customization:** Primarily via theming (colors, fonts) and configuration props.
- **Reference:** [js-sdk-demo repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/js-sdk-demo) and the hosted SDK demo.

### 2. Hooks SDK (React Hooks)
This approach offers more flexibility than the Components SDK. You build your own custom UI components while using Orderly's React hooks to handle data fetching, authentication, and order management.

- **Best for:** Teams requiring a custom UI/UX who are comfortable with React.
- **Customization:** Full control over the UI layer; logic handled by hooks.
- **Reference:** [example-dex repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex).

### 3. Core SDK
The Core SDK (`@orderly.network/core`) is a minimal wrapper around the REST API and EIP-712 signing logic. It is framework-agnostic and can be used with vanilla JavaScript, Vue, Angular, or mobile frameworks.

- **Best for:** Integrations that do not use React or require very specific architectural control.
- **Note:** Documentation for the Core SDK is currently limited; developers may need to reference the source code or types.

### 4. Direct REST API Integration
For maximum control, you can integrate directly with Orderly's REST APIs and Websockets without using any SDK. This requires you to manually implement account registration, EIP-712 signing, and order management.

- **Best for:** Non-standard environments or teams who want to implement every layer themselves.
- **Reference:** "Build on Omnichain" documentation includes examples in Python, TypeScript, and Java.

### 5. Orderly One (No-Code)
Orderly One is a no-code solution that allows you to define branding, appearance, and fees without writing code. It provides a complete DEX frontend along with a broker ID.

- **Best for:** Teams wanting to deploy a trading interface with minimal coding in ~1 hour.
- **Reference:** [Orderly One Dashboard](https://dex.orderly.network/)

### Choosing an Approach
| Approach | Time to Market | Customization | Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Orderly One | Fastest (~1 hour) | Low (Branding/Fees) | None |
| Components SDK | Fast | Low (Theming) | Low |
| Hooks SDK | Medium | High | Medium |
| Core SDK | Slow | Very High | High |
| Direct API | Slowest | Total | Very High |

### Embedding vs. Standalone
Orderly One is designed to be hosted on a custom domain as a standalone DEX. If you need the DEX embedded as part of an existing application, you should either migrate the Orderly One source code into your own codebase or use the SDK directly.

chunks.title: Advanced Trading Features: TP/SL, Trailing Stops, and Margin Modes
Deposit and Withdrawal Features: Zap-In, Exclusive Receiver, and Multi-Collateral
chunks.content:
The Orderly SDK provides advanced deposit and withdrawal features to streamline user onboarding and fund management.

### Deposit Zap-In (Auto-Swap Deposits)

**SDK v2.10.1+** introduced Deposit Zap-In, which allows users to deposit any token into their Orderly perpetual account. The token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral during the deposit process.

**Enable Zap-In:**
```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit  // Enable Zap-In
>
  <YourApp />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

Zap-In Deposit also supports dynamic chain configuration via API, allowing you to customize which chains and tokens are supported for auto-swapping.

### Exclusive Receiver Address

**SDK v2.12.0+** introduced the Exclusive Receiver Address feature, which allows builders to configure a dedicated deposit address for their users. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits without requiring gas fees or wallet connection from the user.

This feature streamlines the onboarding experience by eliminating the need for users to connect wallets or pay gas fees for deposits.

### Multi-Collateral Support

**SDK v2.5.1+** introduced multi-collateral support, allowing users to deposit multiple assets as collateral for trading.

**Supported Assets by Chain:**
- **Ethereum:** USDC, USDT, ETH
- **BNB Chain:** USDC, USDT
- **Base:** USDC, ETH
- **Arbitrum:** USDC, USDT, ETH

Additional collateral types including SOL, USDT on Solana, BNB on BNB Chain, and WBTC on Ethereum are planned or rolling out.

### External Web3 Wallet Withdrawals

**SDK v2.8.9+** enables withdrawals to external Web3 wallets. However, brokers need to apply to Orderly to enable this feature for their DEX. Users can also search by address or account ID when withdrawing to other Orderly accounts.

### BNB Chain Decimal Precision

**Important:** USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. To avoid precision mismatches, always refer to the `decimals` field in the `chain_details` returned by the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.

```typescript
// Always check decimals from API
const tokenInfo = await fetch('/v1/public/token');
const usdcDecimals = tokenInfo.chain_details.decimals; // Use this value
```

SDK v2.3.0 or later is required for BNB Chain support. If not upgrading, use `chainFilter` to explicitly exclude BNB Chain.

chunks.title: SDK v3 Plugin System and Module Marketplace
chunks.content:
SDK v3 introduces a Frontend Plugin System and Module Marketplace that enables builders and DEXs to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of the Orderly trading interface without forking the SDK.

### Overview

The Plugin System allows you to extend the Orderly trading interface with custom functionality while maintaining compatibility with future SDK updates. This eliminates the need to fork the SDK and manually merge upstream changes.

### Extension Points

The plugin system provides extension points in key areas of the trading interface:

- **Order Entry:** Add custom order types or modify order submission logic
- **Chart Overlays:** Add custom indicators or overlays to TradingView charts
- **Data List Tabs:** Add custom tabs to position/order history sections
- **Mobile Trading Layout:** Customize the mobile trading experience

### Development Tools

The plugin developer toolchain includes:

- **`orderly-devkit` CLI:** Command-line tool for scaffolding, building, and testing plugins
- **Plugin Agent Capabilities:** Enhanced agent features for plugin development
- **SDK Docs MCP Server:** Model Context Protocol server for AI-assisted development

### Getting Started

1. Install the devkit:
```bash
npm install -g @orderly.network/devkit
```

2. Scaffold a new plugin:
```bash
orderly-devkit create-plugin my-custom-plugin
```

3. Develop and test your plugin using the provided development server

4. Publish to the Module Marketplace or distribute privately

### Example: Custom Order Type Plugin

```typescript
// plugin.ts
import { definePlugin } from '@orderly.network/plugin-sdk';

export default definePlugin({
  name: 'custom-order-type',
  version: '1.0.0',
  
  extensions: {
    orderEntry: {
      // Add custom order type to the order form
      orderTypes: [
        {
          id: 'twap',
          label: 'TWAP',
          component: TWAPOrderForm,
          validate: (order) => {
            // Custom validation logic
            return order.quantity > 0;
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
});
```

### Version Requirements

- **SDK v3.0.2+** contains critical bug fixes and is strongly recommended
- **SDK v3.1.3** adds expanded Trading page plugin support and a dedicated Crypto market category
- The mobile/desktop responsive breakpoint was raised from 768px to 1024px in v3.0.2

### Benefits

- **No Forking Required:** Maintain compatibility with SDK updates
- **Modular Architecture:** Install only the plugins you need
- **Community Sharing:** Share plugins via the Module Marketplace
- **Type Safety:** Full TypeScript support with plugin SDK types

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings and Pre-TGE Markets
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports advanced market listing features including Permissionless Listings and Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) perpetual markets.

### Permissionless Listings

Orderly's Permissionless Listing framework allows new markets to be listed without the traditional centralized listing process. External parties can list tokens on Orderly-powered DEXes, and brokers earn 100% of liquidation fees and 50% of transaction fees on permissionless-listed assets.

**SDK Support:**
- **SDK v2.12.0+** provides full UI rendering and trading support for permissionlessly listed symbols
- **SDK v3.0.3** fixed an issue where permissionless listing symbols showed empty values for Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee in the funding rate modal on mobile devices

**Broker Responsibilities:**
When new permissionless markets are listed, brokers must:
1. Sync their frontend configuration to support the new symbols
2. Notify users about newly available markets
3. Ensure their SDK version supports permissionless listings (v2.12.0+)

**Managing Permissionless Listings:**
Permissionless listings can be managed through the Admin Portal, which has a dedicated section for this feature. A promotion allows all tiers to list up to 5 assets with no staking requirements.

**Hiding Risk Notice Bar:**
To hide the risk notice bar for permissionless-listed symbols, add this CSS rule to your theme:

```css
.oui-symbol-info-bar-risk-notice {
  display: none !important;
}
```

### Pre-TGE Perpetual Markets

**SDK v3.1.1+** introduced support for Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) perpetual market listings, enabling builders to offer perpetual trading markets before a token's official TGE.

This feature allows traders to speculate on upcoming token launches and provides builders with a competitive advantage by offering early access to new markets.

**Key Features:**
- Full UI rendering and trading support for Pre-TGE markets
- Proper handling of asset conversion quote estimates (fixed in v3.1.1)
- Integration with existing order management and position tracking

### Custom Asset Categories

**SDK v2.12.0+** allows builders to configure custom asset categories for their UI. No categories are set by default — builders choose which categories to display.

**SDK v3.1.3** added a dedicated Crypto market category across market discovery experiences including:
- Market Selector
- Market Search
- Market Sidebar
- Markets page

### Real-World Asset (RWA) Markets

Orderly supports RWA markets including:
- **Indexes:** $SPX500, $NAS100
- **Precious Metals:** Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG) with up to 20x leverage
- **Individual Stocks:** $NVDA, $TSLA, $GOOGL with up to 20x leverage, tradeable 24/7
- **Forex Pairs:** $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD

**SDK v2.8.0** introduced dedicated RWA Market UI elements, and **SDK v2.10.2** added separate RWA and Crypto market sections on the Markets page.

chunks.title: Multilevel Referral Program and Affiliate System
chunks.content:
Orderly Network provides a comprehensive referral and affiliate system, including a Multilevel Referral Program for scaling growth through multi-tier commission structures.

### Built-in Referral System

Orderly's affiliate program supports two types of referral codes:

1. **General Referral Codes:** Any user who reaches a specified trading volume threshold automatically receives a link with a set fee rebate percentage
2. **Custom Referral Codes:** Manually created codes for KOLs or specific users with higher rebate percentages

Both types allow the affiliate to decide how to split the fee rebate between themselves and the referee. The referee gets a discount on trading fees, and the affiliate receives a daily rebate.

### Multilevel Referral Program

**SDK v2.9.0+** introduced the Multilevel Referral Program, enabling brokers to create multi-tier referral structures where affiliates can earn commissions from their referees' referrals.

**Technical Requirements:**
1. Upgrade to SDK version 2.9.0 or later (Orderly One DEXs should ensure they are running the latest version)
2. Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

**Post-Registration Binding:**
**SDK v2.12.4+** allows users to bind referral codes to existing accounts at any time after account creation, eliminating the need to provide a code during initial registration.

### Integration Guide

**1. Validate Referral Codes:**
Use `useCheckReferralCode` to validate codes from URL parameters (e.g., `?ref=CODE`). This works without wallet connection.

```tsx
import { useCheckReferralCode } from "@orderly.network/hooks";

const { isValid, checkCode } = useCheckReferralCode();

useEffect(() => {
  const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
  const refCode = urlParams.get('ref');
  if (refCode) {
    checkCode(refCode);
  }
}, []);
```

**2. Affiliate Dashboard:**
Use the `@orderly.network/affiliate` package for pre-built dashboard components:

```tsx
import { Dashboard, ReferralProvider } from '@orderly.network/affiliate';

<ReferralProvider
  becomeAnAffiliateUrl="/become-affiliate"
  referralLinkUrl="/referral"
  overwrite={{ shortBrokerName: "MyDEX" }}
>
  <Dashboard.DashboardPage />
</ReferralProvider>
```

**3. Auto-Referral Feature:**
Orderly provides an auto-referral API endpoint that automatically assigns referral codes based on broker-defined rules. See the [Builder Auto-Referral Update API](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/private/builder-auto-referral-update).

### Custom Scoring and Leaderboards

For custom scoring or leaderboard systems based on referrals, brokers need to build their own logic on top of Orderly's volume data APIs. The SDK provides the referral infrastructure, but custom gamification features require additional development.

### Dashboard Visibility

The affiliate and trader dashboard pages are independent. If the connected wallet is not an affiliate or trader, the page will display empty data but will still be visible. Hiding navigation links to these pages based on wallet role must be implemented by the builder; it is not handled automatically by the SDK.

chunks.title: Internationalization: RTL Language Support
chunks.content:
The Orderly SDK provides comprehensive internationalization support, including right-to-left (RTL) languages for Middle Eastern markets.

### RTL Language Support

**SDK v3.1.0+** added right-to-left (RTL) language support including:
- **Arabic** (ar)
- **Persian/Farsi** (fa)
- **Hebrew** (he)

The SDK automatically handles:
- **Layout Mirroring:** All layouts, grids, and flexbox containers mirror correctly for RTL locales
- **Typography:** Text alignment and direction adjust automatically
- **Component Mirroring:** Icons, arrows, and directional UI elements flip appropriately
- **Chart Adjustments:** TradingView charts and order books adapt to RTL reading patterns

### Implementation

RTL support is automatic based on the user's locale setting. The SDK detects the language and applies RTL styling when appropriate.

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  locale="ar" // Arabic - automatically enables RTL
>
  <YourApp />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### Supported Languages

In addition to RTL languages, the SDK supports:
- English (en)
- Russian (ru)
- Indonesian (id)
- Turkish (tr)
- Italian (it)
- Portuguese (pt)
- Ukrainian (uk)
- Polish (pl)
- Dutch (nl)
- Chinese (zh)
- Japanese (ja)
- Korean (ko)

### Custom Translations

To add custom translations or override existing ones, use the `translations` prop:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  translations={{
    'order.buy': 'شراء', // Custom Arabic translation
    'order.sell': 'بيع'
  }}
>
  <YourApp />
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### CSS Considerations

When adding custom CSS, use logical properties instead of physical properties to ensure RTL compatibility:

```css
/* Good - works in both LTR and RTL */
.custom-element {
  margin-inline-start: 16px; /* Left in LTR, Right in RTL */
  padding-inline-end: 8px;
}

/* Avoid - breaks in RTL */
.custom-element {
  margin-left: 16px; /* Always left, even in RTL */
  padding-right: 8px;
}
```

### Testing RTL Layouts

To test RTL layouts during development:

1. Set the locale to an RTL language (ar, fa, he)
2. Verify that all UI elements mirror correctly
3. Check that text alignment and direction are appropriate
4. Ensure icons and directional elements flip as expected
5. Test TradingView charts and order books for proper RTL adaptation

chunks.title: Security: Solana Multi-DVN Upgrade and LayerZero Migration
chunks.content:
Following a LayerZero exploit in April 2026, Orderly Network implemented critical security upgrades to its cross-chain messaging infrastructure, particularly for Solana integration.

### Solana Multi-DVN Security Upgrade

**SDK v2.12.3** (mandatory for all DEXs integrating with Solana) upgraded the Solana Vault contract from a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) to a 3-of-3 consensus model using three independent DVNs via LayerZero V2.

**What Changed:**
- **Before:** Single DVN (LayerZero's official DVN) verified cross-chain messages
- **After:** 3-of-3 consensus model with three independent DVNs

**Why This Matters:**
- Eliminates single point of dependency
- Enhances cross-chain security for Solana deposits and withdrawals
- Prevents potential exploits targeting a single verifier

### Impact on DEXs

**Mandatory Upgrade:**
DEXs that do not upgrade to SDK v2.12.3 or later will experience issues with Solana network deposits and withdrawals. The old DVN settings are no longer supported.

**Symptoms of Outdated SDK:**
- Solana deposits failing with errors
- Solana withdrawals failing or delayed
- Cross-chain message verification failures

### Withdrawal Delays (April 2026)

Following the migration, temporary withdrawal delays occurred because the new DVNs were not initially processing messages at full speed. Deposits remained operational throughout.

**Resolution:**
The issue was resolved through coordination with the LayerZero team, and all deposits and withdrawals returned to normal operations across supported chains.

### Upgrade Instructions

**For SDK Users:**
```bash
# Update to SDK v2.12.3 or later
npm install @orderly.network/react-app@^2.12.3
npm install @orderly.network/hooks@^2.12.3
# Update all @orderly.network packages to the same version
```

**For Orderly One Users:**
1. Navigate to the Orderly One dashboard
2. Go to your DEX page
3. Click the update button to apply the latest SDK version
4. The upgrade is typically already live and just needs to be applied through the platform interface

### LayerZero Endpoint V2 Configuration

For testnet integrations (e.g., Sei devnet), key addresses include:

**Sei Devnet (chainKey: sei-testnet, EID: 40258):**
- Endpoint V2: `0x6EDCE65403992e310A62460808c4b910D972f10f`
- SendUln302: `0xd682ECF100f6F4284138AA925348633B0611Ae21`
- ReceiveUln302: `0xcF1B0F4106B0324F96fEfcC31bA9498caa80701C`
- Executor: `0x55c175DD5b039331dB251424538169D8495C18d1`

**DVNs:**
- Bitgo
- LayerZero Labs: `0xf49d162484290eaead7bb8c2c7e3a6f8f52e32d6`
- P2P

### Best Practices

1. **Always use the latest SDK version** to ensure compatibility with security upgrades
2. **Monitor Orderly announcements** for critical security updates
3. **Test cross-chain operations** thoroughly after upgrades
4. **Implement proper error handling** for deposit/withdrawal failures
5. **Keep all @orderly.network packages aligned** to the same version to avoid dependency conflicts

chunks.title: SDK Integration Options and Approaches
chunks.content:
Orderly Network offers multiple integration paths to suit different development needs, ranging from pre-built UI components to low-level API access. Choosing the right approach depends on your desired level of customization and time-to-market.

### 1. Components SDK (React Components)
This is the fastest way to launch a DEX. It provides pre-built, themed React components that handle the full trading experience, including the order book, trading forms, and portfolio views.

- **Best for:** Builders who want to ship quickly with minimal UI development.
- **Customization:** Primarily via theming (colors, fonts) and configuration props.
- **Reference:** [js-sdk-demo repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/js-sdk-demo) and the [hosted SDK demo](https://sdk-demo.orderly.network/).
- **Next.js Template:** [orderly-js-sdk-nextjs-template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-js-sdk-nextjs-template)

### 2. Hooks SDK (React Hooks)
This approach offers more flexibility than the Components SDK. You build your own custom UI components while using Orderly's React hooks to handle data fetching, authentication, and order management.

- **Best for:** Teams requiring a custom UI/UX who are comfortable with React.
- **Customization:** Full control over the UI layer; logic handled by hooks.
- **Reference:** [example-dex repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex) and [live demo](https://orderly-dex.pages.dev/).

### 3. Core SDK
The Core SDK (`@orderly.network/core`) is a minimal wrapper around the REST API and EIP-712 signing logic. It is framework-agnostic and can be used with vanilla JavaScript, Vue, Angular, or mobile frameworks.

- **Best for:** Integrations that do not use React or require very specific architectural control.
- **NPM:** [@orderly.network/core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@orderly.network/core)
- **Note:** Documentation for the Core SDK is currently limited; developers may need to reference the source code or types.

### 4. Direct REST API Integration
For maximum control, you can integrate directly with Orderly's REST APIs and Websockets without using any SDK. This requires you to manually implement account registration, EIP-712 signing, and order management.

- **Best for:** Non-standard environments or teams who want to implement every layer themselves.
- **Reference:** [Build on Omnichain documentation](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/building-on-omnichain) includes examples in Python, TypeScript, and Java.

### 5. Orderly One (No-Code)
Orderly One is a no-code perpetual DEX launcher at [dex.orderly.network](https://dex.orderly.network/) that allows anyone to create and deploy a branded perp DEX in minutes.

- **Best for:** Teams wanting to launch immediately without frontend development.
- **Features:** PWA support, multi-chain support, RWA configuration, multisig admin wallets, Amplitude analytics, customizable points programs (via Fuul), and a graduation flow.
- **Revenue:** Graduated DEXs (those that paid approximately 1K USD) are enabled for revenue share.

### Choosing an Approach
| Approach | Time to Market | Customization | Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Orderly One | Minutes | Medium (Branding) | None |
| Components SDK | Days | Low (Theming) | Low |
| Hooks SDK | 2-3 Weeks | High | Medium |
| Core SDK | Weeks | Very High | High |
| Direct API | Months | Total | Very High |

chunks.title: Configuring the Components SDK
chunks.content:
The Components SDK relies heavily on provider configuration to function correctly. This section details the necessary setup for `OrderlyAppProvider`, network settings, chain filtering, and advanced features.

### Provider Setup
There are two main providers:

- **`OrderlyAppProvider`**: Use this when you are using Orderly React components (like `TradingPage`). It wraps `OrderlyConfigProvider` and adds additional context for UI components.
- **`OrderlyConfigProvider`**: Use this if you are only using hooks and not the pre-built UI components.

```tsx
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react";
import { Arbitrum, Ethereum } from "@orderly.network/types";

function App() {
  return (
    <OrderlyAppProvider
      brokerId="your_broker_id"
      brokerName="Your DEX Name"
      networkId="mainnet"
      chainFilter={{
        mainnet: [Arbitrum, Ethereum],
        testnet: []
      }}
      enableSwapDeposit // Enables Deposit Zap-in
    >
      <YourTradingApp />
    </OrderlyAppProvider>
  );
}
```

### Network Configuration
The `networkId` prop determines whether the app connects to Orderly's mainnet or testnet infrastructure. It must be a string (`"mainnet"` or `"testnet"`), **not** a numeric chain ID.

**Note:** Switching between `mainnet` and `testnet` requires a page reload because they are separate environments.

### Chain Filtering
Control which chains appear in the wallet selector and trading interface using the `chainFilter` prop. You can use predefined chain objects from `@orderly.network/types` or define custom chain objects for newer chains.

```tsx
import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from "@orderly.network/types";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story (custom chain ID)
    ],
    testnet: []
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

For custom chain objects, you can specify properties like `chainInfo` (with `chainName`, `rpcUrls`, `chainId`, `nativeCurrency`, `blockExplorerUrls`), `chainNameShort`, `chainLogo`, `minGasBalance`, and `requestRpc`.

### Deposit Zap-in (Auto-Swap Deposits)
Enable users to deposit any token, which is automatically swapped to a supported collateral during the deposit process:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  enableSwapDeposit
  // ...other props
>
```

Zap-In Deposit also supports dynamic chain configuration via API.

### Exclusive Receiver Address (SDK v2.12.0+)
Builders can configure a dedicated deposit address for their users. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits — no gas fees or wallet connection required from the user. This streamlines the onboarding experience significantly.

### Geo-Restrictions
Configure IP-based geo-restriction on the frontend via the `restrictedInfo` configuration object:

```javascript
<OrderlyAppProvider
  restrictedInfo={{
    enableDefault: true,
    customRestrictedIps: [],
    customRestrictedRegions: [],
    customUnblockRegions: ["United States"],
  }}
>
```

**Note:** Orderly does not enforce geo-blocking from the backend; it is the broker's responsibility to configure restrictions on the frontend for compliance.

### Custom Wallet Connection
If your app already has a connected wallet (e.g., via `ethers` or `wagmi`), implement a **Custom Wallet Connection Provider** to prevent the `TradingPage` from prompting the user to connect again. See the [Custom wallet connection provider docs](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/react/wallet#custom-wallet-connection-provider).

### Privy Wallet Integration
To enable Privy wallet authentication, import `WalletConnectorPrivyProvider` from the separate package `@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy`:

```tsx
import { WalletConnectorPrivyProvider } from "@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy";

<WalletConnectorPrivyProvider config={yourPrivyConfig}>
  <OrderlyAppProvider>
    {children}
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorPrivyProvider>
```

### Troubleshooting
- **"useConfig must be used within Provider"**: Ensure all `@orderly.network` packages are on the same aligned version.
- **Blank page during API downtime**: If using SSR, handle API errors gracefully or separate Orderly-dependent components from your main rendering pipeline.
- **Wallet connects but sign-in fails**: Check that your `networkId` matches the environment where your Broker ID is registered.

chunks.title: Advanced Trading Features: TP/SL, Margin Modes, and Order Types
SDK Version Guide and Critical Upgrades
chunks.content:
Orderly regularly releases SDK updates with new features, bug fixes, and security improvements. This guide covers key versions and mandatory upgrades.

## Critical / Mandatory Upgrades

These versions contain security fixes or critical functionality that all builders should adopt:

| Version | Priority | Key Changes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **v2.3.0** | Critical | Required for BNB Chain integration; USDC decimal handling (18 on-chain vs 6 on Orderly) |
| **v2.4.1** | Critical | Solana wallet connection and network switching fixes |
| **v2.5.1** | Critical | Multi-collateral deposit support (ETH, USDT) |
| **v2.9.0** | Required | Multilevel Referral Program support |
| **v2.12.3** | **Mandatory** | Solana Multi-DVN security upgrade (3-of-3 DVN consensus for LayerZero V2) |
| **v3.0.2** | Critical | Bug fixes for SDK v3; responsive breakpoint raised to 1024px |
| **v3.0.4** | High-Mandatory | Critical wallet registration request update |

### Solana Multi-DVN Security (v2.12.3)

Following a LayerZero exploit, Orderly migrated its Solana Vault contract from a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) to a 3-of-3 consensus model using three independent DVNs. **SDK v2.12.3 is mandatory for all DEXs integrating with Solana.** DEXs without this upgrade may experience issues with deposits and withdrawals on the Solana network.

### BNB Chain Integration (v2.3.0)

USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. Always refer to the `decimals` field in `chain_details` from the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.

## Major Feature Releases

### SDK v2.x Highlights

| Version | Features |
| :--- | :--- |
| **v2.5.1** | Multi-collateral support, order book precision control, customizable header navigation, market UI sorting |
| **v2.6.0** | TP/SL with Limit Orders, one-click leaderboard join, order fill sound notifications |
| **v2.7.3** | VaultSDK for Strategy Vaults (EVM + Solana), drag-to-adjust TP/SL on charts |
| **v2.8.6** | One-Click Reverse Position, enhanced stop-loss protection |
| **v2.10.1** | Deposit Zap-in, Open Interest column, dynamic chain configuration |
| **v2.10.2** | Bulk close by profitability, RWA & Crypto market sections, multiple theme support |
| **v2.11.0** | Isolated margin mode |
| **v2.12.0** | Exclusive Receiver Address, Permissionless Listings support, ISO/Cross margin labels on charts, Asset Categories, Liquidation Price Line Toggle |
| **v2.12.2** | TP/SL logic uses mark price for chart-dragging (lock-profit scenarios) |
| **v2.12.3** | Solana Multi-DVN security, Google OAuth in Mini Apps, Advanced TP/SL with Mark Price offset |
| **v2.12.4** | Referral code binding post-account creation, Vault withdrawals fix |

### SDK v3.x Highlights

| Version | Features |
| :--- | :--- |
| **v3.0.0** | Frontend Plugin System and Module Marketplace |
| **v3.0.2** | Responsive breakpoint raised to 1024px, critical bug fixes |
| **v3.0.3** | Fixed permissionless listing display on mobile (funding rate modal) |
| **v3.0.4** | Critical wallet registration request update |
| **v3.1.0** | RTL language support (Arabic, Persian, Hebrew), ISO max-out order fix |
| **v3.1.1** | Pre-TGE perpetual market support |
| **v3.1.3** | Expanded Trading page plugin support (Order Entry, Chart Overlays, Data List Tabs, Mobile Trading layout), dedicated Crypto market category, optimized K-line history loading |

## Upgrade Process

- **SDK Builders**: Update npm packages to the latest version. Ensure all `@orderly.network/*` packages are version-aligned.
- **Orderly One Builders**: Apply upgrades via the Orderly One dashboard.
- **Check Changelog**: [orderly.network/docs/changelog/sdk](https://orderly.network/docs/changelog/sdk)

## Collateral Assets by Chain

Multi-collateral support varies by chain:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
| :--- | :--- |
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH, WBTC |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT, USDC |

Additional chains and tokens are added over time. Use Deposit Zap-in (v2.10.1+) to allow users to deposit any token, which is automatically swapped to a supported collateral.

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings, RWA Markets, and Pre-TGE Support
chunks.content:
Orderly supports several advanced market features that allow builders to offer diverse trading products on their DEX.

## Permissionless Listings
