The Permissionless Listing framework allows any Orderly builder (Diamond-tier brokers) to list assets not currently on Orderly. Builders pick their oracle and market maker, and the market goes live without going through the standard centralized listing process.

### How It Works

1. **Builder lists a market**: The builder provides their own oracle and market maker.
2. **Revenue**: The market owner earns 100% of liquidation fees plus 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.
3. **Visibility**: Listed pairs appear only on the listing broker's platform by default. Other brokers can manually enable them.
4. **SDK Support**: SDK v2.12.0+ provides full UI rendering and trading support for permissionlessly listed symbols.

### Builder Responsibilities

When new permissionless markets are announced (via the broker channel), builders must:
1. **Sync frontend configuration** to display the new symbols.
2. **Notify users** about newly available markets.
3. **Ensure SDK version** is v3.0.3+ to avoid display issues on mobile (funding rate modal showing empty values for Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, Estimated Funding Fee).

```tsx
// Permissionless symbols are automatically rendered
// if your SDK version is v2.12.0+ and your frontend
// configuration includes them.
```

**Interactive Demo:** [pml-eight.vercel.app](https://pml-eight.vercel.app/)

## RWA (Real-World Asset) Markets

Orderly supports RWA markets including:

| Category | Examples | Max Leverage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stock Indices** | SPX500, NAS100 | Varies |
| **Precious Metals** | Gold (XAU), Silver (XAG) | Up to 20x |
| **Individual Stocks** | NVDA, TSLA, GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN, MSFT, SAMSUNG | Up to 20x |
| **Forex Pairs** | JPY/USD, EUR/USD | Varies |

### SDK Support for RWA

- **v2.8.0**: Dedicated RWA Market UI elements
- **v2.8.13**: RWA tab on the Market page
- **v2.10.2**: Separate RWA & Crypto market sections on Markets page
- **v3.1.3**: Dedicated Crypto market category across Market Selector, Market Search, Market Sidebar, and Markets page

To add RWA markets, include the ticker symbols in your supported assets configuration. Orderly sends listing/delisting notifications to brokers.

## Pre-TGE Markets (SDK v3.1.1+)

Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) perpetual market listings enable builders to offer perpetual trading markets before a token's official TGE. This allows users to speculate on upcoming token launches.

```tsx
// Pre-TGE markets are handled automatically by the SDK
// Ensure you are on v3.1.1+ for full support
```

## Custom Asset Categories (SDK v2.12.0+)

Builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI. No categories are set by default — builders choose which categories to display for their users. This allows organizing markets into groups like "DeFi", "Layer 1", "Meme", "RWA", etc.

## MCP (Model Context Protocol) for AI Agents

You can launch your own MCP server so AI agents can trade directly on your DEX:

1. Add your `brokerID` to the Orderly MCP.
2. AI agents install it by providing the MCP URL.
3. The agent uses your broker ID based on MCP knowledge.

**NPM:** [@orderly.network/mcp-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@orderly.network/mcp-server)
**GitHub:** [OrderlyNetwork/orderly-mcp](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-mcp)

chunks.title: SDK v3 Plugin System and Extensibility
chunks.content:
SDK v3 introduces a Frontend Plugin System and Module Marketplace, enabling builders and DEXs to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of the Orderly trading interface without forking the SDK.

## Overview

The Plugin System allows you to extend the trading UI at defined extension points while staying on the main SDK upgrade path. This means you get new features and security updates without merge conflicts from a forked codebase.

## Extension Points

As of SDK v3.1.3, the following extension points are available:

| Extension Point | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Order Entry** | Add custom order types or modify the order form |
| **Chart Overlays** | Add custom indicators or overlays to TradingView charts |
| **Data List Tabs** | Add custom tabs to the data panel (positions, orders, etc.) |
| **Mobile Trading Layout** | Customize the mobile trading experience |

## Development Tools

### orderly-devkit CLI

The `orderly-devkit` CLI provides tooling for plugin development, scaffolding, and testing.

```bash
# Install the devkit
npm install -g @orderly.network/devkit

# Create a new plugin
orderly-devkit plugin create my-custom-order-type

# Development server
orderly-devkit plugin dev
```

### Plugin Agent Capabilities

SDK v3.0.1+ enhanced plugin agent capabilities and the SDK Docs MCP server, making it easier to develop plugins with AI assistance.

## Module Marketplace

The Module Marketplace allows builders to share and reuse frontend customizations. This creates an ecosystem where common extensions (custom order types, analytics panels, social features) can be installed as plugins.

## Integration with Orderly One

Orderly One builders can apply SDK v3 upgrades and install plugins directly through the Orderly One platform, making it accessible even for no-code builders.

## Key SDK v3 Features Beyond Plugins

- **Responsive Breakpoint**: Raised from 768px to 1024px (v3.0.2)
- **RTL Language Support**: Arabic, Persian, Hebrew with mirrored layouts (v3.1.0)
- **Pre-TGE Markets**: Perpetual trading before token generation events (v3.1.1)
- **Dedicated Crypto Category**: Separate Crypto/RWA market sections (v3.1.3)
- **Optimized K-line Loading**: Stops requests for unavailable historical data before market listing time (v3.1.3)

## Best Practices

1. **Stay on the latest version**: The latest recommended version is v3.1.3.
2. **Use extension points**: Avoid forking the SDK; use the plugin system for customizations.
3. **Test on mobile**: The responsive breakpoint change (1024px) may affect your layout.
4. **Version alignment**: Ensure all `@orderly.network/*` packages are on the same version.

chunks.title: Referral System and Affiliate Program
chunks.content:
Orderly provides a comprehensive referral and affiliate system that brokers can use to incentivize community-driven growth.

## Multilevel Referral Program (SDK v2.9.0+)

The Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program supports up to 15 referral levels, allowing brokers to incentivize community-driven distribution with multi-tier commissions.

### Setup Requirements

1. **Upgrade SDK** to version 2.9.0 or later (Orderly One DEXs should ensure they run the latest version).
2. **Enable the program** via the Admin Tool at [admin.orderly.network](https://admin.orderly.network/) or through the Orderly One dashboard.

### Creating Referral Codes

Brokers can create referral codes via:
- **Admin Portal**: [admin.orderly.network](https://admin.orderly.network/)
- **API**: `POST /v1/referral/create`

Key API parameters:
- `max_rebate_rate` (0–1): The portion of broker commission shared with referrer and referee
- `referrer_rebate_rate`: Share allocated to the referrer
- `referee_rebate_rate`: Share allocated to the referee

### Auto-Generation of Referral Codes

Automatically generate referral codes for users reaching a trading volume threshold:

```
POST /v1/referral/auto_referral_update
{
  "required_trading_volume": 10000
}
```

**Note:** Setting `required_trading_volume` to 0 still requires at least one completed trade.

### Binding Referral Codes

- **SDK v2.12.4+**: Users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration. They no longer need to provide a code during registration.
- **URL Parameter**: Users can bind automatically through SDK-handled referral links (e.g., `?ref=CODE`).
- **API**: Users can bind a referral code via the API.

### Referral Code Scope

Referral codes are platform-unique but can only be used within the broker that created them.

### Order Tag Priority

The `order_tag` parameter on order creation has higher priority than a user's bound referral code for fee commission allocation.

## Frontend Integration

### Using the Affiliate Package

```tsx
import { Dashboard, ReferralProvider } from "@orderly.network/affiliate";

<ReferralProvider
  becomeAnAffiliateUrl="/become-affiliate"
  referralLinkUrl="/referral"
  overwrite={{ shortBrokerName: "MyDEX" }}
>
  <Dashboard.DashboardPage
    classNames={{
      root: "oui-flex oui-justify-center",
      home: "oui-py-6 oui-px-4",
      dashboard: "oui-py-6 oui-px-4",
    }}
  />
</ReferralProvider>
```

### Fixing Legacy Affiliate Page Redirects

If the affiliates page redirects to the home page instead of showing the campaign prompt, locate `app/pages/rewards/Affiliate.tsx` and replace `Rewards.affiliatePage` or `Dashboard.affiliatePage` with:

```tsx
import { Dashboard, ReferralProvider } from "@orderly.network/affiliate";

<Dashboard.DashboardPage />
```

The legacy affiliate page is being replaced by the multilevel referral system.

## Trading Leaderboard Widget

Integrate the trading leaderboard to gamify trading:

```tsx
import { LeaderboardWidget } from "@orderly.network/trading-leaderboard";

<LeaderboardWidget
  campaigns={[]}
  href={{ trading: "/" }}
/>
```

**Important:** Ensure all `@orderly.network/*` packages are version-aligned (e.g., all v2.1.0+) to avoid `configStore is not defined` errors. The widget must be wrapped inside an `OrderlyAppProvider`.

### Campaign Banners

Campaign images use dimensions of **1104x620 pixels**. Trading campaigns must be set up manually by the Orderly team before they appear in the UI.

### PnL Sharing Cards

PnL sharing card dimensions are **1656px width × 930px height** (landscape format). Brokers can customize branding elements like logos and text within these dimensions.

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Common SDK Errors
chunks.content:
This guide addresses frequent errors encountered during Orderly SDK integration and their solutions.

## Bundler and Build Errors

### Webpack `.mjs` Error
**Error:** `Attempted import error: 'createClient' is not exported from '@layerzerolabs/scan-client'`
**Cause:** CRA/Webpack configurations often fail to handle `.mjs` files in `node_modules`.
**Solution:** Add a webpack rule:

```javascript
webpack: (config) => {
  config.module.rules.push({
    test: /\.mjs$/,
    include: /node_modules/,
    type: "javascript/auto",
  });
  return config;
}
```

### Next.js Server Component Error
**Error:** `export 'default' (reexported as 'useSWR') was not found in 'swr'`
**Cause:** Next.js App Router treats files as server components by default.
**Solution:** Add `"use client";` at the very top of the file. Ensure `OrderlyProviders` and `OrderlyAppProvider` wrap your app on the **client side only**.

### Ethers v5/v6 Conflict
**Error:** `Type 'BytesLike' is not assignable to type 'string'` in `abi-coder.ts`
**Cause:** Multiple ethers versions in the dependency tree. Orderly SDK v2 depends on ethers v6.
**Solution:** Delete `node_modules` and lock file, then regenerate. If your project uses ethers v5, use yarn resolutions to force ethers v6:

```json
{
  "resolutions": {
    "ethers": "^6.0.0"
  }
}
```

Verify: `./node_modules/@orderly.network/core/node_modules/ethers` resolves to v6.

## Runtime Errors

### Provider Context Error
**Error:** `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')` from `useConfig`
**Cause:** Mixing Orderly SDK v1 and v2 packages breaks React Context.
**Solution:** Ensure all `@orderly.network/*` packages are on the same aligned version.

### ConfigStore Error
**Error:** `configStore is not defined, please use OrderlyProvider`
**Cause:** Using modules like `@orderly.network/portfolio`, `@orderly.network/affiliate`, or `@orderly.network/trading-leaderboard` without the proper provider wrapper.
**Solution:** Wrap your application with `OrderlyAppProvider` or `OrderlyConfigProvider`.

### useHoldingStream Crash
**Error:** Crash in `useHoldingStream` or a `.find` call inside orderly/react components
**Cause:** Using `usePrivateQuery` for holdings data and caching it in the same React Query key area without a matching formatter.
**Solution:** Add the correct formatter to match Orderly's internal data shape.

### useMarkPricesStream Returns Empty
**Cause:** Infinite loop in component logic (e.g., `useEffect` with state setters triggering re-renders when combined with `useOrderEntry`).
**Solution:** Debug by setting breakpoints in `useEffect` dependencies. Wrap functions like `updateOrderByKey` in `useCallback`.

### maxQty is 0 in useOrderEntry
**Cause:** Typically an issue with order type or form validation, not collateral balance.
**Solution:** Ensure order parameters (type, side, symbol) are correctly configured. Deploy the reference Orderly UI alongside your integration for comparison.

## Wallet and Network Issues

### Solana Wallet Disconnects on Refresh
**Cause:** Bug in earlier v2 versions.
**Solution:** Upgrade to SDK v2.8.10+.

### Wrong Network on Solana Mainnet
**Cause:** Solana wallet adapter defaults to Devnet.
**Solution:**

```tsx
import { WalletAdapterNetwork } from "@solana/wallet-adapter-base";

<WalletConnectorProvider solanaInitial={{ network: WalletAdapterNetwork.Mainnet }}>
  {/* ... */}
</WalletConnectorProvider>
```

### Solana Withdrawal Delays
**Cause:** Following a LayerZero exploit, Orderly migrated to a 3-of-3 DVN consensus model. New DVNs initially processed messages slower.
**Solution:** Upgrade to SDK v2.12.3+ (mandatory for Solana-integrated DEXs).

## UI and Display Issues

### Empty Orderbook for Certain Pairs
**Cause:** Frontend truncates price decimal places for low-priced tokens.
**Solution:** Configure orderbook to display more decimal places or use Order Book Precision Control (SDK v2.5.1+).

### Blank Page During API Downtime
**Cause:** SSR calls Orderly APIs during render; if API fails, page fails.
**Solution:** Handle API errors gracefully in SSR logic or separate Orderly-dependent components from main rendering pipeline.

### TradingView Overrides Not Applying
**Cause:** Free TradingView library or cached localStorage settings.
**Solution:** Ensure valid TradingView license, clear localStorage, verify `tradingViewConfig` overrides syntax.

### TradingView Snapshots
**Note:** Programmatic TradingView snapshots (e.g., `widget.takeClientScreenshot()`) are not currently exposed through the Orderly SDK.

## Validating Symbols

Before passing symbols to `OrderEntryWidget`, validate them:

```tsx
// Fetch valid symbols
const response = await fetch("/v1/public/available-symbols");
const symbols = await response.json();

// Then pass a valid symbol
<OrderEntryWidget symbol="PERP_ETH_USDC" />
```

chunks.title: SDK v3 Plugin System and Module Marketplace
chunks.content:
SDK v3 introduces a **Frontend Plugin System** and **Module Marketplace**, enabling builders to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of the Orderly trading interface without forking the SDK.

## Key Features

### Plugin System
Developers can hook into various interceptor targets to extend the trading experience:
- **Order Entry:** Add custom order types, modify the order-type dropdown, or extend the form body.
- **Chart Overlays:** Inject custom indicators or data layers onto TradingView charts.
- **Data List Tabs:** Add custom tabs to the data lists (e.g., custom analytics or history views).
- **Mobile Trading Layout:** Customize the mobile trading interface.

### Module Marketplace
The Marketplace allows DEXs to share and reuse frontend customizations. Builders can submit modules via the `orderly-devkit` CLI and manage updates without re-submitting.

### Developer Toolchain
- **`orderly-devkit` CLI:** Manage module submission, listing, and updates.
- **Plugin Agent:** Capabilities for automated plugin management.
- **SDK Docs MCP Server:** Enhanced documentation access for plugin development.

## Using the CLI

### Submitting a Module
Use the CLI submission flow to publish a new module. Once published, verify it via:
```bash
orderly-devkit list
```
Or check the public API:
`https://orderly-plugin-marketplace.vercel.app/api/plugins?sort=updated&order=desc&status=available`

### Updating a Module
To release updates to an existing module, publish the new version and run:
```bash
orderly-devkit update
```
This ensures the marketplace reflects the latest metadata and code.

## SDK v3 Key Releases
- **v3.0.2:** Raised mobile/desktop responsive breakpoint from 768px to 1024px. Fixed critical bugs (leverage not updating after switching to isolated margin, incorrect order symbol when switching margin modes).
- **v3.0.3:** Fixed display issues for permissionless listing symbols (funding rate modal showing empty values on mobile).
- **v3.0.4:** Critical feature update for wallet registration requests (high-mandatory upgrade).
- **v3.1.0:** Added RTL (right-to-left) language support for Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew. Fixed isolated margin max-out order rejection by reserving a taker fee buffer.
- **v3.1.1:** Added Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) perpetual market support.
- **v3.1.3:** Expanded Trading page plugin support, added a dedicated Crypto market category, and optimized K-line history loading.

## Integration Note
For Orderly One builders, upgrades are available through the platform dashboard. SDK builders should manually update to the latest version (v3.1.3+ recommended) to access plugin features and critical bug fixes.

chunks.title: Advanced Deposit Features: Zap-in and Exclusive Receiver
chunks.content:
Orderly SDK provides advanced deposit features to streamline user onboarding and improve the deposit experience.

## Deposit Zap-in (SDK v2.10.1+)
Deposit Zap-in allows users to deposit **any token** into their Orderly perpetual account. The token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral (e.g., USDC) during the deposit process.

### Enabling Zap-in
Enable this feature by setting the `enableSwapDeposit` prop on the `<OrderlyAppProvider>` component:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

Zap-In Deposit also supports dynamic chain configuration via API, allowing brokers to add new chains without SDK updates.

## Exclusive Receiver Address (SDK v2.12.0+)
The Exclusive Receiver Address feature allows builders to configure a **dedicated deposit address** for their users. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits — **no gas fees or wallet connection required** from the user.

### Use Cases
- **Simplified Onboarding:** Users can deposit from exchanges or other wallets without interacting with a DEX UI.
- **Gasless Deposits:** Ideal for users who may not have native gas tokens on the deposit chain.

### Configuration
This feature is configured at the broker level. Contact the Orderly team or use the Orderly One dashboard to set up an exclusive receiver address for your DEX.

## Multi-Collateral Support (SDK v2.5.1+)
Users can deposit multiple assets as collateral without swapping to USDC first. Supported collateral by chain includes:
- **Ethereum:** USDC, USDT, ETH
- **BNB Chain:** USDC, USDT
- **Base:** USDC, ETH
- **Arbitrum:** USDC, USDT, ETH
- **Solana:** SOL, USDT

Brokers must upgrade to SDK v2.5.1 or later to enable multi-collateral deposit support.

chunks.title: Isolated Margin Mode and Risk Management
Solana Integration and Multi-DVN Security
chunks.content:
Integrating Solana with Orderly requires specific SDK versions and an understanding of the cross-chain security model.

## Solana Multi-DVN Security (SDK v2.12.3)
SDK v2.12.3 is a **mandatory update** for all DEXs integrating with Solana. It upgrades the Solana Vault contract from a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) to a **3-of-3 consensus model** using three independent DVNs via LayerZero V2.

### Why is this critical?
- **Enhanced Security:** Eliminates single points of dependency for cross-chain messages.
- **Withdrawal Stability:** DEXs that do not upgrade may experience issues with Solana deposits and withdrawals.
- **Mandatory:** All cross-chain messages must be verified by three independent DVNs.

## Adding Solana to Components SDK
Add Solana (chain ID 90009090) to the `chainFilter` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider`:

```tsx
import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from "@orderly.network/types";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
    ],
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

## Solana-Specific Implementation
- **Off-chain Signing:** Solana withdrawals require off-chain signing as a replacement for EIP-712 used on EVM.
- **PDAs:** Calculate Program Derived Addresses using the broker hash and program ID.
- **Vault IDL:** Available in the JS SDK at `packages/default-solana-adapter/src/idl/solana_vault.ts`.

## Withdrawal Delays
Following security incidents, Orderly migrated to the multi-DVN model. During the transition, withdrawals may be delayed while new DVNs ramp up to full processing speed. Deposits typically remain operational, and funds are safe in vaults.

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings and RWA Markets
chunks.content:
Orderly supports permissionless token listings and Real-World Asset (RWA) markets, providing brokers with expanded trading opportunities.

## Permissionless Listings
The permissionless listing framework allows external parties to list tokens on Orderly-powered DEXes without going through the traditional listing process.

### Broker Requirements
- **Insurance Fund:** A $50K deposit (refundable upon delisting, generates yield from trading activity).
- **Market Maker:** A MM bot (e.g., Tread.fi) to provide liquidity.
- **Revenue:** The listing broker earns 100% of liquidation fees and 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

### SDK Handling
- **v2.12.0+:** Full UI rendering and trading support for permissionlessly listed symbols.
- **v3.0.3+:** Fixed display issues for permissionless symbols (e.g., funding rate modal showing empty values on mobile).
- **Symbol Naming:** Permissionless markets may have an `_arthur` suffix and may be configured as 'isolated only'.

Brokers should sync their frontend configuration when new permissionless markets are announced.

## Real-World Asset (RWA) Markets
Orderly supports RWA perpetual markets including:
- **Indexes:** $SPX500, $NAS100
- **Precious Metals:** Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG) — up to 20x leverage
- **Stocks:** $NVDA, $GOOGL, $TSLA, $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT — up to 20x leverage, tradeable 24/7
- **Forex:** $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD
- **Commodities:** $CL (WTI Crude Oil), $BZ (Brent Crude Oil)

### UI Integration
- **v2.8.0+:** Dedicated RWA Market UI elements.
- **v2.8.13+:** RWA tab on the Market page.
- **v3.1.3:** Added a dedicated Crypto market category to separate RWA and Crypto markets.

To make RWA markets more visible, save your DEX configuration in Orderly One to trigger an update that adds a dedicated RWA tab in the asset selection.

chunks.title: Multilevel Referral Program and Affiliate System
chunks.content:
The Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program allows brokers to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral commissions.

## Enabling the Program
1. **Upgrade SDK:** Version 2.9.0 or later (Orderly One DEXs should ensure they are running the latest version on the platform).
2. **Activate:** Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard.

## Key Features
- **Multi-Tier Commissions:** Brokers can set up tiered referral structures.
- **Direct Referrer Bonus:** Direct referrers receive a guaranteed 10% referral bonus commission rate in addition to multilevel commissions.
- **Post-Registration Binding (v2.12.4+):** Users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time, rather than requiring it during initial signup.

## Integration
Use the `@orderly.network/affiliate` package for pre-built dashboard components:

```tsx
import { Dashboard, ReferralProvider } from '@orderly.network/affiliate';

<ReferralProvider
  becomeAnAffiliateUrl="https://your-dex.com/affiliate"
  referralLinkUrl="https://your-dex.com/?referral="
  overwrite={{ shortBrokerName: "YOUR_DEX" }}
>
  <Dashboard.DashboardPage />
</ReferralProvider>
```

## Admin API
To programmatically pull multi-level referral data for all traders under your broker ID, use the `GET /v1/referral/multi_level/admin/info` endpoint. Authentication requires an admin API key with ed25519 message signing.

## Referral Codes
- **User Generation:** Users can generate codes through the affiliate section in the DEX UI.
- **Custom Codes:** Brokers can manually create custom codes for KOLs via the referral admin panel at `https://dex.orderly.network/referral`.
- **Link Format:** `https://your-dex-domain/?referral=CODE`

chunks.title: TradingView Integration and Chart Customization
chunks.content:
Orderly provides TradingView-ready endpoints and React components for advanced charting. However, licensing and configuration require careful attention.

## Licensing
- **Redistribution License:** Orderly's redistribution license is only valid for the `dex.orderly.network` subdomain.
- **Self-Hosted DEX:** If you are hosting your own DEX, you must either:
  1. Apply for your own **Trading Platform for Brokers** license from TradingView to use full trading integration features (e.g., `createPositionLine()`, `createOrderLine()`).
  2. Use `lightweight-charts`, TradingView's free open-source library, which supports candles, lines, and volume without licensing restrictions.

## Components SDK Integration
The `TradingPage` component includes TradingView support:

```tsx
import { TradingPage } from "@orderly.network/trading";

<TradingPage
  symbol={'PERP_ETH_USDC'}
  tradingViewConfig={{
    scriptSRC: "/assets/chart/charting_library/charting_library.js",
    library_path: "/assets/chart/charting_library/"
  }}
/>
```

## Custom Datafeed Adapter
For lower-level custom TradingView integration, use the datafeed adapter from the JS SDK:
`packages/trading-view/src/tradingView/tradingViewAdapter/datafeed/datafeed.ts`

## Chart Features
- **TP/SL from Charts (v2.6.1+):** Set TP/SL directly by dragging on the chart.
- **Mark Price Detection (v2.12.2+):** Uses mark price for TP/SL detection, enabling lock-profit scenarios.
- **ISO/Cross Labels (v2.12.0+):** Position lines display cross/isolated margin mode labels along with leverage.
- **Liquidation Price Toggle (v2.12.0+):** Users can show/hide the liquidation price line.

## Troubleshooting
- **Overrides not applying:** Ensure you have a valid TradingView Advanced Charts license and clear browser localStorage/cache.
- **Empty values for permissionless symbols:** Upgrade to SDK v3.0.3+ to fix funding rate modal display issues on mobile.

chunks.title: Broker Configuration and Chain Management
SDK Integration Options and Approaches
chunks.content:
Orderly Network offers multiple integration paths to suit different development needs, ranging from pre-built UI components to low-level API access. Choosing the right approach depends on your desired level of customization and time-to-market.

### 1. Components SDK (React Components)
This is the fastest way to launch a DEX. It provides pre-built, themed React components that handle the full trading experience, including the order book, trading forms, and portfolio views.

- **Best for:** Builders who want to ship quickly with minimal UI development.
- **Customization:** Primarily via theming (colors, fonts) and configuration props.
- **Reference:** [js-sdk-demo repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/js-sdk-demo), [broker-template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-template), and the [Storybook demo](https://storybook.orderly.network/?path=/docs/overview--docs).

### 2. Hooks SDK (React Hooks)
This approach offers more flexibility than the Components SDK. You build your own custom UI components while using Orderly's React hooks to handle data fetching, authentication, and order management.

- **Best for:** Teams requiring a custom UI/UX who are comfortable with React.
- **Customization:** Full control over the UI layer; logic handled by hooks.
- **Reference:** [example-dex repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex).

### 3. Core SDK
The Core SDK (`@orderly.network/core`) is a minimal wrapper around the REST API and EIP-712 signing logic. It is framework-agnostic and can be used with vanilla JavaScript, Vue, Angular, or mobile frameworks.

- **Best for:** Integrations that do not use React or require very specific architectural control.
- **Note:** Documentation for the Core SDK is currently limited; developers may need to reference the source code or types.

### 4. Direct REST API Integration
For maximum control, you can integrate directly with Orderly's REST APIs and Websockets without using any SDK. This requires you to manually implement account registration, EIP-712 signing, and order management.

- **Best for:** Non-standard environments or teams who want to implement every layer themselves.
- **Reference:** "Build on Omnichain" documentation includes examples in Python, TypeScript, and Java.

### 5. Orderly One (No-Code Solution)
Orderly One is a no-code perpetual DEX launcher that allows builders to create and deploy a DEX without coding. Features include multi-chain support, PWA support, RWA configuration, multisig admin wallets, Amplitude analytics integration, and a revamped admin dashboard.

- **Best for:** Builders who want to launch immediately without frontend development.
- **Reference:** [Orderly One Platform](https://dex.orderly.network/)

### Choosing an Approach
| Approach | Time to Market | Customization | Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Orderly One | Instant | Low (Config) | None |
| Components SDK | Fastest | Low (Theming) | Low |
| Hooks SDK | Medium | High | Medium |
| Core SDK | Slow | Very High | High |
| Direct API | Slowest | Total | Very High |

chunks.title: Advanced SDK Features: Deposits, Margin, and Plugins
chunks.content:
The Orderly SDK includes advanced features for deposits, margin management, and UI extensibility. This guide covers key capabilities introduced in recent SDK versions.

### Deposit Zap-in (Auto-Swap Deposits)
Introduced in SDK v2.10.1, Deposit Zap-in allows users to deposit any token into their Orderly perpetuals account. The token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral during the deposit process.

**Enable via `OrderlyAppProvider`:**
```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```
Zap-In Deposit also supports dynamic chain configuration via API.

### Exclusive Receiver Address
Available from SDK v2.12.0, builders can configure a dedicated deposit address for their users. Funds sent to this address are automatically credited as deposits — no gas fees or wallet connection required from the user. This simplifies the deposit onboarding experience significantly.

### Isolated Margin Mode
Isolated margin mode allows traders to allocate specific margin to individual positions rather than sharing margin across all positions (cross-margin).

- **SDK Support:** Introduced in v2.11.0, rolled out gradually across all Orderly DEXs.
- **Mandatory Update:** SDK v2.11.2 includes critical fixes for the isolated margin infrastructure.
- **UI Labels:** SDK v2.12.0+ adds ISO/Cross margin labels on TradingView chart position lines.
- **Bug Fixes:** SDK v3.1.0 fixed an issue where maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% was rejected. The SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

### Frontend Plugin System (SDK v3)
SDK v3 introduces a Frontend Plugin System and Module Marketplace, enabling builders to develop, share, and install custom modules on top of the Orderly trading interface without forking the SDK.

**Extension Points:**
- Order Entry
- Chart Overlays
- Data List Tabs
- Mobile Trading layout

**Developer Tooling:**
- `orderly-devkit` CLI
- Plugin agent capabilities
- SDK Docs MCP server

### Multi-Collateral Support
Since SDK v2.5.1, Orderly supports multiple assets as collateral including ETH, USDT, and USDC. Additional collateral support has been expanded to include SOL and USDT on Solana, BNB on BNB Chain, and WBTC on Ethereum.

**Supported Collateral by Chain:**
- **Ethereum:** USDC, USDT, ETH
- **BNB Chain:** USDC, USDT, BNB
- **Base:** USDC, ETH
- **Arbitrum:** USDC, USDT, ETH
- **Solana:** SOL, USDT

### Symbol-Level Leverage
Starting with SDK v2.7.3, brokers can configure leverage per symbol instead of account-wide leverage. This gives traders greater flexibility and control over their margin settings for individual markets.

chunks.title: Chain Integration and Configuration
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports multiple chains, and the SDK provides flexible configuration options for adding or filtering chains in your DEX.

### Adding New Chains
To add new chains like Story, Solana, or Monad Testnet to your Orderly DEX, use the `chainFilter` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider` and pass the chain ID.

**Example: Adding Story and Solana**
```tsx
import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from "@orderly.network/types";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  networkId="mainnet"
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story
    ],
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

**Example: Configuring Monad Testnet**
```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId={...}
  brokerName={...}
  networkId="testnet"
  chainFilter={{
    testnet: [{
      id: 10143,
      chainInfo: {
        name: "Monad Testnet",
        public_rpc_url: "https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz",
        chainId: 10143,
        currency_symbol: "MON",
        explorer_base_url: "",
        vault_address: "",
      },
    }],
    mainnet: []
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### Excluding Chains
If you prefer not to support certain chains (e.g., BNB Chain), use `chainFilter` to explicitly exclude them:

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [Arbitrum, Optimism], // Only these chains
    testnet: [] // Disable testnets
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
```

### BNB Chain USDC Decimal Precision
**Critical:** USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. To avoid precision mismatches, always refer to the `decimals` field in `chain_details` from the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.

**SDK Requirement:** SDK v2.3.0+ is required for BNB Chain support.

### Solana Integration
Solana support was introduced in SDK v2.0.0. Solana deposits stay on Solana while trades match with EVM traders via the Orderly chain (Orderly Unity).

**Migration Guide:** [SDK Migration Documentation](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/migrate)

**Example Repositories:**
- Hooks SDK: [example-dex](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex)
- Components SDK: [orderly-js-sdk-nextjs-template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-js-sdk-nextjs-template)

### Solana Multi-DVN Security Upgrade (Mandatory)
SDK v2.12.3 upgrades the Solana Vault contract from a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) to a 3-of-3 consensus model using three independent DVNs for cross-chain message verification. This was implemented following a LayerZero exploit to harden security.

**Impact:** DEXs that do not upgrade may experience issues with Solana deposits and withdrawals. This is a mandatory update for all DEXs integrated with Solana.

chunks.title: Order Types and Trading Features
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports a comprehensive set of order types and trading features. This guide covers advanced order types and TP/SL functionality available in the SDK.

### Trailing Stop Orders
Available since SDK v2.6.3, Trailing Stop orders activate at a trigger price, track price extremes, and execute on retrace. This allows traders to lock in profits while limiting downside risk.

**Configuration:**
- `activated_price`: Price when trailing activates
- `callback_value`: Fixed trailing amount
- `callback_rate`: Percentage trailing

**Order Type:** `TRAILING_STOP` in the `AlgoOrderRootType` enum.

**Calculation:**
- **Fixed Amount:**
  - Long: `trailing_stop = extreme_price - trailing_value`
  - Short: `trailing_stop = extreme_price + trailing_value`
- **Percentage:**
  - Long: `trailing_stop = extreme_price * (1 - trailing_rate)`
  - Short: `trailing_stop = extreme_price * (1 + trailing_rate)`

**Note:** Only one of `callback_value` or `callback_rate` can be used.

### Scaled Orders
Introduced in SDK v2.4.1, Scaled Orders allow placing multiple limit orders across a defined price range with customizable distribution.

### TP/SL with Limit Orders
Since SDK v2.6.0, users can set Partial TP/SL or Full Position TP/SL:
- **Partial TP/SL:** Supports both market and limit order execution
- **Full Position TP/SL:** Supports only market orders

**Advanced Features:**
- **SDK v2.6.1+:** Set TP/SL directly from TradingView charts
- **SDK v2.6.2+:** Edit TP/SL on pending orders
- **SDK v2.12.3+:** Advanced TP/SL with Offset and Offset% values calculated from Mark Price

### Bracket Orders
To create a bracket order (order with attached TP/SL), use the `useOrderEntry` hook and set `algo_type` to `AlgoOrderRootType.BRACKET`, then add the respective TP/SL fields.

**Important:** The `useTPSLOrder` hook can only be used with an existing open position, not for attaching TP/SL at order creation time.

### One-Click Reverse Position
Available from SDK v2.8.6, this feature allows closing the current position and opening the opposite position in one action.

### Hidden, Post-Only, IOC, and FOK Orders
SDK v2.8.13+ includes descriptive tooltips for these advanced order types:
- **Hidden:** Order not visible in the order book
- **Post-Only:** Order must be a maker order
- **IOC (Immediate or Cancel):** Execute immediately or cancel
- **FOK (Fill or Kill):** Execute entirely or cancel entirely

### Real-Time Estimated Liquidation Price
Using the Orderly Hooks SDK, the `useOrderEntry` hook provides real-time estimated liquidation price data during order creation.

**Documentation:** [useOrderEntry Real-time Data](https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/hooks/orders/use-order-entry#real-time-data)

**Example Implementation:** [CreateOrder.tsx](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/example-dex/blob/master/app/components/CreateOrder.tsx)

chunks.title: Referral and Affiliate System Integration
chunks.content:
Orderly Network provides a comprehensive referral and affiliate system that brokers can integrate into their DEX. This guide covers the Multilevel Referral Program and technical requirements.

### Multilevel Referral Program
The Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program allows brokers to scale growth and incentivize communities with multi-tier referral commissions. The program supports up to 15 levels of referrals.

**How It Works:**
- **Level 1 Affiliates:** Users who claim a referral code directly from the DEX's rewards page (e.g., `yourdomain.com/rewards/affiliate`)
- **Level 2-15:** When L1 affiliates invite others, those become L2, and so on up to L15
- **Commission Structure:** Affiliates share a percentage of their trading fee rebates with their downline
- **DEX Benefits:** The DEX earns discounted trading fees but benefits from volume growth across the network

### Technical Requirements for Brokers

1. **SDK Version:** Upgrade to SDK version 2.9.0 or later
   - Orderly One DEXs should ensure they are running the latest version available on the Orderly One platform

2. **Activation:** Enable or upgrade the referral program via:
   - Admin Tool (for SDK builders)
   - Orderly One dashboard (for no-code builders)

### User Experience

**Claiming Referral Codes:**
- Users claim codes from the rewards page rather than receiving shared codes
- Existing single-level referral codes remain usable
- New codes are generated through the multilevel system

**Post-Account Creation Binding:**
As of SDK v2.12.4, users no longer need to provide a referral code during registration and can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time.

### Integration Steps

1. **Upgrade SDK:**
```bash
npm install @orderly.network/react@latest @orderly.network/hooks@latest
```

2. **Enable Program:**
   - For SDK builders: Use the Admin Tool to activate the multilevel referral program
   - For Orderly One builders: Navigate to the Orderly One dashboard and enable the program

3. **Integrate UI:**
Use the `@orderly.network/affiliate` package for pre-built dashboard components:

```tsx
import { Dashboard, ReferralProvider } from '@orderly.network/affiliate';

<ReferralProvider
  becomeAnAffiliateUrl="https://yourdomain.com/rewards/affiliate"
  referralLinkUrl="https://yourdomain.com/rewards/affiliate"
  overwrite={{ shortBrokerName: "YourDEX" }}
>
  <Dashboard.DashboardPage />
</ReferralProvider>
```

### Documentation Resources
- **Brokers Quick Guide:** [Orderly DEX Affiliate Program - Brokers](https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/be-a-broker/orderly-dex-affiliate-program-brokers-quick-guide)
- **Affiliates Quick Guide:** [Orderly DEX Affiliate Program - Affiliates](https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/be-a-broker/orderly-dex-affiliate-program-affiliates-quick-guide)

### Backend Integration
To integrate the referral system, you need to develop a backend that generates referral keys and distributes them to your users. Documentation is available at [Referral System User Flows](https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/user-flows/referral-system).

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings and Pre-TGE Markets
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports permissionless token listings and Pre-TGE (Token Generation Event) markets, allowing builders to offer trading on new assets without manual coordination.

### Permissionless Listings
Permissionless listings allow external parties to list tokens on Orderly-powered DEXes without requiring Orderly team approval. Builders get 5 free listing slots and earn 100% of liquidation fees plus 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

**SDK Support:**
- **SDK v2.12.0+:** Fully supports permissionlessly listed symbols with proper UI rendering and trading support
- **SDK v3.0.3+:** Fixed an issue where permissionless symbols showed empty values for Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee on mobile

**Builder Responsibilities:**
When new permissionless markets are announced, builders should:
1. Sync their frontend configuration to support the new symbols
2. Notify users accordingly
3. Ensure their SDK version is up to date

### Pre-TGE Perpetual Markets
Introduced in SDK v3.1.1, Pre-TGE market support enables builders to offer perpetual trading markets before a token's official Token Generation Event (TGE).

**Use Case:**
This feature allows traders to speculate on token prices before the token is officially launched, providing early liquidity and price discovery.

**SDK Requirement:**
- SDK v3.1.1 or later

### RWA (Real-World Asset) Markets
Orderly supports RWA markets including:
- **Stock Indices:** $SPX500, $NAS100
- **Commodities:** Gold ($XAU), Silver ($XAG) with up to 20x leverage, WTI Crude Oil ($CL), Brent Crude Oil ($BZ)
- **Individual Stocks:** $NVDA, $TSLA, $GOOGL with up to 20x leverage, $AAPL, $AMZN, $MSFT, $META, $COIN, $HOOD, $SAMSUNG
- **Forex Pairs:** $JPY/USD, $EUR/USD

**UI Support:**
- **SDK v2.8.0+:** Dedicated RWA Market UI support
- **SDK v2.8.13+:** Separate RWA tab on the Market page
- **SDK v3.1.3+:** Dedicated Crypto market category alongside RWA

### Custom Asset Categories
From SDK v2.12.0, builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI. No categories are set by default — builders choose which categories to display.

**Example Categories:**
- Privacy
- Memecoins
- L1s
- DeFi
- Gaming

**Note:** Adding custom market sectors or categories to the trading UI is not currently a builder-configurable feature beyond the predefined categories. This type of UI customization would need to be evaluated by the Orderly SDK team for potential future implementation.
