|------|-----------|-----------|
| Public | 3 bps | 0 bps |
| Platinum | 1–3 bps | Negative (rebate) |
| Diamond | 1 bps | -0.20 bps |

Previously, RWA taker fees were 1–3 bps due to higher market-making costs.

### Permissionless RWA Markets
- Fee structure: **Maker -0.20 bps / Taker 1 bps**
- Same revenue split as permissionless crypto markets

## Leverage Considerations for Stocks

- Stock perps generally support **10x–20x** leverage
- **Ultra-high leverage (50x+) is NOT available** for stock perps
- **Reason**: Price gaps of 2–3% during off-hours could cause significant liquidations
- Orderly prioritizes automatic leverage reduction features before expanding limits

## Builder Integration Notes

### Adding RWA Markets to Your DEX
1. RWA markets are available by default on Orderly-powered DEXs
2. Enable specific pairs in your Orderly One dashboard
3. Ensure your frontend displays RWA-specific disclaimers if required by your jurisdiction

### Geo-Fencing Limitations
- You **cannot** hide specific pairs based on user IP/location
- You **can** geo-fence the entire platform by region
- You **can** hide pairs globally for all users

### Oracle Configuration
For permissionless RWA listings:
- Offchain feed delivery is supported and preferred
- Typically requires 2–3 reliable price feeds
- Median Price logic filters outliers

## AI Trading Agent Integration (MCP)

Builders can launch their own **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** to allow AI agents to trade directly on their DEX:
1. Add your `brokerID` to the Orderly MCP
2. AI-powered trading strategies execute through your Orderly-powered DEX
3. Details available via Orderly announcements

chunks.title: Permissionless Vaults and Trading Strategies
chunks.content:
Permissionless Vaults allow anyone to create community-managed trading vaults on Orderly-powered DEXs, monetize strategies, and attract capital — all without coding.

## Overview

Launched April 2026 alongside Permissionless Listings, Permissionless Vaults create a closed-loop growth and monetization system:

1. **List any asset** (crypto or RWA)
2. **Provide liquidity** as a market maker
3. **Launch vaults** and raise funds from the community
4. **Earn performance fees** on successful strategies

## Getting Started

### Access
```
http://app.orderly.network/vaults
```

### Deployment Time
~30 minutes from creation to live vault

## Vault Architecture

### Key Components

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Strategy Provider (SP)** | Creates and manages the vault's trading strategy |
| **SP Sub-account** | Isolated trading account for vault operations |
| **Community Depositors** | Users who allocate funds to the vault |
| **Performance Fee** | Fee charged on profits above high-water mark |

### Reserved Margin
- Fixed at **50,000 USDC** for permissionless vaults
- Ensures sufficient collateral for strategy execution

### Performance Fee Settlement
- Auto-settles when SP exceeds the **high-water mark**
- Paid as **additional SP shares** (not cash)
- Aligns incentives between SP and depositors

## Builder Benefits

### Volume Attribution
- Vault trading volume and fees can be attributed to a specific **broker ID**
- Counts toward your builder tier volume requirements
- Increases overall DEX trading activity

### Revenue Streams
1. **Trading fees** from vault activity
2. **Increased volume** helping achieve higher builder tiers
3. **Community engagement** through vault participation

## Tread.fi Market-Making Vault Partnership

Orderly partners with Tread.fi to offer specialized market-making vaults:

### How It Works
1. Users deposit **USDC** into Tread.fi vaults
2. Vaults run market-making strategies through the builder's DEX
3. Participants earn rewards from a prize pool based on:
   - Vault trading volume
   - Uptime consistency

### Builder Benefits
- Additional trading activity and fees on your DEX
- Access to Tread.fi's market-making infrastructure
- Support for future token listings and trading strategies

## Configuration for Builders

### Attributing Vault Volume
When setting up vaults, ensure the vault's trading activity is linked to your broker ID for proper volume tracking.

### Integration with DEX
- Vaults operate on top of Orderly's infrastructure
- No additional smart contract deployment required
- Vault UI accessible through your DEX or the main Orderly app

## Documentation
- Full docs: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/permissionless-vault`

## Related Features

### Trading Competitions
- Partner with **Fuul** for permissionless trading competitions
- Points programs available for all Orderly One DEXs
- No coding required

### Network-Wide Competitions
- Orderly One DEXs can participate in network competitions (e.g., 'I Love Perps')
- Enable campaigns in the Orderly One dashboard
- Users register at: `https://app.orderly.network/campaigns/perps-competition`
- Works regardless of public/private leaderboard setting

chunks.title: Order Types, Execution, and Trading Mechanics
chunks.content:
This guide covers Orderly's order types, execution rules, and trading mechanics for developers building trading interfaces.

## Order Types

### Standard Orders
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **LIMIT** | Rests on orderbook until filled or cancelled |
| **MARKET** | Executes immediately against existing orders |
| **POST_ONLY** | Limit order that only adds liquidity (never takes) |
| **IOC** (Immediate or Cancel) | Fills immediately; unfilled portion cancelled |
| **FOK** (Fill or Kill) | Must fill entirely or cancel entirely |

### Setting order_type
When using time-in-force options, pass the specific type:
```json
{
  "order_type": "POST_ONLY",
  "side": "BUY",
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "order_quantity": "0.1",
  "order_price": "65000"
}
```

> **Important**: Use `POST_ONLY`, `IOC`, or `FOK` as `order_type` — not just `LIMIT`.

### Algo Orders
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **STOP** | Triggers market/limit order at trigger price |
| **TP_SL** | Combined Take Profit / Stop Loss |
| **BRACKET** | Entry order with attached TP and SL |
| **POSITIONAL_TP_SL** | TP/SL attached to an existing position |

### Hidden Orders
- Not visible in the orderbook
- Generally charged as **taker fees** (do not provide visible liquidity)
- Exception: Two hidden orders matching each other — passive may get maker rate
- **Recommendation**: Use `POST_ONLY` to guarantee maker fee treatment

### Chase Limit Orders
- **Not supported** at the infrastructure level
- No current plans for implementation

## Price Tick Rules

Orders must satisfy the tick size requirement:
```
(price - quote_min) % quote_tick == 0
```

**Example** (BTC):
- `quote_min` = 0
- `quote_tick` = 0.1
- Valid price: 96000.0 (96000 / 0.1 = no remainder) ✓
- Invalid price: 96000.05 (remainder exists) ✗

## Maker vs Taker Determination

In trade records, the `is_maker` field indicates execution type:
```json
{
  "is_maker": 0,  // Taker order
  "fee": 0.0003   // Taker fee applied
}
```
```json
{
  "is_maker": 1,  // Maker order
  "fee": -0.00005 // Maker rebate applied
}
```

### TP/SL with place_algo_order
When placing an order with TP/SL using `place_algo_order` with a limit and trigger price:
- Executes as a **taker order** when triggered
- Taker fee applies (not maker rebate)

## Position Limits

### POSITIONAL_TP_SL Limits
| Limit | Scope |
|-------|-------|
| 1 untriggered | Per (user, symbol, close-side) |
| 10 untriggered TP/SL | Per asset |

**Example**: A user can have:
- 1 POSITIONAL_TP_SL on PERP_ETH_USDC (long close)
- 1 POSITIONAL_TP_SL on PERP_BTC_USDC (short close)
- These are independent limits

## Slippage on Low-Volume Markets

### Why It Happens
On thin-liquidity markets, large market orders:
1. Consume available orderbook depth rapidly
2. Fill in multiple batches within the same second
3. Later batches match against progressively worse prices

### Mitigation Strategies
- Use **limit orders** instead of market orders
- Stage large closes into smaller chunks
- Higher-liquidity pairs (BTC, ETH) have significantly stronger depth

## Hedge Mode

- **Not currently available** (on roadmap, not prioritized)
- **Workaround**: Use sub-accounts or hybrid isolated/cross margin

## Sub-Accounts

Live since June 2025:
- Manage multiple strategies under one wallet
- Hedge positions by counter-trading yourself
- Isolate risk without juggling multiple wallets

### Limitations
- Cannot create custodian accounts with sub-accounts for multiple users
- Each user must register their own account with their own wallet signature
- Positions cannot be isolated for different users under the same account

## System Maintenance Impact

### During Maintenance Windows
- Users **cannot** place or cancel orders
- **Algorithmic orders do NOT trigger** (by design — prevents price spikes from low liquidity)
- Withdrawals suspended

### Builder Recommendations
- Notify users before scheduled maintenance
- Advise closing positions or adjusting algo orders beforehand
- Orderly is developing zero-downtime deployments

## Deposit Requirements

All DEXs built with Orderly require users to:
1. Pre-position the correct asset
2. Deposit on the correct chain
3. Funds must be in the Orderly vault **before** order execution

> **Note**: This is a prerequisite step — no trading on margin without deposited collateral.

## Cross-Chain Architecture

- All volume settled on **Orderly Chain** (L2, OP Stack)
- Users deposit into vault contracts on their desired chain
- **LayerZero** message passing informs Orderly Chain
- Funds technically remain on source chain
- Off-chain matching engine, on-chain settlement
- Vault rebalancing occurs when imbalanced due to withdrawals

## Real-Time Volume Calculation

For builders tracking user volume:
```javascript
// perp_trading_volume_ltd: Daily snapshot at 00:00 UTC
// perp_trading_volume_today: Near real-time via Redis cache

const realTimeVolume = perp_trading_volume_ltd + perp_trading_volume_today;
```

> **Note**: `perp_trading_volume_today` resets at 00:00 UTC and may only start updating from 01:00 UTC onward.

## PnL Settlement

- On-chain settlement transfers losses from one trader to gains of another at vault level
- Before settlement, actual funds in on-chain vault are not affected
- Users can only withdraw after settling unrealized PnL
- Full amount withdrawal is possible even with negative unsettled PnL (settlement button not strictly required)

chunks.title: TradingView Integration and DEX Customization
chunks.content:
This guide covers TradingView chart licensing, DEX domain configuration, and UI customization for Orderly-powered platforms.

## TradingView Advanced Charts License

### Requirements
TradingView charts are included by default in Orderly DEXs, but builders **must apply for a license** once their site is live.

### Application Process
1. **Prerequisites**:
   - Site must be publicly accessible
   - Working SSL certificate
   - Custom domain configured and propagated
   - Personal GitHub profile (enterprise accounts NOT accepted)
   - Corporate email address (Gmail/ProtonMail NOT accepted)

2. **Apply at**: `https://www.tradingview.com/advanced-charts/`
   - Registered company: Not required
   - Data feed: Indicate you have your own data feed
   - Create a GitHub profile if you don't have one

3. **Timeline**:
   - DNS propagation: Up to 24 hours
   - License approval: Typically a few days to a week
   - Secure your domain BEFORE applying to avoid back-and-forth

### Important Notes
- **One license per domain**: Each DEX on a separate domain needs its own license
- The TradingView attribution link is included in the DEX by default
- Without a valid license, TradingView may contact the builder
- License is **free** to use

## Custom Domain DNS Configuration

### Setup Steps
1. Add a **CNAME** DNS record for your subdomain
2. Point to the deployment target

**Example** (V2 DEX Creator):
```
Type: CNAME
Name: trade (or your subdomain)
Value: orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io
```

### Propagation Times
| Provider | Typical Time |
|----------|-------------|
| Cloudflare | ~5 minutes |
| cPanel | May take longer |
| Others | Up to 24 hours |

## PnL Poster Customization

### Configuration
In the DEX creator, navigate to PnL poster settings and upload custom backgrounds.

### Specifications
| Property | Requirement |
|----------|-------------|
| Aspect Ratio | 16:9 |
| Recommended Size | 960 × 540 px |
| Left Side | Dark colors (for text contrast) |

### Design Notes
- Trading data overlays the **left side** of the image
- Both profit and loss trades use the same poster unless separate configurations are added
- Ensure sufficient contrast for overlaid white/light text

## Markets Page Configuration

### Enabling via Orderly One
- Navigate to navigation menus configuration
- Enable the Markets page toggle

### Custom Market Pages
For features beyond the default Orderly One offering:
1. Fork the existing repository
2. Self-host your DEX
3. Add custom code for market page features

## Spot Swap Module

Orderly One DEXs include integrated spot swap functionality (powered by WOOFi).

### Enable Swap
1. Open Orderly One dashboard
2. Enable the swap page in configuration

### Example URL
```
https://dex.orderly.network/{your-dex}/swap
```

### Source Code
```tsx
// Available at:
// https://github.com/OrderlyNetworkDexCreator/{your-dex}/blob/main/app/pages/swap/Index.tsx
```

### Notes
- Swap is an on-chain transaction
- Trading fees viewable from the Orderly One graduation page

## Referral System Setup

### Multi-Level Referral
1. Navigate to: `https://dex.orderly.network/en/referral`
2. Login credentials available via button on the referral page
3. Set default commission rate (e.g., 10%)
4. Manually assign referral codes to specific traders

### Configuration Options
| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Commission Rate | Percentage of broker fee shared with referrer |
| Minimum Volume | Threshold before referral link generates (cannot be absolute 0) |
| Multi-Level | Up to 15 layers supported |

### Current Limitations (v1 Multi-Level)
- Affiliates cannot create multiple tracking links themselves
- Cannot rename/label links
- Cannot filter reporting by individual tracking link and date
- Only root (L1) affiliate codes can be created by builders

### Referral Fee vs Rebate
- **Referral Fee**: Portion given to the referrer
- **Rebate**: Portion given back to the referee as a discount

### Admin Dashboard
```
https://admin.orderly.network/referral
```
View volume, commissions, and earnings per client.

## DEX Board Listing

### Getting Listed
1. Fill out DEX information: `https://dex.orderly.network/dex/card`
2. Complete at least one test trade (non-zero volume)
3. Your DEX appears at: `https://dex.orderly.network/board`

### Volume Tracking
- DEX board: `https://dex.orderly.network/board`
- Updates approximately every hour
- Set up your board on Orderly One

## Geo-Fencing and Pair Visibility

### What You CAN Do
- Hide trading pairs **globally** for all users
- Geo-fence the **entire platform** by region (block/allow access)

### What You CANNOT Do
- Hide specific pairs based on user IP address
- Selectively remove individual pairs by geography

## Trading Competitions

### Network-Wide Competitions
1. Enable campaign in Orderly One dashboard
2. Campaign displays at top of your DEX
3. Users register at: `https://app.orderly.network/campaigns/perps-competition`
4. Works with public or private leaderboard settings

### Custom Competitions
- Partner with **Fuul** for permissionless competitions and points programs
- No coding required
- Multi-level referral system (CEX-style, up to 15 levels)

## Competition Winnings Distribution
- Sent to user's **Orderly trading account** (AccountID)
- NOT sent to external Web3 wallet
- Appears as internal deposit/transfer
- Users check trading account balance for credited amount

chunks.title: Trading Fees, Tiers, and Revenue Sharing
chunks.content:
Orderly's fee structure is designed to give builders flexibility in monetization while offering competitive rates to traders. This guide covers base fees, the Builder Tier System, maker rebates, and revenue distribution.

## Base Fee Structure

Orderly charges a base fee that varies by builder tier. Builders set their own user-facing fees; the difference between the user fee and the base fee is the builder's revenue.

| Asset Type | Base Taker Fee | Base Maker Fee |
|------------|---------------|----------------|
| Crypto | 3 bps (Public tier) | 0 bps (rebates available) |
| RWA | 1–3 bps (aligned with crypto as of July 2026) | 0 bps (rebates available) |

**Important:** Fees are collected in the **received (converted) token**, not the source token. For example, if a user swaps USDC → ETH, fees are charged in ETH. Fees are deducted post-trade and do not affect the order price.

## Builder Tier System

Builders are categorized into tiers based on **30-day average trading volume** OR **$ORDER tokens staked**:

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Volume Requirement | Staking Requirement |
|------|---------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Public | 3 bps | Default | Default |
| Silver | Reduced | Mid-tier | Mid-tier |
| Gold | Reduced | Higher | Higher |
| Platinum | 2 bps | ≥$750M | ≥3M ORDER |
| Diamond | 1 bps | ≥$2B | ≥7M ORDER |

Higher tiers unlock benefits including marketing support, listing campaigns, and reduced base fees.

## Maker Fee Rebates

As of 2026, Orderly offers **negative maker fees** (rebates) ranging from **-0.20 bps to 0 bps** for Silver tier and above. This means:

- Builders can effectively **pay users** to provide liquidity
- Builders can keep the rebate as revenue or pass it to users as volume incentives
- Negative maker fees settle **immediately** on each execution for traders
- Builder revenue (maker + taker) is batched and settled **once per day** at 00:00 UTC

### Example Minimum Fee Configuration (Diamond Tier)

```
Crypto: Maker -0.002%, Taker 0.01%
RWA:    Maker -0.002%, Taker 0.03%
```

## Custom Fees Per Order

As of the April 28, 2026 upgrade, Orderly supports **custom trading fees per order**, allowing granular fee configuration at the individual order level.

## Configuring Volume-Based Fee Tiers

Use the Python fee admin script to configure per-user fee tiers based on trading volume:

```bash
# Clone the fee admin tool
git clone https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin
```

Configure tiers in a YAML file:

```yaml
rate:
  fee_tier:
  - maker_fee: 0.03%
    taker_fee: 0.07%
    tier: '1'
    volume_max: 500000
    volume_min: 0
  - maker_fee: 0.02%
    taker_fee: 0.05%
    tier: '2'
    volume_max: 2000000
    volume_min: 500001
```

**Important:** This script updates **per-user** fee tiers — it does not change the default/static fee displayed on the UI. Run it periodically (e.g., via cron job). Default fees are changed separately in the admin console at `https://admin.orderly.network/`.

## Revenue Sharing and Fee Collection

### How Fees Are Distributed
- **Maker volume**: 100% of fees go to the broker
- **Taker volume**: Base fee goes to Orderly, remainder to broker
- Staking $ORDER reduces Orderly's share, increasing broker revenue

### Referral Fee Splits
The referrer and referee share the broker's **net fee** (gross fee minus Orderly's base fee):

```
Example:
- User fee: 4 bps taker / 1 bps maker
- Orderly base: 3 bps / 0 bps
- Broker net: 1 bps / 1 bps
- With 50/50 referral split:
  - Broker: 0.5 / 0.5 bps
  - Referrer: 0.5 / 0.5 bps
  - Trader: no discount
```

The `order_tag` parameter overrides any existing referral code. Rebates are credited daily.

### Checking and Withdrawing Fees
Connect the admin wallet to the Orderly UI to view withdrawable balance. For multisig wallets, use the broker registration tool at `https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/`.

## Excalibur Club

Brokers earn a **0.5 bps rebate** on all trading volume from users exceeding **250M USDC** in trailing 30-day volume. Rewards are calculated and paid monthly.

## Tracking Volume and Revenue

Use the Dune Analytics dashboard filtered by broker ID:
- Daily volume: `https://dune.com/queries/3369147/5652166`
- Daily active users: `https://dune.com/queries/3369187/5652252`
- Full dashboard: `https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-dashboard`

chunks.title: Margin Modes, Leverage, and Liquidation
chunks.content:
Orderly supports both Cross Margin and Isolated Margin modes for perpetual futures trading. Understanding these modes is critical for risk management and position sizing.

## Margin Modes Overview

| Feature | Cross Margin | Isolated Margin |
|---------|-------------|----------------|
| Collateral | Entire account balance | Fixed allocation per position |
| Max Loss | Entire account balance | Capped at allocated margin |
| Collateral Assets | USDC, USDT, ETH, BNB, SOL (chain-dependent) | **USDC only** |
| Simultaneous Positions | Shared margin pool | Independent per position |
| Permissionless Markets | Not supported | Supported |

**Key Point:** Both modes can operate simultaneously on the same account. Traders specify the margin mode per order. You can even hold a Cross long and an Isolated short on the same symbol at the same time.

## Multi-Collateral Support

Orderly supports native multi-collateral trading — no need to swap to USDC first:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDT, USDC |

**Note:** Isolated Margin positions require **USDC only**. Convert other assets to USDC before trading in Isolated mode.

## Leverage Configuration

Leverage is set **per symbol, per margin mode** independently:

```
Example:
- BTC-PERP Cross Margin: 10x
- BTC-PERP Isolated Margin: 20x
- ETH-PERP Isolated Margin: 5x
```

Higher leverage in Isolated mode means less margin allocated and a tighter liquidation price.

### Effective Maximum Leverage

The actual maximum leverage available depends on existing open positions and available margin. If other positions consume margin, you may not be able to open a full maximum leverage position.

### Cross-Margin Displayed Leverage

With cross-margin, as a position becomes profitable, the **displayed leverage decreases** because unrealized PnL is added to margin:

```
Example:
- Start: $100 margin, $400 position → 4x leverage
- Price doubles: margin = $500 ($100 + $400 PnL), position = $800
- Displayed leverage: 800/500 = 1.6x
```

## Adding/Reducing Margin on Isolated Positions

Use the `POST /v1/position_margin` endpoint:

### Add Margin (lowers liquidation price)
```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "amount": "100",
  "type": "ADD"
}
```

### Reduce Margin (frees up balance)
```json
{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "amount": "50",
  "type": "REDUCE"
}
```

- **ADD**: Transfers from available balance → isolated position
- **REDUCE**: Transfers from isolated position → available balance

## Liquidation Price Formula

```
Position Liq. Price = max(
  mark_price_i + (
    total_collateral_value - sum(abs(position_qty_i) * mark_price_i * MMRi)
  ) / (abs(position_qty_i) * MMRi - position_qty_i),
  0
)
```

Where:
- `mark_price_i` = mark price of the position
- `total_collateral_value` = total collateral in the account
- `position_qty_i` = position quantity (signed)
- `MMRi` = Maintenance Margin Rate for the symbol (e.g., 0.05 for 5%)
- `Total MM = positionQty * MMR`

### Why Liquidations May Occur Before Displayed Price

1. **Liquidation fees**: The displayed price may not account for the liquidation fee, which can be significant
2. **Funding fees**: Accumulated funding fees can erode collateral and shift the liquidation price
3. **Cross-margin interactions**: Other losing positions in cross-margin mode consume shared collateral

### Isolated Margin Liquidation

When an Isolated position is liquidated, **only the margin assigned to that position is lost**. All other positions and remaining balance are untouched.

## Mark Price and Index Price

- **Index Price**: Aggregated from external CEX sources (Binance, OKX, KuCoin, Gate, Bybit), weighted by volume
- **Mark Price**: Based on index price plus Orderly market conditions
- **Oracle System**: Orderly uses its own aggregator pulling from 3+ sources (CEX spot + on-chain oracles like Pyth/Stork)

**Note on Price Differences:** Orderly displays prices in **USDC** (settlement asset), while most exchanges display in USDT. Converting USDT prices to USDC (dividing by ~1.0006) typically aligns them with Orderly's prices.

## Funding Rate

The funding rate uses a fixed formula and is capped. It is charged based on market conditions — heavily skewed trading activity results in larger funding rates. Full formula: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/funding-rate#funding-rate`

chunks.title: Permissionless Listings and Custom Markets
chunks.content:
Orderly's Permissionless Listing framework allows builders to list any perpetual market — crypto, RWA, Pre-TGE tokens, forex, commodities — without waiting for Orderly to add data sources.

## Overview

Permissionless Listings operate under an **isolated-risk model**:
- Listed markets are available in **Isolated Margin only** (no Cross Margin)
- Each builder gets **5 free listing slots**
- Market owners earn **100% of liquidation fees** plus **50% of Orderly's base fee** on that market
- No listing fee required

## Standard Listing Requirements

For standard (non-permissionless) listings, the following criteria must be met:

1. **Price Index**: At least 3+ price feed sources
2. **Market Maker**: An integrated MM must be engaged with Orderly
3. **Minimum FDV**: 20M+
4. **Liquidity Requirements**:
   - Minimum 20K USD in -2% depth
   - Minimum 20K USD in +2% depth
   - Minimum 15 levels in -2% and +2% depth
   - Spread ≤ 50 bps
   - Uptime ≥ 90%

## Custom Oracles

With Permissionless Listing, builders can push their own asset price data directly to Orderly:

- Custom oracle feeds can be **combined** with existing CEX and oracle price feeds
- Orderly covers the cost of price feeds (including Pyth and Stork) for permissionless listings
- Builders do not need to source or pay for their own price feeds

Documentation: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/custom-oracle#custom-oracle`

## Supported Asset Categories

Orderly supports a wide variety of markets beyond crypto:

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| Crypto Perpetuals | BTC, ETH, SOL, and 100+ altcoins |
| RWA - Stock Indices | SPX500, NAS100 |
| RWA - Precious Metals | Gold (XAU), Silver (XAG) — up to 20x leverage |
| RWA - Individual Stocks | NVDA, TSLA, GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN, MSFT — up to 20x, 24/7 |
| RWA - Commodities | WTI Crude Oil, Brent Crude Oil |
| RWA - Forex | JPY/USD, EUR/USD |
| Pre-TGE Markets | Synthetic Pre-TGE Oracle with tightened risk caps |

## Listing Workflow

1. **Choose your asset** and ensure price data availability
2. **Configure your oracle** (custom or existing feeds)
3. **Engage a market maker** or deploy an MM bot
4. **List the market** via the Permissionless Listing interface
5. **Sync your frontend** configuration to display the new market

**Important:** New permissionless markets require frontend configuration sync to display correctly on your DEX.

## RWA Market Details

Orderly operates its own orderbook and liquidity infrastructure for RWA markets — it does not rely on third-party RWA providers. Prices are sourced through oracles, and market makers provide liquidity to keep markets aligned with reference prices.

### RWA Fee Structure (Updated July 2026)

RWA pair fees are now **equal to crypto pair fees**:
- RWA Taker Fee: reduced from 1–3 bps to **1–3 bps**
- RWA Maker Fee: 0 bps (rebates available)

## Community Vote to Retain

Tokens with sustained low metrics may face delisting via a community vote:

- A 5-day voting period is opened
- To retain a token, **>3% (or 5%) of staked $ORDER** must vote "AGAINST Delisting"
- Tokens without sufficient votes are delisted
- The index/mark price is **fixed at the average price of the last hour** before delisting

Brokers are encouraged to participate and inform their communities about tokens at risk.

## Viewing Supported Markets

- Full market list: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/supported-markets`
- Demo site with all symbols: `demo.orderly.network`

## Symbol Format

Orderly uses the format `PERP_<SYMBOL>_USDC` for all trading pairs:
```
PERP_ETH_USDC
PERP_BTC_USDC
PERP_NVDA_USDC
PERP_XAU_USDC
```

chunks.title: Order Types, Execution, and Common Issues
chunks.content:
This guide covers Orderly's order types, execution behavior, and solutions to common trading issues.

## Order Types

### Standard Orders
- **LIMIT**: Executes at specified price or better
- **MARKET**: Executes immediately at best available price

### Time-in-Force Options
- **GTC** (Good Till Cancel): Default, remains open until filled or cancelled
- **FOK** (Fill or Kill): Must be fully filled immediately or entire order is cancelled
- **IOC** (Immediate or Cancel): Fills as much as possible immediately; remainder cancelled

### Algo Orders
- **TP_SL**: Take Profit / Stop Loss attached to entry orders (bracket orders)
- **POSITIONAL_TP_SL**: TP/SL attached to an existing open position
- **BRACKET**: Combined entry + TP + SL order
- **STOP**: Stop/trigger orders

**Important:** Each bracket order supports only **one** Positional or full-quantity TPSL. For multiple TP/SL levels, place multiple bracket orders with different quantities.

### Hidden Orders
Hidden orders are **always counted as taker orders** in volume data, regardless of whether they were placed as limit orders. This is by design in the matching engine.

## FOK and IOC Cancellation Issues

### Problem: FOK/IOC orders get cancelled immediately

**Cause:** Insufficient liquidity at or better than the specified price.

- **FOK**: Cancelled without any execution if cannot be fully filled
- **IOC**: Matches what's available; remaining quantity cancelled

**Solutions:**
1. Leave room in your price relative to the current best bid/ask
2. Subscribe to orderbook updates (pushed every ~200ms) for freshest pricing
3. Use BBO stream (pushed every ~1s) as a lighter alternative

## Multi-Hop Swap Failures

### Problem: Second hop fails in a multi-hop swap (e.g., SWEAT → USDC → NEAR)

If the first FOK order fills but the second fails, funds remain in the intermediary token (e.g., USDC).

**Solution:**
1. Retry with a more aggressive price
2. Fall back to market orders
3. Accept small slippage/fee loss on the buyback

**Note:** There is no built-in atomic rollback across multiple orders. Your application logic must handle recovery.

## Order Validation Errors

| Error Code | HTTP | Meaning | Solution |
|-----------|------|---------|----------|
| -1102 | 400 | Order value (price × size) too small | Increase order size or price |
| -1103 | 400 | Price validation failure | Check min/max price and tick size |
| -1105 | 400 | Price too far from mid price | Adjust limit price closer to mid price |
| -1008 | 400 | Settlement quantity exceeds limit | Reduce settlement quantity |

## Volume Counting

### How Volume Is Calculated
- Volume is based on **notional value** (e.g., $10 margin at 10x leverage = $100 notional)
- Opening and closing a position counts as **two separate orders** (counted twice)
- The 7-day trading volume display uses a **rolling window**, settled daily at 00:00 UTC

### Why Volume May Decrease
Large older transactions falling out of the 7-day window while smaller new ones enter can cause displayed volume to decrease.

## PnL Calculation

- **All Time PnL** reflects only **gross trading PnL** — it does NOT include trading fees
- To calculate net PnL, deduct total trading fees from the All Time PnL value
- `realized_pnl` field returns `null` for fills older than 24 hours (archived data doesn't retain this column)

## Price Protection

Orderly's order-book based system provides built-in price protection through **limit orders**, which prevent execution at unexpected prices. There is no separate anti-slippage mechanism — use limit orders for price certainty.

## Tick Size Adjustments

As of the April 28, 2026 upgrade, Orderly supports **configurable tick size** changes for trading pairs, allowing more granular price levels.

## Omnichain Balance Behavior

Your balance is **shared across all chains** within the same environment (all testnets or all mainnets). Seeing the same balance on Monad and Arbitrum is expected — you can withdraw to any supported chain.

## Withdrawal Issues

### Margin Check Error on Spot-Only Accounts
A previously identified bug could incorrectly block spot-only users from withdrawing. This has been fixed. If encountered, Orderly support can manually clear the user's cache.

### Insufficient Liquidity on Target Chain
If the target withdrawal chain lacks sufficient liquidity, an additional cross-chain transfer fee is deducted to facilitate the transfer.

chunks.title: Permissionless Vaults and OmniVault
chunks.content:
Orderly offers two vault systems: **Permissionless Vaults** for builders to deploy custom yield strategies, and the **OmniVault** as the flagship protocol-level vault.

## Permissionless Vaults

Permissionless Vaults allow anyone to deploy yield strategies on Orderly in under 30 minutes, creating a closed-loop growth and monetization system.

### Workflow

1. **List any asset** (crypto or RWA) via Permissionless Listing
2. **Provide liquidity** as a market maker
3. **Launch your vault** with a custom strategy
4. **Raise funds** from the community
5. **Earn performance fees** on profits

### Getting Started

- Portal: `http://app.orderly.network/vaults`
- Documentation: `https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/permissionless-vault#permissionless-vault`

### How PMV and PML Work Together

Permissionless Vaults (PMV) provide liquidity infrastructure for Permissionless Listings (PML):

- Vaults are managed by **Strategy Providers (SPs)** who can opt-in to connect with specific Brokers
- Participation is **voluntary** — no forced assignment or automatic linking
- A Permissionless Vault can function purely as an investment fund without any Broker association
- A permissionlessly listed market does not require a Permissionless Vault

### Vault Operation Reserve

When creating a vault, a **non-refundable deposit of 0.1 ETH per chain** is required to cover future cross-chain transfer operations. If the vault's ETH balance is depleted:
- Cross-chain fund transfers will fail
- New LP deposits cannot enter the DEX for trading
- The creator is responsible for maintaining sufficient ETH balance

## OmniVault (Protocol Vault)

OmniVault is Orderly's flagship vault built on the Strategy Vault infrastructure.

### Key Details

| Feature | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Strategy | Delta-neutral market-making |
| Strategy Provider | Vovega Research (transitioned from Kronos Research) |
| Markets | Top 40 markets on Orderly |
| Hedging | Binance via Ceffu custody integration |
| Fees | Zero fees charged to users |
| Max Drawdown | 0.22% since inception |
| Revenue Sources | Up to 40% of Orderly fees + liquidation proceeds |
| Chains | Multiple chains including SEI |

### How Yield Is Generated

1. Users deposit **USDC** from any supported chain
2. Funds are mirrored to a custodial account (Ceffu) for trading on Binance
3. Strategy Providers execute fully-hedged market-making strategies
4. Users earn a proportional share of the vault's PnL

### Share Price Calculation

```
share price = mainAssetsAfterFee / mainShares
```

The vault smart contract is custom (not ERC-4626 compliant). Contract addresses can be found on the Orderly Explorer.

### Integration

OmniVault is integrated with:
- Binance Web3 Wallet
- Gate
- DeBank

### Multisig Support

Multisig wallets can interact with the vault, though **nested multisigs** may encounter issues.

## Strategy Vault Infrastructure

Strategy Vault is the core technical product providing:
- Underlying smart contracts
- CeFi clearing capabilities
- Foundation for protocol-level vaults like OmniVault

It sits alongside the core builder integration path as a separate product offering.

## Risk Disclaimer

All yields are subject to market risks and may fluctuate. Past performance is not indicative of future results, and returns are not guaranteed. Strategy Providers operate at arm's length from Orderly, and Orderly does not guarantee their performance or assume liability for their actions.

chunks.title: Broker Setup, Admin, and DEX Operations
chunks.content:
This guide covers the operational aspects of running an Orderly-powered DEX, from initial setup to ongoing management.

## Broker Registration

### Setting Up a Broker ID

Register at: `https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/` (supports EVM and Solana)

**Required Information:**
- Broker ID (e.g., 'mybroker')
- Broker Name
- Default Taker Fee
- Default Maker Fee
- Domain (needed for TradingView license)

**Base Fees:** Orderly charges 0.03% taker / 0% maker. Anything above the base taker fee is retained by the broker.

### Admin Wallet Setup

1. Register your wallet at the broker registration portal
2. Orderly team upgrades it to admin status
3. Connect to your DEX UI with the admin wallet
4. Accumulated fees appear and can be withdrawn

**Important:** Fees are only collected from registration time forward (not retroactively). Multisig wallets are supported on EVM.

### Using a Solana Wallet as Admin

The registration UI doesn't yet support Solana wallet selection directly. Workaround:
1. Clone the DEX creator template
2. Change broker ID in `.env`
3. Switch to Solana chain
4. Complete registration

Alternatively, use an EVM wallet as admin even for Solana-only trading.

### Depositing from a Multisig Wallet

1. Connect via WalletConnect
2. Select the proper chain
3. Select 'EOA wallet' as registration type (even for multisig)
4. Sign the approval transaction in the multisig interface
5. Initiate the deposit transaction (also routed to multisig)

**Tip:** If balance doesn't appear, switch chains back and forth to refresh the RPC connection.

## DEX Graduation

Before graduation, all trades route through the 'demo' broker ID with default fees (0.06% taker / 0.03% maker).

**To Graduate:**
1. Click 'Graduate now' in the Orderly One panel
2. Define Maker and Taker fees
3. Set your custom broker ID
4. Pay a $10 graduation fee (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate)

After graduation, you can set custom fees (decimals like 2.5 bps supported).

**Warning:** Changing from 'demo' to a custom broker ID may cause issues for existing users' balances and trades. Consider setting up a new DEX instance for migration.

**Note:** Historical trading data cannot be cleared (recorded on-chain). To start fresh, create a new broker ID.

## TradingView License

Brokers must obtain their own TradingView license:
- **Advanced Charts**: Apply at `https://www.tradingview.com/advanced-charts/` — typically free, takes a few days
- **Trading Platform (TP)**: Paid at $50,000/year — apply directly with TradingView (discounts may be available for Orderly builders)

### Attribution Requirements
The free Advanced Charts license requires:
- TradingView logo on your public website
- A mention/hyperlink on a public page (e.g., 'Partners' page)
- TradingView reviews sufficiency case-by-case

### Customizing Chart Colors (Self-Hosted)

Modify `app/utils/config.tsx`:

```typescript
tradingViewConfig: {
  overrides: {
    "paneProperties.background": "#000000",
    "scalesProperties.textColor": "#FFFFFF",
  },
}
```

This customization requires forking the repo — not directly supported on Orderly One.

## Referral System

### Constructing Referral Links

Append a `ref` query parameter:
```
https://trade.yourdomain.xyz/en/perp/PERP_ETH_USDC?ref=ABCDEFG
```

### Auto Referral Code

When enabled, users reaching a configurable minimum volume (e.g., 10,000 USD) automatically become affiliates and can generate referral codes.

### Referral Structure

Orderly supports a **2-tier model only**: Operator → Partner → Trader. Multi-tier (3+) systems are not supported due to legal concerns (MLM classification).

## Trading Competitions and Campaigns

### Points System

Orderly One supports a customizable points system:
- Records trading volume and PnL
- Converts to points
- Supports trading competitions and airdrop campaigns
- Redemption system still in development

### Competition Scoring

Uses a 'Hybrid Volatility-Adjusted Scoring Mechanism':
- Considers both PnL and ROI for fair competition across account sizes
- Referral bonuses: 10% of invitee's points
- Social sharing bonuses (X, Telegram)
- 'Loser boost': Bottom 50% get +10% point boost next season

### Prize Pool Configuration

```json
{
  "prize_pools": [
    {
      "pool_id": "trading1",
      "label": "Trading volume",
      "total_prize": 20000,
      "currency": "USDC",
      "metric": "volume",
      "tiers": [
        { "position": 1, "amount": 1400 },
        { "position": 2, "amount": 1200 },
        { "position_range": [4, 5], "amount": 750 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Note:** Trading competitions cannot be configured directly via Orderly One no-code platform — they require backend setup.

## Broker Offboarding

Orderly can disable deposits for a specific broker but cannot stop trading or force-close positions. The broker must:
1. Wind down their frontend
2. Direct users to `https://offboarding.orderly.network/`
3. Users can still manage positions and withdraw funds there

## Sharing Broker IDs

Sharing a single broker ID across multiple DEX frontends is **not recommended**. Instead:
1. Invite others as referrers in your affiliate program
2. Join the **Vanguard Distributor Program** (`https://dex.orderly.network/distributor`) to invite builders to create their own DEXs while you earn distributor rewards

## Growth Strategies

Successful strategies observed across Orderly brokers:
1. **Trading competitions** to drive volume
2. **KOL partnerships** to leverage influencer communities
3. **Unique features** like copy trading and innovative functionality

## CSS Theming

Use CSS custom properties prefixed with `--oui-`:

```css
:root {
  --oui-color-primary: #your-color;
  --oui-color-secondary: #your-color;
  --oui-color-trading-profit: #00b894;
  --oui-color-trading-loss: #ff6b6b;
}
```

For Orderly One, paste CSS in the theme editor. For custom deployments, include in your app's styles directory.

## PnL Share Banners

Upload custom backgrounds for PnL banners:
- 16:9 aspect ratio
- Empty space on the left (trading info displayed here)
- Custom design on the right side

chunks.title: Orderly DEX Swap and Omnichain Features
chunks.content:
Orderly provides omnichain trading features that extend beyond perpetual futures, including token swaps and cross-chain operations.

## Orderly One Swaps (DEX Swap)

Orderly One Swaps allow DEXs to offer omnichain token swaps powered by WOOFi.

### Key Features
- Connects to **15+ chains** with aggregator-level pricing
- Brokers earn **70% of all swap trading fees**
- Optionally configure custom fee structures
- Frontend UI appearance remains similar — fee-earning is the key addition

### Activation
Upgrade your DEX via the Orderly One dashboard to activate swap functionality.

## Omnichain Architecture

Orderly's system is organized into three layers:

| Layer | Location | Function |
|-------|----------|----------|
| **Asset Layer** | Each supported chain | User-facing: registration, deposits, withdrawals |
| **Settlement Layer** | Single chain | Transaction ledger behind the scenes |
| **Engine Layer** | Centralized | Orderbook, order management, execution |

### Self-Custody Model

Users keep control of their wallets while interacting with your application. All operations (registration, deposits, withdrawals, trading) happen from the user's **native chain** via the Asset Layer — no chain switching required.

### Shared Balance Across Chains

Your balance is shared across all chains within the same environment:
- All testnets share one balance
- All mainnets share one balance
- Withdraw to any supported chain within the same environment

## Supported Chains

| Chain | Deposit/Withdraw |
|-------|-----------------|
| Arbitrum | ✅ |
| Optimism | ✅ |
| Base | ✅ |
| Mantle | ✅ |
| Ethereum Mainnet | ✅ |
| Avalanche | ✅ |
| SEI | ✅ |
| Morph | ✅ |
| Sonic | ✅ |
| Solana | ✅ (native via Orderly Unity) |
| Polygon | ❌ (exclusivity agreement) |

## Tracking TVL and On-Chain Data

To track protocol interaction and TVL, index these contract events:

```javascript
// Deposit events
AccountDepositTo  // user: args.userAddress
AccountDeposit    // user: args.userAddress

// Withdrawal event
AccountWithdraw   // user: args.receiver (NOT args.sender)
```

**TVL Calculation:**
```
TVL = sum(deposits) - sum(withdrawals)
```

For withdrawals, the fee is already deducted from the `amount` field — use `price * amount` directly.

### Contract Addresses
- All chains: `https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/addresses`
- Solana-specific: `https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/addresses#solana`
- Contract ABIs: `https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/contract-evm-abi`

## Testnet Access

Enable/disable testnet from the Orderly One dashboard:
1. DEX owner enables testnet chains in dashboard settings
2. Users connect to testnet
3. Use the faucet to load wallets for testing

### Testnet Faucet
- Each wallet can claim up to **3 times**
- If depleted, Orderly team can resupply
- Users who exhaust claims can register a new wallet
- **Use Orderly's testnet USDC** (not official Monad testnet USDC) — it's integrated with the UI trading faucet

## Exporting Trading History

Use the Orderly Explorer dashboard for tax purposes:
`https://dashboard.orderly.network/explorer`

## Viewing User Data

While Orderly's backend doesn't expose traders' personal information publicly, deposit/withdrawal/trade data is posted to Orderly's settlement L2:
- Indexer dashboard: `https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/`
- Data is delayed by a few minutes

## Custom Points/Rewards Programs

Orderly provides access to raw trading data (commission paid, trading volume) for building custom points programs. The built-in Point Program on Orderly One covers standard metrics, but raw data enables custom implementations.

## Prediction Markets and Custom Products

Orderly's CLOB infrastructure can potentially power prediction market platforms. The integrating team handles their own liquidity and market management while using Orderly's orderbook. Contact the Orderly BD team to discuss feasibility and white-label options.

For other custom products (binary options, etc.), Orderly is open to adding new products to its own engine and risk management layers. Discuss feasibility directly with the technical team.

chunks.title: Broker Registration and Admin Wallet Setup
chunks.content:
Setting up a broker on Orderly Network requires registering a Broker ID, configuring an admin wallet, and linking them to your DEX. This guide covers the complete registration lifecycle.

## Step 1: Request a Broker ID

Provide the Orderly team with the following details for backend configuration (takes 1–3 days including multisig signing):

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| **Broker ID** | Unique lowercase string identifier | `my_dex` |
| **Broker Name** | Display name for your DEX | `My DEX` |
| **Default Taker Fee** | Fee charged to takers | `0.06%` (6 bps) |
| **Default Maker Fee** | Fee charged to makers | `0.02%` (2 bps) |
| **Broker Tier** | Fee tier classification | `public` |
| **Staking Wallet** | Wallet holding staked ORDER tokens (optional) | `0x...` |
| **Environment** | Production, Staging, or both | `Production` |

> **Development Tip:** Use Broker ID `demo` during development and testing. Switch to your assigned Broker ID before going live. Migrating users from `demo` to a production Broker ID is **not possible** — users would need to withdraw, redeposit, and re-register.

## Step 2: Register an Admin Wallet

After your Broker ID is created, register an admin wallet at:

```
https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/
```

### Registration Process
1. Connect your designated admin wallet (EOA or multisig)
2. Select your Broker ID from the dropdown
3. Click **Load Connected Address** (ignore Delegate Signer Address if using an EOA)
4. Sign the registration message
5. Share the wallet address with the Orderly team to complete backend linking

> **Important:** Registration must be done **separately for testnet and mainnet**. You can use different admin wallets for each environment.

### Admin Wallet Functions
The admin wallet serves three critical roles:
1. **Receiving broker fees** (distributed daily, typically a few minutes past midnight UTC)
2. **Managing user fee rate configurations**
3. **Managing referral codes and affiliate programs**

A single admin account handles all three roles — it cannot be split into separate wallets for different functions.

## Step 3: Access the Admin Console

Once configured, access the admin dashboard:

| Environment | URL |
|-------------|-----|
| **Mainnet** | `https://admin.orderly.network/login` |
| **Testnet** | `https://testnet-admin.orderly.network/login` |

Log in using the registered admin wallet.

## Step 4: Configure Your DEX Environment

For self-hosted deployments, update your environment configuration with your Broker ID:

```javascript
// config.js
window.__RUNTIME_CONFIG__ = {
  "VITE_ORDERLY_BROKER_ID": "your_broker_id",
  "VITE_ORDERLY_BROKER_NAME": "your_broker_name",
  "VITE_DISABLE_MAINNET": "false",
  "VITE_DISABLE_TESTNET": "false"
};
```

## Testnet Setup

To enable testnet for your broker:
1. Register a testnet admin wallet at the broker registration portal (select a testnet chain like Arbitrum Sepolia)
2. Use `http://testnet-dex.orderly.network/` to obtain testnet USDC
3. Perform graduation with the same Broker ID as mainnet

> **Note:** Mainnet and testnet are separate systems. Users must log in again when switching environments, and separate Orderly keys are required for each.

## Adding Your DEX to the Leaderboard

To appear on the Orderly leaderboard at `dex.orderly.network/board`:
1. Log in with any wallet at `https://dex.orderly.network/`
2. Click **Start building** → define a name → **Create DEX Now**
3. Click **Setup DEX Card** and fill in all required information
4. Notify the Orderly team to link your Broker ID to the card

## Security Best Practices

- **Never share** your Orderly secret key or wallet private key with external developers
- The **Broker ID is public** and safe to share
- If a wallet private key is compromised, an attacker could create Orderly key pairs and manipulate funds
- If the Orderly secret is compromised, an attacker could withdraw funds and adjust referral rebates
- Contact Orderly support immediately if credentials are compromised

chunks.title: Multisig Admin Wallets and Delegate Signer Configuration
chunks.content:
Brokers can use multisig wallets (e.g., Gnosis Safe) as their admin wallet for enhanced security. Since multisig contracts cannot directly sign EIP-712 messages, the **Delegate Signer** feature allows an EOA to act on behalf of the multisig.

## Why Use a Multisig Admin Wallet?

- **Enhanced security** for broker fee collection
- **Multi-party approval** for administrative actions
- **ORDER token staking** verification for broker tier classification

## Setup Process

### Step 1: Register the Multisig

1. Go to `https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/`
2. Select **Multisig Wallet** and your Broker ID
3. Connect the multisig address
4. Register a **delegate signer** (an EOA wallet like MetaMask)

> **Critical:** Do NOT use Gnosis Safe's interface for the delegate signer registration step — use a standard EOA wallet (e.g., MetaMask) to sign the delegation message.

### Step 2: Establish the Delegate Link

The delegate signer connection requires your smart contract to call `delegateSigner` somewhere in its logic. The `DelegateContract.sol` provided by Orderly is just an example — you can use any smart contract.

```solidity
// Example: Your contract must call delegateSigner
// The function name doesn't need to be "delegate"
// execAction is just an example function name
function execAction() external {
    // Your contract logic
    delegateSigner(...);
}
```

A multisig like Safe is commonly used to initiate the delegate signer link by creating a transaction that calls the delegation function.

### Step 3: Generate Orderly Keys

1. Sign in to the broker registration page with the **delegated EOA**
2. Click **Generate Orderly Key**
3. The Orderly key is bound to the multisig account, but signed by the EOA

### Step 4: Complete Backend Setup

Provide the multisig wallet address to the Orderly team to finalize configuration.

## Fee Withdrawals with Multisig

- Withdrawals are **approved by the delegated EOA**
- The **withdrawal destination** is the multisig account
- The EOA can be replaced later using the same delegation process
- Broker fees are credited to the account associated with the multisig wallet

## Orderly One Multisig Support

Multisig support has been added to Orderly One with the following flow:
1. **DEX creation and graduation** is performed via an EOA wallet (multisigs cannot sign off-chain messages)
2. After graduation, a step can be completed via the multisig (with instructions for creating the transaction manually in the Safe UI)
3. Once set up, the multisig serves as the admin wallet for fee collection and ORDER staking verification

## Changing the Admin Wallet

If you need to change the admin wallet (e.g., to a new multisig):
1. Register the new wallet at the broker registration portal
2. If using a multisig, register a new delegate signer
3. Contact Orderly support with the new address to complete the update

> **Note:** Revenue settlement history is tied to the admin account. Switching to a new admin account means previous history remains with the old account (preserving revenue data integrity).

## Compromised Admin Wallet Recovery

If an admin wallet is compromised:
1. **Immediately stop** using all devices containing the private key
2. **Contact Orderly support** to change the admin wallet
3. Orderly support will update the Orderly One login wallet
4. Monitor the DEX closely during the transition
5. After the change, the attacker can only potentially modify the DEX itself and the Broker ID

chunks.title: Broker Fee Distribution, Withdrawal, and Tier Management
chunks.content:
Understanding how broker fees are calculated, distributed, and withdrawn is essential for managing your DEX's revenue on Orderly Network.

## Fee Distribution

Broker fees are:
- **Distributed daily** to the broker's Orderly account (associated with the admin wallet and Broker ID)
- Credited to the **Orderly L2 balance** (not directly to the EOA wallet)
- Typically processed a few minutes past midnight UTC

> **Critical:** The admin account must be set up correctly before going live. Without proper registration, the broker will **not accrue any fees** paid by users.

## Fee Structure

### Base Fees (as of 2026)

Orderly's base fee on EVM is **3 bps taker** and **0 bps maker**. Brokers can charge any additional fee on top, which they keep entirely.

**Example:**
- Broker sets taker fee: 6 bps
- Orderly base fee: 3 bps
- **Broker earns: 3 bps per trade**

### RWA Fee Updates

RWA (Real World Asset) fees now match crypto fees:
- RWA Taker Fee aligned with crypto (**1–3 bps**)
- Brokers can choose to lower RWA fees for competitiveness or keep existing fees for higher margins

### Updated Tier Volume Requirements

| Tier | Monthly Volume | ORDER Staked | Base Taker Fee |
|------|---------------|-------------|----------------|
| Public | < $50M | - | 3 bps |
| Silver | >= $50M | >= 100K | 2.75 bps |
| Gold | >= $200M | >= 300K | 2.5 bps |
| Platinum | >= $750M | >= 3M | 2 bps |
| Diamond | >= $2B | >= 7M | 1 bps |

## Withdrawing Broker Fees

### Method 1: Broker Registration Portal
1. Log in at `https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/` with the admin wallet
2. Create an Orderly key if needed
3. Navigate to the **Assets** tab
4. Initiate a withdrawal

### Method 2: Admin Portal
1. Log in at `https://admin.orderly.network/login`
2. View accumulated fees
3. Initiate withdrawal

### Method 3: DEX UI
Connect the admin wallet to your DEX UI, create an account, and withdraw from there. This method is recommended to **preview withdrawal fees** before confirming.

### Withdrawal Fees by Chain

| Chain | Approximate Fee |
|-------|----------------|
| Arbitrum, Base, Optimism | ~$1 (flat) |
| Ethereum Mainnet | Variable (can be significant) |

> **Tip:** Switch to a cheaper network (e.g., Arbitrum) to reduce withdrawal fees. Withdrawals typically take 30 seconds to a few minutes depending on chain congestion.

## Configuring Tiered Fee Structures

### Using the Broker Fee Admin Tool

A tiered fee structure can be configured using the custom fee functionality:

**Repository:** `https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin`

This tool requires your admin account's Orderly key to control fee settings after initial setup by the Orderly team.

### Per-User Custom Fees

Brokers can set custom fee rates per user via the admin console or API:

```
PUT /v1/client/fee_rate
```

### Default Fee Adjustment

Fee rates (maker/taker) can be adjusted at any time via the admin console at `https://admin.orderly.network/login`.

## Futures Fee Collector Migration

When migrating to a new Futures Fee Collector account:

1. **Generate the new account** via the broker registration portal using the delegate signer flow
2. **Pre-fund the new account** before the system maintenance cutoff:
   - Deposit sufficient USDC into the new fee collector account
   - The new account only collects fees generated *after* the switch
   - The first broker rebate occurs the following morning based on the previous day's total fees
   - Without pre-funding, the rebate will fail due to insufficient balance
3. **Deposit methods:**
   - Send USDC to the proxy contract address and execute a deposit via the broker registration portal
   - Call the `depositTo` function directly on the vault contract with correct `accountId`, `brokerHash`, and `tokenHash` parameters

## Staking Wallet

The staking wallet holds staked ORDER tokens and is used to assign the broker the correct discounted fee tier. It is **not** the wallet that receives markup fees — a separate EVM wallet must be provided for receiving broker fee payouts.

chunks.title: EIP-712 Signing: Domains, Message Types, and Key Management
chunks.content:
Orderly Network uses EIP-712 typed data signing for account registration, key management, withdrawals, and PnL settlement. Understanding the domain structure and message types is critical for correct implementation.

## EIP-712 Domain Types

Orderly uses **two distinct EIP-712 domains**:

### Off-Chain Domain
Used for **Registration** and **AddOrderlyKey** messages (processed entirely off-chain).

```json
{
  "name": "Orderly",
  "version": "1",
  "chainId": 42161,
  "verifyingContract": "0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC"
}
```

> The `verifyingContract` is a fixed placeholder address for off-chain operations.

### On-Chain Domain
Used for **Withdraw**, **SettlePnl**, and all **Delegate** variants.

```json
{
  "name": "Orderly",
  "version": "1",
  "chainId": 42161,
  "verifyingContract": "0x6F7a338F2aA472838dEFD3283eB360d4Dff5D203"
}
```

| Environment | Ledger Contract Address |
|-------------|------------------------|
| Mainnet | `0x6F7a338F2aA472838dEFD3283eB360d4Dff5D203` |
| Testnet (Arbitrum Sepolia) | `0x1826B75e2ef249173FC735149AE4B8e9ea10abff` |

## EIP-712 Message Types

### 1. Registration
```json
{
  "brokerId": "string",
  "chainId": "uint256",
  "timestamp": "uint64",
  "registrationNonce": "uint256"
}
```

### 2. AddOrderlyKey
```json
{
  "brokerId": "string",
  "chainId": "uint256",
  "orderlyKey": "string",
  "scope": "string",
  "timestamp": "uint64",
  "expiration": "uint64"
}
```

> **Maximum expiration:** 365 days from creation time. The expiration is specified in **UNIX milliseconds**.

### 3. Withdraw
```json
{
  "brokerId": "string",
  "chainId": "uint256",
  "receiver": "address",
  "token": "string",
  "amount": "uint256",
  "withdrawNonce": "uint64",
  "timestamp": "uint64"
}
```

### 4. SettlePnl
```json
{
  "brokerId": "string",
  "chainId": "uint256",
  "settleNonce": "uint64",
  "timestamp": "uint64"
}
```

### 5. Delegate Variants
All delegate message types include an additional `delegateContract` (address) field:
- **DelegateSigner** — includes `registrationNonce` and `txHash` (bytes32)
- **DelegateAddOrderlyKey** — same fields as AddOrderlyKey + `delegateContract`
- **DelegateWithdraw** — same fields as Withdraw + `delegateContract`
- **DelegateSettlePnl** — same fields as SettlePnl + `delegateContract`

## Orderly Key Generation (Client-Side)

Orderly private keys are generated client-side using **Ed25519**:

```javascript
import * as utils from '@noble/ed25519';
import { encodeBase58 } from 'ethers';

const privateKey = utils.randomPrivateKey();
const publicKey = await utils.getPublicKeyAsync(privateKey);
const orderlyKey = `ed25519:${encodeBase58(publicKey)}`;
```

The derived public key is sent to the Orderly backend for verification. The user's Orderly private key alone is sufficient to **create and delete orders** using the user's vault — no additional permission settings are required.

### Key Limits
- **Maximum Orderly Keys per account:** 30
- **Maximum expiration:** 365 days
- Keys are stored in `localStorage` and are device-specific

### Key Transfer Between Devices
Orderly keys are bound to the device where they were created. Generating a new key on a new device creates a **separate key** — it does not migrate the existing one. If using biometric authentication, the key is tied to the original device's biometric profile.

## PnL Settlement

PnL settlement can be triggered by **anyone** — the account owner, a backend service, or a relayer. This enables automated settlement without requiring users to sign at that moment.

The signing uses the **on-chain EIP-712 domain** (not the off-chain domain used for key registration).

## Withdrawal Security

- Withdrawals **cannot** bypass EIP-712 signing by calling a smart contract function directly
- Withdrawal processing must be handled on the Orderly side
- Funds sent directly to the Orderly vault contract (bypassing the deposit function) are **not recoverable**

## Solana Key Registration

When registering Orderly keys for Solana:
- Set `chainType` to uppercase `"SOL"` (not `"sol"`)
- The `keyExtraParams` field is not needed
- Reference: `https://gist.github.com/wuzhong-zhu/ef97ecb0d26d93dc396ea7e1ededaeee`

## Common Signing Errors

| Error | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `address and signature do not match` (Solana) | `chainType` not uppercase | Use `"SOL"` not `"sol"` |
| Signature verification failed | Using `personal_sign` instead of `signTypedData` | Use proper EIP-712 typed data signing |
| Timestamp drift | Request timestamp differs >300s from server | Sync client clock |
| Key expired | Orderly key past expiration date | Generate a new key pair |

chunks.title: Multi-Level Referral and Affiliate System
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports a comprehensive multi-level referral system with up to 15 levels, enabling brokers to build affiliate programs with flexible commission structures.

## System Architecture

### Referral Levels
- **L1 Affiliates:** Top-level affiliates created directly by the DEX owner (no referrer above them)
- **L2–L15 Affiliates:** Referred by upstream affiliates in a chain
- Each affiliate can have **only one** multilevel referral code

### Commission Flow
```
DEX Owner → L1 Affiliate → L2 Affiliate → L3 Affiliate → ... → L15
```

## Setting Up Referral Codes

### Step 1: Create L1 Affiliate Accounts

The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Once registered, you can create referral codes for them.

> **Important:** Attempting to register a referral code before the user has signed in will result in an `address is not registered` error.

### Step 2: Assign Commission Rates

The DEX owner assigns commission rates via the admin dashboard:
- **Default base rate:** Set globally for all affiliates
- **Custom per-affiliate rates:** Override the default for specific L1 affiliates (e.g., 100% to a key partner)

**Example:** DEX owner assigns 75% commission to an L1 affiliate, retaining 25%.

### Step 3: Downstream Splitting

Each L1 affiliate controls how much of their rebate they pass to downstream referees:

**Example:**
- L1 affiliate receives 80% rebate
- L1 keeps 20%, shares 60% with L2 referees
- L2 can further split with L3, and so on

> Referees do **not** see what level they are — they only see the rebate percentage offered to them.

## Configuring KOL Campaigns

To set up a KOL campaign with specific splits:
1. Create an account with the desired maximum rebate
2. Create an L2 code from that account specifying the split
3. Share the L2 code with the KOL's audience

## Direct Referral Bonus

In addition to the multi-level split, a configurable **direct referral bonus** (e.g., an additional 5–10%) can be added on top of the standard commission.

## Migration from Single-Level to Multi-Level

When upgrading from single-level to multi-level referrals:
- **Existing legacy referral links** remain functional and configurable
- **New single-level affiliate codes** can no longer be created
- All new codes follow the multi-level structure

## Admin Dashboard Management

Referral codes and commission rates are managed through the admin console at `https://admin.orderly.network/login`:
- Create and manage referral codes
- Set default and custom commission rates
- Configure referral thresholds and fee splits
- Monitor referral chain performance

## Best Practices

1. **Pre-register KOL accounts:** Ensure affiliates have connected their wallets before creating codes
2. **Set competitive rates:** Higher L1 commissions attract better affiliates
3. **Monitor chains:** Track which referral levels drive the most volume
4. **Use custom rates:** Reward high-performing affiliates with elevated commission percentages

chunks.title: Privy Social Login and Email Authentication Setup
chunks.content:
Orderly Network supports Privy for email and social login authentication, providing a CEX-like onboarding experience for users who may not have a Web3 wallet.

## Overview

Privy enables:
- **Email-based login** and signup
- **Social authentication** via Google, X (Twitter), and other providers
- **Passkey support** for passwordless authentication
- A more familiar onboarding flow compared to traditional wallet connections

> **Note:** Orderly accounts are based on the user's public key and Broker ID, so a Web3 wallet connection is still required under the hood. Privy abstracts this by creating embedded wallets.

## Orderly One Configuration

Enable Privy in your Orderly One project by adding the Privy App ID to `config.js`:

```json
{
  "VITE_PRIVY_APP_ID": "your_privy_app_id",
  "VITE_PRIVY_LOGIN_METHODS": "email,passkey,twitter,google",
  "VITE_PRIVY_TERMS_OF_USE": "https://yourdomain.com/terms",
  "VITE_ENABLE_ABSTRACT_WALLET": "true"
}
```

## Privy Dashboard Setup

1. Create an app at `https://dashboard.privy.io/`
2. Obtain the **App ID**
3. Configure login methods in the Privy dashboard
4. For social logins (Google, X), set up **OAuth credentials**:
   - Create a Google Developer App for Google OAuth
   - Create an X Developer App for Twitter OAuth
   - Configure redirect URIs to match your DEX domain

> **Note:** OAuth setup is considered advanced configuration and requires developer accounts with each social provider.

## SDK Integration

### Using the Privy Wallet Connector

```tsx
import { WalletConnectorPrivyProvider } from "@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy";

<WalletConnectorPrivyProvider
  network={networkId === 'mainnet' ? Network.mainnet : Network.testnet}
  privyConfig={{
    appId: privyAppId,
    config: { loginMethods: ['email', 'google', 'twitter'] }
  }}
  wagmiConfig={{ connectors: getEvmConnectors() }}
  solanaConfig={getSolanaConfig(networkId)}
>
  <OrderlyAppProvider brokerId="..." brokerName="..." networkId={networkId}>
    <YourApp />
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorPrivyProvider>
```

### Connecting via Privy

```tsx
import { useWalletConnector } from '@orderly.network/hooks';
import { WalletConnectType } from '@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy';

const { connect } = useWalletConnector();

async function connectPrivy() {
  await connect({ walletType: WalletConnectType.PRIVY });
}
```

> **Critical:** You must connect through `useWalletConnector().connect()` with `WalletConnectType.PRIVY`. Do not just call Privy's login hooks directly — the account is only recognized when connected through the Orderly wallet connector.

## Accessing User Email Data

Email login information is **not stored by Orderly**. Brokers can obtain user email data from Privy's dashboard or API, which handles the email-based authentication layer.

## Telegram Mini Apps

Privy with Google OAuth is supported within Telegram Mini Apps (SDK v2.12.3+). The SDK detects `window.Telegram?.WebApp` and routes OAuth through the external browser via `Telegram.WebApp.openLink()`.

## Version History

| Version | Fix/Feature |
|---------|-------------|
| v2.4.1 | Initial Privy support |
| v2.8.13 | Fixed network switching issues with Privy login |
| v2.11.2 | Fixed duplicate Solana addresses via Privy |
| v2.12.3 | Google OAuth in Telegram Mini Apps |

chunks.title: DNS Configuration and Custom Domain Hosting
chunks.content:
Hosting your Orderly-powered DEX on a custom domain requires proper DNS configuration. This guide covers common setups and troubleshooting.

## Subdomain Setup (Recommended)

If your main domain (e.g., `www.yourdomain.com`) is already assigned to another service via a CNAME record, you **cannot** assign a second CNAME with the same name. Use a subdomain instead.

### Step 1: Configure DNS

In your DNS provider (e.g., GoDaddy, Cloudflare), add a new CNAME record:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Type** | CNAME |
| **Name** | `app` (or your chosen subdomain) |
| **Value** | `orderlynetworkcreator.github.io` |
| **TTL** | 3600 (or automatic) |

This will make your DEX accessible at `app.yourdomain.com`.

### Step 2: Configure Orderly One

1. In the Orderly One dashboard, set the domain to your subdomain (e.g., `app.yourdomain.com`)
2. Redeploy the DEX

> **Note:** You do not need to purchase a new domain. A subdomain of your existing domain is sufficient.

## Main Domain Setup

If your main domain is **not** already in use:

1. Set a CNAME record for `www` pointing to `orderlynetworkcreator.github.io`
2. Configure the root domain (`@`) with an A record or ALIAS record as supported by your DNS provider
3. Set the domain in Orderly One to your main domain

## Security Considerations

### HTTPS Enforcement

Ensure that HTTPS connections are enforced on your DNS server. If users encounter errors on mobile when accessing your DEX subdomain, verify:
- SSL/TLS certificates are properly configured
- HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS
- Your DNS provider supports automatic SSL (e.g., Cloudflare Universal SSL)

### Developer Access

**Developers do NOT need access to your admin wallet private key** to configure DNS or domain settings. DNS configuration is handled independently of the DEX admin wallet.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| DEX not loading on custom domain | CNAME not propagated | Wait up to 48 hours for DNS propagation |
| SSL certificate error | HTTPS not configured | Enable SSL in your DNS provider or hosting |
| `www` domain conflicts | Existing CNAME on `www` | Use a subdomain (e.g., `app.` or `trade.`) |
| Mobile browser errors | Mixed content or missing HTTPS | Enforce HTTPS redirect at DNS/server level |

## Updating DEX Card Information

Builders who launched via Orderly One can update their DEX card information at:

```
https://dex.orderly.network/en/dex/card
```

The process takes approximately 3 minutes and can significantly improve the DEX's visibility on the Orderly ecosystem.
