{"category":"Wallet","chunks":[{"title":"Broker ID Registration and Setup","category":"Operations","content":"Registering a Broker ID is the foundational step for launching a DEX on Orderly Network. This guide covers the registration process, required parameters, and environment configuration.

## Required Information

To register a new Broker ID, provide the following details to the Orderly team:

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Broker ID** | Unique lowercase identifier (cannot be changed later) | `my_dex` |
| **Broker Name** | Human-readable display name | `My DEX` |
| **Environment** | `Production`, `Staging`, or both | Both |
| **Default Taker Fee** | Fee charged to takers (minimum 3 bps base) | `0.06%` (6 bps) |
| **Default Maker Fee** | Fee charged to makers (minimum 0%) | `0.03%` (3 bps) |
| **Broker Tier** | Initial tier level | `public` |
| **Staking Wallet** | Wallet for ORDER staking (optional, can be added later) | `0x123...` |

> **Important:** The Broker ID is finalized on-chain and **cannot be changed** after creation. A new Broker ID would effectively mean a new DEX for users. For development and testing, you can temporarily use the `demo` Broker ID.

## Registration Methods

### Manual Registration (Standard)
1. Contact the Orderly team (DevRel or BD) with the required details above.
2. The setup requires multisig approval and typically takes **1–3 business days**.
3. Once the Broker ID is live, proceed to register your admin wallet.

### Orderly One (No-Code / Instant)
Brokers can use [Orderly One](https://dex.orderly.network/) to get a Broker ID instantly (paid option). The graduation process requires a payment of **$10** (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate).

## Environment Separation

Mainnet and testnet are **completely separate systems**. You must:
- Register an account on each environment independently.
- Use the broker registration portal for each network:
  - **Mainnet:** `https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/`
  - **Testnet:** Same portal, but connect to a supported testnet (e.g., Ethereum Sepolia)

You can use the same or different wallet addresses for testnet and mainnet admin wallets.

## Fee Structure Overview

Orderly charges a **base taker fee of 0.03% (3 bps)** and **0% maker fee**. Brokers set their own default fees on top:

- Any amount charged **above** the 3 bps base taker fee becomes broker revenue.
- Example: If broker taker fee is 6 bps, the broker earns 3 bps per taker transaction.
- Orderly retains 3 bps on taker fees and 0 bps on maker fees.
- Brokers **cannot** charge performance fees on realized PnL; revenue comes from the maker/taker fee split only.

Fee rates can be adjusted later via the admin wallet after initial setup.

## Reducing Base Taker Fees

Brokers can reduce the base taker fee through the **Builder Staking Program**:

| Tier | Requirement | Base Taker Fee |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Public | Default | 3 bps |
| Silver | 100K ORDER staked | 2.75 bps |
  | Gold | 300K ORDER staked | 2.5 bps |
| Platinum | ≥$750M 30d volume or 3M ORDER staked | 2 bps |
| Diamond | ≥$2B 30d volume or 7M ORDER staked | 1 bps |

The staking wallet can be different from the admin wallet. If different, provide the staking address to Orderly support for manual linking.

## Using a Single Broker ID Across Multiple Projects

A single Broker ID **can** be used across multiple DEX projects. However:
- All projects sharing the same Broker ID will share the same admin wallet.
- Users will have the **same account** across all platforms using that Broker ID.
- If separate user accounts per platform are desired, distinct Broker IDs are required.","keywords":["broker ID","registration","setup","fee structure","staking","Orderly One","graduation","environment"]},{"title":"Admin Wallet Configuration and Management","category":"Operations","content":"The admin wallet is the central control point for broker operations on Orderly Network. It is used to collect fees, configure settings, and access the admin dashboard.

## Registering an Admin Wallet

After your Broker ID is created, register the admin wallet:

1. **Visit the broker registration portal:** `https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/`
2. **Connect the wallet** you intend to use as the admin wallet.
3. **Complete the standard Orderly account registration flow** under your Broker ID.
4. **Provide the wallet address** to the Orderly team so they can configure admin privileges on the backend (requires multisig approval, typically 1–2 days).

> **Note:** For Orderly One DEXes, go to your DEX URL (e.g., `https://dex.orderly.network/{your-broker-id}/`) and complete registration on any mainnet using the same wallet used to create the DEX. Then notify the Orderly team.

### Admin Wallet Requirements
- **One admin wallet per Broker ID** per environment (mainnet/testnet).
- Can be an **EOA (Externally Owned Account)** or a **multisig wallet** (e.g., Gnosis Safe).
- For multisig wallets, use the 'delegate signer address' field in the broker-registration portal.
- The chain you register on does **not** need to match your deployment chain.

### Best Practices
- Use a **multisig wallet** for mainnet admin operations for enhanced security.
- Use an easily accessible **EOA** for testnet/development.
- **Avoid frequent changes** to the admin wallet.
- Register admin wallets for **both testnet and mainnet** for completeness.

## Changing the Admin Wallet

The admin wallet can be changed after initial setup (e.g., if the original wallet is compromised):

1. **Register the new wallet** at `https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/` under your Broker ID.
2. **Contact the Orderly team** with the new wallet address to switch admin privileges.
3. The update requires **multisig approval** on Orderly's side and cannot be done through the DEX UI.
4. The previous admin wallet's revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

> **Security Note:** In the event of a wallet compromise, Orderly can freeze the affected wallet's fund movement and set up a new one. However, some broker functionalities on Orderly One may be affected, and a hacker could potentially alter broker fee rates before the wallet is frozen.

## Safe Wallet (Multi-sig) Considerations

Separating the admin wallet and fee/earnings wallet can introduce potential risks. The recommended alternative is:
- Use a **smart contract as the admin account**.
- The admin wallet can be a **delegated wallet**.
- The earning wallet will be the **smart contract itself**.

> **Note:** Multi-sig is not currently supported natively in Orderly One, and automated multi-party fee splitting is not available. Brokers needing to share revenue must handle settlements off-chain.

## Admin Dashboard Access

Once configured, access the admin dashboard:
- **Standard Dashboard:** `https://admin.orderly.network/`
- **Beta Dashboard (revamped):** `https://dex-beta.orderly.network`

### Beta Dashboard Features
- DEX analytics & user lookup
- Finances & fee management
- Affiliate management
- Points campaigns
- Permissionless listings dashboard
- Improved UX organization

## Orderly Account ID Calculation

The Orderly Account ID is a unique identifier derived from the wallet address and Broker ID:

```typescript
import { AbiCoder, keccak256, solidityPackedKeccak256 } from "ethers";

export function getAccountId(userAddress: string, brokerId: string): string {
  const abicoder = new AbiCoder();
  return keccak256(
    abicoder.encode(
      ['address', 'bytes32'],
      [userAddress, solidityPackedKeccak256(['string'], [brokerId])]
    )
  );
}
```

A single wallet can have **multiple non-interlinked accounts**, one per broker. Each account is scoped to a specific broker.","keywords":["admin wallet","broker registration","multisig","admin dashboard","account ID","wallet change","delegate signer"]},{"title":"Broker Fee Collection and Revenue Management","category":"Operations","content":"Understanding how broker fees accrue, where they are stored, and how to withdraw them is essential for DEX operators on Orderly Network.

## Fee Accrual Mechanism

Broker fees are **not** sent directly to your on-chain wallet balance. Instead:

1. Fees accrue to the **admin wallet's Orderly account balance** (on Orderly L2).
2. Fees are distributed **daily**, typically around **midnight UTC**.
3. Fees are paid in **USDC** on Orderly's network.
4. The balance is added to the **portfolio balance** of the admin wallet.

## Accessing and Withdrawing Fees

### Method 1: DEX Frontend
1. Log into your DEX frontend using the **admin wallet address**.
2. Navigate to your portfolio/balance section.
3. Fees will be visible within the Orderly account balance.
4. Withdraw to any supported chain.

### Method 2: Broker Registration Portal
Useful for multisig wallets or when the DEX frontend is unavailable:
```
https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/
```
Or the legacy portal:
```
https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/
```

### Method 3: API
Check accumulated fees using the private `Get Current Holding` endpoint:
```bash
curl -X GET https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/client/holding \
  -H "orderly-key: <ADMIN_PUBLIC_KEY>" \
  -H "orderly-signature: <SIGNATURE>" \
  -H "orderly-timestamp: <TIMESTAMP>" \
  -H "orderly-account-id: <ADMIN_ACCOUNT_ID>"
```

## Fee Revenue Breakdown

| Component | Rate | Recipient |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Base Taker Fee | 3 bps (0.03%) | Orderly Network |
| Broker Taker Markup | Configurable (e.g., 3 bps) | Broker |
| Maker Fee | 0% base (configurable) | Broker (if set > 0%) |

**Example:** If the broker sets a 6 bps taker fee:
- Orderly retains 3 bps.
- Broker earns 3 bps per taker transaction.

## Updating Fee Configuration

Fee rates can be adjusted after initial setup via the admin wallet:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/client/update_fee \
  -H "orderly-key: <ADMIN_PUBLIC_KEY>" \
  -H "orderly-signature: <SIGNATURE>" \
  -H "orderly-timestamp: <TIMESTAMP>" \
  -H "orderly-account-id: <ADMIN_ACCOUNT_ID>" \
  -d '{"maker_fee_rate": 0.0002, "taker_fee_rate": 0.0005}'
```

> **Note:** Fee changes may not be immediate and are often applied during periodic backend checks (next-day).

## Monitoring Revenue

- **Dune Dashboard:** Use the Dune dashboard builder section to monitor net fees.
- **Admin Dashboard:** The revamped beta dashboard at `https://dex-beta.orderly.network` provides detailed finances & fee management tools.

## Troubleshooting Fee Discrepancies

If there is a discrepancy between dashboard revenue figures and the actual USDC balance:
1. Verify you are connected with the correct admin wallet.
2. Check that fees have been distributed (daily at ~midnight UTC).
3. Contact Orderly support with your wallet address for investigation.

## Changing the Fee Collection Wallet

The fee collection wallet and admin wallet **must be the same address**. To change it:
1. Register a new wallet as described in the Admin Wallet Configuration guide.
2. Contact the Orderly team to update the configuration.
3. Note: Changing the fee wallet detaches the Orderly One account from the original admin wallet.","keywords":["fee collection","broker revenue","USDC","withdrawal","fee configuration","admin balance","rebates"]},{"title":"Wallet Connection Troubleshooting","category":"Troubleshooting","content":"This guide addresses common wallet connection issues encountered by users and developers on Orderly-powered DEXes.

## Spinning/Loading Circle on Wallet Connect

**Symptom:** The DEX frontend shows a spinning/loading circle indefinitely when trying to connect a wallet.

**Cause:** The app is trying to fetch the on-chain balance through the wallet's RPC and the call is not completing.

**Solutions:**
1. **Switch wallets:** Try a different wallet (e.g., MetaMask) to determine if the issue is wallet-specific.
2. **Check VPN status:** Certain regions (e.g., Indonesia) may have connectivity issues that prevent RPC calls from completing. Disable the VPN or switch regions.
3. **Verify SSL certificate:** Ensure the SSL certificate for your custom domain has been properly created and propagated.

## Mainnet Switch Button Not Clickable

**Symptom:** The mainnet switch button in the broker template is unresponsive.

**Causes and Solutions:**
1. **Network mismatch:** The connected wallet network does not match the web application's expected network. Ensure the wallet is connected to the correct chain.
2. **Broker ID casing:** Ensure the Broker ID in the `.env` file uses **lowercase letters only** (e.g., `bgsc` not `Bgsc`).

## Phantom Wallet Red Warning / Blocked Transactions

**Symptom:** Phantom wallet shows a red warning or blocks deposit transactions.

**Cause:** The DEX frontend uses a non-standard wallet connector (e.g., Reown/WalletConnect + Proxy provider) instead of the standard WalletConnector or Privy's Solana adapter. This alters the provider configuration, preventing Phantom from parsing and simulating the transaction.

**Solutions:**
1. Switch to the **default Orderly connector** or **Privy connector**.
2. Ensure the domain is reviewed and trusted by Phantom/Blowfish.

## WalletConnect for Mobile EVM Wallets

**Symptom:** Mobile users on iOS Safari cannot connect EVM wallets.

**Cause:** Safari on iOS does not support built-in EVM wallet injection.

**Solution:**
1. Obtain a **Project ID** from [Reown](https://dashboard.reown.com/) (formerly WalletConnect).
2. Configure the Reown Project ID in the Orderly One dashboard or your `.env` file.
3. Clear the site cache to ensure WalletConnect appears as a connection option.

## Privy Embedded Wallet Issues

### "Embedded wallet is only available over HTTPS"
**Cause:** Privy requires an HTTPS connection. If the site is served over HTTP (e.g., waiting for SSL certificate provisioning on GitHub Pages), the app will throw this error.

**Solution:** Ensure your hosting enforces HTTPS and that the SSL certificate is properly configured and active.

### HTTP to HTTPS Redirect Issues
**Cause:** Custom domain not properly configured with HTTPS.

**Solution:** Ensure the domain has valid HTTPS certificates and proper redirect rules.

### "Fund Wallet" Error on Email-Based Wallet Creation
**Cause:** A disabled setting in the Privy configuration.

**Solution:** Toggle the relevant funding option **on** in the Privy settings panel for the DEX.

## Coin98 Wallet Integration

To integrate Coin98 wallet:
1. Turn off other wallet providers in Web3 Onboard.
2. Turn on **'Override Metamask'** on Coin98.
3. Test the Connect Wallet flow.

## Tangem Wallet Compatibility

Tangem wallet is compatible with Orderly Network because it is supported through **WalletConnect**.

## Web3-Onboard (Blocknative) to ThirdWeb Migration

**No migration required.** After ThirdWeb acquired Web3-Onboard from Blocknative, ThirdWeb confirmed that current Web3-Onboard users will experience no interruptions. Web3-Onboard remains operational, actively supported, and will be enhanced over time.

## General Debugging Checklist

| Check | Action |
|:---|:---|
| Wallet connected to correct chain? | Verify chain ID matches expected network |
| Broker ID lowercase in config? | Check `.env` and config files |
| SSL certificate active? | Verify HTTPS is working |
| Reown Project ID configured? | Required for WalletConnect/mobile |
| VPN disabled? | Some regions block RPC calls |
| Wallet provider compatible? | Check supported wallet list |","keywords":["wallet connection","troubleshooting","Phantom","WalletConnect","Privy","Coin98","RPC","HTTPS"]},{"title":"Deposit and Withdrawal Troubleshooting","category":"Troubleshooting","content":"This guide covers common issues with deposits and withdrawals on Orderly Network, including cross-chain relay fees, gas errors, and balance discrepancies.

## Deposit Issues

### CALL_REVERTED Error on Mainnet Deposits

**Symptom:** A `CALL_REVERTED` error occurs during a deposit on mainnet.

**Cause:** The user does not have enough ETH (or the native gas token) in their wallet to cover the **cross-chain message relay fees** charged by LayerZero.

**Solution:** Ensure the user's wallet holds sufficient native token balance before initiating the deposit.

### Additional ETH Transfer on Arbitrum Deposits

**Symptom:** A deposit transaction on Arbitrum includes an additional ETH transfer.

**Explanation:** When depositing tokens (e.g., USDC) into Orderly Network on Arbitrum, an additional ETH amount is attached to cover the cost of the cross-chain message relayed from Arbitrum to Orderly chain via LayerZero. If the attached ETH exceeds the actual relay cost, the **excess amount is refunded** back to the sender's wallet.

### Calculating Deposit Fees Programmatically

Call the Vault smart contract's `getDepositFee` function:

```solidity
// DepositData struct
struct DepositData {
    bytes32 accountId;
    bytes32 brokerHash;    // keccak256(brokerId)
    bytes32 tokenHash;     // keccak256(tokenSymbol)
    uint256 tokenAmount;
}

// Call getDepositFee to get required msg.value in WEI
uint256 fee = vault.getDepositFee(userAddress, depositData);
```

The returned fee must be sent as `msg.value` when calling the deposit function.

### Deposits from CEX or Custodial Wallets

If users are depositing from a **Centralized Exchange (CEX)** or a custodial wallet that does not support DApp interactions:
- Use the **Deposit by Transfer** method instead of the Standard Vault Deposit.
- The Standard Vault Deposit requires the user to connect their wallet and invoke the Vault contract's `deposit` function, which is not possible from CEX or custodial wallet contexts.

### Solana Deposit Gas Errors

**Symptom:** Fee or gas error when trying to deposit on Solana via an Orderly DEX.

**Cause:** Depositing on Solana is an on-chain action that requires native **SOL tokens** in the user's wallet to pay for gas fees.

**Solution:** Ensure the wallet has sufficient SOL for the transaction to proceed.

### MetaMask call_reverted on Arbitrum

**Solutions:**
1. Ensure sufficient ETH in the wallet for gas fees on Arbitrum.
2. Verify funds are being sent to the correct **Orderly Vault address** (not an incorrect contract address).
3. If the issue persists, contact Orderly support with the transaction ID.

## Withdrawal Issues

### User Cannot Withdraw Full PnL or Balance

**Common causes:**

1. **Open positions with unrealized PnL:**
   - Users must close all positions and settle unrealized PnL before withdrawing.
   - Check for any remaining open positions (even small ones).

2. **Fees accrued in Orderly account, not external wallet:**
   - Broker fees accumulate in the Orderly account and must be withdrawn via the broker registration portal.

3. **Withdrawal delays:**
   - Cross-chain withdrawals (especially Solana) may experience delays during security upgrades or LayerZero DVN migrations.

**Debugging:** Provide the user's wallet address to Orderly tech support to check backend data including `totalCollateral`, `totalUpnl`, and open positions.

### Tracking Cross-Chain Withdrawals

1. Search for the user's transactions on the Orderly dashboard:
   ```
   https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{WALLET_ADDRESS}?broker_id={BROKER_ID}
   ```
2. Find the withdrawal transaction and use the transaction ID (txid) to track it on [LayerZero Scan](https://layerzeroscan.com).

## Margin and Order Errors

### Error -1101: "The margin will be insufficient after"

**Cause:** Not enough margin (collateral) in the Orderly account.

**Solution:** Deposit USDC (or the relevant collateral token) into the Orderly account before placing orders. Orderly **cannot** automatically deduct tokens from the user's wallet — the user must explicitly send the deposit transaction.

### Isolated Margin Order Failure with Sufficient Balance

**Possible causes:**
1. **Unsettled PnL** from previous positions reducing available balance.
2. **Order quantity exceeding maximum position size** for the configured leverage tier.
3. **Incorrect tick size/step size formatting** — each symbol has its own minimum tick size.
4. In isolated margin mode, only the **allocated margin** is considered, not the total account free balance.

## Recovering Funds Deposited Under Wrong Broker ID

If a user deposited under `demo` or `orderly` instead of the custom Broker ID:

1. Access the recovery dashboard with correct parameters:
   ```
   https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{WALLET}?broker_id=demo&user_id={USER_ID}
   ```
2. Or connect to any DEX using the Orderly or Demo Broker ID:
   - Orderly: `https://dex.orderly.network/{broker-slug}/`
   - Demo: `https://dex.orderly.network/demo/perp/PERP_ETH_USDC`

## Cross-Chain Architecture Notes

Orderly uses a single **CrossChainManager (CCManager)** contract:
- **EVM chains:** Uses the `LedgerCrossChainRelay` channel.
- **Solana:** Uses a separate `SolConnector` contract based on LayerZero V2.
- Direct interaction from unsupported chains via LayerZero is **not possible**. Use a supported chain as an intermediate step.","keywords":["deposit","withdrawal","CALL_REVERTED","LayerZero","gas fees","margin","cross-chain","Solana"]},{"title":"EIP-712 Domain Configuration for Account Registration","category":"API","content":"Orderly uses EIP-712 typed structured data signing for account registration and key management. This guide provides the exact domain separator configuration needed for EVM chains.

## Off-Chain Domain (Registration & Orderly Key)

For off-chain operations such as account registration and Orderly key creation, use the following **hardcoded** domain values regardless of the connected chain:

```json
{
  "name": "Orderly",
  "version": "1",
  "chainId": "<connected_chain_id>",
  "verifyingContract": "0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC"
}
```

### Key Points
- **`name`**: Always `"Orderly"`.
- **`verifyingContract`**: A hardcoded placeholder address (`0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC`). No real smart contract verifies it for off-chain operations.
- **`chainId`**: Must match the chain the user is currently connected to (e.g., `84532` for Base Sepolia testnet, `42161` for Arbitrum One mainnet).

## On-Chain Domain (Vault Operations)

For on-chain operations (e.g., vault deposits/withdrawals), use the **Ledger contract address** on Orderly L2 as the `verifyingContract`.

Refer to the supported chains documentation for contract addresses:
```
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/addresses
```

## Complete Registration Example

### TypeScript Implementation

```typescript
import { AbiCoder, keccak256, solidityPackedKeccak256 } from "ethers";

// Step 1: Define the EIP-712 domain
const domain = {
  name: "Orderly",
  version: "1",
  chainId: 42161, // Arbitrum One
  verifyingContract: "0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC"
};

// Step 2: Define the types
const types = {
  Registration: [
    { name: "brokerId", type: "string" },
    { name: "chainId", type: "uint256" },
    { name: "timestamp", type: "uint64" },
    { name: "registrationNonce", type: "string" }
  ]
};

// Step 3: Construct the message
const message = {
  brokerId: "my_dex",
  chainId: 42161,
  timestamp: Date.now(),
  registrationNonce: "fetched_nonce_from_api"
};

// Step 4: Sign with the user's wallet
const signature = await signer.signTypedData(domain, types, message);

// Step 5: Submit to Orderly API
await fetch("https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/register_account", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    message,
    signature,
    userAddress: await signer.getAddress()
  })
});
```

### Calculating the Orderly Account ID

After registration, the Account ID is deterministically derived:

```typescript
export function getAccountId(userAddress: string, brokerId: string): string {
  const abicoder = new AbiCoder();
  return keccak256(
    abicoder.encode(
      ['address', 'bytes32'],
      [
        userAddress,
        solidityPackedKeccak256(['string'], [brokerId])
      ]
    )
  );
}

// Example:
const accountId = getAccountId("0x1234...5678", "my_dex");
```

## Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Signature verification fails | Wrong `chainId` in domain | Ensure `chainId` matches the connected wallet's chain |
| `verifyingContract` error | Using real contract address for off-chain | Use the hardcoded placeholder for registration |
| Nonce expired | Registration nonce is valid for only 2 minutes | Fetch a fresh nonce before signing |
| Account already exists | Wallet already registered under this Broker ID | Check with `GET /v1/get_account` first |","keywords":["EIP-712","domain separator","registration","signature","account ID","verifyingContract","typed data"]},{"title":"Orderly One DEX Deployment and Migration","category":"Operations","content":"Orderly One is the no-code DEX creation platform for Orderly Network. This guide covers deploying a new DEX, migrating an existing one, and the graduation process.

## Deploying a New DEX

### Step-by-Step Process

1. **Visit Orderly One:** Go to [https://dex.orderly.network](https://dex.orderly.network)
2. **Connect your wallet:** This wallet becomes the admin wallet for fee collection and management.
3. **Configure your DEX:**
   - Set your Broker ID
   - Select supported chains
   - Configure wallet support (e.g., Abstract via Privy, EVM, Solana)
   - Apply CSS theming in the theme editor
   - Set up custom menu entries, Reown Project ID, and images
4. **Graduate your DEX** (see Graduation section below).
5. **Configure custom domain** via CNAME DNS entry.

### DNS Configuration
Update your DNS CNAME record to point to:
```
orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io
```
Replace any previous CNAME (e.g., `cname.vercel-dns.com`).

### Wallet Configuration
- The DEX creator supports **disabling specific wallet types** (EVM, Solana).
- Filter to specific chains as needed.
- Configure **Reown App ID** (formerly WalletConnect Project ID) for mobile wallet support.

## Graduation Process

Graduation activates revenue generation for your DEX.

### Cost
- **Flat fee:** $10 (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate)

### Process
1. Navigate to the graduation page: `https://dex.orderly.network/dex/graduation`
2. Click **'Register with Orderly and Start Earning'**.
3. Complete the payment.
4. Register your admin wallet if not already done.

> **Note:** Before graduation, the DEX is functional but does **not** generate revenue.

### Payment Methods
- **EOA wallet:** Pay directly through the Orderly One platform.
- **Multisig wallet:** Make the payment manually and provide the transaction hash to the Orderly team.

### Troubleshooting Graduation

#### "Quorum not met" Error
**Cause:** Occurs during graduation fee verification even when the correct token and chain are selected.

**Solution:** If the manual verification field (for entering the transaction hash) is not clickable, provide your wallet address and desired Broker ID to Orderly support for manual processing.

#### Verification Fails Despite Successful Transfer
**Causes:**
1. Using the wrong payment token (e.g., ORDER instead of USDC when USDC was selected).
2. Wrong chain selected for verification.
3. Indexer has not picked up the transaction.

**Solutions:**
- Ensure you select the **correct payment token and chain** matching the transaction.
- If the indexer fails, provide the transaction hash and wallet address to Orderly support.
- A legacy incompatibility may require the DEX to be created first via `https://dex.orderly.network/en/dex` before graduation can proceed.

#### Automated Process Fails
If the automated Broker ID graduation fails, the Orderly DevRel team can manually process it. Provide:
- Transaction hash
- Wallet address used on Orderly One
- Desired Broker ID
- Verify the selected chain matches the token's chain

## Migrating an Existing DEX to Orderly One

### Migration Steps

1. Visit [https://dex.orderly.network/](https://dex.orderly.network/) and connect your wallet.
2. Configure the DEX settings (skip optional steps if needed — they can be refined later).
3. Apply your theme CSS in the theme editor.
4. Set up custom menu entries, Reown Project ID, and images.
5. Copy over existing CSS themes, logos, and Reown App IDs from your previous deployment.
6. Once configured and tested, update your DNS CNAME record.
7. Contact the Orderly team to switch your Broker ID.

> **Important:** Open orders, positions, and deposits on the old deployment may need to be closed before migration.

### Linking Broker ID to Orderly One
If a DEX was created using Orderly One and you have an existing Broker ID:
1. Provide the Broker ID and DEX URL to Orderly support.
2. If an admin wallet was already configured separately, the team will verify compatibility and complete the linkage.

## Reown App ID

The Reown App ID (formerly WalletConnect Project ID) is used for WalletConnect integration:
- Found in your project's `.env` file.
- When migrating, you can reuse your existing Reown App ID or create a new one.
- This step is optional during Orderly One setup but required for mobile wallet support.","keywords":["Orderly One","DEX deployment","graduation","migration","no-code","CNAME","Reown","custom domain"]},{"title":"Position Management and Trading Edge Cases","category":"Trading","content":"This guide covers important trading behaviors, position constraints, and edge cases that developers and users should understand when building on Orderly Network.

## Position Constraints

### One Position Per Symbol Per Wallet
A wallet can only hold **one position per symbol** at a time. You cannot hold both a long and short position for the same symbol simultaneously.

- You **can** have multiple open (unfilled) orders for the same symbol.
- To gradually build a position (similar to TWAP), submit multiple smaller orders over time that aggregate into a single position as they fill.

### Hedge Mode
Hedge mode (holding both long and short positions for the same symbol) is **on Orderly's roadmap** but not yet available. In the meantime, implementing split accounts for the same wallet would need to be developed independently by the broker.

### Sub-Accounts
Sub-account support is planned but was not available as of early 2025. The feature is on the roadmap for future release.

> **Note:** A maximum of **10 sub-accounts** can be created under a main account (when available). This is a security constraint.

## Liquidation Behavior

### Partial Liquidations
If a user's position shows a **smaller quantity** than their filled order, a partial liquidation likely occurred.

**How it works:**
- Liquidations are triggered when the **maintenance margin ratio (MMR)** is breached:
  ```
  start_collateral / start_holding_notional < MMR
  ```
- The position quantity is **reduced** during liquidation.
- The remaining quantity stays open.

**Debugging:**
- Check the user's position history for liquidation events.
- Use the Orderly dashboard:
  ```
  https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{ADDRESS}?broker_id={BROKER_ID}
  ```
- Provide the wallet address to Orderly tech support for detailed backend analysis.

## Referral Code Management

### Changing Referral Codes
Once a referral code has been **bound to at least one referee**, it **cannot be changed**. A new code can only be created if no referees are bound yet.

**Workaround:** To use a different code, the user must register with a new wallet.

### Migrating Referral Relationships
Referral relationships **cannot be migrated** between wallets. As an alternative, the Orderly team can manually reduce the rebate rate on the existing referral chain.

## Governance and Token Mechanics

### $ORDER Governance
Orderly has a governance system where $ORDER stakers can vote on proposals:
- A passed governance proposal redirects up to **60% of Orderly fees** into $ORDER buybacks.
- **50%** goes to stakers (as esORDER with 3-month vesting).
- **50%** goes to a community-controlled wallet (usage decided via vote).
- The community can also vote on token delistings via the **'Vote to Retain'** process.

### Staking and Unstaking
- **Unstaking ORDER** requires a **7-day waiting period**.
- **esORDER** requires a **90-day conversion period** to ORDER with no yield during conversion.
- Brokers can stake ORDER from the Orderly One dashboard's graduation page or any wallet (provide staking address to Orderly support for manual configuration).

## NEAR-Specific Notes

### Checking Bridged nETH Balance
Bridged nETH may not appear in the NEAR Wallet UI due to indexing issues. Verify via CLI:

```bash
NEAR_ENV=mainnet near view aurora ft_balance_of '{"account_id": "<your_account>.near"}'
```

### Bridging from Gnosis Safe to NEAR
There is no Gnosis Safe equivalent on NEAR. The recommended approach:
1. Bridge assets from Gnosis Safe to a regular ETH wallet.
2. Use Rainbow Bridge to transfer to NEAR.
3. On NEAR, use **Sputnik DAO** as a multisig alternative.

## Permissionless Vault (PMV)

Permissionless Vault lets any EOA wallet deploy a fully functional Strategy Vault in a single transaction:
- No applications, approvals, or manual onboarding required.
- Backend automation handles cross-chain registration, account provisioning, and configuration.
- Time to live is under **30 minutes** with zero manual intervention.
- Leverages deterministic contract deployment (CREATE3), cross-chain messaging (LayerZero V2), and automated backend provisioning.

> **Disclaimer:** A permissionlessly created vault is deployed and operated by its creator, not by Orderly. Orderly does not vet, operate, or backstop these vaults.","keywords":["position management","liquidation","hedge mode","referral","governance","ORDER staking","PMV","NEAR"]}]}

chunks.title: Broker Configuration and Fee Structures
chunks.content:
Setting up and managing your broker identity, fee structures, and revenue sharing is fundamental to operating an Orderly-powered DEX. This guide covers broker registration, fee tiers, and revenue mechanics.

## Broker Registration

To configure a new broker on Orderly Network, provide the following information to the Orderly team:

1. **Environment**: Testnet or Mainnet
2. **Broker ID**: A unique string identifier (e.g., `my_dex`)
3. **Broker Name**: Display name for your DEX
4. **Default Taker Fee Rate**: Must be ≥ 0.03% (3 bps)
5. **Default Maker Fee Rate**: Must be ≥ 0%
6. **Broker Admin Account**: EVM address (registered after broker ID is configured)

### Testing vs Production

- **Testing**: Use the `demo` broker ID for initial development and testing.
- **Production**: Create your own broker ID via Orderly One for $10 (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate).

> **Warning**: Never use the default `Orderly` Broker ID in production. It is reserved for Orderly's internal use and may result in higher fees, account visibility issues, and lost asset access.

### Changing Your Broker ID

The broker ID and name are configured on the Orderly backend and cannot be renamed directly. To change your DEX name:
1. Set up a new broker ID
2. Update the broker ID in your DEX's `.env` file
3. Note: Existing users will lose access to their transaction history under the old broker ID (funds are not lost but become inaccessible under the new ID)

You can display any name on your UI regardless of the underlying broker ID.

## Fee Structure

### Base Fees (What Orderly Charges)

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Base Maker Fee | Requirements |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------------|
| Public | 3 bps (0.03%) | 0 bps | Default |
| Gold | 2.5 bps | -0.10 bps | 300,000 $ORDER staked |
| Platinum | 2 bps | -0.15 bps | ≥$750M 30-day volume OR 3M $ORDER staked |
| Diamond | 1 bps | -0.20 bps | ≥$2B 30-day volume OR 7M $ORDER staked |

### Broker Revenue

Brokers set their own user-facing fees. The revenue is the difference between what you charge users and Orderly's base fee:

```
Broker Revenue = User Fee - Orderly Base Fee
```

**Example (Gold Tier, 2.5 bps base):**
- You charge 6 bps taker, 3 bps maker
- Orderly keeps 2.5 bps taker, 0 bps maker
- **You earn**: 3.5 bps taker, 3 bps maker

On $10M volume (100% taker): $3,500 broker revenue
On $10M volume (100% maker): $3,000 broker revenue

### Fee Tier Updates

Fee tier changes (from staking ORDER tokens) are processed by a backend script that runs daily around 00:10 UTC. Changes typically take effect by 2-3 AM UTC the following day.

### Referral and Affiliate Fees

- Orderly's base fee is **excluded** from referral fee splits
- Only the broker's fee portion is shared with referral participants
- Brokers configure maximum rebate and initial referral ratio
- Referrers can adjust the ratio afterwards

**Example**: If taker fee is 4 bps with 3 bps going to Orderly, the remaining 1 bps (broker fee) is split between builder, referrer, and referred user.

### Withdrawal Fees

Withdrawal fees are retained entirely by Orderly and are not shared with broker partners.

### Swap Fees

Swap fees can be configured in the Orderly One dashboard:
- Maximum fee: 100 basis points (1%)
- 70% of the markup goes to the DEX broker
- A fee under 0.2% is recommended to remain competitive

## Campaigns and Competitions

A single campaign can track activity across multiple broker IDs simultaneously. Provide broker IDs as a comma-separated list:

```
woofi_pro, vooi, bitoro_network, what_exchange
```

> **Note**: Broker IDs can be added before the campaign starts, but adding brokers after the campaign has begun may not retroactively capture earlier data.

To add a campaign page to your Orderly One DEX, enable the 'Campaign' option in your dashboard.

chunks.title: Omnichain Architecture and Cross-Chain Operations
chunks.content:
Orderly Network operates as an omnichain perpetual trading infrastructure built on an OP Stack L2 settlement layer. Understanding the cross-chain architecture is essential for proper integration.

## High-Level Architecture

Orderly splits the stack into three layers:

1. **Asset Layer (Vaults)**: Smart contracts deployed on each supported chain where users deposit and withdraw funds
2. **Settlement Layer (Orderly L2)**: An OP Stack L2 that acts as the transaction ledger
3. **Engine Layer (Orderbook)**: Provides order matching and execution services

### How Cross-Chain Works

Tokens are **not** actually moved across chains. The flow is:

1. User deposits into the Orderly Vault smart contract on Chain A
2. LayerZero sends a cross-chain message to Orderly's L2 to track the deposit
3. User can withdraw from Chain B — Orderly rebalances the Vault smart contracts internally
4. All transaction records are securely logged on Orderly Chain

## Supported Chains

Orderly supports 17+ chains including:
- **EVM**: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, BNB Chain, Mantle
- **Non-EVM**: Solana, Movement (Fungible Asset standard only)

> **Note**: Polygon is not available due to an exclusivity agreement with another broker. Some chains may not be available to all brokers.

### Chain Requirements for New Integrations

For Orderly to deploy on a new chain, it must have:
1. EVM compatibility
2. USDC support (native or wrapped)
3. LayerZero integration for cross-chain messaging

> **Important**: LayerZero integration is a hard requirement. Native bridges alone (e.g., Hyperlane) are not sufficient.

## Multi-Collateral Support

Multi-collateral varies by chain:

| Chain | Supported Collateral |
|-------|---------------------|
| Ethereum | USDC, USDT, ETH, YUSD, wBTC |
| BNB Chain | USDC, USDT, BNB |
| Base | USDC, ETH |
| Arbitrum | USDC, USDT, ETH |
| Solana | SOL, USDC, USDT |

ETH has an 80% collateral margin ratio. Additional chains and tokens are added over time.

## Deposit Operations

### Deposit Fees

Orderly does not charge deposit fees. Costs include:
- Network gas fee on the source chain
- LayerZero cross-chain messaging fee (varies by chain and network conditions)

Fees must be fetched on-chain via the vault contract's `depositFee` function at transaction time — they cannot be reliably hardcoded.

### Depositing on Behalf of Another User

Use the `depositTo` function on the Vault smart contract instead of the standard `deposit`:

```solidity
// Vault contract (e.g., Arbitrum: 0x816f722424B49Cf1275cc86DA9840Fbd5a6167e9)
vault.depositTo(accountId, brokerHash, tokenHash, amount);
```

### Decoding Deposit Transaction Data

The deposit function uses selector `0x322dda6d`. Parameters (32 bytes each):
1. Account ID
2. Broker Hash (identifies the broker/frontend)
3. Token Hash (Keccak-256 hash of the token symbol string)
4. Token Amount (uint256)

To identify a token from its hash, compute `keccak256("USDT")` and match against the data field.

### AI Agent / Bot Deposits

Orderly settlement occurs on Arbitrum. When depositing from other chains:
- Bridge tokens to Arbitrum first, then call the deposit function, OR
- Use the proper cross-chain deposit flow

> **Critical**: Sending tokens directly to a vault address on a non-Arbitrum chain (e.g., sending Base USDC to an Arbitrum vault address on Base) will result in **unrecoverable loss**.

Reference: [Orderly Skills Repository](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/skills)

## Withdrawal Operations

### Withdrawable Balance Calculation

```
Withdrawable ≈ Total Balance + Unrealized PnL - Maintenance Margin
```

Capped by total account balance. When a position is closed, realized PnL is added to collateral.

### Vault Liquidity

Most vaults support 1M+ withdrawals. If a vault has insufficient liquidity:
- Orderly's auto-rebalancer moves funds between chains (typically < 1-2 minutes)
- Users can withdraw from another chain with available liquidity instantly

### Handling Unsupported Token Deposits

If a user deposits an unsupported token (e.g., USDT to a USDC-only address):
- Funds are held in the smart contract but not credited
- Once native support launches, the backend indexer automatically scans historical blocks and credits funds (may take up to a day)
- For manual recovery before native support, contact Orderly support

## Cross-Chain Messaging (LayerZero DVN)

Following security upgrades, Orderly pathways require at least a 3/3 DVN configuration:

- **Required**: Canary
- **Optional**: Horizen, LZ Labs, Nethermind
- **Optional Threshold**: 2

When selecting DVN addresses from metadata, use the address where `lzReadCompatible` is `false` if multiple addresses exist for the same provider.

### Solana Address Mapping

For deposits/withdrawals, Orderly saves the original Solana address as bytes32. For staking/rewards, the Solana address is converted to EVM via keccak256 hashing truncated to 20 bytes.

chunks.title: Orderly One: DEX Creation, Customization, and Deployment
chunks.content:
Orderly One is a low-code/no-code platform for creating and customizing perpetual DEX frontends. This guide covers the full lifecycle from creation to deployment.

## Getting Started

Access Orderly One at [https://dex.orderly.network/](https://dex.orderly.network/). A tutorial video is available at [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TKtT4yagr0A).

### Testnet

Testnet is enabled by default when creating a new DEX unless you explicitly check 'disable testnet' during setup.

### Graduation

After building your DEX, pay the graduation fee ($10 (USDC, USDT, or equivalent $ORDER, no rebate)) to:
- Gain access to customize fees
- Monetize your platform
- Get your DEX card displayed on the Orderly One board

> **Note**: Staked ORDER tokens cannot be used for graduation. The fee must be paid with liquid (unstaked) funds.

> **Known Bug**: The graduation UI may not accept decimal fee values. Use whole numbers during graduation and adjust fees afterward. Alternatively, use the beta panel at `https://dex-beta.orderly.network/`.

## Theme and UI Customization

### Logo Setup

- Use a transparent background (alpha channel) image
- Dimensions: 600x120 pixels
- Icon on the left, text on the right
- For seamless top navigation bar integration: remove the logo background or match it to your DEX background color

### Secondary Logo

Configure the Secondary Logo in broker settings to prevent the UI from falling back to the default Orderly Network logo during certain interactions.

### Color Configuration

- Click 'Edit Desktop' and click directly on page sections to change colors
- The color picker is available directly from the section editing screen (no need to go into 'Themes')
- **Primary color** affects: leverage indicator, close buttons, and UI elements
- Links at the top use a gradient between 'Primary' and 'Primary Light'

### CSS Customization

Apply custom CSS via the Orderly One dashboard using CSS variables prefixed with `--oui-`:

```css
:root {
  --oui-color-primary: #your-color;
  --oui-font-family: "Your Font", sans-serif;
  --oui-rounded-lg: 8px;
  --oui-spacing-md: 16px;
}
```

#### Hiding 'Powered by Orderly'

```css
.oui-scaffold-footer-powered-by {
  display: none;
}
```

Or for the bottom-right label:

```css
body>div.oui-scaffold-root>div.oui-box.oui-scaffold-footer>div>div.oui-box.oui-flex {
  display: none;
}
```

> **Known Issue**: Platform upgrades may override custom CSS styling. Re-apply your custom CSS after upgrades.

> **Known Bug**: Brand gradient and button colors may not sync with the primary color setting. Set these via CSS directly as a workaround.

### PnL Card Customization

Configure PnL card settings in `app/utils/config.tsx`. Reference: [Sample Config](https://gist.github.com/wuzhong-orderly/419c8bd0fbc38f91444cbb84aa39d528)

Replace the PnL share background image in the `public/pnl` folder. Reference dimensions: [broker-template/pnl](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/broker-template/tree/main/public/pnl)

## Custom Domain Setup

### DNS Configuration

For a subdomain (e.g., `app.yourdomain.xyz`):

| Type | Name | Value |
|------|------|-------|
| CNAME | app | cname.vercel-dns.com |
| CNAME | testnet | cname.vercel-dns.com |

For Orderly One hosted DEXes, point CNAME to `orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io` (use a dot, not a hyphen).

### Configuration Steps

1. Enter the full subdomain (e.g., `dex.holylabs.xyz`) in the custom URL field
2. Select 'DNS Only' option (disable proxy/CDN features like Cloudflare's orange cloud)
3. Ensure no conflicting DNS entries exist
4. Enforce HTTPS for automatic redirects
5. SSL certificate propagation can take 1-2 days

> **Tip**: Use a subdomain like `app.yourdomain.xyz` to avoid collisions with a landing page on the root domain.

### Domain Card Configuration

Configure domain and card info at `https://dex.orderly.network/dex/card` to prevent broken links when self-hosting.

## Feature Configuration

### OmniVault Deposits

1. Enable the Vaults menu from the Orderly One dashboard
2. Click 'Update DEX' to apply
3. Deposits available via the Vault page or `https://app.orderly.network/`

### Affiliate/Referral Program

- Supported on the no-code white-label product
- Multi-level affiliate system available from the DEX admin dashboard
- Activate directly from the admin panel

### Analytics

- **Orderly One**: Amplitude analytics available as a built-in feature
- **Custom deployments**: Integrate Google Analytics or other providers by modifying frontend code

## Known Issues

### Chain Disappearing After Config Changes

Orderly One disables certain chains by default. When a broker ID is manually configured to support additional chains (like SEI), any UI configuration change resets supported blockchains to the default set. Contact the Orderly team to re-enable unsupported chains after config changes.

### Affiliate Link Reverting

Referral links may revert to the default `orderly.network` domain instead of your branded domain. Contact the Orderly team to apply a fix. The issue may reappear after DEX configuration changes.

### 'Visit DEX' Link

The 'Visit DEX' link set during graduation cannot be modified from the UI. Contact the Orderly DevRel team to manually update it on the backend.

chunks.title: Order Execution, Positions, and Liquidation Mechanics
chunks.content:
Understanding Orderly's order execution, position management, and liquidation mechanics is critical for building reliable trading applications.

## Order Placement

### Key Fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `order_quantity` | Amount in base asset (e.g., ETH for PERP_ETH_USDC) |
| `order_type` | LIMIT, MARKET, etc. |
| `side` | BUY or SELL |
| `reduce_only` | If true, order can only reduce/close an existing position |
| `slippage` | Expressed as a percentage where 1 = 1% maximum |

> **Common Error**: Using `order_amount` instead of `order_quantity` in Futures mode triggers error `-1005: Placing orders by this order amount is not supported in Futures mode`.

### Reduce-Only Orders

When `reduce_only: true`:
- The order can only reduce an existing position, never open or increase one
- If placed in the opposite direction of a position, it closes (or partially closes) the position
- Users may inadvertently trigger closures if reduce-only is enabled without awareness

**Why reduce-only orders get cancelled:**
- If the position's tokens are locked by active Algo Orders (TP/SL), the system only fills tokens that are free/available
- Remaining tokens are cancelled because reserved tokens cannot be touched
- **Solution**: Ensure reduce-only order quantity does not exceed the unlocked portion of the position

### Stop Orders vs TPSL Orders

| Feature | Stop Order | TPSL Order |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Auto-cancel on position close | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Manual cancellation needed | Yes | No |
| Use case | Standalone triggers | Attached to positions |

> **Note**: You cannot cancel an individual child order (TP or SL) from a `Position_TP_SL` trigger. You must cancel the entire parent order and recreate it.

## Leverage

Leverage on Orderly is **account-level** (cross margin), not per-order:

- The configured max leverage is a cap preventing excessive position sizes
- Actual leverage is estimated based on total collateral, open positions, and pending orders
- Example: $100 USDC collateral with 20x max leverage → can place orders worth up to $2,000

### Hedge Mode

Hedge mode (simultaneous long and short on the same ticker) is **not currently supported** under the same margin mode. Workarounds:
1. Use sub-accounts to hold opposing positions
2. Use a combination of isolated margin + cross margin modes on the same symbol

## Liquidation Mechanics

### Partial vs Full Liquidation

**Partial Liquidation**: Occurs when margin ratio falls below threshold but is not critically low. Only a portion of the position is liquidated to restore required margin.

**Full Liquidation**: Occurs when:
- Margin ratio falls to a critically low level
- Account's total notional value falls below minimum threshold
- Margin ratio equals the target ratio

The outcome also depends on the liquidator, position notional value, and symbol.

### Impact Margin Notional

As of October 3, 2025, the impact margin notional is **1000** for all perpetual contracts.

### Liquidation Execution

- Liquidation orders are handled **off-chain** on Orderly
- There is **no on-chain transaction hash** associated with liquidations
- There is no way to immediately trigger a liquidation for testing
- There is no way to subscribe to liquidation events filtered by broker ID

For liquidation bot development, refer to: [liquidation-searcher](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/liquidation-searcher)

### Liquidation API Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Get Positions Under Liquidation | Positions that can still be claimed by a liquidator |
| Get Liquidated Positions Info | Positions already claimed by a liquidator |

## Sub-Accounts

- Only the **main account** can make deposits and withdrawals
- Sub-accounts only support internal fund transfers between main and sub-account
- Funds deposited always go to the main account first
- Sub-accounts and main accounts share the same credentials
- Internal transfers appear in the **Withdrawal History** tab, not Transfer History

## Orders and Positions Relationship

Orders and positions are **separate entries** in the Orderly system:
- A single position can be constructed from many orders in both directions
- There is no built-in mechanism to tag positions with custom metadata (e.g., external order IDs)

## Execution Latency

Orderly's median latency is approximately **0.2 seconds**, matching or beating competitors. Makers may experience faster execution due to a 0.15s delay applied to taker orders.

## Isolated Margin

Isolated margin support was introduced at the system level in the March 2026 upgrade. Margin adjustment history for isolated positions is not currently tracked.

chunks.title: Troubleshooting Common Integration Issues
chunks.content:
This guide addresses common issues encountered during Orderly integration, with solutions and workarounds.

## Broker ID Issues

### Account and Positions Disappear After Refresh

**Symptom**: After refreshing the page, account and positions are missing.

**Cause**: The Broker ID is not properly configured in the DEX frontend code. The system falls back to using `Orderly` as the default Broker ID, which is reserved for internal use.

**Solution**: Ensure your specific Broker ID (e.g., `demo` for testing or your registered production ID) is explicitly set in the configuration.

```tsx
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"  // Not "Orderly" or "orderly"
  networkId="mainnet"
>
```

If assets are stuck under the wrong Broker ID, contact Orderly support for recovery assistance.

### No Networks Available to Select

**Symptom**: After configuring a broker ID in the frontend, no networks appear.

**Cause**: The broker ID has not yet been registered by the Orderly team.

**Solution**: Use the `demo` broker ID for testing until your custom broker ID is confirmed and registered.

### 'BrokerNotAllowed' Error on Deposit

**Symptom**: Deposit contract call fails with `BrokerNotAllowed`.

**Cause**: The broker ID has not been whitelisted on the smart contract for that specific chain. This can happen on mainnet even if deposits worked on testnet.

**Solution**: Contact the Orderly team to ensure your broker ID is registered on the target chain's contracts. Each chain must be configured separately.

## Deposit and Withdrawal Issues

### Testnet Deposits Stuck in Pending

**Symptom**: Testnet deposits remain pending for extended periods.

**Cause**: Cross-chain transaction issues with LayerZero on testnet.

**Solution**: Once the LayerZero cross-chain transaction completes, assets are automatically credited. Contact Orderly support if delays persist.

### 'Insufficient Balance' on Withdrawal (Specific Chains)

**Symptom**: Withdrawal fails with 'insufficient balance' on chains like BNB Chain.

**Cause**: The specific chain's vault has insufficient USDC liquidity.

**Solution**:
- Wait for Orderly to manually rebalance funds (requires multi-sig approval, may take several hours)
- Withdraw using alternative assets (e.g., USDT) or from a different chain
- Cross-chain messaging congestion can compound delays

### Deposit Not Reflected in Account

**Troubleshooting steps**:
1. Verify the transaction on the relevant block explorer
2. Check that the user has selected the correct time range in deposit history
3. If confirmed on-chain but not reflected, provide the user's address and transaction hash to the Orderly team

### Withdrawal to Unsupported Chain

**Symptom**: Error 'Withdrawal to this chain is not supported' for Polygon.

**Cause**: Polygon is not supported due to an exclusivity agreement between Polygon, QuickSwap, and WOOFi.

## UI and Configuration Issues

### DEX Logo Reverting to Orderly Network Logo

**Cause**: Secondary Logo has not been configured for the broker.

**Solution**: Set up the Secondary Logo in the broker configuration.

### Button Text Not Visible

**Symptom**: Text on 'Create Account' or 'Deposit' buttons is invisible.

**Solution**: Adjust the Primary Contrast color in the theme config to black or white.

### Deposit Widget Missing on Mobile

**Cause**: Portfolio page is disabled in DEX configuration.

**Solution**: Enable the portfolio page in DEX settings.

### Collateral Asset Ordering

**Limitation**: Prioritizing or reordering specific collateral assets in the deposit selection UI is not currently configurable. Builders cannot remove specific deposit collaterals or change display order.

## Fee Configuration Issues

### taker_fee_rate Validation Error

**Symptom**: Misleading error message about fee format.

**Valid range**: `0.0003` (3 bps) to `0.01` (100 bps) in **decimal format**, not percentage.

```javascript
// Correct
{ taker_fee_rate: 0.0006 }  // 6 bps

// Incorrect
{ taker_fee_rate: 6 }       // Not percentage
```

## Cross-Chain and LayerZero Issues

### InvalidInboundNonce on Solana (Error 6007)

**Cause**: Messages delivered out of order on an ordered execution pathway. A previous message failed and was not retried before subsequent messages.

**Solution**: Implement a retry system that processes failed messages in nonce order. Ensure the `nextNonce` function is correctly implemented in your OApp.

### Cross-Chain Delays

Delays can occur due to LayerZero infrastructure issues. During such events:
- Funds remain safe
- Processing is paused while LayerZero resolves issues
- Monitor the Orderly System Maintenance Telegram channel for updates

## Support Channels

- **Technical Support**: [The Cantina Discord](https://discord.com/invite/cantina)
- **Ticketing**: [Support Channel](https://discord.com/channels/1345243643853803613/1351943310700183572)
- **System Updates**: Orderly System Maintenance Telegram channel
- **Audit Reports**: [GitHub Audits](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/Audits)
- **Brand Kit**: [Notion Brand Kit](https://coral-shark-13c.notion.site/Orderly-Network-Brand-Kit-bbc1f6513c26439c90dda117b83e063e)

chunks.title: Governance, Staking, and Token Delisting
chunks.content:
Orderly Network includes governance mechanisms, a staking program, and community-driven token retention processes that brokers should understand and communicate to their users.

## $ORDER Staking

### Staking Overview

- **APR**: Approximately 20%, paid in USDC
- **Supported Chains**: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon
- **Staking Page**: [https://app.orderly.network/staking](https://app.orderly.network/staking)

> **Note**: Airdrop claims are only available on Ethereum, but staking can be done on any supported chain.

### Smart Contract Integration

Staking is done through the proxy contract at `0xC8A8Ce0Ab010E499ca57477AC031358febCbbF17`.

```javascript
// 1. Approve ORDER token for the proxy contract
const ORDER_TOKEN = "0x4E200fE2f3eFb977d5fd9c430A41531FB04d97B8";
await orderToken.approve(PROXY_CONTRACT, amount);

// 2. Fetch LayerZero fee
const lzFee = await proxyContract.quoteStakeOrder(amount, userAddress);

// 3. Call stakeOrder with LZ fee as value (app multiplies by 1.1 for safety)
await proxyContract.stakeOrder(amount, userAddress, { value: lzFee * 1.1n / 10n });
```

### Third-Party Staking Integration

Protocols can integrate Orderly staking via two strategies:

1. **USDC-Based Strategy**: Users deposit USDC; a portion buys and stakes ORDER in the background
2. **ORDER-Based Strategy**: Users deposit ORDER directly, earning both Orderly staking APR (USDC) and additional protocol rewards

### Unstaking

Press the down arrow in the staking interface to reveal the unstake button.

## Builder Staking Program Tiers

Staking ORDER tokens reduces the base taker fee for brokers:

| Tier | Base Taker Fee | Requirement |
|------|---------------|-------------|
| Public | 3 bps | Default |
| Gold | 2.5 bps | 300,000 $ORDER staked |
| Platinum | 2 bps | ≥$750M 30-day volume OR 3M $ORDER staked |
| Diamond | 1 bps | ≥$2B 30-day volume OR 7M $ORDER staked |

Fee changes take effect the day after staking (processed around 00:10 UTC, effective by 2-3 AM UTC).

## Community Vote to Retain

### How It Works

When tokens are identified for potential delisting due to sustained low metrics, a **Vote to Retain** governance process is initiated.

### Voting Mechanics

- **Threshold**: More than 3% (or 5% depending on the proposal) of total staked $ORDER must vote **'AGAINST Delisting'**
- **Voting Period**: Typically 5 days
- **Voting Token**: Staked $ORDER tokens only

### Broker Responsibilities

Brokers are encouraged to:
1. Inform their communities about upcoming votes
2. Encourage participation using staked $ORDER
3. Monitor the Orderly governance blog for vote announcements

Tokens that do not receive sufficient 'AGAINST Delisting' votes are delisted from the platform.

## Snapshot Voting Configuration

To configure Snapshot voting for Orderly governance:

```json
{
  "name": "orderly-staked-order",
  "params": {
    "symbol": "ORDER"
  }
}
```

The `address` and `decimals` parameters are not needed. Only `symbol` is required to display voting power in the UI.

Reference: [snapshot-strategies PR #1775](https://github.com/snapshot-labs/snapshot-strategies/pull/1775)

### Embedding Snapshot on Link3

Use the Snapshot block under the "Other" category. Legacy URL format required:
```
https://snapshot.org/#/orderlygov.eth
```

## Permissionless Listings

Builders can list any asset themselves without relying on Orderly:
- Earn 50% of Orderly's base fees from listed assets
- Earn 100% of liquidation fees from listed assets

## Negative Maker Fees

Orderly pays builders for placing maker orders with rebates of up to **0.20 bps** depending on DEX tier and asset. This helps bootstrap liquidity and tighten spreads.

## Permissionless Vaults

Users can create community vaults and monetize their strategies on any Orderly-powered DEX. OmniVault deployment requires coordination with the Orderly team as a strategy provider.

Reference: [OmniVault Onboarding Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1scvOWLkgK556mMl4xZrPeXgYixAxdgsQlfArMW0gf1U)

chunks.title: DefiLlama, Analytics, and External Integrations
chunks.content:
This guide covers how to list your Orderly-powered DEX on analytics platforms, integrate with external services, and leverage Orderly's ecosystem tools.

## DefiLlama Integration

### Listing Your DEX

To report fees and volumes to DefiLlama:

1. Fork the DefiLlama dimension-adapters repository
2. Use the Orderly adapter template: [defillama-adapter-template](https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/defillama-adapter-template/tree/main)
3. Set the chain to `'Orderly Chain'` in your adapter configuration
4. Submit a PR with your broker ID
